AsValue's Swift cases became nested subclasses/objects of the Kotlin sealed class in the same order, with the payload property named `value` and capitalised case names (Kotlin style); `String` is written as `kotlin.String` because the nested class shadows it inside the sealed class body.

AsObject is a typealias for `Map<String, AsValue>`: the decoder builds values with MutableMap and hands them back as read-only maps, matching Swift's value-type dictionaries; encodeAsObject iterates the map entries.
AmfError is a sealed class extending Exception whose singleton objects carry the Swift case names as messages, so `throw AmfError.NotNumber` and friends keep the original call sites unchanged.
AsEcmaArray.get throws NoSuchElementException("Not found") because Swift threw a bare String error for a missing key.
`String.utf8Data` maps to `toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8)`; the short/long string limit test uses `data.size.toUInt() > UShort.MAX_VALUE.toUInt()`.

Date maps to java.time.Instant: encodeDate writes `epochSecond * 1000.0 + nano / 1_000_000.0` and decodeDateValue rebuilds the Instant from truncate/roundToLong so Double-second precision is preserved like Swift's Date.
decodeInt reproduces Swift's `Int(exactly: ...rounded(.towardZero))` with a truncate-toward-zero plus NaN/range check instead of Kotlin's saturating toInt().

ByteWriter/ByteReader from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util are assumed to be interfaces exposing writeUInt8/writeUInt16/writeUInt32/writeDouble/writeBytes and readUInt8/readUInt16/readUInt32/readDouble/readUtf8Bytes(length: Int), all throwing on failure.
Struct with only stored properties becomes a data class; the Swift memberwise initialiser becomes the primary constructor with every parameter required.
ContinuousClock.Instant maps to Long holding monotonic nanoseconds (System.nanoTime() base); use it only for elapsed-time arithmetic.
Date maps to java.time.Instant.

WeatherCondition becomes String (the WeatherKit case name that com.moblin.android.platform.weatherkit gives), Measurement<UnitTemperature> becomes Double? in degrees Celsius and Measurement<UnitSpeed> becomes Double? in metres per second, the units of the weatherkit shim.
heartRates keeps nullable values, so the Kotlin type is Map<String, Int?>.
runningMetrics values come from WorkoutDeviceRunningMetrics (com.moblin.android.integrations.workoutdevice) and gForce from GForce (com.moblin.android.various.managers).
Swift Testing struct WorkoutDeviceCyclingPowerSuite becomes a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions.
powerMeasurement and powerAndCrankMeasurement stay file-private top-level helpers building the little-endian cycling-power measurement payloads byte for byte.
Int16 power -> Short, so call sites use e.g. 200.toShort(); revolutions and eventTime stay Int since they are only written little-endian into the payload.
Self-referencing try on handleMeasurement is dropped: the Kotlin handleMeasurement(value: ByteArray): Pair<Int, Int?> does not throw.
#expect(power == 100) -> assertEquals(100, power), #expect(cadence == nil) -> assertNull(cadence), #expect(cadence == 90) -> assertEquals(90, cadence).
Results do not depend on locale or time zone, so no @Config qualifiers or TimeZone setup is needed.
Swift Testing suite becomes a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions; every @Test func keeps its name.
#expect(try x == true/false) on Booleans became assertTrue/assertFalse, other equality checks became assertEquals(actual-first-order swapped).
Hex byte literals above 0x7F need .toByte(); Data([...]) literals became byteArrayOf(...).
Data equality is asserted with assertContentEquals because Kotlin ByteArray uses identity-based equals.
Numeric reader results are compared via toLong() so Int, Long, UInt or ULong return types from NalUnitReader all compile and compare correctly.
#expect(throws: (any Error).self) maps to assertFailsWith<Throwable>, the closest analogue of Swift's any Error.
The Swift suite has no init block, so no @Before fun setUp() was emitted.
NalUnitReader is in the same package as this test, so no import is needed; its constructor is called positionally as (data, offset).
@MainActor has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped; these classes are plain classes and callers must ensure main-thread access.
The failable Swift init? becomes a private primary constructor plus a companion operator fun invoke returning RemoteControlRelay? so call sites keep the RemoteControlRelay(...) form.
Swift URL values are stored as String; java.net.URI is used only to validate the control URL the way URL(string:) did.
Decodable structs became kotlinx.serialization @Serializable data classes; Kotlin property names already match the Swift coding keys so no @SerialName is needed.
Deque<Connection> maps to kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque using addLast and removeFirstOrNull (popFirst).
logger.info/debug map to android.util.Log.i/d with the tag "RemoteControlRelay".
WebSocketClient is assumed to expose delegate, start(), stop(), send(string) and constructors (url) and (url, loopback) matching the Swift type.
The String -> Data conversion in handleControlMessage is unnecessary and was dropped; decoding uses the raw String.
Manufacturer-data constants are kept as private top-level ByteArray vals with the same names as the Swift globals.
Swift's `data[2...3]` inclusive range is translated with `copyOfRange(2, 4)` (exclusive upper bound) after the `data.size < 4` guard.
Byte-slice comparison uses `contentEquals` instead of a Swift `switch` on `Data`, expressed as a `when` chain preserving the original case order.
`prefix(2)` becomes `take(2).toByteArray()`, which also yields an empty array for short input exactly like Swift.

Enum cases are referenced as `SettingsDjiDeviceModel.unknown`, `.osmoAction2`, `.osmoAction3`, `.osmoAction4`, `.osmoPocket3`, `.osmoPocket4`, `.osmoAction5Pro`, `.osmo360`, `.osmoAction6`; the ported enum is assumed to use these Swift camelCase entry names.
Hex literals above 0x7F require `.toByte()` in Kotlin, which does not change the wire bytes.
No state, no coroutines and no Android APIs are involved, so the translation is side-effect free and deterministic.
JUnit 4 test class with kotlin.test assertions, mirroring the Swift Testing suite; no suite-level setup existed so no @Before is emitted.

CMTime(value:timescale:) is converted to 90 kHz tick arithmetic; timescale 90000 with value 0 maps to the Long microsecond/millisecond timestamp 0L used by the ported MpegTsPacketizedElementaryStream.

CMTime.invalid has no direct Kotlin analog in this port; TSTimestamp.invalid is used as the sentinel for decodeTimeStamp. Adjust if the ported MpegTsPacketizedElementaryStream declares decodeTimeStamp as a plain Long sentinel.
Data([0x65]) becomes byteArrayOf(0x65); Data(repeating: 1, count: n) becomes ByteArray(n) { 1 } so byte values stay identical.
arrayOfPackets(256, true, nil) becomes arrayOfPackets(256, true, null); the program clock reference argument is passed as 1234L for the two PCR tests.
packets.count becomes packets.size and MpegTsPacket.size is referenced as the companion constant of the ported packet type.
All types under test (MpegTsPacket, MpegTsPacketizedElementaryStream, TSTimestamp) live in com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg, so no imports for them are required.
AVFoundation import was dropped; no AVFoundation symbols are used in the test bodies.
UInt32 bitrate parameters/returns map to Int (bitrates are not wire-format here) and all Int64 arithmetic maps to Long.
adaptiveBitrateRistFastSettings is a top-level val, exactly like the other adaptive bitrate settings globals in this package.

Assumes the base AdaptiveBitrate exposes a nullable/protected delegate, logAdaptiveAcion(actionTaken:) and open overridable members setTargetBitrate/setSettings/getCurrentBitrate/getCurrentMaximumBitrateInKbps/getFastPif/getSmoothPif/update.
StreamStats.packetsInFlight and StreamStats.rttMs are Double (the Swift arithmetic requires it), while AdaptiveBitrateSettings.packetsInFlight and the other settings integers are Long.
stats.limitByTransportBitrate(currentMaximumBitrate) is called with one positional argument, i.e. as it is declared in the StreamStats translation.
The Swift check Int32(fastPif - smoothPif) > settings.packetsInFlight * 2 is performed in Long because packetsInFlight is 64-bit in Kotlin.
Multi-line Swift log messages are collapsed into single-line strings.
The unused Swift import of Collections is dropped.
Tests are plain JUnit 4 @Test methods; Swift `throws` disappears because Kotlin has no checked exceptions.
Assumes MobcamStreamMessageReader.read() returns Pair<MobcamStreamMessageType, ByteArray>? and append() takes a ByteArray, so `.0`/`.1` become `.first`/`.second`.

Assumes ByteReader(data) exposes readUInt8(): UByte, readUInt16(): UShort, readUInt32(): UInt, readUInt64(): ULong, readBytes(count): ByteArray; results are compared via toInt()/toLong() so numeric literals still work.
Assumes the pack helpers take a ULong presentation timestamp plus a ByteArray payload (wire format types kept unsigned).
Swift `Data == Data` comparisons became kotlin.test assertContentEquals on ByteArray.
JSONDecoder for the device hello payload became kotlinx.serialization Json.decodeFromString over the UTF-8 decoded bytes.
Hex byte literals above 0x7F (0x90, 0x80, 0xBB) need an explicit .toByte() in Kotlin.
`mobcamStreamProtocolVersion + 1` is written as `(mobcamStreamProtocolVersion.toInt() + 1).toByte()` to stay valid for any integral type of the constant.
WavSuite is a JUnit 4 class: @Test methods use org.junit.Test and assertions come from kotlin.test.
Swift #expect(wav == createMonoWav(...)) on Data became assertContentEquals, because Kotlin ByteArray == compares references rather than contents.
ByteWriter methods are assumed to take wire types: writeUInt32Le(UInt), writeUInt16Le(UShort), writeUTF8Bytes(String), and expose data: ByteArray, per the byte-parsing mapping rule.
Int16 -> Short; UInt16(bitPattern: sample) -> sample.toUShort(), which preserves the same 16 bits. UInt32(...) -> .toUInt(), UInt16(...) -> .toUShort().
createWav is assumed to be (sampleRate: Int, samples: List<List<Short>>): ByteArray; it lives in this same package so it is not imported.
The Swift line comments (int16, Mono/Stereo, sample rate, 192 kbps) were dropped because comments are not allowed in the output; the byte values are unchanged.
List literals of Int16 are built with listOf(...).map { it.toShort() } to avoid implicit Int literal narrowing.
zip(...) with tuple destructuring became samplesRight.zip(samplesLeft) inside for ((a, b) in ...).
Swift's weak var processor becomes a nullable Processor property; JVM GC handles the weak semantics without an explicit WeakReference here.
Swift's unlabeled first parameter of update(_:_:) maps to a named parameter presentationTimeStamp in Kotlin, consistent with reading order of the source.
Int(fps) truncation is preserved with fps.toInt().
Integer division framesCounter / 2 matches Swift Int division exactly.
nextFpsReportTime == 0 becomes == 0.0 on the Double property.
The delegate call is chained as processor?.delegate?.streamVideoFps(fps) to preserve Swift's optional chaining.
Swift Testing #expect became kotlin.test assertEquals/assertNull inside a JUnit 4 class (org.junit.Test).
ByteArray literals with values above 0x7F (0x8D, 0xCF, 0xFF, 0x80, 0xC0, 0xF1) need .toByte() in Kotlin.
The 'try' before the throwing OptionalHeader initializer is dropped; Kotlin has no checked exceptions, tests declare no throws.
CMTime(value:timescale:) is replaced by a local cmTime(value, timescale) helper that converts to microseconds: value * 1_000_000 / timescale.
CMTime.invalid is replaced by the local constant CM_TIME_INVALID = Long.MIN_VALUE; adjust it to whatever sentinel the ported OptionalHeader actually returns.

Assumed OptionalHeader API: OptionalHeader(), OptionalHeader(data: ByteArray), encode(): ByteArray, getPresentationTimeStamp(): Long, getDecodeTimeStamp(): Long, setTimestamp(presentationTimeStamp: Long, decodeTimeStamp: Long) in microseconds.
Assumed TSTimestamp API: encode(value: Long, marker): ByteArray, decode(data: ByteArray, offset: Int = 0): Long?, dataSize: Int, matching the nil return used by the decodeTooShort case.
optionalHeaderRoundTrip only passes if the port rounds when converting microseconds back to 90 kHz ticks (11111 us <-> 1000 ticks); the 900/90000 case is exact either way.
Swift's `Deque` from the Collections package is replaced by Kotlin's `ArrayDeque` (append/removeFirst map to addLast/removeFirst).
The enum cases keep their lowercase Swift names so `toString()` in the log messages stays byte-identical ("audio"/"video").
`logger.debug` becomes `android.util.Log.d` with the tag "DriftTracker" declared in the companion object.
The Swift labeled tuple `(lower:upper:)` is translated into a private data class `Deviations`, added next to the other private helpers.
In `update` the two `guard let state` bindings shadow each other; Kotlin cannot redeclare a same-scope local, so they are named `mediaState` and `minState` (values are unchanged).
`min(by:)` is translated to `minByOrNull` and `map(\.1.lower).min()` to `minOfOrNull`; tie-breaking for equal deviations differs slightly from Swift.
The Swift multi-line string literals with a trailing `\` continuation are emitted as single-line concatenated strings with identical text.
`formatThreeDecimals` is imported from com.moblin.android.common.various and assumed to take a Double and return a String.
Swift struct with a single stored property becomes a Kotlin data class holding the raw bytes as ByteArray.
The throwing Swift init(reader:) maps to a Kotlin secondary constructor with the same parameter name; Kotlin has no checked exceptions so the signature stays clean.
NalUnitReader.readRawBytes() and NalUnitWriter.writeRawBytes(ByteArray) are imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg.
The Swift memberwise initializer is not synthesized because the struct declares a custom init, so only the reader constructor is kept alongside the data property.
Data is mapped to ByteArray; no Apple-only API is used in this file.
Swift enum with associated values becomes a Kotlin sealed class named MpegTsVideoConfig with nested data classes Avc and Hevc.
The AVC and HEVC payload types are imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg.avc and com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg.hevc as given in the glossary.
Nested case types are named Avc/Hevc so pattern matching on the sealed class reads like the Swift switch over .avc / .hevc.
No behaviour is lost: the file only models the two possible video configs, so every member is preserved.
Consumers in Swift that did `case .avc(let config)` become `is MpegTsVideoConfig.Avc ->` with access to `config`.
No Apple frameworks, coroutines or serialization are involved, so the translation is a direct structural mapping.
The sealed class is declared in the same package as the mpeg helper types, keeping the original directory-to-package mapping.

httpGet from com.moblin.android.common.various is used as `suspend fun httpGet(request: Request): Pair<ByteArray, Response>?` and `suspend fun httpGet(url: String): Pair<ByteArray, Response>?`; verify these signatures against the real helper.
URLRequest.setAuthorization is not in the glossary, so the token is sent as an OkHttp header `Authorization: Bearer <apiToken>` inside createRequest.

Swift coding keys with underscores are preserved as property names (voice_id) and repeated in @SerialName; a private Json with ignoreUnknownKeys = true mirrors JSONDecoder's leniency about extra keys.
Locale(identifier:) is mapped to java.util.Locale.forLanguageTag with '_' replaced by '-'; an empty region or language becomes null exactly like Swift's optional chaining.
Swift's `metadata.split(separator: "|")` omits empty subsequences, so firstMetadataPart returns null for an empty metadata/first part, matching the Swift guards.
generateTts returns the downloaded audio as ByteArray (Swift Data) and decodes TtsMonsterGenerateResponse before fetching the produced URL.
baseUrl is a file-private HttpUrl built once; request paths are appended with HttpUrl.Builder.addPathSegment.
The second `guard let (data, response)` in generateTts is renamed audioData/audioResponse because Kotlin forbids redeclaring a local name in the same scope.
The Swift enum with associated values becomes a sealed class CatPrinterCommandMxw01 with object/data class cases named after the Swift cases.
The failable init?(data:) is translated to a companion operator fun invoke(data: ByteArray) so call sites keep reading CatPrinterCommandMxw01(data); it returns null where Swift returns nil.
CatPrinterCommandId is a file-private enum with a rawValue property and a fromRawValue companion; CatPrinterPrintMode is public with the same shape since catPrinterEncodeImageRow consumes it.
Data -> ByteArray, UInt8 -> UByte (UShort for the little-endian count), [UInt8] rows -> UByteArray, [[UInt8]] -> List<UByteArray>.
reasons.isBitSet(index:) comes from com.moblin.android.common.various, and readUInt8() results are compared against unsigned literals (0x22u).
String(bytes:encoding:.utf8) ?? "unknown" is a strict UTF-8 decode (invalid bytes give null, as in Swift) with the leading BOM stripped, falling back to "unknown".
logger.info(...) becomes Log.i with the class name as tag; the thrown Swift Strings become a file-private CatPrinterCommandException whose toString() is the message, so the logged text matches.

ByteWriter/ByteReader from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util and the CrcSwift shim are called with their Kotlin signatures; catPrinterEncodeImageRow and catPrinterWidthPixels are reused from CatPrinter.kt in the same package.
Swift `final class` subclass becomes a plain Kotlin `class` extending the open `RtmpMessage` class.
The superclass initializer is called through Kotlin constructor delegation, so `RtmpAggregateMessage` forwards `RtmpMessageType.aggregate` as the message type.
No other members exist in the Swift source, so the Kotlin class body is empty apart from the inheritance clause.
The enum entry is referenced as `RtmpMessageType.aggregate` to match the Swift case name; align the casing with the sibling RtmpMessageType declaration if that file used uppercase constants.
`RtmpMessage` is imported from the same package `com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.rtmp.message`, so no extra import statement is required.
No state, no coroutines and no platform APIs are involved; behaviour is identical to the Swift original.
Swift's private Codable structs became private @Serializable data classes; the file-level `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }` mirrors JSONDecoder's tolerance of unknown keys.
`OpenAiError` is a sealed class extending Exception so kotlin's Result can carry it; the Swift `description` property is kept and `toString()` returns it (CustomStringConvertible).
`ask` keeps the callback API and now hands back `Result<String>`; the failure type is always OpenAiError, which is a Throwable.

The URLRequest plus setAuthorization/setContentType becomes an OkHttp request built inline; okhttp3.Request is written fully qualified because this file already declares a private `Request` payload type that would otherwise shadow the import.
`URL` is mapped to java.net.URI for the base URL, and the stored url is a plain String built as base + "/chat/completions" so it can be passed to OkHttp.

httpRequest is called as `(okhttp3.Request, (ByteArray?, NetworkResponse?, Throwable?) -> Unit)`, matching the ported helper's shape; success and 429 are checked through `NetworkResponse.statusCode` (200..299, 429) instead of helper properties.
@MainActor has no direct Kotlin equivalent, so every completion is dispatched through a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) held by the class.
`try? JSONDecoder().decode(...)` becomes runCatching { json.decodeFromString(...) }.getOrNull().
Swift struct becomes a Kotlin data class with the same defaulted properties: bitrate, channelsMap and format.
AVAudioFormat and AudioStreamBasicDescription are modelled with android.media.MediaFormat; sample rate and channel count are read via KEY_SAMPLE_RATE and KEY_CHANNEL_COUNT.
AVAudioCompressedBuffer (packetCapacity 1, maximumPacketSize 1024 * channelCount) becomes a ByteArray of that maximum size, because MediaCodec owns the packet buffers on Android.
AAC and Opus are represented by MediaFormat.MIMETYPE_AUDIO_AAC and MediaFormat.MIMETYPE_AUDIO_OPUS.
framesPerPacket (1024 for AAC, 960 for Opus) and MPEG4ObjectID format flags have no MediaFormat counterpart; the platform codec handles packetisation.
private static let maximumNumberOfChannels is a private const in the companion object and is used by makeAudioFormat to clamp the channel count to 2.
Nested enum Format has no raw values, so it stays a plain enum class with aac and opus entries; makeAudioFormat keeps an optional return type to mirror AVAudioFormat?.

AvcSeiPayloadPictureTiming is a class whose properties are private-set vars; the Swift failable init?(reader:) becomes the companion factory fromReader(reader) returning null, because Kotlin constructors cannot be failable.

UInt8/Data were mapped to UByte/ByteArray and NalUnitReader/NalUnitWriter are assumed to expose readBits/readBit/readBitsU32/skipBits and writeBits/writeBit/writeBitsU32/writeBytes/data over those types.
Swift's thrown String errors became IllegalStateException with the identical message text.
The imported global `calendar` is not used: the clock initializer uses java.time Instant/ZoneId on the system zone, which is what Calendar.current.year/.hour would give.
AvcNalUnitSei's throwing init(reader:) is a secondary constructor delegating to a private companion function readPayload(reader) that throws.
The top-level hevc helpers writeRbspTrailingBits and writeMoreDataInPayload are called with the writer argument, matching the Swift call sites.
enum with raw value -> enum class AvcSeiPayloadType with rawValue and fromRawValue; enum with associated value -> sealed class AvcNalUnitSeiPayload with nested data class PictureTiming.
Log.i is used with the class name as tag in place of logger.info.
RtmpMessage is assumed to expose an overridable 'encoded' property of type ByteArray (modeled from the Swift 'encoded: Data'); it is accessed via super.encoded in both accessors.
RtmpMessageType.windowAck is assumed to be the Kotlin enum entry matching the Swift '.windowAck' case; both types live in the same package so no imports are needed.
Swift's UInt32 constructors/initializers become secondary constructors delegating to super(RtmpMessageType.windowAck), since the base class has no no-arg constructor.
size stays a UInt because this class is RTMP wire-format code; byte serialization helpers convert to/from big-endian bytes matching Swift's 'bigEndian.data' idiom.
The setter reads the first 4 bytes big-endian, matching Swift's 'UInt32(data:).bigEndian' net behaviour (zero-fill for short arrays).
Swift's `@unchecked Sendable` has no Kotlin counterpart and was dropped.
`encoded` is fully overridden with a custom getter/setter that delegates to `super.encoded` for lazy caching; this assumes the base `RtmpMessage.encoded` is an open `var ByteArray`.
`Data` equality (`==`/`!=`) is translated to `ByteArray.contentEquals` and `Data.count` to `ByteArray.size`.
`Amf0Encoder.writeUInt8` is assumed to take a `UByte`; the Swift literal `0` becomes `0.toUByte()`.
Swift's `AsValue.string(handlerName)` is translated as the nested case `AsValue.String(handlerName)` of the AMF sealed type.
`logger.info(...)` is translated to `Log.i("RtmpDataMessage", ...)` using a private companion TAG.
`arguments` is declared `MutableList<AsValue>` so `decoder.decode()` results can be appended in the setter.
The inherited `type` property is compared against `RtmpMessageType.amf3Data`, matching the Swift `.amf3Data` case.
Enum entries keep the Swift case names verbatim; RtmpCommandName.fromRawValue(rawValue) returns null instead of the Swift optional, and the call site keeps the '?? .unknown' fallback.

The two Swift initializers became secondary constructors delegating to RtmpMessage(commandType); RtmpMessage is assumed to expose open 'encoded: ByteArray', 'length: Int', 'streamId: UInt32' and 'type'.
`encoded` overrides the base property and uses super.encoded for the cached value exactly like the Swift getter/setter pair (no backing field is generated).

Swift's do/catch became try/catch (e: Exception); Amf0Decoder/Amf0Encoder are assumed to expose decode(), decodeString(), decodeInt(), decodeObject(), bytesAvailable, position, encode(), writeUInt8() and data.
AMF values are built as AsValue.String / AsValue.Number / AsValue.Object / AsValue.Null; those sealed-class constructor names must match the AMF0.kt translation.
logger.info is mapped to Log.i with the class name as tag; Data.hexString() is not part of the glossary, so a private ByteArray.hexString() helper (lowercase hex) is provided at file level.
arguments is exposed as MutableList<AsValue> with a private setter so the in-place append/removeAll semantics of the Swift array are preserved.
The 'length == newValue.count' guard and the public setter write-through to super.encoded are kept unchanged.

RtmpSetPeerBandwidthMessage has no primary constructor: the two Swift inits become secondary constructors, both delegating to super(RtmpMessageType.BANDWIDTH) (assumed to be the existing RtmpMessageType entry for 0x06).

Swift's nested 'enum Limit: UInt8' becomes a nested Kotlin enum class with a UByte rawValue plus Limit.fromRawValue(...) replacing the failable raw-value initialiser; Swift cases hard/soft/dynamic/unknown are written HARD/SOFT/DYNAMIC/UNKNOWN per Kotlin enum conventions.

UInt32 fields stay unsigned (UInt) because they are wire-format values; size.bigEndian.data is produced with a big-endian java.nio.ByteBuffer and UInt32(data:).bigEndian is parsed with ByteBuffer.wrap(value, 0, 4).int.toUInt(), so both directions are big-endian on the wire.
Swift slicing newValue[0 ..< 4] is replaced by ByteBuffer.wrap(value, 0, 4) (offset overload) so no copy of the payload is made.
Data counting, appending and equality map to ByteArray.size, ByteBuffer.put, and contentEquals.
The overridden encoded getter/setter read and write the superclass storage via super.encoded, exactly like the Swift code uses super.encoded.
The payload is always 5 bytes: 4 bytes of size followed by the limit raw value byte, matching the RTMP Set Peer Bandwidth message layout.
No Apple-only frameworks are used, so nothing is stubbed out.
The Swift extension on Model becomes two top-level extension functions on Model in the same package.
Model's members used here (database, sceneSelector, isSceneVideoSourceActive(sceneId:), selectScene(id:)) must be at least internal in the Kotlin Model for these extension functions to compile.
SceneSelector.selectedSceneId is treated as a non-nullable java.util.UUID, matching the Swift non-optional argument passed to isSceneVideoSourceActive(sceneId:).
database.disconnectProtection.fallbackSceneId and liveSceneId are treated as nullable UUID values and unwrapped with ?: return, preserving the Swift guard-let order and short-circuiting.
No explicit java.util.UUID import is needed because the type only appears through inference in this file.
Swift guard ... else { return } is expressed as an early `if (condition) return`, keeping the logic byte-identical.
Swift failable initializer init?(reader:) has no Kotlin constructor equivalent, so it became the companion factory HevcSeiPayloadTimeCode.from(reader:).
Throwing initializers that throw a String now throw IllegalStateException.
private(set) var maps to a Kotlin var with a private setter; the clock initializer stays a public secondary constructor.
readBits/writeBits are assumed to take/return Int and readBitsU32/writeBitsU32 to use UInt; adjust if the ported NalUnitReader/NalUnitWriter use UByte.
Date maps to java.time.Instant and calendar is a java.util.Calendar; it is cloned before mutation so the shared instance is untouched.
logger.info maps to android.util.Log.i with the class name as tag.
writeRbspTrailingBits and writeMoreDataInPayload are invoked as top-level functions taking the writer, matching their Swift signatures.
UInt8/UInt32 are kept as UByte/UInt because this is wire-format code.
RtmpChunkType becomes a Kotlin enum class with a UByte rawValue and a companion fromRawValue, keeping entry names zero/one/two/three.
The nested ChunkStreamId enum keeps UShort raw values and gets its own fromRawValue companion.
chunkStreamId comparisons are done via toInt() because Kotlin unsigned types do not compare against differently-typed literals.
Data is ByteArray; subdata(in:) becomes copyOfRange and count becomes size.
message.timestamp/streamId are treated as UInt, message.length as a mutable Int, matching the RtmpMessage port in the message package.
Little-endian (chunkStreamId - 64) and big-endian timestamp encodings are written byte-by-byte since Kotlin has no zero-cost byte-order wrapper.
ByteWriter is imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util and used with writeBytes/writeUInt8/writeUInt24/writeUInt32/writeUInt32Le/data.
The stride(from:to:by:) split loop is reproduced with an equivalent while loop stepping by maximumSize.
Only the call inside togglePhotoShoot changed: reattachCamera() -> attachCamera(), matching the Swift diff.
Everything else in the file is unchanged, including startPhotoShoot/stopPhotoShoot and formatting.
RtmpUserControlMessage subclasses RtmpMessage(RtmpMessageType.user) through a Kotlin primary constructor; the two Swift initializers map to the primary constructor plus one secondary constructor.
Swift's nested `Event: UInt8` becomes a nested `enum class Event(val rawValue: UByte)` with a companion `fromRawValue`, replacing `Event(rawValue:)`.
The overridden `encoded` property keeps the lazy getter/setter semantics: the getter returns the stored payload when non-empty, otherwise it builds it from `event` and `value` and stores it.
`Data` maps to `ByteArray`; `value.bigEndian.data` is produced by explicit big-endian shift/mask conversion, and the setter parses the tail big-endian.
Where Swift used the inherited `length`, this port reads `super.encoded.size` to avoid re-entering the overridden getter (which has side effects).
`Int32` maps to `Int`; `Int32(data:...).bigEndian` is reproduced by reading the trailing bytes big-endian, capped at the 4-byte value width.

Swift `throw "..."` (a thrown String) has no Kotlin counterpart, so the file declares DjiMessageError whose toString() is the message, following the DataChannelError/SrtError convention; it is not an unsupported API.
`CrcSwift.computeCrc8/16` are called with the unsigned literal arguments from the shim (0xEEu, 0x31u, 0x496Cu, 0x1021u) exactly like the Swift call.
ByteReader methods do not throw in Kotlin, so every `try reader.readX()` became a plain call and the parsed value is compared directly.
`writer.data` is used verbatim as in Swift for the header and body CRC computations and for the returned bytes.
`value.utf8Data` / `url.utf8Data` map to `String.toByteArray()` (UTF-8), and the UInt8 truncation of the length is `(size and 0xFF).toByte()`.

`DjiMessage` is a non-final Swift class, so it is an `open class` with `open` members; `init(data:)` is a secondary constructor delegating to the primary one.
The Swift local `let data = data.subdata(...)` shadow is renamed payloadData to avoid shadowing the constructor parameter.
@MainActor has no Kotlin counterpart: the class is a plain class whose methods are expected to be invoked from the main dispatcher (Dispatchers.Main).
@Published properties are exposed as read-only StateFlow with private MutableStateFlow backing fields (_name / name).

posts is exposed as StateFlow<List<ChatPost>> where index 0 is the newest post, matching Swift Deque.prepend/first/removeLast semantics; posts.count maps to list.size and posts.removeLast() to removeAt(size - 1).
newPosts and pausedPosts keep Deque semantics via kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque (addLast/removeFirst/isEmpty/size).
MainTimer.startSingleShot is called positionally with 5.0 seconds plus a trailing lambda; adjust the literal if the ported MainTimer signature differs.
post.state.deleted and post.isRedLine() are used as-is from ChatPost/ChatPostState in com.moblin.android.various.
Every mutation of the published collection is applied in a single StateFlow assignment so observers see one update per update()/endReachedWhenPaused() call.
StateFlow suppresses assignments equal to the current value, so no redundant emissions occur when the list is unchanged.

makeErrorToast(title = , subTitle = ) is assumed to exist on Model in package com.moblin.android.various.model, as used by the Swift original.
apple_only: MusicKit MusicAuthorization.request()
MusicKit MusicCatalogResourceRequest / MusicCatalogSearchRequest (Song lookup by URL id and search by term)

notes: @MainActor has no Kotlin equivalent; the function is a plain top-level function and callers are responsible for main-thread dispatch.
Swift's count(where:) becomes Kotlin's count { } on the pairs list.

Swift's `extension Model` becomes top-level extension functions on `Model` in the same package. A Kotlin file cannot add interface conformances, so `Model` must declare `: SpeechToTextDelegate, TranslatorDelegate` (or their Kotlin equivalents); the same-package extension functions then act as the interface implementations.

All Model members touched here must be visible outside Model's own file (at least `internal`): `speechToText`, `speechToTextLatestPosition`, `speechToTextLatestText`, `speechToTextAlertMatchOffset`, `speechToTextTextAligners`, `textEffects`, `browserEffects`, `enabledAlertsEffects`, `widgetsInCurrentScene(onlyEnabled:)`, `makeErrorToast(title:)`, `playAlert(alert:)`.
The `#available(iOS 26.0, *)` guards around the Translation framework are dropped: on Android the ported `Translator` runs unconditionally on the TranslationManager shim.
Swift counts Characters; `text.indexOf(string, startIndex, ignoreCase)` plus `string.length` are used instead, so offsets in the alert matcher are UTF-16 code units.
`Set(widget.widget.text.subtitles.map(\.identifier))` becomes `map { it.identifier }.toSet()` over nullable identifiers with an explicit null check inside the loop.
Assumes the widget model exposes `WidgetType.text` / `WidgetType.alerts` / `WidgetType.browser` and the alert enum case is `Alert.SpeechToTextString(id)` in package com.moblin.android.various.model.
`Translator.translators` is assumed to be a mutable list exposed by Translator's companion object (`clear()` / `add()`).
Swift Testing ValidateSuite becomes a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions.

#expect(x == nil) maps to assertNull(x) and #expect(x != nil) maps to assertNotNull(x).
The allowedSchemes argument is passed positionally as listOf("srt") so the call does not depend on the Kotlin parameter name.
No suite-level setup exists in the Swift source, so no @Before method is generated.
Swift's private serial DispatchQueue is a top-level single-thread executor dispatcher; write()/flush() launch coroutines on the coroutine scope built from it so ordering is preserved.
The fileManager property was dropped: every FileManager operation maps directly to java.io.File (listFiles, deleteRecursively, createNewFile, length).

sorted by lastPathComponent becomes sortedBy { it.name }; maximumLogFileSizeBytes is a Long because it is not wire-format/byte-parsing code.
createAndGetDirectory and formatFilenameDateAndTimeIsoish are called positionally as in the Swift source (createAndGetDirectory("Logs")).

Swift Testing suite translated to a JUnit 4 class (org.junit.Test) with kotlin.test assertions; helper functions stay private top-level in this file.
DriftTracker calls are written positionally (DriftTracker(""), addMedia(media, fillLevel), setDrift(value), update(media, ...)) because the Kotlin signatures live in DriftTracker.kt.

DriftTrackerMediaState is not referenced by this file, so it is not imported.
Swift Testing suite translated to a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions; each @Test becomes org.junit.Test fun and the struct becomes a plain class.

Wheel revolutions stay unsigned (UInt, UInt.MAX_VALUE for Swift .max) because UInt32.max does not fit an Int; the 16-bit crank wheels and event times use Int with explicit and 0xFF masks inside the helper.

No test depends on locale or time zone, so no @Config qualifiers or TimeZone default are needed.
Swift Testing #expect(throws: "msg") { } is translated to kotlin.test assertFailsWith<Exception> plus an equality check on the thrown Throwable's message.
The Swift functions are `throws`; Kotlin has no checked exceptions so the calls are plain (no try/catch needed on the success paths).
@testable import Moblin is dropped because the types under test live in the same package com.moblin.android.media.rtspclient.
Test method names, order and string literals are kept byte-identical to the Swift source.
No suite-level init existed in Swift, so no @Before setUp is emitted.
If the ported error type wraps the text (e.g. prefixes the class name), the assertEquals on error.message must be adjusted to match the ported error's message/description.

appendTwitchRaidChannel is called with a List of SettingsStreamTwitchRaidChannel and returns the new list, matching the Swift value-semantics helper.

ByteReader is expected to expose position: Int (var), bytesAvailable: Int, readUInt8(): UByte, readUInt16Le(): UShort, readUInt24(): UInt, readUInt32(): UInt, readUInt32Le(): UInt and a throwing readBytes(count: Int): ByteArray.
messageHeaderSize() is kept as a function call on RtmpChunkType, mirroring the Swift declaration.

RtmpChunkStream in Swift is a struct copied in and out of the dictionary; in Kotlin it is a data class held by reference, so mutations apply to the stored instance. The observable behaviour is identical because every re-entry re-reads the same bytes from the same offset.
Swift's UInt32 timestamps map to Kotlin UInt, chunk stream ids to UShort, in line with the wire-format rule.
Swift's &+ / &+= wrapping arithmetic is preserved implicitly: Kotlin unsigned operators are implemented over signed Int arithmetic and wrap on overflow.
data.subdata(in:) becomes ByteArray.copyOfRange(offset, size); try! becomes a plain call to a throwing ByteReader method.
The private file-level types RtmpBasicHeader and RtmpChunkStream stay private to this file, as in the Swift source.

Swift structs that only hold static members became Kotlin objects: DjiPreparingToLivestreamMessagePayload, DjiConfirmStartStreamingMessagePayload and DjiStopStreamingMessagePayload (call sites drop the parentheses).
UInt8/UInt16 became UByte/UShort; ByteArray literals with values above 0x7F use .toByte() because Kotlin byte literals are signed.
ByteWriter is called with writeBytes(ByteArray), writeUInt8(UByte), writeUInt16Le(UShort) and the data property reading back a ByteArray; adjust if the ported ByteWriter uses Int parameters.

Enum entries of SettingsDjiDeviceResolution / SettingsDjiDeviceImageStabilization are referenced with UPPER_SNAKE_CASE names (R480P, R720P, R1080P, OFF, ROCK_STEADY, ROCK_STEADY_PLUS, HORIZON_BALANCING, HORIZON_STEADY), matching the port's Kotlin naming convention.

Primary constructor parameters of DjiStartStreamingMessagePayload and DjiStartStreamingMessagePayload2 follow the Swift stored-property order, which differs from the Swift init parameter order, so call sites should use named arguments.

The failable init DjiStatusMessagePayload.init?(payload:) became a companion operator fun invoke(payload: ByteArray) returning null for short payloads, keeping the call site DjiStatusMessagePayload(payload) unchanged.
Codable StartStreamingPayload became @Serializable with byte-identical property names (including EnhancedRTMP); no property has a default value, so all keys are always encoded, matching JSONEncoder.
try? JSONEncoder().encode(...) ?? Data() became runCatching { Json.encodeToString(...) }.getOrNull()?.encodeToByteArray() ?: ByteArray(0).
@Published properties become private MutableStateFlow backing fields plus public read-only StateFlow, as required by the porting rules.

kotlinx.serialization cannot serialize StateFlow fields, so SettingsMoblinkStreamer and SettingsMoblinkRelay use hand-written nested KSerializer objects that read/write the backing flows and always emit every key like Swift's encode(to:).
Swift's custom container.decode(_:_:_:isValid:) fallback is reproduced inside the custom deserializers: a missing key (or a url that fails isValidWebSocketUrl) yields the Swift default value.

CodingKeys server/client of SettingsMoblink do not match its property names, so @SerialName maps streamer->server and relay->client; the nested serializers use the Swift key names directly as descriptor element names.
The Swift UInt16 port is translated to Int because DefaultTcpPorts.moblinkStreamer and the rest of the ported code treat ports as Int; this file is not wire-format code.
SettingsMoblink itself stays a plain @Serializable class since it has no published properties; its nested types are resolved through their @Serializable(with = ...) serializers.
The explicit Swift init() initializers are implicit no-arg constructors in Kotlin; Swift's required init(from:) becomes the nested serialize/deserialize pair.
Swift Testing struct suite translated to a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions.
JSONDecoder().decode(T.self, from:) becomes Json.decodeFromString<T>(string) with a Json instance configured with ignoreUnknownKeys = true to mirror Swift's default tolerance of extra keys.
Swift raw string #"..."# maps to a Kotlin triple-quoted raw string; the payloads contain no '$' so no escaping is needed.
`throws` test methods become plain @Test methods; decode failures propagate and fail the test as JUnit would.
SettingsMoblinkRelay lives in the same package com.moblin.android.various.settings, so no import is required.
CheermotesSuite is a plain JUnit 4 class; the Swift @MainActor annotation and the throws clauses have no Kotlin counterpart and were dropped.
The Cheermotes.getUrlAndBits(word:) signature is unresolved in this file; it is assumed to return Pair<java.net.URI, Int>? based on the Swift URL return value.
URL.absoluteString maps to URI.toString() and URL.lastPathComponent maps to uri.path.substringAfterLast("/") since java.net.URI has no lastPathComponent.
#require(...) maps to kotlin.test.assertNotNull, which returns the non-null value, so destructuring with val (url, bits) keeps working.
Nil comparisons from #expect(... == nil) map to kotlin.test.assertNull.
Twitch API model properties keep their Swift snake_case names (min_bits, static_) to match the ported model declarations.
makeCheermotes takes a Map<String, List<Int>>; linkedMapOf is used where a test builds more than one prefix so iteration order stays deterministic.
Assertion argument order follows kotlin.test.assertEquals(expected, actual), so the literal side of the Swift comparison is passed first.
String.Index cursor arithmetic is translated to Int UTF-16 offsets; identical for the ASCII format templates this file parses.

Foundation's Measurement unit types UnitSpeed, UnitTemperature and UnitLength do not exist on Android and are declared locally in this file with the same symbol strings, so symbol()/toSystem()/toString() behave exactly as on iOS.
@MainActor is dropped; TextFormatLoader is a plain class driven from the caller's scope.
String(localized:) is translated to localized() imported from com.moblin.android.
Failable enum initializers (init?(_:)) become companion functions fromString(value).
CaseIterable is exposed as companion property allCases backed by the enum entries.
Swift regex literals are translated to Kotlin Regex objects and prefix-matched with find(input, 0) plus a range.first == 0 check.
The Swift custom toString() on the unit enums is translated as override fun toString(): String.
Parameterized `@Test(arguments:)` cases became `@Test fun` bodies that loop over `intArrayOf` rows, because JUnit 4 cannot parameterize individual methods with different data sets in one class.
`Issue.record(...)` followed by `return` is translated to kotlin.test `fail(...)`, which throws and therefore stops the test.

Assumed the failable Swift initializers `HevcSeiPayloadTimeCode(reader:)`, `HevcNalUnit(data:offset:)` and `AvcNalUnit(data:offset:)` were ported as throwing constructors, so `try #require(...)` becomes a direct constructor call; if the port returns nullables instead, an explicit null check must be added here.

Assumed sealed payload case names keep the Swift spelling (`HevcNalUnitPayload.prefixSeiNut`, `HevcNalUnitSeiPayload.timeCode`, `AvcNalUnitPayload.sei`, `AvcNalUnitSeiPayload.pictureTiming`) with an associated-value property of the same name, and that enum entries keep the Swift spelling (`HevcNalUnitType.prefixSeiNut`, `AvcNalUnitType.sei`).
Wire-format integer mapping applied: `hours`/`minutes`/`seconds` are `UByte` and `frame` is `UInt`, so assertions convert the `Int` loop values with `toUByte()`/`toUInt()`.

`clock(...)` takes and returns `java.time.Instant`; the hevc `calendar` global is not used because the test must build the clock in UTC, matching the production `makeClock()` value asserted with `epochSecond % 86400`.
`Data` comparisons use `assertContentEquals` since Kotlin `ByteArray` equality is identity based, and `assertNotEquals`/`assertTrue` were not needed.
Byte literals above 0x7F keep their exact values and are written with `.toByte()` where Kotlin requires it.
The Swift file-private enum `CatPrinterCommandId` is renamed to `CatPrinterCommandsCommandId` so its .class file cannot collide with the private enum of the same name in CatPrinterCommandsMxw01.kt.
`logger.info(...)` became `Log.i("CatPrinterCommand", ...)`; the tag is this file's command type name, as on iOS.

`init?(data:)` became `operator fun invoke(data:)` returning `CatPrinterCommand?`; the do/catch that returned nil is `runCatching { unpack(data) }.getOrNull()` and the thrown Swift strings are IllegalStateException.
Image rows are UByteArray (`[[UInt8]]` -> `List<UByteArray>`), matching catPrinterEncodeImageRow and catPrinterPackPrintImageCommandsMxw01.
Data literals became byteArrayOf with `.toByte()` on values >= 0x80 so the bytes stay identical.
`reader.readUInt8() == 0x51` uses `0x51.toUByte()` because ByteReader returns UByte and bare hex literals are Int.
The case values SetEnergy/FeedPaper keep UShort and SetQuality keeps UByte, written through ByteWriter.writeUInt16Le/writeUInt8.
DrawRow and Lattice are data classes holding arrays, so their generated equals/hashCode compare references; no code in this file compares two commands by value.
Swift Testing's @Test(arguments:) has no JUnit 4 equivalent here, so bool(), decodeIntNotRepresentable() and the other parameterised cases run as one @Test that loops over the argument list.
Swift's `func null()` and `func object()` are hard keywords in Kotlin and had to be declared with backticks so the method names stay identical.
A private top-level `bytes(vararg Int)` helper was added so every Data([...]) byte literal stays byte-identical while producing a ByteArray; Data comparisons use kotlin.test.assertContentEquals.
Assumes Amf0Type is a sealed class with PascalCase subclasses (Number, Bool, String, Object, TypedObject, Null, Undefined, EcmaArray, StrictArray, Date) and that each payload is exposed as `value`.
Assumes AsValue is a sealed class with String/Number/Bool/EcmaArray subclasses and that AsObject is a Map<String, AsValue> (dictionary literals become mapOf).
Assumes AmfError is a sealed Throwable hierarchy with NotNumber and TooDeep objects, so assertFailsWith<AmfError.NotNumber> / <AmfError.TooDeep> is used for #expect(throws:).
RtmpCommandName is imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.rtmp.message and used through RtmpCommandName.fromRawValue(...) / RtmpCommandName.Result per the enum mapping convention.
Swift Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 15) becomes Instant.ofEpochSecond(15); ecmaArray.get(key:) becomes get(...) and swiftArray decoding yields a List<AsValue>.
Added shoutoutCreates list, delegate override twitchEventSubChannelShoutoutCreate and the shoutoutCreate test, matching the Swift diff.
The delegate implements the override for twitchEventSubChannelShoutoutCreate like the other TwitchEventSubDelegate callbacks.
Expectations use assertEquals/assertNull with kotlin.test as in the rest of the file, JUnit 4 via RobolectricTestRunner.
Swift URL file paths become java.io.File; Date becomes java.time.Instant (Date(timeInterval:since:) -> plusSeconds).
Recording's failable init?(recording:) is translated as a companion factory `create(recording:)` returning Recording?, with a private constructor taking the mutable fields.
The candidate-filename loop mutates a temporary Recording, exactly mirroring how Swift's init assigns filename and resolves recordingPath inside url().
createAndGetDirectory and formatFilenameDateAndTime are called positionally to avoid depending on their Kotlin parameter names.
final class RecordingsStorage becomes a plain Kotlin class (final by default).
Security-scoped bookmark resolution (URL(resolvingBookmarkData:)) has no Android equivalent and is replaced with TODO in loadRecordingPath().

encode() re-implements Apple's JSONEncoder output (keys sorted alphabetically, `"key" : value` separators, two-space pretty printing, '/' escaped as '\/') on top of kotlinx.serialization, so every expectation literal from the Swift suite is kept byte-identical.
Swift `try`/`throws` disappear: encode() returns String and never throws; the generic reified signature also serves the two non-request encode calls.

kotlinx.serialization prints Double(1.0) as '1.0' where Apple prints '1', so every literal whose expected JSON shows an integer (10, 30, 90, 250, 4200, 22, 17, 3...) was kept as an Int argument; decimals stay Double.

Foundation Measurement / UnitTemperature / UnitSpeed are replaced by the port's Measurement, UnitTemperature and UnitSpeed types in com.moblin.android.various, with celsius and metersPerSecond kept so the wire shape (unit.converter.coefficient/constant + symbol) is unchanged.
WeatherKit WeatherCondition.clear has no Android counterpart and is passed as its raw value "clear" (the string the Swift encoder produced).

Date(timeIntervalSince1970:) -> Instant.ofEpochSecond(...) and .now -> Instant.now(); note the expectation `"date" : 745043166` is Apple's 2001 reference-date encoding, which the port's serializer must keep to stay wire compatible.

Names for the sealed request cases were inferred from the Swift enum (RemoteControlRequest.SetGimbalTracking/SetGimbalMovement/AnimateGimbal/SaveGimbalPreset/SendMessage, motion RemoteControlRequest.GimbalMotion.Kapow), as were RunningMetrics and the nullable gForce accessors.
Json is configured with encodeDefaults = true (all stored properties are always encoded) and explicitNulls = false (nil Optionals are omitted, matching Swift's encodeIfPresent).
httpGet is assumed to be a suspend function returning Pair<ByteArray, NetworkResponse> that throws on transport errors, mirroring the iOS (Data, HTTPURLResponse) tuple plus thrown errors.
Emote is constructed with a String url (URL is only stored), so makeUrl(emote:) validates the string with java.net.URI and returns the string.
Dictionary merging with `{ $1 }` becomes MutableMap.putAll, which also keeps the newer value on duplicate keys; on failure nothing is merged because the fetch completes before putAll runs.
Swift's `throw "Not successful"` (String error) becomes throw Exception(...) because Kotlin can only throw Throwable.
The channel URL interpolates platform.rawValue, since the ported EmotesPlatform keeps the Swift raw value used by the BTTV API path.
JSONDecoder's tolerance for unknown keys is kept with Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }; optional CodingKeys map to nullable properties defaulting to null.
logger.info -> Log.i with the file-level tag "Bttv"; String(localized:) -> localized().
BttvEmote/BttvChannel remain private top-level @Serializable data classes and are decoded with explicit serializers.

@Published properties are translated as plain mutable properties instead of MutableStateFlow, because every one of these types is a persisted @Serializable settings payload that also implements Named (a String name); the observation layer lives outside this file.

Hand-written encode(to:)/init(from:) were replaced by @Serializable classes whose @SerialName keys match the Swift CodingKeys exactly, and every property keeps the same default value the Swift decoder used for a missing key.

java.util.UUID has no built-in kotlinx.serialization serializer, so id carries @Contextual; the SerializersModule passed to the settings Json instance must register a UUID serializer or id must be handled manually at runtime.
UInt16 ports (port, srtPort, srtlaPort, virtualDestinationPort) and Int32 latencies became Int, so makeUniqueVirtualDestinationPort() and srtlaSrtPort() return Int.
SettingsRistServerStream.connected is not part of the Swift CodingKeys, so it is marked @Transient to keep it out of the serialized payload.
clone() keeps the Swift name and deep-copies streams by appending stream.clone(), matching the original use of .init().
SettingsRtspTransport keeps a rawValue property plus a fromRawValue() companion helper; its toString() overrides Any.toString() and yields the same strings as the Swift toString().
Identifiable has no counterpart declared in this port, so id stays a plain property and the classes only conform to Named.
@Published properties are translated to private MutableStateFlow fields exposed as read-only StateFlow; id stays a plain var because it is not @Published in Swift.

Codable's hand-written encode(to:)/init(from:) become a KSerializer implemented by each class's companion object (referenced with @Serializable(with = <Class>.Companion::class)); the CodingKeys enum is replaced by a private @Serializable surrogate whose property names match the Swift coding keys one-to-one.
java.util.UUID has no built-in kotlinx.serialization serializer, so ids are written to the wire as their canonical string form and parsed back with UUID.fromString.

The surrogate properties carry the same defaults as the Swift container.decode(_:_:_:) fallbacks, so missing keys decode to id = random UUID, name = "", enabled = false, printChat = false, faxMeowSound = true, printSnapshots = true.
Swift's empty init() {} maps to the implicit no-arg constructor, so both classes still have one.
SettingsCatPrinter.baseName lives in the companion object because Kotlin has no static stored properties.
Named conformance assumes Named in com.moblin.android.various.utils declares name as StateFlow<String>, matching the @Published mapping used for this port.
Both classes serialize through their companion KSerializer and therefore never use a compiler-generated serializer.
FfzImages/FfzEmote translated to private @Serializable data classes with @SerialName("1x"/"2x"/"4x") matching the Swift coding keys.
Assumed the glossary function httpGet(url) is a suspend function returning Pair<ByteArray, NetworkResponse>; if the real port signature differs, only fetchEmotes must be adjusted.
response.isNotFound / response.isSuccessful are kept as NetworkResponse members.
Swift's thrown String replaced with Exception(" Not successful") so the surrounding try/catch behaves the same.
URL(string:) validation replaced with java.net.URI parsing; makeUrl returns String? and the value is passed straight to Emote(url = ...).
String(localized:) -> localized(...); logger.info -> android.util.Log.i with tag "Ffz".
EmotesPlatform does not exist in the glossary list given but is stated to live in this same package, so no import is needed; interpolation $platform mirrors \(platform).
message stays a local var and the return is the Kotlin Pair emotes to message.
Swift enum cases map to a Kotlin enum class; entry names are kept lowercase and byte-identical so persisted raw values keep working.
Codable without explicit raw values is synthesized as the case name, so rawValue is the case name and no @Serializable annotation is required for kotlinx.serialization defaults.
CaseIterable maps to the Kotlin 2.x enum `entries` property, exposed for callers through the companion `allCases()`.
Codable decoding of an unknown case returns nil in Swift; `fromRawValue` returns a nullable Platform for the same behaviour.
String(localized: "...") becomes the shared top-level `localized` function imported from com.moblin.android.
imageName() returns the same asset identifiers; on Android these resolve against drawables of the same lowercase-ish name when consumed by the UI layer.
No state is stored, so the enum has no mutable members and is thread-safe.
None of the glossary types are referenced by this file, so no cross-package imports besides `localized` are needed.

`@Published` members become private `MutableStateFlow` fields with public get/set accessors, which keeps ObservableObject-style observation and still satisfies the `Named` interface (`override var name: String`).
The hand-written `Codable` becomes `@Serializable(with = ...)` classes plus custom `KSerializer` objects using private surrogate data classes whose property names equal the Swift coding keys.
Because surrogate property names match the Swift `CodingKeys` strings exactly, JSON keys need no `@SerialName` and stay byte-identical.
The Swift decoder's per-key default fallback becomes Kotlin default values on the surrogate properties; kotlinx.serialization applies them for missing keys.
`SettingsDjiDeviceUrlType`, `SettingsDjiDeviceResolution` and `SettingsDjiDeviceVideoCodec` have raw values that differ from their case names, so they get explicit serializers that write `rawValue`.
`SettingsDjiDeviceImageStabilization` and `SettingsDjiDeviceModel` raw values equal their case names, so the generated enum serializer already writes the correct strings.

Swift `toString()` label helpers become overrides of `Any.toString()`; the `CodingKeys` enums are kept as nested enums for source parity, and `CaseIterable` is covered by `entries` in the `fromRawValue` companions.
A private `UuidSerializer` encodes `java.util.UUID` as its canonical string form; `djiDeviceBitrates` uses `UInt` to mirror `[UInt32]`.

httpGet is the shared helper from com.moblin.android.common.various; it is called positionally as httpGet(url) and assumed to return a destructurable (data: ByteArray, response) pair whose response exposes isSuccessful, isNotFound and statusCode.
Swift threw plain String errors; each is now an IllegalStateException carrying the identical message ("Not successful", "Emotes missing", "Emotes list empty").
Swift's Dictionary.merging(other) { $1 } maps to Map.plus (emotes + other), which is also right-hand-wins and returns a new immutable map.

The private Codable structs become private @Serializable data classes with @SerialName for static_name and emote_set; a shared Json instance sets ignoreUnknownKeys = true to match JSONDecoder's default.
Decoding uses the ByteArray's decodeToString() plus the reified kotlinx.serialization.decodeFromString extension.
URL values are only stored/passed to the HTTP helper, so they are plain String per the port mapping (no java.net.URI parsing needed).
URL(string:) guards that can never fail on Android were dropped; makeEmote still returns null exactly when there is no .webp file.
logger.info becomes Log.i with the file-level TAG "Seventv"; the platform path segment uses EmotesPlatform.rawValue, matching the Swift enum interpolation.
@MainActor on the Swift class is represented by a private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) owned by the class; the polling loop runs in that scope.
Swift `Task<Void, any Error>?` becomes a nullable kotlinx.coroutines.Job, and `Task.isCancelled` becomes the coroutine scope's `!isActive` check inside the launched loop.
httpGet from com.moblin.android.common.various is assumed to return an okhttp3.Response; the body bytes are read and decoded to a String before kotlinx.serialization parsing (URLSession -> OkHttp).
JSONDecoder().decode(_:from:) is replaced by kotlinx.serialization: the struct becomes an @Serializable data class with the same stored property name currentSumViewer.
PlatformStatus.unknown / .live(viewerCount:) from com.moblin.android.various.model are used as PlatformStatus.Unknown and PlatformStatus.Live(viewerCount = ...) (sealed-class style).
URL(string:) cannot fail for an interpolated Kotlin String, so the Swift `guard let url` early return is dropped; the URL stays a plain String.
sleep(seconds: delay) from com.moblin.android.common.various is called with the Int second count; the Swift `delay = 5` then `delay = 60` cadence is preserved.

The caught exception is intentionally broad (Exception), matching the Swift catch-all; a CancellationException raised by sleep will therefore set the status to unknown before the isActive check breaks the loop.
Added the new guard calling isTextToSpeechOutputAllowed() right after the existing filter checks in isTextToSpeechEnabledForMessage, matching the Swift insertion point.

Added Model.isTextToSpeechOutputAllowed() and Model.stopTextToSpeechIfOutputNotAllowed() between isTextToSpeechEnabledForMessage and the private isTextToSpeechEnabledForAnyAlertWidget, keeping Swift declaration order.
The Swift guard in stopTextToSpeechIfOutputNotAllowed is written as an early-return if with the negated condition (!textToSpeechEnabled || isTextToSpeechOutputAllowed()).
The new functions reference database.chat.textToSpeechBluetoothSpeakerOnly and isBluetoothAudioOutput, which are translated verbatim from the Swift source.
@Published is not mapped to MutableStateFlow here: the hand-written Codable and the Named(name: String) conformance require plain, directly serializable properties, so observation is left to callers.

SettingsGimbal keeps the identical flat wire format (shutter*/flip* keys) through the private SettingsGimbalData DTO and SettingsGimbalSerializer, because kotlinx.serialization cannot inline a nested object into its parent.
Missing keys fall back to the same defaults as the Swift decoder: zoomSpeedDefault, true, true, .record, .switchScene, .kapow, empty preset list and null ids.
UUID is persisted as its string form via the private UuidStringSerializer (kotlinx.serialization has no built-in java.util.UUID serializer); decoding uses UUID.fromString like Swift's decoder.
SettingsGimbalPreset.baseName uses localized("My preset") from package com.moblin.android.
Enum entries are referenced with the Swift case names (record, switchScene, kapow) as declared by SettingsControllerFunction and SettingsGimbalMotion.
Identifiable is dropped; id stays a plain UUID property with a fresh UUID default.
SettingsGimbal is annotated @Serializable(with = SettingsGimbalSerializer::class); callers may also use SettingsGimbalSerializer directly.
ObservableObject/@Published is modelled as plain properties inside @Serializable classes (these types are Codable, so StateFlow backing would break kotlinx.serialization).
The hand-written Swift encoders/decoders become @Serializable classes; Swift's fallback decode values become Kotlin property default values, so absent keys fall back identically.
Swift UUID is mapped to java.util.UUID and serialized as a string.
Swift UInt32 bitrate is a config value, not wire bytes, so it is mapped to Int; goProDeviceBitrates is List<Int>.
Enum raw values are preserved byte-identically with @SerialName; CaseIterable becomes the Kotlin enum entries property.
SettingsGoProLens.toString() replaces the Swift display-name helper and overrides Any.toString().
state and autoRestartStreamTimer are not in the Swift CodingKeys, so they are marked @Transient.
Swift switch over rtmpUrlType is exhaustive (only server/custom), so the Kotlin when has no else branch.

AVFoundation is replaced by the com.moblin.android.platform.avfoundation shims (AVAsset, AVAssetReader, AVAssetReaderTrackOutput, AVMediaType) and every CMTime becomes a Long in microseconds, so start/latest video and audio times are Long.

The Swift global pixelFormatType is not part of this file's Kotlin dependencies, so the pixel buffer format key uses kCVPixelFormatType_32BGRA from com.moblin.android.platform.video (every platform buffer is RGBA8 whatever the tag).
deinit is expressed as AutoCloseable.close() which stops the output timer; callers must call close() when they drop a MediaPlayer.
The file's private serial DispatchQueue becomes a CoroutineDispatcher over a single thread executor, and every mediaPlayerQueue.async { } becomes CoroutineScope(mediaPlayerQueue).launch { }.
MediaSample.replacePresentationTimeStamp returns a non-null sample on Android, so the Swift guard around the replaced buffer is dropped and the buffer is used directly.
MediaPlayerDelegate loses its AnyObject constraint (Kotlin has no weak references), so a delegate must be cleared manually if it must not outlive the player.
settings.playlist is indexed through the bounds check with .size, and getCurrentFile yields null outside the range exactly like Swift.
String(format: "%02d", ...) becomes String.format(Locale.US, "%02d", ...) so the output does not depend on the device locale.

ContinuousClock.Instant is mapped to kotlin.time.TimeSource.Monotonic.ValueTimeMark: '.now' becomes TimeSource.Monotonic.markNow() and 'time.duration(to: .now) > .seconds(5)' becomes 'time.elapsedNow() > 5.seconds'.
CyclingSource keeps the Swift case names (watch, cyclingPower, cyclingSpeedCadence) and the raw values 0/1/2, and gains the usual companion fromRawValue(rawValue).

Swift's 'extension Model: WorkoutDeviceDelegate' cannot be expressed by Kotlin extension functions, so the delegate callbacks stay as top-level extension functions with identical names; Model must declare WorkoutDeviceDelegate and forward its overrides to these functions (or the delegate must be assigned through an adapter).

Assumed Model members used here: workoutDevices (MutableMap<UUID, WorkoutDevice>), currentWorkoutDeviceSettings, statusTopRight.workoutDeviceState, heartRates / runningMetrics keyed by lowercased device name, cyclingPower / cyclingCadence / cyclingSpeed, latestCyclingPower / latestCyclingCadence and addWorkoutHeartRate / addWorkoutCyclingPower / addWorkoutCyclingCadence.
The Swift 'guard let device = ...' shadowing of the parameter is renamed to deviceSettings because Kotlin forbids shadowing a parameter name.
DispatchQueue.main.async becomes mainScope.launch, with mainScope a file-private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) declared in this file.
Iterating workoutDevices.values is copied with toList() before calling stop() so that mutating the map inside the loop matches Swift's value-semantics iteration.
WorkoutDeviceState entries are referenced by their Swift names (.disconnected, .connected) and the unused first parameter of the two cycling delegate callbacks is kept as a named 'device' parameter.
`@MainActor` on the Swift class has no Kotlin equivalent; access must be confined to the main dispatcher by callers.
`@Published currentSwitcherId` is exposed as a `StateFlow`; the backing `MutableStateFlow` is `internal` so the `Model` extension functions in this file can write to it.
`ContinuousClock.Instant` is mapped to `java.time.Instant`; `switchTime`, `now` parameters and `.now` all use it.
`IndexSet` is mapped to `Set<Int>`; offsets are removed in descending order so earlier removals do not shift later indices.
`popLast()` maps to `removeLastOrNull()`, `removeAll()` maps to `clear()`, and `[UUID]` becomes `MutableList<UUID>`.
`logger.info(...)` becomes `Log.i("Model", ...)`; the tag is the enclosing type name.
`autoSceneSwitcher.currentSwitcherId` is a StateFlow, so reads from the extensions go through the internal backing flow's `.value`.
The remote control state call uses the app's `RemoteControlState`/`RemoteControlAutoSceneSwitcher` types, imported from this same package.
ContinuousClock.Instant is mapped to monotonic nanoseconds from System.nanoTime() and ContinuousClock.Duration to Long nanoseconds (1_000_000_000L per second).
Deque<SrtDataPacket> becomes kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque and OrderedSet<UInt32> becomes LinkedHashSet<UInt> (insertion order, first()/remove() emulate removeFirst()).

Data/UnsafeRawBufferPointer buffers become ByteArray; the in-place writes done through withUnsafeMutableBytes are performed by the private ByteArray.writeUInt32(value, offset) extension declared in this file.
ByteReader/ByteWriter are assumed to expose readUInt16(): UShort, readUInt32(): UInt, readBytes(count): ByteArray, writeUInt16(UShort), writeUInt32(UInt), writeBytes(ByteArray) and data: ByteArray.
Atomic<SrtPerformanceData> is assumed to provide value and mutate { }, and SrtPerformanceData is created with its no-argument constructor in place of Swift's .zero.
delegate lost its weak semantics: SrtSenderDelegate is held as a plain nullable reference and must be cleared by the owner.
srtlaClientQueue.async { } became srtlaClientQueue.launch { }, so srtlaClientQueue must be a CoroutineScope; SimpleTimer.startSingleShot is called with the timeout in seconds as Double.
Swift's thrown String errors are translated as a private SrtSenderException type, and logger.info maps to Log.i with tag "SrtSender".
Swift Testing struct translated to a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions and @Test methods; imports from the glossary packages are used.
The private createSegments helper keeps its Swift signature, with the emotes parameter defaulting to emptyList().
Swift's `id: inout Int` has no Kotlin equivalent, so the ported Emotes.createSegments is assumed to return Pair<List<ChatPostSegment>, Int>, where second is the next id used by the caller.
#expect(a == b) was mapped to assertEquals(b, a) so the literal stays the expected value; #expect(cond) became assertTrue(cond).
Comparisons against [nil, ...] use listOf<String?>(null, ...) so the expected list has the same nullable element type as texts()/emoteNames().
The Swift suite has no init, so no @Before setUp() method is generated.
makeEmotes, texts and emoteNames are imported from com.moblin.android; ChatPostSegment from com.moblin.android.various.
Test order, names and byte-identical string literals match the Swift source.
ContinuousClock.Instant and ContinuousClock.Duration are mapped to Long nanoseconds obtained from System.nanoTime(); `.advanced(by:)` becomes plain addition.

The UInt32 bitrate surface (init targetBitrate, setTargetBitrate, getCurrentBitrate, delegate callback) is mapped to Int following the project convention, while the internal 64-bit bitrate stays Long.
logger.info is replaced by android.util.Log.i using the class name as the log tag.
logAdaptiveAcion is inherited from AdaptiveBitrate (same package) and is called with the named argument actionTaken.

AdaptiveBitrateSettings field types are assumed to be Int for counts (packetsInFlight, rttDiffHighAllowedSpike) and Long for bitrate-shaped values; minimumBitrate is Long because the Swift code compares it to an Int64.
Swift multiline strings with backslash continuations are collapsed into single-line interpolated strings.
defaultSrtLatency is wrapped with toDouble() so the elvis result matches the Double type of StreamStats.latency.
stats.mbpsSendRate is force-unwrapped with !!, stats.latency and stats.relaxed keep the Swift optional fallbacks via ?:.
Swift Testing async throws tests become @Test fun ...() = runTest { } so the suspend AdaptiveBitrate calls run inside a coroutine.
Deque<UInt32> from swift-collections maps to kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque<Int> with addLast/last/isEmpty.
Bitrate values (targetBitrate, transport bitrate, delegate callback) are translated as Int rather than UInt, since they are encoder bitrates, not wire-format data.
Int64 transport bitrate and the makeStats parameter become Long; the Swift Int literals 5_000_000 / 1_000_000 are typed as Long where required.
The Handler class and its AdaptiveBitrateDelegate conformance (a Swift extension in the same file) are merged into one Kotlin class with override.
makeStats and update stay file-private top-level functions, matching the Swift private helpers, and update is a suspend function because it calls sleep.
Named arguments are kept (targetBitrate, delegate, settings, stats, bitrate, milliSeconds) so the call sites read identically to the Swift source.
Test types live in the same Kotlin package, so no imports are needed for AdaptiveBitrateSrtBelabox, StreamStats, AdaptiveBitrateDelegate or adaptiveBitrateBelaboxSettings.

The @Test(arguments:) suite became a JUnit 4 Parameterized class: the timestamp argument is a constructor property named `value`, and JUnit runs the other two tests once per argument set (Swift Testing ran them once).
ntpUnixEpochSeconds stays a top-level private value of type ULong so the 64-bit NTP shifts and mask literals (0xFFFF_FFFF, 0x8000_0000) remain byte-identical.
decodeNtpTimestamp is assumed to take the wire-format ULong (parameter label `v`) and to return Double? seconds; assertNotNull is used in place of try #require to unwrap it.
#expect(decodeNtpTimestamp(v: value) == nil) became assertNull; #expect(timestamp == 0) became assertEquals(0.0, timestamp) because timestamp is a Double.

isEqual is imported from com.moblin.android and called positionally for the first two arguments with the Swift label `epsilon` kept as a named argument; adjust the call if the ported signature differs.
The Swift `throws` on decodeNtpTimestampAtUnixEpoch was dropped: Kotlin assertions do not need a throws clause.
WebrtcIngestClient, VideoCodec, TrackTimestamper and WebrtcIngestClientDelegate are not referenced by this suite, so no imports for them were added.
CMSampleBuffer is replaced by MediaSample from com.moblin.android.media; presentation times are converted from seconds to microseconds.
Swift `===` identity checks map to kotlin.test.assertSame because BufferedAudio hands back the same MediaSample instances that were appended.
expectSequence takes the timestamp as a parameter and returns the advanced value, because Kotlin has no Swift-style `inout` parameter.

createSampleBuffer builds a silent MediaSample directly, since CMSampleBuffer.createSilent has no Android counterpart; the format comes from MediaFormat.createAudioFormat(MIMETYPE_AUDIO_RAW, 48000, 1) and 1024 frames of 16-bit mono are represented by a zero-filled ByteArray.
DriftTracker.setDrift(drift:) keeps the Swift argument label as the Kotlin parameter name; adjust it if the ported signature uses a different name.
cameraId uses UUID.randomUUID() for the Swift `.init()` default UUID.
JUnit 4 (org.junit.Test) with kotlin.test assertions; the suite has no init block, so no @Before setUp method is generated.
Suite becomes a plain JUnit 4 class (class GoProBleProtocolSuite) with @Test methods in the same order; assertions use kotlin.test.
ByteArray has no value equality, so list/byte comparisons use assertContentEquals instead of assertEquals.
Byte literals >= 0x80 must be written with .toByte() in Kotlin (0xBC, 0x85, 0x80); the byte values themselves are unchanged.
Swift Data.prefix(2) becomes ByteArray.copyOfRange(0, 2) and Data((0..<64).map(UInt8.init)) becomes ByteArray(64) { it.toByte() }.
ByteArray.hexString() is assumed to be the ported Moblin extension that exists elsewhere in the project; it is not declared in this file.
The Swift throws/#require in packetizesAndAccumulatesLongMessage is unnecessary in Kotlin, so the last packet is taken directly with packets.last().

response.result == .resultSuccess is translated against the ported constant goProResponseSuccessStatus, and the protobuf serializedBytes initializer becomes OpenGopro_ResponseGetApEntries.parseFrom(...).

Named arguments follow the Swift labels (payload, on, ssid, password, scanId, startIndex, maximumEntries, url, resolution, bitrate, lens, packet); the enum type names GoProLiveStreamResolution/GoProLiveStreamLens are assumed for the .r1080p/.auto/.linear cases.
JUnit 4 test class with kotlin.test assertions, mirroring the two Swift Testing cases one-to-one.
SettingsChatFilter, SettingsStream, SettingsStreamProtocol and SettingsStreamDetailedProtocol are in this same package, so they need no import.
The Swift `.init(id:text:)` message segment maps to ChatMessageSegment, imported from com.moblin.android.chat; verify the actual package name if it differs.
messageStartWords is assigned with mutableListOf so it works whether the Kotlin property is List<String> or MutableList<String>.
DefaultTcpPorts comes from com.moblin.android.various.network and provides mobcamStream.
Boolean results are asserted with assertTrue/assertFalse following the cond -> assertTrue mapping.
Enum comparisons use the fully qualified SettingsStreamProtocol.mobcam / SettingsStreamDetailedProtocol.mobcam values.
No suite-level setup was needed since the Swift struct has no init or shared mutable state.
Swift Testing struct converted to a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions; @Test maps to org.junit.Test.
macroActionIfBars(actions:) becomes the top-level function macroActionIfBars(actions) imported from the same package.
Key-path maps such as $0.map(\.level) become nested map lambdas over MacroActionIfBar.level/isFirst/isLast.
Expected nested arrays use emptyList<Int>()/emptyList<Boolean>() so generic inference matches List<List<Int>> and List<List<Boolean>>.
The makeAction/makeIfAction helpers stay private methods in the test class and build SettingsMacrosAction with the snapshot/ifCondition enum cases.
assertEquals(expected, actual) keeps Swift's left-hand argument first, matching #expect(a == b).
There is no suite-level init in the Swift source, so no @Before setUp is emitted.
SettingsMacrosAction and SettingsMacrosActionFunction are imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings.

@Published properties are exposed as StateFlow backed by MutableStateFlow; the backing fields are declared `internal val _name` (not private) so the hand-written kotlinx.serialization serializers of the same module can update them.
SettingsMic is annotated with a custom KSerializer because the Swift decoder falls back to getDefaultMic() when the stored raw value is unknown; fromRawValue mirrors that.

SettingsMicsMic, SettingsMics and SettingsAudio use custom KSerializers instead of generated ones so that their real codable state (delay, mics, autoSwitch, gainDb, preferStereoMic) is still persisted even though those properties are StateFlows.
JSON keys are kept byte-identical to the Swift CodingKeys: 'all' for mics, 'dataSourceID' for dataSourceId, 'audioOutputToInputChannelsMap' for outputToInputChannelsMap.
Missing keys in the payload keep the Swift defaults (name/inputUid "", dataSourceId nil, delay 0.0, mics empty, autoSwitch true, defaultMic "", gainDb 0, preferStereoMic false).
`id` stays a computed property: "$inputUid ${dataSourceId ?: 0}".
Equatable on SettingsMicsMic (inputUid + dataSourceId) becomes equals() plus a matching hashCode().
The eight is*CameraOrMic helpers are imported from com.moblin.android.common.various.
All tested types (ChatBotCommand, ChatBotMessage, the argument enums, makeChatPostTextSegments) live in com.moblin.android.various, the same package as this suite, so no imports are needed for them.

Swift Testing '@Test(arguments:)' cases were folded into loops inside the identically named test functions (fuzzyMatch, fuzzyMatchShortWords, fuzzyMatchFilter, fuzzyMatchReaction) because JUnit 4 Parameterized allows only one parameterized method per class.
