'try #require(ChatBotCommand(...))' becomes the new private helper createCommand(), which wraps the construction in assertNotNull so a nullable Kotlin factory/constructor still yields a non-null value.

Assumed Kotlin signature for the fuzzy lookup: popFirstArgument(ChatBotMainArgument::class), i.e. a KClass parameter mirroring the Swift metatype argument; a reified generic version would be called as popFirstArgument<ChatBotMainArgument>().
Assumed the ChatBotMessage platform argument enum is named ChatPlatform with a 'twitch' entry; it is not listed in the glossary because Swift only wrote the implicit '.twitch' member reference.
makeChatPostTextSegments is called with the named argument text, matching the Swift helper's parameter label.
Null comparisons use assertEquals with an explicit String? type argument so kotlin.test picks the generic overload unambiguously.
ModelMock folds the Swift extension into its class declaration by implementing SrtSenderDelegate directly.
MessageQueue<Void> becomes MessageQueue<Unit>; put is called synchronously from the delegate callbacks while get stays suspend, matching the sync SrtSenderDelegate surface.
The Swift Testing suite becomes a JUnit 4 class; connectDisconnect is a @Test method whose body runs in runBlocking because the model waits are suspend.
Data maps to ByteArray; the private file-level helpers HexByteArray.hexString() and dataFromHexString() replace Data.hexString() and Data(hexString:).
UInt32(packet.substring(...), radix: 16)! becomes packet.substring(...).toUInt(16); a malformed string throws NumberFormatException instead of trapping on nil.
Date.now.advanced(by: .seconds(6)) becomes Instant.now().plusSeconds(6) for SrtSender.send(now:).
String.substring(begin:end:) maps to Kotlin String.substring(startIndex, endIndex) on the hex strings captured by the mock.
The Swift multi-line hex literals continued with a backslash are written as concatenated Kotlin string literals with byte-identical content.
Bundle.main / Bundle(for:) have no Android equivalent: both file readers now load classpath resources through a private BundleToken class, so test resources must live in src/test/resources.
Swift's FloatingPoint-constrained generics are replaced by Double and Float overloads of isEqual/areEqual; callers picking one overload keep the same call site shape.
MessageQueue is backed by kotlinx.coroutines Channel(UNLIMITED): put() stays non-suspending via trySend and get() becomes a suspend function using receive().
makeEmotes assumes the ported Emote exposes a url constructor parameter typed as String; adapt the call if the Emote signature in com.moblin.android.integrations.emotes differs.
URL.lastPathComponent is emulated with String.substringAfterLast('/') on ChatPostUrl.still, which is assumed to be a String in the Kotlin port.
readMainFile and readTestFile read the same classpath: Android unit tests do not separate an app bundle from a test bundle.
No @Test members exist in the Swift source, so this file stays a plain helper file that JUnit 4 suites import.
No TODO() markers were needed; every construct had a usable Kotlin counterpart.
CMSampleBuffer is replaced by com.moblin.android.media.MediaSample; presentation timestamps are read as presentationTimeUs / 1_000_000.0 to reproduce CMSampleBuffer.presentationTimeStamp.seconds.
Swift Data == Data value equality becomes ByteArray.contentEquals, because Kotlin ByteArray equality is referential - the zero buffers are compared with data.contentEquals(ByteArray(2048)).
Data(hexString:) has no counterpart in the glossary, so a private file-local hexStringToData() helper is added and the hex literals are kept byte-identical.

MpegTsReader and MpegTsReaderDelegate live in this same package, so they need no import; the constructor is called with the Swift argument labels (name, decoderQueue, timecodesEnabled, softwareDecoding, targetLatency) and Dispatchers.Main for DispatchQueue.main.
handlePacketFromClient is treated as a suspend function and the test body runs inside runBlocking.
The Swift Testing #require unwraps become kotlin.test.assertNotNull, which returns the non-null value.
#expect(cond) becomes assertTrue(cond) / assertFalse(cond); #expect(a == b) becomes assertEquals(b, a) with the expected value first.
mock.audioSampleBuffers and videoSampleBuffers are MutableList<MediaSample>, and count maps to size.
Model is declared in the same package (com.moblin.android.various.model), so this Swift extension becomes top-level Kotlin extension functions on Model with no extra import for Model itself.
Only SoopChat and SoopPlatformStatus are imported, from com.moblin.android.streamingplatforms.soop.
Force unwraps (soopChat!, soopPlatformStatus!) were replaced by assigning to a local val, which keeps the original create-then-use order without using !!.

The Swift platform enum cases .soop and .unknown are emitted as Platform.Soop and PlatformStatus.Unknown; align these with the actual Kotlin enum declarations of Platform/PlatformStatus if they differ.
StreamingPlatformStatus is assumed to have the same two-argument constructor (platform, status) as in Swift, so it is called with named arguments.
soopChat and soopPlatformStatus are treated as mutable properties on Model declared in Model.kt; no redeclaration happens here.

resetChat(), setTextToSpeechStreamerMentions(), isRemoteControlChatAndEvents(platform:) and updateChatMoreThanOneChatConfigured() are member functions of Model declared in other files and are called unchanged.
Function order matches the Swift source so both files can be read side by side.
@MainActor has no Kotlin equivalent: the class owns a private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main + SupervisorJob()) and all state changes stay on the main dispatcher.
Task<Void, any Error>? becomes Job?; stop() cancels the Job exactly like task?.cancel().
Task.isCancelled becomes the kotlinx.coroutines CoroutineScope.isActive check inside the launched coroutine.
sleep(seconds:) from com.moblin.android.common.various is assumed to be a suspend function taking Double, so the local delay is kept as Double (1.0 then 30.0).

PlatformStatus is assumed to be a sealed class in com.moblin.android.various.model with Unknown, Offline and Live(viewerCount: Int) variants matching the Swift cases .unknown, .offline and .live(viewerCount:).
The thrown error from getKickChannelInfo is caught as Exception, matching Swift's untyped catch which sets .unknown.
The C-style while true loop and the delay escalation from 1 to 30 seconds are preserved unchanged.
The type returned by getKickChannelInfo is used only through inference, so no import for it is required.
Swift's `extension Model` becomes top-level extension functions on `Model` in this same package, keeping names and order identical.

`ContinuousClock.Instant` is mapped to `kotlin.time.TimeSource.Monotonic.ValueTimeMark` and `ContinuousClock.now` to `TimeSource.Monotonic.markNow()`; the type must match `Variables.timestamp` in com.moblin.android.various.
`Date` becomes `java.time.Instant` (`Date.now` -> `Instant.now()`).
`"\(Int(slopePercent))%"` becomes `"${slopePercent.toInt()}%"`; Kotlin `toInt()` truncates toward zero exactly like Swift's `Int(_:)` for Double.
`Variables(...)` is built with named arguments, so the Kotlin data class parameter names must match the Swift memberwise initializer labels.
`systemMonitor.format()` is imported as an extension function from com.moblin.android.common.various.
`getSystemMonitor()` and `getBrowserTitle()` remain file-private extension functions, matching Swift's private extension members.
`loadTextFormat(...)` is invoked positionally to avoid depending on an unverified parameter name.
Swift Testing struct TextEffectSuite becomes a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions, run under Robolectric so the app context, resources and locale are available.

The two `.enabled(if: Locale.current.identifier == "en_SE")` guards are replaced by @Config(qualifiers = "en-rSE") plus TimeZone/Locale defaults set in @Before (Europe/Stockholm, en-SE), so the time and date tests run unconditionally with the same values as on iOS.
The suite is @MainActor in Swift, but the formatter under test is pure string/number formatting, so tests stay plain @Test; only the locale and time zone need to be pinned.
WeatherCondition is not part of the port (Variables.condition is a String?), so `.clear` / `.rain` are passed as the lowercase condition strings "clear" / "rain".
TextFormatLoader().load(format:) is called through the kept top-level function loadTextFormat(format = ...), which is what the port declares for the same loader logic.

Sealed cases are written with the ported nested names: TextEffectPartData.Text / TextEffectPartData.ImageSystemNameTryFill and TextFormatPart.Speed / TextFormatPart.Text / TextFormatPart.HeartRate / TextFormatPart.Subtitles etc.
Locale-dependent expected numbers (grouped thousands) are copied verbatim from the Swift source, and the measurement unit strings keep their original spacing.

createVariables mirrors the Swift helper parameter order and fills every Variables field with the same value, with timestamp = ContinuousClock.now.nanoseconds and date = Instant.ofEpochSecond(1_723_350_366).

Swift's `id: inout Int` counter cannot exist in Kotlin, so `createKickSegments` is called with a `() -> Int` lambda holding a local `var id`; adjust the call if the ported function uses a different holder.
`makeEmotes(...)` from package com.moblin.android supplies the emotes manager that the Swift test builds from the emotes list.
`url?.still?.absoluteString` becomes `url?.still?.toString()` because the Android ChatPostUrl stores parsed URIs rather than NSURL.
Expected value lists are typed as List<String?> so they unify with the nullable results of `texts` and `emoteNames`.
Swift's `compactMap` maps onto Kotlin's `mapNotNull`.
Everything under test (createKickSegments, ChatPostSegment, makeEmotes, texts, emoteNames) lives in the same package or com.moblin.android, hence no local re-declarations.
Run as a plain JUnit 4 test class; no suite setup was needed because the Swift struct has no stored state.

The suite's production API changed: interpolate3d now takes a (Int, Int, Int) -> SIMD3 sampler instead of a List<SIMD3>, makeLutCube(dimension, sampler) is new, and lutEffectConvertCube returns a (dimension, cubeData) pair. Signatures were inferred from the Swift call sites because the dependency listing still shows the previous list-based overloads.
makeCubeData is now a file-private test helper (dimension + function) that packs SIMD4(x, y, z, 1) as little-endian Float32; it no longer calls the production makeCubeData(entries:).
sampler(lut, dimension) returns a Kotlin function value (Int, Int, Int) -> SIMD3 indexing lut[(blue * dimension + green) * dimension + red].

LutEffectSuite.lutEffectConvertCube is assumed to return Pair<Float, ByteArray> (Swift's Int(dimension) proves the dimension is not Int) and makeLutCube is assumed to return Pair<Int, ByteArray>; adjust if the production declarations differ.

renderBigPngLutWithMetalPetal is left out as instructed; the newly added renderCubeLutWithMetalPetal is left out as well because it also renders with MetalPetal/GL and cannot run under Robolectric, so both live in the hand-written instrumented LutEffectRenderSuite.
Byte comparisons of cube data keep the existing wrapper of ByteBuffer.wrap(data).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN).asFloatBuffer().
Swift Testing suite translated to a JUnit 4 test class using org.junit.Test with kotlin.test assertions (#expect(a == b) -> assertEquals(b, a), #expect(cond) -> assertTrue(cond)).
File-private helpers (makeTwitchEmote, makeTwitchGif, gifNames, textFragment, emoteFragment, twitchEmoteIds) stay as private top-level functions in this file, in the same order as the Swift source.
ChatMessageEmote.url / stillUrl are treated as String in this port, so URL(string:) literals became plain string interpolation.

Swift's URL.path has no String counterpart, so twitchEmoteIds parses the still URL with java.net.URI; the Swift split/dropFirst(2) idiom gained a filter { it.isNotEmpty() } because Kotlin's split keeps empty parts.
gifNames reproduces lastPathComponent with substringAfterLast('/') on the assumed String URL in bigGifUrl.moving.
ClosedRange<Int> parameters became IntRange (3 ... 7 -> 3..7).
createTwitchSegments's Swift `id: inout Int` is assumed ported as a trailing () -> Int id supplier; only uniqueness of ids is asserted, so the exact values do not matter.
Lists that can contain nulls are written with an explicit listOf<String?> type argument so the generic assertEquals resolves.
WeatherKit has no Android counterpart, so Variables.condition is treated as a String and conditionToEmoji matches the Swift WeatherCondition case names.
Foundation MeasurementFormatter is replaced by android.icu NumberFormatter + MeasureUnit + Precision; the "system" unit choice uses the locale country (US/LR/MM = imperial).
DateFormatter and Date.FormatStyle are replaced by java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter bound to ZoneId.systemDefault().
ContinuousClock.Instant is modelled as Long nanoseconds: a duration between instants is (end - now) / 1_000_000_000.0.
Variables.temperature and Variables.feelsLikeTemperature are assumed to be Double degrees Celsius because Measurement<UnitTemperature> has nothing equivalent on Android.
Icon names (checkmark.square, mic.slash) and emoji plain-text values are kept byte-identical so rendering stays the same.

Moblin.format / Moblin.formatPace map to the top-level format() / formatPace() of com.moblin.android.common.various; Duration.formatWithSeconds() and TextFormatSpeedUnit.toSystem() are assumed to live in the packages shown by the glossary.
Emitted lines keep a reference to the mutable parts list, so parts is always replaced by a fresh list right after a line is appended (same value semantics as the Swift array).
WiFiAware is Apple-only in Swift; here it is replaced by the port's counterpart types in com.moblin.android.media.wifiaware (Sender, Receiver, WiFiAwareSender, WiFiAwareReceiver).

The iOS capability check WACapabilities.supportedFeatures.contains(.wifiAware) is translated as WACapabilities.supportedFeatures.contains(WAFeature.wifiAware); this assumes those two symbols live in com.moblin.android.media.wifiaware.
The role enum is assumed to be WiFiAwareRole with entries sender/receiver (Swift case names kept).
Swift Task { } is translated to a coroutine launched on a file-private CoroutineScope; the stored task handles become Job? properties of Model (wiFiAwareSenderTask / wiFiAwareReceiverTask).
logger.info(...) maps to android.util.Log.i with the class name "Model" as tag.
#if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst) and @available(iOS 26, *) are compile-time/availability guards with no Android equivalent and are dropped.
The Swift private extension methods stay as private top-level extension functions on Model, in the same order as the Swift file.
Suite constants and the private layout()/position() helpers were kept as private members of the class; no @Before is needed because nothing is set up.

The platform CGPoint is declared as a plain class without structural equals, so every position check compares x and y through a private assertPosition() helper instead of asserting on the CGPoint instance.
SettingsAlignment.allCases became SettingsAlignment.entries (Kotlin 2.x enum entries).
metalPetalLayerPosition and the CIImage.move extension live in com.moblin.android.videoeffects, the same package as this suite, so they need no import.
#expect(abs(position.x - expected.x) <= 1) became assertTrue(abs(position.x - expected.x) <= 1.0).
Assertions use kotlin.test (assertEquals, assertTrue) inside a JUnit 4 class, per the test tier rules.

Network.framework (NWListener/NWConnection/NWProtocolWebSocket) has no Android counterpart, so the transport is implemented with java.net.ServerSocket/java.net.Socket plus a hand-written WebSocket upgrade handshake and RFC 6455 text/close framing (client frames are unmasked, server frames are written unmasked).

MessageQueue<T> from com.moblin.android is used with the assumed suspend API put(value) / get(): T; if the real class exposes a non-suspending put, the enclosing functions can stay suspend without change.
Swift `throw "some string"` becomes a private ObsMockException(message) since Kotlin can only throw Throwable.
The mock's url() returns a String ("ws://127.0.0.1:port") rather than a URL/URI, since the value is only built and handed to a client.
deinit { listener.cancel() } is dropped; Kotlin has no destructors, so the ServerSocket/coroutine scope is only released when the mock is garbage collected or the socket is closed via disconnect().
@MainActor / MainActor.assumeIsolated / Sendable conformances are dropped; the class runs on ordinary coroutines on Dispatchers.IO.
logger.info(...) is mapped to android.util.Log.i with tag "ObsWebSocketServerMock"; unit tests on the JVM need unitTests.returnDefaultValues or Robolectric for Log not to throw.
jsonString uses kotlinx.serialization and recursively sorts object keys to match Swift's .sortedKeys option.

AVAudioConverter has no Android counterpart; the conversion engine is android.media.MediaCodec and the pull based convert(to:error:withInputFrom:) becomes dequeueInputBuffer/queueInputBuffer plus dequeueOutputBuffer.
AudioStreamBasicDescription and AVAudioFormat are both represented by android.media.MediaFormat (KEY_SAMPLE_RATE, KEY_CHANNEL_COUNT, KEY_CHANNEL_MASK), which is what MediaCodec uses natively.
AVAudioCompressedBuffer maps to MediaSample from com.moblin.android.media; the CMSampleBuffer.withAudioBufferList wrapper is replaced by reading MediaSample.data.
The DispatchQueue lockQueue is a CoroutineDispatcher, and every lockQueue.async block becomes a launch on a CoroutineScope bound to that dispatcher.
The port's Atomic is assumed to expose a settable value, so bitrate.mutate { $0 = x } is written as bitrate.value = x.

setBitrate stays an extension function on the converter but only clamps and tracks the value, because Android audio encoders cannot change their bitrate after configure; the value takes effect on the next converter creation.

makeChannelLayout has no channel layout object on Android, so the discrete in order layout tag becomes a MediaFormat channel mask with the low channel bits set; both statics are consolidated into one companion object placed where makeAudioFormat appears in the Swift file.
As in the Swift source, setInputSourceFormat never assigns inSourceFormat, so that field is only cleared by stopRunningInternal; this behaviour is kept identical.
URL properties become String paths; mediaStorage.makePath returns java.io.File, so .path is taken and checkResourceIsReachable becomes File.exists().
Deque -> kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque; getPlayer passes a copy so the player keeps Swift's value semantics when AlertsEffectGifImages consumes frames.
DispatchQueue.global().async -> a file-private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO); DispatchQueue.main.async -> a file-private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main.immediate).
Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:) -> Bundle.url; Data(contentsOf:) -> File(url).readBytes(); FileManager.createFile -> File.writeBytes.
Int16(bitPattern: reader.readUInt16Le()) -> sample.toShort(), and the throwing read is wrapped in runCatching.
path.appendingPathExtension("wav") -> "$path.wav", since the stored value is already a plain path string.
AlertsEffectMedia is a non-final Swift class, so it becomes open class with open getPlayer/update and private helpers.
SettingsWidgetAlertsAlertMediaType is assumed to have the entries gifAndSound and video.

FuzzyMatchingSwift has no Android equivalent, so its matcher is reimplemented in-file: a case-insensitive subsequence test combined with a Levenshtein similarity ratio, gated by the same threshold (0.34) and distance (1000) options.
The failable initializer init?(message:aliases:) becomes a companion `operator fun invoke(...)` returning `ChatBotCommand?`, so the call syntax `ChatBotCommand(message, aliases)` is preserved.
Swift Deque<String> becomes kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque<String>, using addLast / removeFirstOrNull / firstOrNull.

Kotlin has no CaseIterable; matchArgument and popFirstArgument take a reified type parameter bounded by Enum<T> and use enumValues<T>(). Both are `internal` so the inline bodies may reference each other.
Enum raw values are preserved byte-identically through an `override val rawValue` constructor parameter, including irregular ones: "wheelofluck", "4:3", "toggle-playback".
Swift enum case names are kept verbatim (lower camel case) as Kotlin enum constant names so both files read side by side.
Swift's split(separator: " ") drops empty subsequences; the Kotlin version filters empty strings before drop(1).
String.trim() / lowercased() map to Kotlin trim() / lowercase().
formatLog takes List<LogEntry> instead of Swift's Deque<LogEntry>: kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque would not accept the MutableList held by Model.log.
formatLog returns the written file's absolute path as String (URL -> String) and writes to context.cacheDir instead of FileManager temporaryDirectory, so Model must expose a context.
The temporary file name uses epoch millis ("Moblin-log-<millis>.txt") because Swift's Date() description contains characters that are awkward in Android file paths.

The extension functions assume Model exposes mutable collections/properties named log, fileLog, logId, logsStorage, logger, database, remoteControlLog and context; Kotlin extension functions cannot reach private members, so these must be internal or public in Model.kt.
logger.handler is assigned a lambda `{ message -> debugLog(message) }` because a bound callable reference to a private file-level extension function is not expressible as a plain (String) -> Unit.
DispatchQueue.main.async is dispatched on a file-private mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main).
formatDate(.now) became formatDate(Instant.now()) following the Date -> java.time.Instant mapping.
log.map { $0.message }.joined(separator: "\n") became joinToString(separator = "\n") { it.message }.
JUnit 4 with kotlin.test assertions replaces Swift Testing; the suite class name and all test method names are kept identical, and there is no suite init so no @Before is emitted.
makeRtmpUri(url:) and makeRtmpStreamKey(url:) are top-level functions from com.moblin.android.common.various and are called positionally.
RtmpConnection(name:queue:) loses the DispatchQueue argument; the Kotlin port creates the connection with the name only (queue becomes a dispatcher inside the class).
callCompletions is treated as a MutableMap<Int, (List<AsValue>) -> Unit>; the captured local var arguments is reassigned inside the lambda, which Kotlin allows.
Data slicing uses ByteArray.copyOfRange(from, to); the expected buffer equality is checked with contentEquals because ByteArray has no structural equals in Kotlin.
commandType is passed as RtmpChunkType.amf0Command - the Swift RtmpMessageType enum is represented by RtmpChunkType in this port, confirm the entry name.
The AMF result payload is built with AsObject(mutableMapOf("code" to AsValue.String(...))); confirm the AsObject/AsValue constructors in com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.rtmp.amf.
makeConnectResultChunkData stays a private helper in the same file and returns a ByteArray produced by RtmpChunk.encode().
CGFloat is mapped to Double (HSV and chroma math), Float stays Float as in Swift's MTIColor/SIMD2 APIs.
DispatchQueue.main.async -> CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main.immediate).launch, and asyncAfter(0.25) -> launch + delay(250), because no mainScope global is declared for this package.
DispatchQueue.global().async -> CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Default).launch.

processorPipelineQueue is a CoroutineScope, so its .async blocks become .launch; the nonisolated(unsafe) let and the shadowing local val of the same name are kept as a plain local val with this@RemoveBackgroundEffect at the assignment.
CIColorCubeWithColorSpace.cubeData is a ByteArray, so the Swift [Float] cube is packed with ByteBuffer in native (little-endian) order, count * 4 bytes, as Data(bytes:count:) did.
Swift's switch-expression returning a tuple (red, green, blue) becomes a `when` returning Triple, with `default:` as `else` (Int(sector) -> sector.toInt(), same truncation).
filterMetalPetal.inputBackgroundImage = .transparent -> MTIImage.transparent; both `?? image` fallbacks kept.
The three private file-level structs become private data classes with their Swift names and member order.
Swift Testing @Suite(.serialized) becomes a plain JUnit 4 class; JUnit already runs methods of one class serially, so no annotation is needed.
DispatchSemaphore -> CountDownLatch; FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory -> the java.io.tmpdir system property.
CMTime(value: 1, timescale: 30) is stored as a Long of microseconds (videoFrameDuration), and CMTime(seconds:) becomes a Long of microseconds.
AVAudioPCMBuffer / CVPixelBuffer sample creation is replaced by MediaSample instances built from raw PCM 16-bit little-endian bytes and a YUV420 frame buffer.
AVURLAsset and AVAssetReader track inspection are replaced by MediaExtractor plus MediaCodec decoding of the written mp4.
processorPipelineQueue.sync {} is assumed to be an ExecutorService submit/get on that top-level val from the same package.
Recorder.startRunning output settings are assumed to be android.media.MediaFormat values (AAC audio, AVC video) mirroring the AVFoundation dictionaries.
deinit file removal is translated into an AutoCloseable.close() on RecorderTester.

XMLCoder does not exist on Android: decoding uses javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory plus small org.w3c.dom helpers, encoding uses a hand-built string with an XmlNode.toXml(root) serializer (kept so Open and Auth keep their DynamicNodeEncoding attribute/element split).

URLSessionWebSocketTask is replaced by an OkHttp WebSocket; the callback-based listener pushes incoming text into a kotlinx Channel of unlimited capacity that receiveMessages() suspends on, and channel closure makes the receive throw so the reconnect loop still runs.
The @MainActor class keeps a private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) plus a Job; Task.isCancelled becomes coroutineContext.isActive, and sleep(seconds: 5) becomes delay(5000).
The hard-coded ws://192.168.50.72:5443/ws socket created in the Swift init is dropped, because the OkHttp socket is only created in setupConnection() from the real url property.
The Swift inout Int parameter of makeChatPostTextSegments is assumed to be intArrayOf(0) (a one-element IntArray) in the Kotlin port; adjust if that helper used a different convention.
model.appendChatMessage is called with named arguments matching the Swift labels, and the chat platform case is assumed to be ChatPlatform.openStreamingPlatform from com.moblin.android.various.model.
private top-level Swift structs become file-private (private) top-level Kotlin declarations in the same file, preserving declaration order.
The XML message is wrapped in <container> before parsing because XMLCoder matches the outer root's child element, exactly as in the Swift original.
The Swift tuple (displayName, segments, isAction) inside Delegate is replaced by a private DelegateMessage data class so messages is a MutableList<DelegateMessage>.
@MainActor is dropped; TwitchChat delegate callbacks are assumed to be invoked synchronously inside webSocketClientReceiveMessage, so the test can assert right after the call.
Swift multi-line string literals with trailing-backslash line continuations are rewritten as Kotlin string concatenation so the IRC wire text stays byte-identical.
try? X becomes runCatching { X }.getOrNull(); try #require(x) becomes a direct x.first() access with kotlin.test assertions.
#expect(a == nil) uses assertNull, #expect(!x) uses assertFalse, #expect(a == b) uses assertEquals(expected = b, actual = a).
URL.absoluteString comparisons become plain String comparisons: ChatMessageEmote.url and ChatPostUrl.still are treated as String URLs in the Android port.
twitchEmoteIds builds the path with java.net.URI and splits/filters empty components to match Swift String.split(omittingEmptySubsequences: true) semantics.
TwitchChatCommand cases are assumed to be PascalCase (PrivateMessage, UserNotice, ClearMsg, ClearChat, Ping) and userBadges/sourceChannelIcon are assumed String-based.

This is SwiftProtobuf generated code: the message model is translated to plain Kotlin classes, and the runtime encode/decode plumbing (SwiftProtobuf.Decoder / SwiftProtobuf.Visitor) has no counterpart in this port's stack, so those two methods keep their names but take Any parameters and are TODO().
UnknownStorage is represented as ByteArray, and equality uses contentEquals/contentHashCode.
Protobuf field presence is preserved exactly: nullable private backing field, computed property falling back to the proto default, a hasX property and a clearX() function.
The Swift enum init() (which selects .resultUnknown) cannot be an enum constructor in Kotlin, so it becomes the companion function defaultValue().
The bytecode-encoded _protobuf_nameMap is translated into an explicit Map of enum/proto name to field number, keeping the same property name.
static func == is expressed as equals()/hashCode() overrides since Kotlin has no static operator.
Sendable conformance has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped.
SwiftProtobuf.ProtobufAPIVersionCheck is kept as private marker interfaces plus a private object, since Kotlin has no nested typealias.
inout Int is modeled with kotlin.jvm.internal.Ref.IntRef; Emotes.createSegments is called positionally with that holder.
Swift's JSONSerialization-based decodeEvent is reimplemented with kotlinx.serialization Json.parseToJsonElement; the thrown String becomes IllegalStateException.
The shared Json instance sets ignoreUnknownKeys = true because Swift's JSONDecoder silently ignores unknown JSON keys.
URL(string:) validity checks are dropped: badge and emote URLs are plain Strings (ChatPostUrl(moving, still)).
logger.debug/info map to Log.d/Log.i with the tag "KickPusher".
@MainActor is dropped and the weak delegate is a plain nullable property; emotes callbacks are passed as function references.
getKickChannelInfo is invoked with a trailing lambda, assuming the ported API keeps its callback (non-suspend) signature.
All Decodable structs keep their snake_case JSON keys as Kotlin property names and are annotated @Serializable.
DispatchQueue is replaced by a CoroutineDispatcher constructor parameter plus an internal CoroutineScope; queue.async -> scope.launch and queue.asyncAfter -> scope.launch { delay(...) }.

AVFoundation types are mapped as follows: AVAudioFormat and CMFormatDescription -> android.media.MediaFormat, AVAudioCompressedBuffer -> ByteArray, CMTime -> Long microseconds, CMSampleBuffer -> MediaSample, so presentationTimeStamp.seconds becomes presentationTimeUs / 1_000_000.0.
MediaSample has no decode timestamp, so calcVideoCompositionTime returns 0 and the video sample path uses presentationTimeUs where the Swift code preferred decodeTimeStamp when it was valid.

Because AVAudioCompressedBuffer carries no AudioStreamBasicDescription, the audio codec is remembered in the new audioMime field set by audioEncoderOutputFormatInternal and checked with the literal "audio/opus".

The delegate overrides assume the port's AudioEncoderDelegate/VideoEncoderDelegate take (MediaFormat), (ByteArray, Long) and (VideoEncoder, MediaFormat)/(VideoEncoder, MediaSample, Long); adjust if the codec files chose other Android types.
RtmpConnection, RtmpChunk, RtmpChunkType, RtmpStreamInfo and RtmpStreamStats live in this same package, so they are used without imports; processorPipelineQueue is treated as a CoroutineScope.
SimpleTimer is built from the coroutine dispatcher and startSingleShot is called with a Double timeout in seconds (20.0), matching the Swift API.
info.bitrateStats.mutate { it.add(bytesTransferred = length) } is kept as-is, assuming RtmpStreamStats exposes the same mutate helper as the Swift version.
MessageKind entries are PascalCase (Null, One, Two, ...) because `null` is a reserved word in Kotlin; raw values are unchanged.

URLSessionWebSocketTask is replaced by an OkHttp WebSocket whose WebSocketListener pushes binary/text frames into an unlimited Channel, so the receive loop can simply await messages like Swift's `try await webSocket.receive()`.
The `webSocket` property is nullable because OkHttp starts connecting as soon as newWebSocket is called, unlike the dummy URLSessionWebSocketTask created in the Swift initializer.
Swift's String errors (`throw "Bad kind"`) become plain `Exception(message)` throws; the strict UTF-8 decoder keeps the 'Bad message not UTF-8' failure path intact.
`sleep(seconds: 5)` / `sleep(seconds: 60)` map to `sleep(5.0)` / `sleep(60.0)` imported from com.moblin.android.common.various.
Platform.Soop is assumed to live in com.moblin.android.various.model (the type is not in the provided glossary); adjust the import if the Android port names it differently.

`emotes.createSegments(text:id:)` is called as `createSegments(message, id)` assuming the signature `(String, Int): List<ChatPostSegment>` (the Swift `inout` counter is only mutated and never read afterwards).

The "chat" subprotocol of `webSocketTask(with:protocols:)` is sent through the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header, and the POST body's content type is set via toRequestBody("application/x-www-form-urlencoded").

Every Codable class becomes an @Serializable kotlinx.serialization class; Swift optional properties get a Kotlin default of null so they are omitted from JSON exactly like the synthesized encodeIfPresent, while non-optional properties stay constructor parameters without defaults and are always encoded (and required when decoding).

The Swift encoder used .sortedKeys plus .withoutEscapingSlashes; toString() re-sorts every JsonObject key alphabetically (kotlinx.serialization has no sortedKeys option) and kotlinx does not escape '/' by default, so the output matches.
Swift throws String values as errors; in Kotlin those become Exception(message) with the identical message text, since String can no longer implement Throwable.
UInt32 bitrate and UInt16 port are wire-format values and map to UInt/UShort as required by the unsigned-type rule.
MoblinSettingsRemoteControlServerRelay conformed to ObservableObject but declares no @Published property here, so it translates to a plain serializable class without StateFlow.

MoblinSettingsRemoteControl keeps the Swift declaration order (assistant, streamer, password), which means the non-default 'password' parameter follows defaulted ones; callers must use named arguments.
fromString decodes with ignoreUnknownKeys = true because Swift's JSONDecoder silently skips keys that are not part of the model, while kotlinx.serialization throws by default.
fromString/toString both throw SerializationException on malformed JSON, replacing Swift's EncodingError/DecodingError.
libdatachannel's C API has no Android/JNI binding, so RtcTrack and PeerConnection keep their exact signatures but every native call site is TODO().
whipQueue becomes a single-thread CoroutineDispatcher; whipQueue.async maps to whipScope.launch and whipQueue.sync maps to runBlocking(whipQueue).
WhipStreamDelegate.whipStreamPerform now takes an OkHttp Request/Response with a (ByteArray?, Response?, Throwable?) completion instead of URLRequest/URLResponse/Error.
The encoder-delegate overrides were written against ByteArray, MediaFormat and MediaSample with Long microsecond timestamps; align them with the audio/video codec packages.
AVAudioCompressedBuffer is reduced to a ByteArray and its packet descriptions are dropped, matching Android's one-access-unit-per-buffer codec output.
DataChannelConnectionState and DataChannelGatheringState only exist in the Swift DataChannel module, so they are declared here with a fromValue(rawInt) companion.
Enum entries for SettingsStreamCodec (H264AVC/H265HEVC), SettingsStreamAudioCodec (OPUS/AAC) and the MpegTsVideoConfigAvc/Hevc create(format) factory are inferred.
logger.info/debug are replaced with Log.i/Log.d using the tag WhipStream.
Swift `extension Model` becomes top-level extension functions on Model in the same package, keeping the original member names and order.

Kotlin has no retroactive protocol conformance: Model must declare `: BlackSharkCoolerDeviceDelegate` so that `delegate = this` compiles, and forward its two interface callbacks to these extension functions.
BlackSharkLib.CoolingState has no counterpart in the Android port, so blackSharkCoolerDeviceStatus receives phoneTemperature and heatsinkTemperature (Double) directly instead of the status object.
DispatchQueue.main.async becomes mainScope.launch using a file-private `CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main)`.
`device.bluetoothPeripheralId!` is translated to an early return on the nullable id (`?: return`) so it can be reused for the map key and the start call.
disableBlackSharkCoolerDevice keys the map by `device.id` exactly like the Swift source, not by bluetoothPeripheralId.
blackSharkCoolerDevices is expected to be a MutableMap<String, BlackSharkCoolerDevice> on Model, matching the Swift dictionary usage.

DockKit is Apple-only: every DockAccessory/DockAccessoryManager interaction (state observation, system tracking, orientation, animation, angular velocity, accessory events) is replaced by TODO("no Android counterpart for DockKit").
The Swift #if canImport(DockKit) / #else variants collapse into one Kotlin class whose public signatures match the stub branch; isConnected() still mirrors 'accessory != null'.
Spatial.Vector3D has no Android type, so a local data class Vector3D(x, y, z) is declared in this file; it is used only in gimbal signatures.
DockAccessory is kept untyped as Any? because its members do not exist in Kotlin; the private observer methods take Any for the same reason.
Fire-and-forget Task { } bodies become gimbalScope.launch { }, a private file-level CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) standing in for @MainActor + Task.
setOrientation/getCurrentOrientation are suspend functions; their '!tracking' guards and the nil result while tracking is enabled are preserved.

handleAccessoryEventCameraShutter/Flip/Zoom are fully translated against Model.database.gimbal, Model.handleControllerFunction and Model.setZoomX (Float conversions added because the Kotlin settings types are unknown).
Those camera event handlers stay unreachable until an Android gimbal backend feeds handleAccessoryEvent, which is itself a TODO.
apple_only: DockKit (DockAccessoryManager, DockAccessory, DockAccessory.StateChange, DockAccessory.AccessoryEvent, DockAccessory.Animation): no Android counterpart, replaced with TODO

notes: ChatDescription and SponsorshipsHeaderRenderer gained the authorExternalChannelId field, placed right after authorName with a null default like the other optional fields.
handleChatDescription now passes chatDescription.authorExternalChannelId as userId instead of null.

The Swift diff's fourth hunk (userId in handleGiftPurchaseDescription) has no matching Kotlin line: this file's handleGiftPurchaseDescription body is a hand-written Android deviation that ends before the model.appendChatMessage call, so it was left byte-identical.
All other declarations, imports and formatting are unchanged from the previous Kotlin file.

Hand-written Codable encode(to:)/init(from:) with CodingKeys is translated to @Serializable classes with @SerialName per key; every property keeps the same default the Swift decoder used for a missing key.

@Published / ObservableObject is not mapped to MutableStateFlow here because these model objects are persisted with kotlinx.serialization (StateFlow fields cannot be serialized); the properties stay plain mutable vars and are observed by the Compose settings layer.
UInt32 bitrate is mapped to Int and Int32 to Int since no wire-format/byte-parsing code is involved.

kotlinx.serialization has no built-in serializer for java.util.UUID, so a top-level UuidSerializer (KSerializer<UUID>, encoded as a string exactly like Swift's Codable UUID) was added and applied to every id property.
DeepLinkCreatorStreamAudio.bitrateFloat is not encoded in Swift and was derived from bitrate in init(from:), so it is a @Transient computed property here.
DeepLinkCreatorStream.baseName is a static let, translated to a companion object property built with localized("My stream").
[T] arrays are MutableList because the settings objects are mutated; .init() becomes ClassName().
Identifiable has no Kotlin counterpart; the id property is kept and the class only declares the Named interface (from com.moblin.android.various.utils).
The Swift diff only adds `colorRange: .full` to three `Processor(...)` initialisations.

The Kotlin `Processor` declared for this port takes a single `delegate` parameter and exposes no `colorRange`, and no Kotlin color-range type exists in the platform glossary, so the three `Processor(delegate = modelMock)` calls stay unchanged rather than inventing a parameter.
Everything else in the file is untouched and kept byte-identical.
The custom `RtmpServerMock` (ServerSocket based) still stands in for the Swift NWListener actor.
ModelMock keeps the RtmpStreamDelegate and ProcessorDelegate overrides as before.
readMessages/readMessage helpers, byte literals and toBigEndianBytes/joinBytes extensions are unchanged.
runBlocking is still used inside the two connection tests, as in the current port.
No new imports were required by the Swift change.

Kotlin extensions cannot add interface conformance, so the GoProDeviceDelegate implementation of Model is emitted as a top-level extension function; Model must declare GoProDeviceDelegate in its own file and this function is the body used for it.
IndexSet is replaced by Set<Int>; the settings list is trimmed in descending index order so the remaining indices stay valid.
Swift switch expressions over RtmpUrlType and GoProDeviceState become Kotlin when expressions with uppercase enum entries (SERVER/CUSTOM, CONNECTING/STREAMING/WIFI_SETUP_FAILED/FAILED).
String(localized:) becomes the top-level localized() from package com.moblin.android.
The weak self/weak device captures of the Swift closures are dropped; the lambdas run on the calling coroutine scope and capture the extension receiver directly.
autoRestartStreamTimer is expected to expose startSingleShot(timeout: Double, onFire: () -> Unit) and stop(), matching the Swift timer wrapper.
NetworkInterfaceType, IpType and IpType.formatAddress are assumed to live in com.moblin.android.various.model, hence no import is written for them.
Model members used but not declared here (goProDevices, database, getRtmpStream, makeToast, makeErrorToast) must already exist on Model.
iOS 18 availability guards are dropped; the Gimbal APIs are assumed always available in the Android port.
Apple's Spatial framework has no Android counterpart, so a local Vector3D data class is declared in this file; verify it matches the port's Gimbal.setMovement/setOrientation parameter types.
Task { } and DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter use a file-private mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main); the 0.3s deadline becomes delay(300) and defer becomes try/finally.
Deque.popFirst()/append() map to MutableList.removeFirstOrNull()/add() on Model.moveToGimbalPresetQueue.
String(localized:) maps to the top-level localized() function from package com.moblin.android.
error.localizedDescription maps to Throwable.message.
setQuickButton uses SettingsQuickButtonType.gimbalTracking, inferred from the Swift `.gimbalTracking` case; confirm that enum exists in com.moblin.android.various.settings.
makeErrorToast, setZoomX, setQuickButton and remoteControlStateChanged are Model members declared in other files and are called with the same argument labels as in Swift.
Model extension members became top-level extension functions on Model in the same package; cleanWizardUrl, createStreamFromWizardCustomUrl and createStreamFromWizardUrl remain file-private helpers.
WizardPlatform, WizardNetworkSetup and WizardCustomProtocol are Kotlin enum classes that keep the Swift case names and order.
URLComponents is replaced with java.net.URI and URLEncoder; validity of the parsed URL is expressed with runCatching(...).getOrNull().
Faithful to the Swift optional chaining: the SRT streamid is only set when the URL already contains a query string, so a URL without '?' is returned unchanged.
String(localized:) maps to localized() imported from com.moblin.android.
SettingsStream(name = ...) as well as the named arguments of makeErrorToast, setCurrentStream, sceneUpdated and the keychain helpers assume the ported signatures keep the Swift argument labels.
database.streams.add(stream) replaces Swift Array.append.
DefaultTcpPorts.mobcamStream from com.moblin.android.various.network is used to build the mobcam URL.
Swift `extension Model` members become top-level extension functions on Model in com.moblin.android.various.model; the private helpers stay `private` so they are only visible inside this file.

Swift `extension Model: DjiDeviceDelegate` cannot add interface conformance in Kotlin, so `djiDeviceStreamingState` is emitted as a top-level extension function; Model itself must declare `DjiDeviceDelegate` and the matching override in its own file for `djiDevice.delegate = this` to compile and for callbacks to arrive.
The `[weak self, weak device]` timer closures are plain Kotlin captures; on Android the ViewModel/Model lifetime is handled by the owning CoroutineScope, so no WeakReference is used.

`statusOther.ipStatuses` filtering compares `interfaceType`/`ipType` with their `.name` strings ("wifi"/"ipv4") because those enum types are not declared in this file's glossary and cannot be imported.
`device.autoRestartStreamTimer` is assumed to expose `startSingleShot(timeout) { }` and `stop()`; that timer type is declared with SettingsDjiDevice in com.moblin.android.various.settings.
Swift `IndexSet` offsets become `Set<Int>` and the removal is done over descending indices so that `removeAt` positions stay valid, mirroring SwiftUI's `remove(atOffsets:)`.
The `switch` over `rtmpUrlType` becomes an exhaustive `when`; the `switch` over `DjiDeviceState` keeps an `else -> {}` branch for the remaining states.
`String(localized:)` maps to the top-level `localized()` from com.moblin.android, which is imported explicitly.
Generated SwiftProtobuf file: every Swift enum became an enum class with rawValue plus a companion fromRawValue; the message structs became mutable Kotlin classes.
Swift's computed storage/`has...`/`clear...` triplets (protobuf field presence) are kept verbatim as backing nullable fields `_x`, a property with default, a `hasX` Boolean and a `clearX()` function.
`SwiftProtobuf._NameMap(bytecode:)` was decoded by hand into a plain `Map<Int, String>` (`protoMessageName` / `_protobuf_nameMap`) since the runtime no longer exists.
`SwiftProtobuf.UnknownStorage` has no Android counterpart; `unknownFields` is represented as a `ByteArray` (empty by default) and compared with contentEquals.
`decodeMessage(decoder:)` and `traverse(visitor:)` need the SwiftProtobuf runtime (Decoder/Visitor) and are stubbed with TODO; they are the only unsupported items in this file.
The Swift `fileprivate struct _GeneratedWithProtocGenSwiftVersion` version probe is kept as a private class with nested `_2`; Kotlin cannot declare a `Version` typealias inside a class.
`SwiftProtobuf.Internal.areAllInitialized(self.entries)` became `entries.all { it.isInitialized }`.
Only `==` is written in Swift; `equals`/`hashCode` were added (with a private `byteArraysEqual` helper) so the Kotlin classes behave as value objects.
Inserted Model.banYouTubeUser between updateYouTubeStream and getYouTubeAccesssToken, matching the Swift diff position.
Used stream.value, NetworkResponse.Success and localized(...) exactly like the rest of the Kotlin port.
compactMap(\.liveStreamingDetails.activeLiveChatId) became mapNotNull { it.liveStreamingDetails.activeLiveChatId }.
The shared remaining/failed counters are captured by the insertLiveChatBan completions like the Swift closure captures.
No other line of the existing file was changed.
Async Swift tests become @Test fun ... = runBlocking<Unit> { ... }; if ObsWebSocket marshals work onto Dispatchers.Main this source set also needs Dispatchers.setMain.
CompletionResult is a private sealed shim replacing Swift's Result<Value, String> so the failure value stays a String message.

Mock/helper members are called with the names and labels of the Swift originals: receiveRequest, receiveRequestBatch, respond(request, data=/errorCode=/comment=/results=), sendEvent(type=, intent=, data=), send(text=/op=), ObsMockResult.Success/Failure, ObsMockRequest(type=, id=, data=), ObsMockRequestBatch(id=, requests=).
ObsWebSocket's async initializer is invoked as the constructor ObsWebSocket(url, password, delegate) and ObsWebSocketServerMock(password).

getMediaSourcesSettingsBatch is assumed to deliver settings objects exposing input/isLocalFile, which are mapped to Pair<String, Boolean> for the completion; if the ported callback already yields Pair the map collapses to a pass-through.
areEqual is assumed to take List<Float> values and a Float epsilon.
For Completion<Unit> the onSuccess() extension is invoked from a lambda because completion::onSuccess would be ambiguous with the member function.
assertContentEquals is used for the ByteArray screenshot comparison instead of assertEquals.
Only one line changed: toggleCameraPreview now calls attachCamera() instead of reattachCamera().
Everything else in the file is byte-identical to the previous translation.
Swift's POSIX getaddrinfo/addrinfo/getnameinfo block is replaced with java.net.InetAddress.getAllByName, which is the supported Android resolver path.

DnsLookupFamily keeps its Swift lowercase case name and order; toCFamily() maps to android.system.OsConstants AF_INET/AF_INET6/AF_UNSPEC and is retained for API parity although the lookup itself filters with Inet4Address/Inet6Address.
The Swift 'unspec' family matched every returned address; the Kotlin translation keeps that behaviour by not filtering in that branch.
The returned value is the first matching hostAddress string, matching Swift's addresses.first, or null when the lookup fails or yields no matching family.
Logger calls map to android.util.Log.i with the file-level tag "DnsLookup".
Swift's import Network is unnecessary on Android and is dropped; no Network.framework API from this file survives the port.
CryptoKit Insecure.MD5 is replaced by java.security.MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5") over the UTF-8 bytes.
Swift Data maps to ByteArray; String.utf8Data is replaced by Kotlin's stdlib String.encodeToByteArray().
Data.base64EncodedString(options: .lineLength64Characters) maps to java.util.Base64.getMimeEncoder(64, LF), which is available from Android API 26.
The three Swift overloads become three Kotlin top-level functions with the same names and order; the String/ByteArray overloads stay unambiguous.
The java.util.Base64 MIME encoder pads with '=' and wraps at 64 characters, matching the Swift line-length option; callers that need an unwrapped token should strip the line breaks.
No Moblin-internal extension (utf8Data) is imported or redeclared, so this file has no dependency on other Moblin files.
MD5 is cryptographically broken but is kept unchanged because the HaishinKit protocol path depends on those exact digests.
No permission handling is needed for digest calculation.

CBytePerfMon is a libsrt C struct with no Kotlin binding in this port, so a mirror data class named CBytePerfMon is declared in this file with the same field names and C types (int32_t -> Int, double -> Double); SrtNative is expected to populate it.
The Swift memberwise init is the Kotlin primary constructor; the init(mon:) becomes a secondary constructor so both call shapes stay identical.
static let zero maps to val zero in the companion object.
Int32 in Swift maps to Int in Kotlin; Double stays Double.
The Swift mon.pktRecvNAKTotal is exposed as pktRecvNakTotal to match the existing Swift property spelling.
No native (JNI) symbols are called in this file, so no System.loadLibrary call is needed here.
Kotlin data class equality, hashCode and toString are generated, which the Swift struct got for free.
Moblin keeps these counters as plain values, so no state flow or observable wrapper is required.

NEHotspotNetwork.fetchCurrent comes from the NetworkExtension shim (platform/networkextension/NEHotspotNetwork.kt): WifiInfo from the ConnectivityManager transport info on Android 12 and later, WifiManager before that, and null without WiFi or location permission, like iOS.
fetchCurrentWiFiSsid keeps the same callback shape: a top-level function taking (String?) -> Unit, so callers do not change.
DispatchQueue.main.async becomes mainScope.launch on a private file-level CoroutineScope on Dispatchers.Main.
The macCatalyst CoreWLAN dynamic-lookup helper is preserved as a private function of the same name returning null.
No types are declared by this file, only top-level functions, so declared_types is empty.
BluetoothScanner is an ObservableObject but not a settings class, so @Published discoveredPeripherals became MutableStateFlow<List<CBPeripheral>>; views collect it with collectAsState().
The Swift class is non-final, so it is declared open class with open val discoveredPeripherals and open funs.
private var centralManager uses CBCentralManager.holder(), so assigning null releases the manager and closes its connections exactly like ARC.
The Swift extension that conforms to CBCentralManagerDelegate is folded into the class header, and the delegate methods use override because the shim interface provides default bodies.
CBCentralManager(delegate: self, queue: .main) maps to CBCentralManager(delegate = this, queue = null): the main queue is the default.
discoveredPeripherals.append(peripheral) becomes a value assignment on the flow (value = value + peripheral), and the duplicate check reads .value.
The delegate methods are declared with all four parameter names even though the Swift code ignores advertisementData and rssi.
CMMotionManager, CMAccelerometerData and OperationQueue.main come from the CoreMotion shim (platform/coremotion/CoreMotion.kt), so the constructor keeps the Swift parameter motionManager.
startAccelerometerUpdates(to: .main) becomes startAccelerometerUpdates(to = OperationQueue.main); the handler runs on the main thread, paced to the 0.1 s accelerometerUpdateInterval.
data.acceleration is a CMAcceleration in g on iOS axes with gravity included, so the magnitude is about 1 at rest, as on iOS.
guard let data, error == nil else { return } becomes an early return@startAccelerometerUpdates.
GForce is a @Serializable data class; its property names match the Swift coding keys exactly, so no @SerialName is needed.
getLatest() keeps the Swift optional return type GForce? even though the Swift implementation always returns a value.
NSObject is dropped; ObservableObject with @Published array becomes MutableStateFlow<List<GoProDiscoveredDevice>> per the scanner rule, so readers use discoveredDevices.collectAsState().
centralManager is a stored optional CBCentralManager backed by CBCentralManager.holder(); assigning null releases it like ARC (scan stops, no more delegate calls).
The Swift extension conformance is merged into the class header, so both delegate methods are override fun of CBCentralManagerDelegate.
CBCentralManager(delegate:self, queue:.main) uses queue = null because .main, DispatchQueue.main and nil all map to the main queue in the shim.

goProControlServiceId is not declared in this file: it is expected as a top-level CBUUID val in package com.moblin.android.integrations.gopro (GoProDevice.kt); no import is needed since it is the same package.
String(localized: "Unknown") becomes localized("Unknown") from com.moblin.android.
discoveredDevices.append(.init(...)) becomes a value reassignment with a new list plus a GoProDiscoveredDevice, and the duplicate check uses any { it.peripheral.identifier == peripheral.identifier }.
The whole class stays main-actor-less: the shim delivers every central delegate call on the queue given to the manager (here the main queue), in order.
NWPathMonitor is replaced with ConnectivityManager.registerDefaultNetworkCallback, so a Context parameter was added to the constructor because Android needs it.
NWInterface.InterfaceType has no Android counterpart and is replaced by a local InterfaceType enum keeping the same case names (cellular, wifi, wiredEthernet, other).
The DispatchQueue queue parameter is kept as a CoroutineDispatcher to preserve the public API shape but is not used by the Android connectivity callback.
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin equivalent and was dropped.
Collections.Deque is replaced with kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque.
pathUpdateHandler is mapped to onCapabilitiesChanged; since only the default network is observed, .other is used when the network exposes none of the wifi/cellular/ethernet transports.
The `if self.cellular` guard is expressed as `this@NetworkInterfaceTypeSelector.cellular` inside the anonymous NetworkCallback.
The registration is never unregistered because the Swift file exposes no cancel path; the owner must call unregisterNetworkCallback if needed.

`@Published var discoveredPeripherals` became `open val discoveredPeripherals = MutableStateFlow<List<CBPeripheral>>(emptyList())`, read with collectAsState and mutated with `.value = ...` so it stays observable.
The `CBCentralManagerDelegate` extension was folded into the class header with `override fun`s, as the shim's delegate methods use those names.
`.main` as the central manager queue maps to `queue = null` (the shim then delivers callbacks on the main thread).
`centralManager` is held with `by CBCentralManager.holder()` so assigning null releases the old manager like ARC, closing its scan.
`localName.wholeMatch(of: /S[0-9a-f]{16}C/)` is `Regex("S[0-9a-f]{16}C").matches(localName)`, an entire-string match.
`discoveredPeripherals.contains(where:)` uses the shim's `==` on `CBPeripheral`, which compares identifiers; appending rebuilds the list (`+ peripheral`) because a StateFlow holds an immutable list.
`static let shared` became `companion object { val shared by lazy { ... } }`, read as `TeslaVehicleScanner.shared`.

CoreBluetooth ids stay CBUUID, as required for BLE device protocol files: workoutDeviceHeartRateServiceId and workoutDeviceHeartRateMeasurementCharacteristicId are top-level vals built with CBUUID(string = ...).
HeartRateMeasurement keeps its Swift shape as a file-private class with a secondary constructor taking the value bytes, since a data class cannot hold the parsing init.
Swift throws/try disappear: ByteReader's readUInt8/readUInt16Le are non-throwing in Kotlin, so handleMeasurement is a plain function and the init needs no try.
UShort is used for the 16-bit heart-rate field because this is BLE wire parsing; Int(measurement.heartRate) becomes measurement.heartRate.toInt().
UInt16(reader.readUInt8()) is a widening conversion, written readUInt8().toUShort().
flags.isBitSet(index:) comes from com.moblin.android.common.various and takes the UByte flags of the measurement byte.
Data parameters become ByteArray and the class is open because the Swift class is non-final, so its members are open too.
The private top-level format-index constant stays private in this file.

Swift's throwing `init(value:)` on the file-private struct becomes the companion factory `CyclingSpeedCadenceMeasurement.parse(value)`; ByteReader throws naturally, so Kotlin needs no `throws` clause.
The 32-bit wheel-revolution delta is widened to Long so the `+ 4294967296` wraparound cannot overflow Kotlin's Int.
`flags.isBitSet(index:)` comes from com.moblin.android.common.various and is imported explicitly.
`ContinuousClock.now` and `ContinuousClock.Instant` come from com.moblin.android.platform.core; the 3-second guard uses `3.seconds` from kotlin.time.
UInt/UShort values are value-preserving converted with `toLong()`/`toInt()` and never reinterpreted as bytes.
`measurementCharacteristic` is stored but only tested by `isAnyCharacteristicDiscovered()`, exactly as in Swift.
The class stays `open` with `open` members because the Swift class is not final; all stored state stays `private`.
Average calculator and crank cadence come from the same Kotlin package, so no imports are needed for them.
ByteReader's Kotlin methods do not throw, so the Swift `throws` on RscMeasurement's init and on handleMeasurement is dropped; callers that wrap the call in try still compile.
The throwing Swift init of RscMeasurement became `RscMeasurement.create(value)` on a private data class, because a Kotlin constructor cannot parse with several statements.
`flags.isBitSet(index:)` is the extension from com.moblin.android.common.various, imported and called with the named argument as on the shim contract.
`lastRscUpdateTime.duration(to: now).seconds` becomes `duration(to = now).toDouble(DurationUnit.SECONDS)` from com.moblin.android.platform.core.ContinuousClock.
WorkoutDeviceRunningMetrics is a synthesized-Codable struct, so it is an @Serializable data class with the Swift property names and null defaults so absent JSON keys decode like Swift.
WorkoutDeviceRunning is a non-final Swift class, so it becomes an open class with open members and private backing properties.
The two CoreBluetooth UUID constants are top-level vals built with CBUUID(string = "..."), matching the shim constructor.
The two flag indices stay file-private constants with their Swift names.
A Context is now a constructor parameter because ConnectivityManager cannot be obtained without one; pass the application context.
NWPathMonitor is replaced by ConnectivityManager.registerDefaultNetworkCallback with a main-Looper Handler, so callbacks arrive on the main thread like the Swift @MainActor code.
NWInterface.InterfaceType became the local InterfaceType enum, mapped from NetworkCapabilities transports (wifi/cellular/ethernet, otherwise other).
The ifaddrs walk is replaced by ConnectivityManager.allNetworks for the interface list and java.net.NetworkInterface.getByName(name).inetAddresses for the addresses.
IPv6 scope suffixes such as %wlan0 are stripped from hostAddress before the address is reported.
start() needs ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE on the manifest; the permission request stays in the Activity layer.
Swift's init only installed monitor.pathUpdateHandler; that handler is now the NetworkCallback overrides, so init just builds the callback object.
Swift URL is stored only, so pushUrl/stopUrl are plain String fields built from baseUrl and pushKey.
The failable init? becomes a regular primary constructor because there is no URL parsing failure path once URL is a String; call sites get a non-null RealtimeIrl.
CLLocation maps to android.location.Location: coordinate.latitude/longitude -> latitude/longitude, speed -> speed, altitude -> altitude, timestamp.timeIntervalSince1970 -> location.time / 1000.0.
The POST body is built as a plain JSON string like the Swift version; content type application/json is set via OkHttp MediaType.
httpRequest is expected to take an okhttp3.Request; the JSON body is sent with toRequestBody().
stop() sends an empty POST body because OkHttp rejects a POST with a null body.
Location permission requests are left to the Activity layer.
Network.framework NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket; reads happen on a Dispatchers.IO coroutine and writes are fire-and-forget coroutines, matching .idempotent send semantics.
ContinuousClock.Instant is represented as monotonic Long nanoseconds from System.nanoTime(); isActive compares the delta against removeTimeoutNanos.
The Swift connection.batch / receiveMessage batch-of-100 pattern becomes a single blocking InputStream.read loop; connectionReceiveBatchSize is kept but unused.
A private ByteArray.setUInt32Be extension is added locally because the common package only guarantees createSrtlaPacket, srtControlTypeSize and the packet parsers.
logger.info/debug map to Log.i/Log.d with tag SrtlaServerClientConnection.
SrtlaServerClientConnectionDelegate protocol becomes a Kotlin interface; AckPacket struct becomes a mutable class.
isSrtDataPacket, getSrtControlPacketType and getSrtSequenceNumber from the common package are used as ByteArray member extensions.
connection.cancel() maps to Socket.close(); stop() also cancels the receive coroutine.
Swift's `nonisolated(unsafe) let ... = CBUUID(string:)` globals become top-level vals calling the CBUUID shim with `string =`.

The private PowerMeasurement/PowerVector structs keep their throwing `init(value:)` as a Kotlin class whose `init` block parses through ByteReader; call sites stay `PowerMeasurement(value)` / `PowerVector(value)`.
`try` disappears: ByteReader's reads throw on their own, so the parsing code is a plain sequence of calls.
UInt8 flags use ByteReader.readUInt8() -> UByte; the direction mask is a private UByte val because a UByte literal cannot be a `const val`, and the shift goes through toInt() since UByte has no shr.
The private raw-value enum gets a `rawValue` property and a companion `fromRawValue` returning null for unknown values, matching the Swift failable `init?(rawValue:)`.
`isBitSet(index:)` comes from com.moblin.android.common.various; WorkoutDeviceAverageCalculator/WorkoutDeviceCrankCadence are in this same package so they need no import.
Crank data is read with readUInt16Le (little-endian) exactly as in Swift, and the tuple result of handleMeasurement becomes Pair<Int, Int?>.
`now: .now` becomes ContinuousClock.now from com.moblin.android.platform.core.
CoreLocation maps to android.location: CLLocation -> Location, CLPlacemark -> Address, CLGeocoder -> android.location.Geocoder.
The class gains a Context constructor parameter because Geocoder needs one; every other member keeps its Swift name and signature.
@MainActor becomes a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main), and Task<Void, any Error> becomes kotlinx.coroutines.Job; the geocoding call is moved to Dispatchers.IO via withContext.
Task.isCancelled becomes isActive of the launch scope, so the polling loop still exits after cancellation.
sleep(seconds:) is assumed to be the suspend function sleep(seconds: Int) from com.moblin.android.common.various; the delay variable stays an Int number of seconds.
The do/catch around the sleep and geocode becomes runCatching { ... } so a failed lookup keeps the loop alive, exactly like the Swift catch.
Geocoder.getFromLocation is blocking, so it must not run on the main dispatcher.
Location.distanceTo returns Float while Swift returned CLLocationDistance (Double); the 1001/1000 literal fallback and threshold stay the same numbers.
The Swift `extension Model: CBCentralManagerDelegate` becomes a top-level extension function `fun Model.centralManagerDidUpdateState` in this package, since Model itself is declared in Model.kt.
`Model.bluetoothAllowed` is a `MutableStateFlow<Boolean>`, so the assignment writes `bluetoothAllowed.value = ...`.
`CBCentralManager.authorization == .allowedAlways` maps to `CBManagerAuthorization.allowedAlways` from the CoreBluetooth shim.
The `@MainActor` attribute is dropped; when a CBCentralManager is created it is given `delegate = { model.centralManagerDidUpdateState(it) }` and its queue, and that queue defines the thread.
`let bluetoothNotAllowedMessage` is a global String constant and becomes a top-level `const val`.
The unused `_: CBCentralManager` parameter is named `central` in Kotlin.
CLLocation maps to android.location.Location, the same type the WeatherService shim accepts.
The Swift Task<Void, any Error>? loop becomes a Job launched from a main-dispatched CoroutineScope; Task.isCancelled is checked with the coroutine scope's isActive.
try await sleep(seconds: delay) is sleepSeconds(seconds = delay) from com.moblin.android.common.various.
weatherService.weather(for: location) is called with the backticked keyword parameter `for` exactly as the shim declares.
logger.debug is android.util.Log.d with "WeatherManager" as the tag.
The non-final Swift class keeps open members so subclasses can override, matching Swift.
The private stored properties stay private, so they are never marked open.

NetServiceBrowser and NetService are replaced by android.net.nsd NsdManager discovery and resolve listeners; the class now implements NsdManager.DiscoveryListener and NsdManager.ResolveListener instead of the two NetService delegate protocols.
MoblinkScanner now takes a Context as its first constructor parameter, needed to obtain NsdManager via Context.NSD_SERVICE.
moblinkBonjourDomain is unused: android.net.nsd has no domain parameter, discovery always runs in the local domain.
resolve(withTimeout: 5.0) has no counterpart; NsdManager has no resolve timeout and failures arrive in onResolveFailed, which stays empty like the Swift file's missing didNotResolve.
service.addresses is reduced to NsdServiceInfo.host, so at most one websocket url is appended per resolved service.
Discovered services are matched by serviceName because NsdServiceInfo equality is not reliable across API levels.

@MainActor is dropped; the delegate is notified from a mainScope coroutine on Dispatchers.Main. The weak delegate reference cannot be expressed in Kotlin, so it is stored strongly in a nullable property.
NsdManager allows only one outstanding resolve per listener; onServiceFound resolves directly with this listener, so overlapping resolves can report onResolveFailed.

libsrt is reached through an `internal object SrtNative` declared in this file: it loads libsrt in its init block and exposes `external fun srt_setsockopt` with the same name and argument order as the C API. Keep a single SrtNative per package and extend it with the other srt_* calls as later files need them.

SRT_SOCKOPT and SRT_TRANSTYPE numbers come from the libsrt C header and are declared here as file-private const vals (srt.h 1.5 numbering); verify them against the libsrt fork bundled in the NDK build, SRTO_SRTLAPATCHES in particular.
snddropdelay keeps the raw option number 32 of the Swift source, exposed as the named constant SRTO_SNDDROPDELAY.

URL/URLComponents/removingPercentEncoding are replaced by android.net.Uri.queryParameterNames + getQueryParameter, which already percent-decodes values; getQueryItems therefore takes a String, not a URI.
Enum entry names stay lowercase exactly as in Swift so that rawValue (the query-string key, e.g. "srtlaPatches") is byte-identical.
MemoryLayout.size(ofValue:) is reproduced with fixed widths: Int -> 4 bytes, Int64 -> 8 bytes, written in native byte order (Android is little-endian).
The Swift enumeration branch sized its buffer from the String value (16 bytes) instead of the SRT_TRANSTYPE; the Kotlin version writes the intended 4-byte Int32 value.
logger.info(...) becomes Log.i with the class name as tag.
observableObject without settings semantics: discoveredDevices is a MutableStateFlow<List<DjiDiscoveredDevice>>, mutated through .value as the BLE shim section requires
centralManager is stored with the CBCentralManager.holder() property delegate so assigning null releases the old manager like ARC
DjiDeviceScanner now implements CBCentralManagerDelegate in its class header because Swift's delegate extension moves into the type
NSObject and ObservableObject have no Kotlin counterpart and are dropped; no other supertype is needed
CBCentralManager(delegate: self, queue: DispatchQueue.main) becomes CBCentralManager(delegate = this, queue = null), since .main maps to a null queue
logger.info is translated to android.util.Log.i with the class name as tag
the backslash-joined Swift multi-line log string is a single line here, with manufacturerData.hexString() from com.moblin.android.common.various
the struct DjiDiscoveredDevice becomes a data class with the same property names and order
Model, StatusTopRight, LocationManager and the settings/database types are assumed to live in com.moblin.android.various.model, so only RealtimeIrl and the Android/JDK types are imported.

CLLocation maps to android.location.Location: coordinate.latitude/longitude -> latitude/longitude, horizontalAccuracy -> accuracy, verticalAccuracy -> verticalAccuracyMeters, distance(from:) -> distanceTo() widened to Double.
The privacy-region loop assumes the region type exposes contains(latitude: Double, longitude: Double); the Swift version took a CLLocationCoordinate2D.
statusTopRight.location = location assumes StatusTopRight exposes a mutable location property (class with var), not an immutable data class.
ContinuousClock.Instant is replaced by monotonic Long nanoseconds from System.nanoTime(), so updateAverageSpeed takes now: Long and resetAverageSpeed stores System.nanoTime().
getLatestKnownLocation() returns Pair<Double, Double>? because Swift returns an optional tuple.
The Moblin LocationManager wrapper is used with the same call shape (status/stop/start/getLatestKnownLocation); the onUpdate callback is passed as a Kotlin lambda.
Location permission requests are left to the Activity layer; this file only starts/stops updates.

Kotlin cannot add protocol conformance from an extension, so Model's HttpProxyServerDelegate conformance is kept as the extension function httpProxyServerPortReady plus an anonymous adapter object assigned to HttpProxyServer.delegate.
NWEndpoint.hostPort is represented as java.net.InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", port) and NWEndpoint.Port as Int, so getHttpProxyServerEndpoint returns InetSocketAddress?.
Model must already declare httpProxyServer: HttpProxyServer?, httpProxyPort: Int? and database whose httpProxy exposes enabled, localNetwork and port.
setWebBrowserProxy() and setBrowserEffectsProxyServer() are resolved as Model members or extension functions in com.moblin.android.various.model.
DispatchQueue.main.async is replaced by a file-private mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) plus launch.
All functions are top-level extension functions on Model in this package, matching the Swift extension.
Network.framework NWConnection/NWListener are replaced by java.net.Socket / java.net.DatagramSocket running in coroutines on Dispatchers.IO; NWEndpoint host+port become String + Int.
The `weak var delegate` becomes a plain strong `var delegate` because Kotlin has no weak properties.
The original callback-driven receive chain is rebuilt as coroutine while-loops so a long stream does not grow the JVM stack.
Reading exactly N bytes is done with a loop over InputStream.read since Kotlin has no minimumIncompleteLength/maximumLength receive API.
stop() closes the sockets (to unblock the blocking reads) and then cancels the CoroutineScope.
ByteWriter (com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util) is assumed to expose writeUInt8(UByte), writeUInt16(UShort), writeBytes(ByteArray) and the `data` property.
logger.debug/info map to Log.d/Log.i with the tag "RtspTransport".
rtspTransportDisconnected() is never invoked because the Swift transport never calls it either.

The file-private serial DispatchQueue becomes a single-thread CoroutineScope(Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor().asCoroutineDispatcher()); start/stop/setWheelCircumference keep hopping onto it with launch.
centralManager is stored through CBCentralManager.holder() so assigning null releases the previous manager and its connections exactly like ARC.
delegate stays a plain nullable var (Swift weak); no WeakReference is used.
The @MainActor global workoutDeviceScanner becomes a top-level val constructed from the four service ids.
WorkoutDevice implements CBCentralManagerDelegate (fun interface) and CBPeripheralDelegate in the class header; only the delegate methods the Swift file uses are overridden.
In peripheralDidDiscoverCharacteristicsFor the CBPeripheral parameter is named peripheralArg because the body uses the stored peripheral property.
Swift's try around the delegate calls is dropped (the Kotlin delegate methods and handleMeasurement do not throw); the do/catch around characteristic handling stays as try/catch.
logger.debug/info become Log.d/Log.i with tag "WorkoutDevice"; CBUUID interpolation uses uuidString.
Network.framework NWConnection/NWListener are replaced with java.net.Socket/ServerSocket on Dispatchers.IO; the callback-driven receive loops became blocking read loops inside coroutines.
NWEndpoint is replaced by a host String plus a port Int, so HttpConnectRequestParser.Result carries destinationHost/destinationPort instead of an NWEndpoint.

The file-level serial DispatchQueue is a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO); Swift's serial execution guarantee is lost, so the shared `connections` list and `stopping` flag would need extra synchronization in production.
logger.info calls become android.util.Log.i with tag "HttpProxyServer".
HttpParser.getLine is assumed to return Pair<String, Int>? and HttpParser.data a ByteArray; both live in this same package so nothing is imported.
NWInterface/NWInterface.InterfaceType map to android.net.Network: NetworkInterfaceTypeSelector.getType() returns Network? and markBad takes it.
NWListener state updates are collapsed into handleStateUpdate(error: Exception?), where null means the ready state and a non-null value the failed state.
The body byte range is stored before connectToDestination runs (Swift sets it after the async connect) so the tunneling socket can flush it.
URLRequest is translated as okhttp3.Request: request.url/host/scheme/method are non-null, url.port is always the effective port, and url.path()/query become url.encodedPath/encodedQuery.
The URLSession uploadTask fallback is replaced by the project's OkHttp-based httpRequest helper with the body attached through RequestBody.toRequestBody(), so no URLSession shim is used.
MainActor.assumeIsolated is dropped: InterfaceTypeHttpClient runs its callbacks on Dispatchers.Main (the queue passed to NWConnection.start) and on MainTimer.
Data becomes ByteArray; Swift's Data.advanced(by:) is written as copyOfRange, which rebases indices to 0 exactly as the Swift code assumes when it re-adds offset.
String(bytes:encoding:.utf8) is failable in Swift, so decodeUtf8Strict decodes with a CharsetDecoder set to REPORT, returns null on malformed UTF-8 and strips a leading BOM.
Int(String) is strict in Swift, so parseIntStrict validates [+-]?[0-9]+ before toIntOrNull; Swift's split omits empty subsequences, so every split here is split(" ").filter { it.isNotEmpty() }.
The Swift tuple returned by createRequest becomes the private data class InterfaceTypeHttpClient.CreatedRequest, destructured at the call site.
NWEndpoint is imported from com.moblin.android.platform.network; that explicit import shadows the unrelated same-package NWEndpoint declared in NetworkUtils.kt for this file only.
Global `logger` becomes android.util.Log with tag "ObsWebSocket"; `logger.debugEnabled` maps to Log.isLoggable(TAG, Log.DEBUG).

The untyped JSON envelope (op/d/eventType/...) is parsed with org.json (the Android counterpart of JSONSerialization); typed payloads use kotlinx.serialization with ignoreUnknownKeys = true so unknown keys are skipped like Swift's JSONDecoder.
Swift's `throw "some string"` became IllegalStateException("..."), and `try?` became runCatching { ... }.getOrNull(); `try { } catch {}` became runCatching { }.onSuccess { }.
`weak let delegate` has no Kotlin equivalent: delegate is a strongly referenced constructor property, so the caller must drop the ObsWebSocket instance to break the cycle.
