@MainActor is emulated with a private mainScope (CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main)) used only inside the WebSocketClientDelegate callbacks; all public methods must be called from the main dispatcher as before.
The UInt64 event-subscription bitmask is kept as ULong (wire format) and serialized by kotlinx.serialization's built-in unsigned serializer.

Assumed WebSocketClient API (from com.moblin.android.various.network): constructor WebSocketClient(url: String, loopback: Boolean), var delegate: WebSocketClientDelegate?, start(), stop(), send(string) -- verify against the Kotlin port of WebSocketClient.kt.

`URL` is stored as String and `url.isLoopback()` (not present in the glossary) is replaced by a private isLoopback(String) helper using java.net.URI; request bodies are pre-encoded with Json.encodeToString at the call site because Kotlin cannot encode an `any Encodable`.
pauseBetweenMessages default changed from 0.0 to 0.5.
Added isPausingBetweenMessages and a SimpleTimer on textToSpeechDispatchQueue that gates trySayNextMessage, mirroring AVSpeechUtterance.preUtteranceDelay removal.
skipCurrentMessageInternal now waits 0.5 s before the next message; sayFinished waits pauseBetweenMessages.
reset() also stops the pause timer via stopPauseBetweenMessages().
The Android-only delay that emulated preUtteranceDelay inside utterApple is removed because the pause is now scheduled centrally.
NLLanguageRecognizer has no Android port, so dominantLanguage/languageProbability stay as local stubs; the filter keeps its 0.7 threshold.
deleteByUserId keeps the previous Kotlin name for Swift delete(userId:).

WiFiAware (Wi-Fi Aware listener/connection) and Network.framework's declarative NetworkListener/NetworkConnection have no counterpart in this port, so listen() keeps its signature and its body is TODO("no Android counterpart for WiFiAware").
actor WiFiAwareReceiver -> plain class with suspend members; the Swift 'static let shared' singleton becomes 'val shared' in the companion object.
private struct Sender -> file-private data class Sender; Swift Task<Void, Never> -> kotlinx.coroutines.Job, cancelled with task.cancel().
NetworkConnection<UDP> has no Kotlin type equivalent here, so 'connection' is typed Any; the Android realization of the UDP data path would be a java.net.DatagramSocket driven on Dispatchers.IO.
The 'connections' array is exposed as a file-private MutableList<Sender> of the class; actor isolation must be provided by a Mutex if the list is later mutated concurrently.
Swift 'async throws' becomes a suspend function; errors surface as thrown exceptions rather than a checked error type.
The '#if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst)' compile guard and '@available(iOS 26, *)' annotations are dropped since they have no Kotlin meaning.
logger.info(...) lines disappear with the stubbed body; when the body is implemented use android.util.Log.i with the class name as tag.
apple_only: WiFiAware framework (Wi-Fi Aware listening, publishable/subscribable service pairing)
Network.framework declarative NetworkListener / NetworkConnection API

notes: NWListener/NWConnection (UDP) are replaced by one loopback DatagramSocket. The 'connection' is the remote InetSocketAddress of the first peer that sends a packet, and packets are sent back over that same socket so the local source port stays stable for the SRT peer.
onReady passes the port as Int because Android exposes ports as Int; UInt16 is only used for wire formats in this port.

srtlaClientQueue is assumed to be a CoroutineDispatcher/CoroutineContext, so the class builds CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + srtlaClientQueue). If it is declared as a CoroutineScope instead, replace this with srtlaClientQueue.launch { }.
NWListener.State is replaced by a private nested enum ListenerState(setup, ready, failed); setup is a no-op and every other failure maps to the same 'bad network state' error message as in Swift.
The receive loop drains incoming datagrams so the peer endpoint can be detected; the payload is discarded because the Swift file exposes no receive handler on its connection.
stop() closes the socket, which also unblocks the blocking DatagramSocket.receive; the scope itself is not cancelled so the listener can be started again.
DatagramSocket.send is blocking and therefore dispatched onto srtlaClientQueue from the non-suspend sendPacket().
All logging uses android.util.Log.i with tag LocalListener and the same message text as the Swift logger calls.
CoreBluetooth ids stay top-level CBUUID vals built with CBUUID(string = ...), and the UInt8 protocol ids stay top-level UByte vals.
Data becomes ByteArray: Data([a, b]) -> byteArrayOf(a.toByte(), b.toByte()), concatenation uses ByteArray.plus, and Data() -> ByteArray(0).
Byte parsing uses (x.toInt() and mask) then .toByte(), so the UInt8 masks and header shifts keep Swift's unsigned semantics.
Protobuf requests use the ported types with the same property names (result, phoneName, scanID, maxEntries, bypassEulaCheck, ...); Int32 maps to Int and UInt32 to UInt.
The file-private SwiftProtobuf.Message.encoded() extension becomes a file-private fun Message.encoded() using runCatching { serializedData() }.getOrNull() ?: ByteArray(0).
The two toProtobuf() extensions are kept, one file-private for SettingsGoProLaunchLiveStreamResolution and one public for SettingsGoProLens returning a nullable OpenGopro_EnumLens.
GoProBleMessageAccumulator keeps its switch as a when expression so headerLength is definitely assigned, and reset() reassigns payload to ByteArray(0).
The ScanEntry helpers test the flags with Int bitwise and against OpenGopro_EnumScanEntryFlags rawValue.
MoblinkStreamer gains a Context constructor parameter (first position) because the Bonjour advertisement now uses android.net.nsd.NsdManager; port/password/name keep the Swift names and order.
NWListener/NWConnection are replaced by java.net.ServerSocket plus a file-private WebSocketConnection that performs the RFC 6455 HTTP upgrade and frame coding on Dispatchers.IO.
NWConnection.start(queue:) has no equivalent and its call site was dropped: the Kotlin connection is usable as soon as the handshake helper returns it.
NWEndpoint is represented as host String + port Int, so MoblinkStreamerDelegate takes host/port instead of an endpoint object and Relay stores tunnelEndpointHost/tunnelEndpointPort.
moblinkBonjourDomain has no NsdManager counterpart, so only name/type/TXT attributes are registered.
@MainActor is modelled with CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main): all relay bookkeeping and delegate callbacks are dispatched there, so the mutable relay list needs no locks.
MainTimer, SimpleStringStorage(key:) and randomString() call sites assume the Kotlin ports kept the Swift labels; MainTimer intervals are passed as Double seconds per the TimeInterval mapping.

MoblinkRequest/MoblinkResponse/MoblinkMessageToRelay/MoblinkMessageToStreamer are matched with `is` checks and property names taken from the Swift case labels (id, result, data, apiVersion, authentication).
NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket; connect, read and write run as coroutines on Dispatchers.IO and all blocking calls stay off the caller thread.
NWProtocolTLS.Options is mapped to javax.net.ssl.SSLContext? (null keeps plain TCP); an RTMPS caller passes an SSLContext whose socket factory creates the SSLSocket.

The DispatchQueue constructor argument became a CoroutineDispatcher named queue, still used for the delayed close and the too-much-buffered disconnect; short latency trickles stay on the caller side otherwise.
NWConnection.viabilityUpdateHandler has no Android counterpart, so viabilityDidChange is kept intact but must be driven by the caller (e.g. a ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback).
NWConnection.State has no Android counterpart; it is modelled by the private sealed class RtmpSocketConnectionState (Ready/Failed/Cancelled) declared in this file and fed from connect().
weak var delegate cannot be expressed in Kotlin; delegate is a plain nullable property and the owner must clear it when the socket is released.
RtmpChunk.split, RtmpMessage.length, RtmpHandshake.sigSize, RtmpHandshake.createC0C1Packet/createC2Packet and RtmpConnectionCode.eventData() are assumed from the sibling files of the same package.
logger.info is replaced by android.util.Log.i with the tag "RtmpSocket".
CLLocationManager, CLBackgroundActivitySession and the delegate protocol come from com.moblin.android.platform.corelocation; CLLocation is android.location.Location, imported as AndroidLocation.

LocationManager has no desiredAccuracy/distanceFilter: the accuracy choice selects the provider (ACCURACY_FINE for best and nearestTenMeters, ACCURACY_COARSE for hundredMeters) and the distance filter sets the private minDistance Float, both applied by the private startUpdatingLocation() once a location permission is granted.

The class implements android.location.LocationListener and CLLocationManagerDelegate: didFailWithError becomes onProviderDisabled, didUpdateLocations becomes onLocationChanged, and onProviderEnabled/onStatusChanged are kept as empty overrides for Android 10 and older.
@Published isDenied is a MutableStateFlow(false); format(speed:) from com.moblin.android.common.various is called as formatSpeed(location.speed.toDouble()).

start()'s manager.delegate / requestWhenInUseAuthorization calls go through the CLLocationManager authorization shim, whose locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization also restarts location updates when the user grants permission and onUpdate is set.
The iOS 17 availability check around CLBackgroundActivitySession is dropped because the shim always exists on Android.
Location takes the application Context in its constructor (Model passes AppDelegate.context).
logger.debug/info become Log.d/Log.i with the "Location" tag.

Network.framework's NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket; the NWConnection.stateUpdateHandler/NWConnection.State has no Android counterpart, so handleStateUpdate now takes a String state description and is invoked as 'ready'/'failed: ...' when the loopback socket connects or fails.
All blocking socket reads (receive loop) and writes happen inside a CoroutineScope built from srtlaServerQueue, which is assumed to be a CoroutineDispatcher (kotlinx.coroutines).

SRT wire values keep unsigned Kotlin types per the port rules: the NakPacket sequence numbers, timestamps and socket ids are UInt and the control-packet type/bit values are UShort (i.e. isSrtSnAcked(sn, ackSn) is called with UInt arguments).

The srtla.common helpers are called in their Swift free-function form (isSrtDataPacket(packet), getSrtControlPacketType(packet), getSrtSequenceNumber(packet), processSrtNak(packet) { }); if the sibling file declared them as ByteArray extension functions the calls only need a receiver/argument swap.
packet.getUInt32Be(8)/getUInt32Be(12) is assumed to exist as a ByteArray extension in com.moblin.android.media.srtla.common; it is not listed in the glossary but is used by the Swift file.
srtPort is an Int (port numbers are not wire-format data), and the loopback connection is created with InetAddress.getByName("127.0.0.1").
ContinuousClock.Instant is mapped to java.time.Instant, so duration comparisons use Duration.between(...) (millis for the 25 ms data flush, precise nanos for the 10 s client removal timeout).

NWConnection.batch/send(content:completion:) have no counterpart: the local SRT server socket is written through its OutputStream inside scope.launch, keeping Swift's 25 ms coalescing of data packets.
DispatchQueue(label:) becomes a single-thread CoroutineDispatcher; every `async { }` becomes CoroutineScope(queue).launch { }.
centralManager uses `by CBCentralManager.holder()` so assigning null releases the manager and its connections exactly like ARC on iOS.
ProcessInfo.thermalState comes from com.moblin.android.platform.core; `@unknown default` becomes `else`.
logger.debug/info become Log.d/Log.i with the tag "BlackSharkCoolerDevice".
`weak var delegate` becomes a plain nullable var, since the port has no weak references; the delegate protocol stays an interface.
`[weak self]` inside the periodic cooling-stats timer is dropped, as for other platform callbacks.
Swift's locals named coolingPower/fanSpeed shadow the stored properties and are never written back; reads use explicit `this.` to preserve that behaviour.
CBUUID comparison stays inside `when` branch conditions built with CBUUID(data = ...), matching Swift's `case CBUUID(data:)` pattern.
Apple-only tier: every HealthKit-touching body is TODO("no Android counterpart for HealthKit"); properties keep null defaults so callers still compile.
Workout stays a file-private singleton reached through Workout.shared; the HealthKit delegate protocols become plain member functions keeping the same names and parameters.

Kotlin has no argument labels, so add(heartRate:), add(cyclingPower:) and add(cyclingCadence:) become addHeartRate, addCyclingPower and addCyclingCadence; the private add(type:unit:value:) keeps its name.
WatchProtocolWorkoutType is declared here as a placeholder enum (WALKING, RUNNING, CYCLING) because the watch protocol file is not in the glossary; delete this declaration once that file is ported.
HKWorkoutSession, HKWorkoutBuilder, HKSampleType, HKQuantityType and HKUnit become Any, Date becomes java.time.Instant, ContinuousClock.Instant also becomes java.time.Instant.
Workout.isActive() and the private types() helper keep real implementations because they use no Apple API; the #available(iOS 26.0) guards are dropped.
The nonisolated delegate callbacks are not dispatched to the main queue any more: coroutine dispatch belongs in the ported watch/health layer, not in these TODO stubs.
Calls to logger, String(localized:), makeErrorToast and setIsWorkout vanish with the TODO bodies, so no logging or localization import is needed.
apple_only: HealthKit (HKHealthStore, HKWorkoutConfiguration, HKWorkoutSession, HKWorkoutSessionDelegate, HKLiveWorkoutBuilder, HKLiveWorkoutBuilderDelegate, HKLiveWorkoutDataSource, HKQuantitySample, HKUnit, HKSampleType, HKWorkoutSessionState)
WatchConnectivity (source of the WatchProtocolWorkoutType workout kinds)
ContinuousClock.Instant and HKWorkoutSession state transitions used for sample rate limiting

notes: NWInterface has no android.net.Network equivalent for type/name/index, so a file-local MoblinkRelayInterface wrapper (network, name, index, type) carries the values read from ConnectivityManager.

NWPathMonitor is replaced by ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback registered with a cellular/ethernet NetworkRequest; MoblinkRelay.applicationContext must be assigned by the Activity layer before start() so the ConnectivityManager can be obtained.

The UDP tunnel uses java.net.DatagramSocket receive loops on moblinkRelayQueue (Dispatchers.IO); NWListener/NWConnection state callbacks have no counterpart, so the listener-ready response and the waitingForCellular -> connected transitions are inlined in handleStartTunnel.
Android has no public API to bind a DatagramSocket to a specific android.net.Network, so the destination socket is created unbound; destinationInterface is only used to select and compare relays.
@MainActor is dropped; mainScope (Dispatchers.Main) and moblinkRelayQueue (Dispatchers.IO) replace the dispatch queues. The delegate is held strongly because Kotlin has no weak references.
UUID.add(data:) is replaced by java.util.UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes over relayId + interface name (then name becomes 'name-index').

Assumed Kotlin APIs from the port: WebSocketClient(url[, cellular]), send(string), delegate; WebSocketClientDelegate.webSocketClientConnected/Disconnected/ReceiveMessage; MainTimer.startSingleShot(timeout, handler); SimpleStringStorage.get()/set(); Moblink* sealed subclasses and remoteControlHashPassword(challenge, salt, password).
MoblinkRelayState and RelayState keep their Swift raw values through a rawValue property plus a fromRawValue companion helper.
CoreBluetooth delegate conformances are folded into the DjiDevice class header as override functions, keeping the Swift member order.
centralManager is backed by CBCentralManager.holder(), so reset() setting it to null releases the manager, its connections and its scan exactly like ARC.
The MainTimer single-shot closures lose [weak self] and call the class method directly; timeout 60 / 10 stay as Double seconds.
logger.debug/info become android.util.Log.d/i with the tag "DjiDevice".

The payload singletons DjiStopStreamingMessagePayload, DjiPreparingToLivestreamMessagePayload and DjiConfirmStartStreamingMessagePayload are Kotlin objects, so the Swift () is dropped and encode() is called on the object.

UInt16 targets/transaction ids are UShort and UInt32 types are UInt; bitrate and bitrateKbps are UInt so they match SettingsDjiDevice.bitrate and DjiStartStreamingMessagePayload's bitrateKbps (built by dividing by 1000 and masking with 0xFFFF).
Data([...]) payload comparisons use contentEquals, and try? DjiMessage(data:) uses runCatching to keep logging corrupt messages.
canStartLive stays a top-level extension function on SettingsDjiDevice in this package, preserving the property reads and the exhaustive when over rtmpUrlType.
Actor -> class with a companion object holding `shared`; the connection table is a ConcurrentHashMap so it is safe from the launched tasks.
Task<Void, Never> -> Job from scope.launch; sleep(seconds: 5) -> delay(5_000); the sender/receiver closure bodies map onto coroutines on Dispatchers.IO.

NWConnection over UDP -> java.net.DatagramSocket; send/receive build and fill DatagramPacket instances, and the peer address comes from remoteSocketAddress, so the socket handed over must already be connected to the peer.

WiFiAware (NetworkBrowser, NetworkConnection, WAPairedDevice) is only reachable through the private suspend helper browseWiFiAware, which is a TODO; on Android this is android.net.wifi.aware (attach/publish/subscribe + WifiAwareNetworkSpecifier) or NetLink ServiceDiscovery.
WAPairedDevice.ID -> String device id used as the map key.
The Swift `try?` around browser.run disappears: browseWiFiAware throws NotImplementedError until it is implemented, so the cleanup and 'Stop' logging after it do not run yet.
DatagramSocket.receive is blocking, so cancelling the receiver task only ends the loop once a packet arrives or the socket is closed.
Receiver keeps the same three stored properties in the same order, with senderTask/receiverTask as Job.
apple_only: WiFiAware NetworkBrowser / NetworkConnection over UDP (Network.framework on Wi-Fi Aware)

notes: DispatchQueue ristQueue became a single-thread coroutine dispatcher (ristDispatcher) plus a CoroutineScope (ristScope); ristQueue.sync { } blocks map to runBlocking(ristDispatcher) { }, ristQueue.async/named queues map to scope.launch.

The Rist C library has no ready JNI binding, so its types (RistPeer, RistSenderContext, RistSenderStats, RistStats, RistSenderContextDelegate) are declared in this file following the libsrt rule: the wrapper keeps the Swift method names and calls a private RistNative object with external fun declarations and System.loadLibrary("rist").
NWEndpoint is replaced by RistEndpoint(host, port); NWInterface.InterfaceType is replaced by an android.net.NetworkCapabilities transport constant (Int?).

NWPathMonitor is replaced by ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback; because a Context is required, the file exposes a top level var ristApplicationContext that the Activity layer must set before starting a bonding stream.
Swift weak references (weak let stream, weak let ristDelegate) became plain strong references; Java GC handles the resulting cycles.
deinit has no Kotlin counterpart and became a close() method that stops the connecting timer; stopInternal also calls close() on removed peers.

MpegTsWriterDelegate and RistSenderContextDelegate overrides keep the Swift parameter names; the exact Kotlin delegate signatures come from the ported Moblin interfaces in com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg and are assumed to match.
SimpleTimer(ristScope), Atomic<Long>(0L), processorPipelineQueue.launch { } and BondingConnection(name:, usage:, rtt:) use the signatures of the ported types listed in the glossary.

NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket: connect, receive and send run in coroutines on the file-private connectionScope (Dispatchers.IO + SupervisorJob); srtlaClientQueue is still what the two SimpleTimer instances are built with.

NWInterface.InterfaceType has no Android counterpart, so `type` is an Int? holding android.net.NetworkCapabilities.TRANSPORT_* values (null means relay/any), and NWParameters.requiredInterface is applied by creating the socket through Network.socketFactory.
Because android.net.Network exposes no interface name, the typeString lookup uses interface?.toString() as the key into SrtlaNetworkInterfaces.names.
NWConnection.State has no Android counterpart: a private top-level ConnectionState enum (ready/failed) stands in for the handleStateUpdate(to:) parameter.
ContinuousClock instants become System.nanoTime(); getKeepAliveTime() and rtt stay millisecond based like the Swift code.

The Data helpers used by this file (getUInt32Be, setUInt32Be, getInt64Be, setInt64Be, randomData) are not part of the glossary, so they are declared as private top-level ByteArray extensions here, implemented with ByteBuffer and SecureRandom.
logger.* maps to android.util.Log with tag RemoteConnection; the weak delegate becomes a strong reference, and deinit is translated as an override of finalize().

sizeFormatter (com.moblin.android.common.various) is assumed to expose format(bytes: Long): String for ByteCountFormatter.string(fromByteCount:), and outgoing packets are written under synchronized(socket) so they cannot interleave.

srtlaClientQueue is a single-thread CoroutineDispatcher: DispatchQueue.async becomes srtlaClientScope.launch and DispatchQueue.sync becomes runBlocking(srtlaClientQueue) (never call those two sync-based getters from the srtla dispatcher itself).

NWPathMonitor/NWPath are replaced by ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback plus a Network->transport map; no Context is available in this layer, so the ConnectivityManager must be published through the new top-level var srtlaConnectivityManager by the Activity (TODO until then).

NWEndpoint parameters are flattened into host: String + port: Int (addMoblink/removeMoblink/startRemote) and NWInterface becomes android.net.Network with its NetworkCapabilities.TRANSPORT_* constant as the interface type.
UInt16 ports became Int, UInt32 sequence numbers became UInt, and ContinuousClock/Duration became System.nanoTime() nanoseconds compared against 15_000_000L.
deinit has no Kotlin counterpart, so the 'srtla deinit' debug log is dropped.
weak let delegate becomes a plain nullable reference (private val delegate: SrtlaDelegate?) since Kotlin has no weak properties.

State is redeclared here as a file-private enum, matching the Swift private enum; SrtlaDelegate's conforming members were moved into the class body because Kotlin interfaces cannot be implemented by extensions.

Sibling APIs are assumed to keep their Swift names: RemoteConnection.networkInterface/type(Int?)/register/setPriority/score/getDataSentDelta/stop(reason), LocalListener.onReady/onError/sendPacket, SimpleTimer-startSingleShot/stop, BondingConnection(name, usage, rtt) and the enum cases SettingsDnsLookupStrategy.ipv4/ipv6/ipv4AndIpv6/system, DnsLookupFamily.ipv4/ipv6/unspec, SettingsStreamSrtImplementation.moblin/official.
Network.framework NWListener/NWConnection are replaced by java.net.ServerSocket/Socket; the accept loop and each connection read loop run as coroutines on Dispatchers.IO.

HttpServer.queue is modelled as a CoroutineDispatcher and the class exposes an internal scope so HttpServerConnection can share it; SimpleTimer is assumed to be constructible as SimpleTimer(queue: CoroutineDispatcher).
NWEndpoint.Port becomes Int (default 80); the NWListener.State failure branch became handleStateUpdate(failed: Boolean) driving the same 1 second retry through retryTimer.
sendFileAndClose takes a java.io.File and streams it in 512 KiB blocking chunks (iterative loop) instead of the recursive NWConnection completion chain.

HttpServerConnection is internal instead of fileprivate because it appears in HttpServerResponse's internal constructor; HttpServerResponse.connection is a plain nullable reference (Kotlin has no weak properties).
HttpParser, declared in the same package, is assumed to be an open class exposing data: ByteArray, append(data: ByteArray) and getLine(data: ByteArray, offset: Int): Pair<String, Int>?.
Data.advanced(by:)/prefix become ByteArray.copyOfRange/copyOf; utf8Data becomes String.toByteArray().
logger.debug/info become Log.d/Log.i with a file level TAG constant because Kotlin has no per-class logger.
@MainActor protocol becomes a plain interface; SDK callbacks (webSocket*) are hopped onto Dispatchers.Main through mainScope so delegate calls stay on the main thread.
Swift 'private weak let delegate' has no Kotlin equivalent; it is a strong nullable property. Callers must drop their delegate reference explicitly to avoid leaking.
URL -> String (stored only). URL.isLoopback() is not in the glossary, so it is re-implemented here as a private String extension using java.net.URI.

Sealed cases of RemoteControlMessageToStreamer / RemoteControlRequest / RemoteControlResponse / RemoteControlEvent / RemoteControlMessageToAssistant are assumed to be named after the Swift cases with a capital first letter (Hello, Request, GetStatus, Response, ...) and their properties after the Swift labels.
RemoteControlResult is treated as an enum class whose entries keep the Swift case names (ok, wrongPassword, error) because the raw values are persisted.
Data -> ByteArray, base64EncodedString() -> android.util.Base64.encodeToString(..., Base64.NO_WRAP); Data.utf8Data -> String.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8).
String(localized:) -> localized() imported from com.moblin.android; logger -> android.util.Log with the file-level TAG.
UUID().uuidString -> UUID.randomUUID().toString() (lowercase, the wire value is still a valid UUID).
The Info.plist lookup for MoblinWebsiteApiUrl is replaced by BuildConfig.MOBLIN_WEBSITE_API_URL; that buildConfigField has to be added to the app module.
DeviceCheck App Attest has no Android counterpart, so attestedKey(), sendLive() and generateAssertion() are TODO(); fetchChallenge() and postLive() keep the whole HTTP flow.
URLSession is replaced by a shared OkHttpClient with 30 s timeouts, and every request runs on Dispatchers.IO.
CryptoKit SHA256 becomes MessageDigest("SHA-256") and Data.base64EncodedString() becomes java.util.Base64 (API 26+).
The Codable structs become @Serializable classes with identical field names; Data becomes ByteArray, which kotlinx.serialization writes as a JSON number array instead of base64.
MoblinWebsiteError is a sealed class extending Exception with the KeyRejected and BadResponse subclasses.

The Twitch/YouTube/Kick callbacks are bridged with suspendCancellableCoroutine; createTwitchApi, getYouTubeApi, createKickApi and the listChannels result type (YouTubeApiResult.Success) must match their own ports.
defer { onCompleted?() } becomes try/finally inside a mainScope.launch block, so the @MainActor completion still runs on the main thread.
apple_only: DeviceCheck DCAppAttestService.generateKey/attestKey/isSupported (App Attest) - attestedKey() and sendLive() bodies are TODO()
DeviceCheck DCAppAttestService.generateAssertion - generateAssertion() body is TODO()

notes: Added the TwitchEventSubChannelShoutoutCreateEvent import in the twitch import block, after TwitchEventSubChannelRaidEvent.
Added the empty override twitchEventSubChannelShoutoutCreate right after twitchEventSubChannelModerate, matching the Swift extension order.
Everything else in the file is untouched, including the hand-written WebSocket server, socket helpers and the RemoteControlWebSocket class.
RemoteControlWebDelegate becomes a Kotlin interface; the Swift `weak` delegate is stored as a plain nullable property because Kotlin has no weak references for interfaces.

Network.framework NWListener/NWConnection is replaced with java.net.ServerSocket plus a hand-rolled RFC6455 WebSocket handshake and frame codec running on Dispatchers.IO; callbacks are dispatched back on a Dispatchers.Main scope.
NWListener.State update handling is reduced to a private `handleWebsocketStateUpdate(failed: Boolean)` helper that drives the same 1s retry timer.
UInt16 ports become Int (ServerSocket takes Int); string interpolation on the port value is preserved in config.mjs.
URL return of `remoteControlWebGetRecordingUrl` maps to java.net.URI; `[[String: String]]` recordings map to List<Map<String, String>>.
JSONSerialization is replaced with org.json.JSONArray and logger.info with android.util.Log.i using the class name as tag.
Sealed-class case names are assumed as RemoteControlRequest.*, RemoteControlResponse.*, RemoteControlMessageToAssistant.* and RemoteControlEvent.* (PascalCase, matching the Swift case labels).
@MainActor isolation is not reproduced; blocking socket work runs on Dispatchers.IO and UI-visible callbacks run on Dispatchers.Main.
Model is declared in the same package, so this file holds top-level extension functions on Model; the Swift file-private `thumbStickDeadZone` became a private top-level `const val`.

GameController has no Android counterpart: GCController is replaced by android.view.InputDevice and the per-button `pressedChangedHandler` / `valueChangedHandler` wiring is gone because the Activity delivers KeyEvent/MotionEvent instead.
`handleGameControllerButton` and `handleGameControllerThumbStick` were private in Swift and are left public on purpose so the Activity layer can forward key and motion events into them.
`button.sfSymbolsName` is replaced by an explicit `buttonId: String` parameter; the Activity is expected to map KeyEvent key codes to the same ids stored in SettingsGameControllerButton.name.
`String(localized:)` became the top-level `localized()` function imported from com.moblin.android.
`Gimbal.shared?.animate(motion:)` keeps the `shared` accessor shape; the iOS 18 availability check is dropped since it does not exist on Android.
The `[weak self]` capture in the gimbal preset long-press timer is dropped; Kotlin lambdas capture strongly, so the timer must be stopped/removed to avoid retaining the Model.
SettingsQuickButtonType is not in the glossary and is assumed to live in com.moblin.android.various.settings; fix the import if the port placed it elsewhere.

The two Swift `extension GoProDevice: ...Delegate` blocks become the class header conformance to CBCentralManagerDelegate/CBPeripheralDelegate with `override fun` members kept in the same order at the end of the body, since Kotlin cannot extend conformance from an extension.
The Swift tuple array `pendingWrites: [(characteristic: CBCharacteristic, packet: Data)]` is a private nested data class PendingWrite.
`[weak self]` is dropped from every MainTimer closure, as required for the hand-written shims.
`try? X(serializedBytes:)` becomes `runCatching { ... }.getOrNull()`; an empty Source returns early exactly like the Swift guard.
The private `state` property keeps its name together with the Swift-named `getState()` / `setState(state:)` methods; Kotlin generates getState/setState accessors for that property.
ByteArray sizes/slices: `message.count` -> `size`, `Data(message.dropFirst(2))` -> `message.copyOfRange(2, message.size)`.

Message header bytes are compared as `message[0].toUByte()`/`message[1].toUByte()` so the UByte action/feature ids stay unsigned; `bitrate` stays `UInt` because goProSetLiveStreamModeMessage takes a UInt.
@MainActor is dropped: these Model extensions run on the main dispatcher like the rest of Model.
The three WatchConnectivity entry points keep their names but their bodies are TODO(...) because the WatchProtocol* payload types have no Android counterpart; their parameters are typed Any.
The scoreboard configs stay file-private top-level vals; configs is declared after the individual configs so top-level initialisation order matches Swift.
Swift switch expressions on scoreboard.sport become when(...) with an else branch, and if/guard let becomes a null check, ?.let or an early return.
clamped(to:) maps to coerceIn, Array.popLast()/removeLast() map to MutableList.removeLastOrNull()/removeLast(), count is read through List.size.

modular.layout and modular.clock.direction are compared against SettingsWidgetScoreboardLayout and SettingsWidgetGenericScoreboardClockDirection taken from the glossary; verify these are the enums used by SettingsWidgetModularScoreboard.
scoreChanges elements are translated as SettingsWidgetScoreboardScoreIncrement.home/.away, and padel/generic score entries as SettingsWidgetScoreboardScore().

modular.home.textColor.toHex() is kept as a member call on the color type of com.moblin.android.common.various, and modular.clock.format() is imported as the top-level extension format() from that package.
TeslaVehicle implements CBCentralManagerDelegate and CBPeripheralDelegate directly; the two Swift extensions became override members at the end of the class body.
responseHandlers is keyed by address.hexString() because ByteArray keys compare by identity.
The P256 public key DER-header extension became a companion invoke operator plus a toBytes() extension in this file.
Deque<Job> is ArrayDeque<Job>: append -> addLast, popFirst -> removeFirstOrNull, removeAll -> clear.
Data.random(length:) -> randomBytes() from com.moblin.android.various.utils; Data.random(length:) for uuid addresses too.
@MainActor and @available(iOS 17) have no Kotlin counterpart, so the auto-reconnect option is set unconditionally.
protobuf .init() assignments name the generated message type explicitly (CarServer_*), as the Kotlin setters need a value.
Log.i/Log.d use the TeslaVehicle tag in place of logger.info/logger.debug.
Data extension becomes an extension function on ByteArray in package com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.extension.
Data.subdata(in:) maps to ByteArray.copyOfRange(fromIndex, toIndex), which also copies into a new array just like subdata.
The Swift `offset ..< offset + thisChunkSize` range is translated to copyOfRange(offset, offset + thisChunkSize) because Kotlin's end index is exclusive.
The returned type is List<ByteArray> instead of [Data].
The Data-returning branch for count < size returns listOf(this), preserving the Swift behaviour of returning the receiver itself.
Declares no Kotlin types, only the top-level extension function chunks.
The CoreMedia import is unused in the Swift body and therefore has no Kotlin import.
No iOS-only API needed a TODO in this file.

AVFoundation's AVFrameRateRange has no Android counterpart, so this file declares a plain data class AVFrameRateRange with minFrameRate/maxFrameRate (Double) in the same package; the extension keeps the Swift member name contains(frameRate:).
Swift's range pattern operator ~= on a ClosedRange is translated to Kotlin's in operator on a ClosedFloatingPointRange, which is the direct equivalent.
Float64 maps to Double and the parameter name is kept as frameRate so both codebases read side by side.
No other call sites of contains(frameRate:) exist inside this file; consumers import this package's declaration.
No hardware, AudioToolbox, or VideoToolbox API is touched here, so no TODO() markers were needed.
AVCaptureDevice.Format has no Android class; it is modelled here as the plain data class AVCaptureDeviceFormat with the same property name videoSupportedFrameRateRanges.
AVFrameRateRange is modelled as a data class with minFrameRate/maxFrameRate and a contains(frameRate:) member, matching AVFrameRateRange semantics (inclusive bounds).
isFrameRateSupported keeps its Swift name and signature and contains the full pure logic port; only the loop style is idiomatic Kotlin with an early return.

CameraX/camera2 exposes frame-rate ranges as Range<Int> (camera2 CONTROL_AE_AVAILABLE_TARGET_FPS_RANGES, high-speed video fps ranges); the call site maps those into AVFrameRateRange entries, so no camera2 import is needed in this file.
No hardware call, no coroutine and no permission handling appears in this file, so nothing became a TODO().
Frame rates stay Double (Swift Float64).
No iOS-only framework call was dropped, so unsupported is empty.
CVPixelBuffer is mapped to android.media.Image as instructed; the extension members are declared on that type.

android.media.Image already exposes width/height via the synthesized Java getters getWidth()/getHeight(), so the two extension properties are shadowed by the members; they are kept for source parity with the Swift file and their getters resolve to the underlying Image accessors.
CGSize is translated to android.util.Size, the Android platform type with 32-bit width/height.
isPortrait() is a pure comparison and is translated verbatim; no hardware access is involved.
No decoding, conversion or MediaCodec call is needed here, so nothing in this file is a TODO.
CMFormatDescription maps to android.media.MediaFormat, so the three members become top-level extension functions on MediaFormat in this package.
atoms() returns the sample-description atom map; on Android the codec-private data lives in the csd-0 ByteBuffer, so it is returned keyed by avcC/hvcC according to the MIME type.
extensions() mirrors CMFormatDescriptionGetExtensions; MediaFormat can only enumerate its keys from API 29, so on API 26-28 the body is TODO().
numberOfAudioChannels() reads MediaFormat.KEY_CHANNEL_COUNT instead of AudioStreamBasicDescription.mChannelsPerFrame.
Channel count is Int in Kotlin (UInt32 is reserved for wire-format byte parsing).
ByteArray replaces NSData/CFData and Map replaces NSDictionary/CFDictionary.
runCatching replaces the optional casts done by 'as?' in the Swift original, so missing or wrong-typed keys yield null.
The returned atom map is derived from csd-0 only; codecs that split parameter sets across csd-0/csd-1 return just csd-0.
AVFoundation import was unused in the Swift source, so no Android media imports are needed.
All enums keep their Swift case names and raw values; raw values are typed UByte/UShort/UInt since FLV is a wire format.
Each enum gains a companion fromRawValue helper as required by the porting contract.
FlvVideoCodec.toString() is translated as an override of Kotlin's Any.toString().
FlvTagType.streamId and headerSize become computed properties (get()) with identical switch semantics.
No hardware-bound or Apple-only APIs appear in this file, so nothing is stubbed.

CoreMedia's CMBlockBuffer has no Android/Java counterpart, so this file declares a minimal immutable Kotlin stand-in class holding a ByteArray; the name is kept so the two codebases read side by side.
Swift's (UnsafeMutablePointer<Int8>, Int) pair is represented as Pair<ByteBuffer, Int>: a read-only java.nio.ByteBuffer positioned at offset 0 plus the total length.

getDataPointer keeps its nullable return type to mirror the failing CMBlockBufferGetDataPointer call, but never returns null for the Android stand-in because an array-backed ByteBuffer always has a valid pointer.
data: Data? becomes data: ByteArray? and copies the bytes out of the buffer, exactly like Data(bytes:count:).
A zero-length block buffer yields an empty ByteArray, not null, matching the Swift behaviour where only a nil data pointer or error returns nil.
The buffer is copied on construction and exposed read-only, so callers cannot mutate the block buffer through the returned ByteBuffer.

VideoToolbox has no Android counterpart: the CFString property keys are carried as opaque Kotlin String values so the MediaCodec configuration layer can map them (e.g. ProfileLevel/ExpectedFrameRate/AverageBitRate -> MediaFormat keys) later.
CFString -> String, AnyObject -> Any.
@unchecked Sendable and Sendable are dropped; Kotlin has no equivalent annotation and these are immutable value holders.
@available(iOS 26, *) on variableBitRate is dropped, the constant is declared unconditionally as in the rest of the list.
static let constants become companion object val properties; declaration order is preserved exactly.
VTSessionProperty remains a data class because the Swift struct has only stored properties.
The type name VTSessionPropertyKey is kept unchanged for side-by-side reading even though there is no VTSession type on Android.
String literals mirror the documented contents of the kVTCompressionPropertyKey_* CFStrings; only the key strings are stored, no MediaCodec session call is performed here.
CMTime becomes a Long of microseconds, so value/timescale arithmetic collapses into plain microsecond maths and halfMaximumTimestamp is exactly maximumTimestamp / 2.
Callers must hand in timestamps already converted to microseconds; the comparison logic here assumes every timestamp shares one timebase.
Swift's `defer` is translated to try/finally so previousTimestamp is mutated after the return value has been evaluated, matching the original ordering.

Faithful to the source: in the branch where `timestamp - previousTimestamp >= halfMaximumTimestamp` the Swift `defer` only covers the inner block, so previousTimestamp is NOT updated there; the Kotlin code preserves that behaviour.
logger.info(...) becomes android.util.Log.i with the tag "WrappingTimestamp" taken from the class name.
The wrap-around detection mutates highTimestamp before returning, exactly as in the Swift original.
No Android API gaps in this file: the whole class is pure arithmetic and none of it is TODO().
CMTime parameters became Long microseconds (presentationTimeStamp, decodeTimeStamp); CMTime.seconds is reproduced with a /1_000_000.0 conversion.
Date became java.time.Instant. The fractional epoch seconds are rebuilt from epochSecond + nano/1e9 so truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1) keeps the same meaning.
logger.info(...) is android.util.Log.i with the class name as tag; the Swift multi-line string continuation is collapsed into one string.
Swift's truncatingRemainder(dividingBy:) and rounded(.down) map to Kotlin's % on Double and kotlin.math.floor, which have identical truncation semantics.
UInt32(frame) becomes frame.toUInt(), which truncates toward zero like the Swift initializer but saturates instead of trapping on out-of-range values.
guard let presentationTimeStampBase becomes an early return with a local val, since the coalesced property cannot be smart-cast after the check.
offsetingFrames.toggle() becomes offsetingFrames = !offsetingFrames.
No Android hardware calls in this file, so no TODO() was needed.

VideoToolbox has no Android counterpart, so an interface VTDecompressionSession wrapping a MediaCodec decoder stands in for it; defaultDecodeFlags lives in its companion object so VTDecompressionSession.defaultDecodeFlags keeps the Swift spelling.
VTDecodeFrameFlags and VTDecodeInfoFlags are modelled as @JvmInline value classes over an Int bit mask, keeping the original _Enable... constant names and a plus/contains operator.
VTDecompressionOutputHandler becomes a Kotlin fun interface; CVImageBuffer maps to android.media.Image and both CMTime arguments map to Long microseconds.
OSStatus is translated as Int; the by-reference flagsOut out-parameter disappears because the decode call is a TODO and output flags arrive with the asynchronous MediaCodec callback instead.

decodeFrame body is TODO(...) because MediaCodec exposes no synchronous decode-with-output-handler entry point; a sample has to be queued into the decoder and the android.media.Image delivered from the codec callback.
invalidate() is real code: guarded MediaCodec.stop() followed by MediaCodec.release().
@inline(__always) is kept as Kotlin inline.
defaultDecodeFlags is retained for call-site parity even though MediaCodec's asynchronous mode makes those flags meaningless.

File-private `barrelKernel` keeps Swift's lazy global semantics with `by lazy`; `Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:)` maps to the platform `Bundle.url` and `Data(contentsOf:)` to `File(url).readBytes()` inside `runCatching`.
`guard let inputImage, let barrelKernel` becomes two early returns with local vals, since Kotlin locals cannot shadow the properties they are read from.
`CIFilter.outputImage` is overridden as `override val outputImage: CIImage? get()`, the shape the platform CIFilter shim expects.
Swift `CGFloat width` becomes `Double width = 1.0`, and `Float(width)` / `Float(extent.height)` become `toFloat()` in the kernel argument list.
The `roiCallback` closure is passed unchanged with named arguments `dx`/`dy`; the platform `CIWarpKernel.apply` takes `(Int, CGRect) -> CGRect`.
Swift `class` (not final) becomes `open class` with `open` members, except the overridden property.
No iOS-only API in this file needs a TODO; only the Core Image kernel and the metallib asset are used, both of which have shims.
The Metal library is loaded from the mirrored Android asset named `default.metallib` (Bundle.url("default", "metallib")).
VNFaceObservation extension methods become top-level extension functions on VNFaceObservation in com.moblin.android.various, since Kotlin cannot reopen a class.
CGFloat parameters and results map to Double; CoreGraphics shim types CGPoint/CGSize/CGRect are used unchanged.
Swift guard-let chains become early returns with firstOrNull()/lastOrNull() and the elvis operator.
private func isEyeOpen/getFacePoints become private top-level extension functions in this same file, matching Swift's file-scoped visibility.
The ASCII landmark-index diagram comment in isEyeOpen is dropped because generated Kotlin carries no comments.
Eye/mouth openness helpers keep their exact numeric thresholds (0.015, factor 6) and clamp behaviour.
rotateFace/rotatePoint/calcBoundingBox stay top-level functions with the same names and parameter labels as the Swift globals.
No iOS-only API without a shim is used: Vision, CoreGraphics and math all map onto the hand-written platform layer.
SwiftUI Canvas maps to a Compose Canvas composable with a DrawScope lambda.
Path stroke becomes drawPath with Stroke(width = 1f) instead of context.stroke.
The view takes an optional Modifier parameter so callers can size it, since Compose composables have no intrinsic frame.
allowsHitTesting(false) has no direct equivalent; the Canvas is left without pointer input so it stays non-interactive.
size.width and size.height are Float in DrawScope, so the 1/3 and 2/3 factors are written as floats.
Color(.gray) maps to androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color.Gray.
The Swift view has no state or bindings, so the composable needs no remember or collectAsState.
StreamGridView becomes a top-level @Composable function, not a class, so no type is declared in this file.
MpegTsAudioConfig is a data class so that Equatable equality covers the same four stored properties (type, frequency, channel, frameLengthFlag).
The failable init?(data:) becomes a companion factory MpegTsAudioConfig.fromData(data) returning null, because Kotlin constructors cannot return null.
MPEG4ObjectID is an AudioToolbox type with no Android counterpart, so AudioObjectType.fromObjectID(objectID: Int) takes the raw MPEG4 object ID; its values 1..9 match the enum raw values exactly.
init(formatDescription: CMFormatDescription) becomes a secondary constructor over android.media.MediaFormat, reading KEY_MIME, KEY_AAC_PROFILE, KEY_SAMPLE_RATE and KEY_CHANNEL_COUNT.
audioStreamBasicDescription() now returns a MediaFormat (audio/mp4a-latm, or audio/opus when the object type is opus) with KEY_SAMPLE_RATE, KEY_CHANNEL_COUNT and KEY_AAC_PROFILE set.
AudioStreamBasicDescription's mBytesPerPacket, mBytesPerFrame, mBitsPerChannel and mReserved have no MediaFormat equivalent and are dropped.
mFramesPerPacket (960/1024) has no MediaFormat key either, so frameLengthFlag is kept on the type but is not written into the format.
Raw values stay UByte to keep the on-wire packing in encode()/fromData() byte-identical; the Swift force-unwraps become nullable fallbacks (unknown, definedInAOTSpecificConfig, hz44100).
SwiftUI's LocalizedStringKey becomes a plain String and is resolved through the package-level localized() helper.
buttonStyle(.borderless) maps to Material 3 TextButton, which is the closest borderless button.
The Swift 'action' closure is kept unchanged as a Kotlin () -> Unit parameter named action.
No view state exists, so no remember/collectAsState is needed.
SwiftUI View struct becomes a top-level @Composable function with the same name, taking the stored closure as a parameter.
Button with a Label is rendered as a TextButton containing an Icon plus Text in a Row.
The SF Symbol "plus.square.on.square" maps to Icons.Default.ContentCopy, the closest Material icon.
Text("Duplicate") uses the localized() helper from package com.moblin.android, as required by the localization rule.
declared_types is empty because the file only declares a top-level composable function.
WebBrowserController was a UIViewController + WKUIDelegate; it is now a plain controller exposing StateFlows that a Compose AlertDialog renders.
The three delegate methods keep the Swift label names but are prefixed with webView, because (Boolean) -> Unit and (String?) -> Unit erase to the same JVM signature and could not be overloads.
WKFrameInfo has no Android counterpart and is kept as an unused 'initiatedByFrame: Any?' parameter so the signatures stay readable side by side.
UIAlertController is replaced by the WebBrowserAlertDialog composable, a Material 3 AlertDialog with Ok/Cancel text buttons.
WebBrowserPanel plus the completeAlert/completeConfirm/completeTextInput functions were added so the dialog can resume the stored completion handler, exactly like the UIAlertAction handlers did.
showAlert is a private MutableStateFlow exposed as a read-only StateFlow; collect it with collectAsState() at the call site.
Button titles use localized("Ok") / localized("Cancel") instead of the hardcoded Swift strings.
The text-input Ok action returns the field text and falls back to defaultText when the field is empty, matching Swift's fallback to defaultText.
SwiftUI View struct becomes a single @Composable function; the struct name is kept as the function name.
`.foregroundStyle(.red)` maps to the Text color parameter using androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color.Red.
`.font(.callout)` maps to MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium as the closest Material 3 style.
`.bold()` maps to fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold.
The two Text views are wrapped in a Column so they stack like the SwiftUI tuple view inside a Form/List.
The `if error != ""` check stays as a plain Kotlin if with no else branch, matching the Swift view builder.
SwiftUI Button with a Label becomes a Material 3 TextButton containing a Row with Icon and Text.
The .tint(.red) modifier maps to red contentColor via ButtonDefaults.textButtonColors(contentColor = Color.Red).
Icons.Default.Delete is the closest Material icon to SF Symbols 'trash'.
The stored closure `action` becomes a parameter of the same name typed () -> Unit.
An extra modifier: Modifier = Modifier parameter is added, which has no Swift counterpart.

VTDecompressionSession is replaced by android.media.MediaCodec configured from the CMFormatDescription-equivalent MediaFormat, using the async MediaCodec.Callback API with a HandlerThread owned by the decoder.
The session property keeps its Swift didSet behaviour with a Kotlin custom setter: the previous codec is stopped and released whenever a new session is assigned.
kVTInvalidSessionErr / VTDecompressionSessionDecodeFrame errors map to MediaCodec.CodecException (a subclass of IllegalStateException), caught in decodeSampleBuffer to trigger a session reset.

makeSession() drops the CVPixelBuffer attributes (kCVPixelBufferPixelFormatTypeKey and friends) because MediaCodec derives the output colour format from the input MediaFormat; the pixelFormatType property lives in another Swift extension and is therefore not referenced.

Decoded frames are delivered as MediaSample(data = raw copy of the MediaCodec output buffer, presentationTimeUs = BufferInfo.presentationTimeUs, isKeyFrame = true, format = codec.outputFormat), matching the pipeline's byte-oriented MediaSample.
softwareDecoding only influences codec selection on API 29+ via MediaCodecInfo.isSoftwareOnly; on API 26-28 the platform default decoder returned by MediaCodecList.findDecoderForFormat is used.
lockQueue is modelled as a CoroutineScope (expected to use a single-threaded dispatcher) and callbacks are dispatched with lockQueue.launch, mirroring DispatchQueue.async.
delegate is stored in a WeakReference so the Swift 'weak var' semantics are preserved; formatDescription is a MediaFormat instead of CMFormatDescription.
UIViewControllerRepresentable that returns a UIActivityViewController becomes a @Composable function with the same name and the same activityItems property, per the platform shim rules.

makeUIViewController and updateUIViewController are dropped: UIActivityViewController from com.moblin.android.platform.swiftui shows the Android share sheet and dismisses the Sheet it is presented in.
The item type is widened to List<Any?> to match the declared platform signature.
SwiftUI Button + Label becomes a Material 3 Button whose content is a Row with Icon and Text.
The .tint(.blue) modifier is mapped to ButtonDefaults.buttonColors(containerColor = Color.Blue) so the control keeps the Swift blue chrome.
The stored closure property 'action: () -> Void' becomes a composable parameter 'action: () -> Unit' named identically.
Image(systemName: "plus.square.on.square") maps to Icons.Default.ContentCopy, the closest Material symbol, with contentDescription = null.
The Swift default Button style with a Label is reproduced with Button(onClick = action) so behaviour stays identical.
No state is held, so no remember/LaunchedEffect is required in this file.
SwiftUI Text with string interpolation becomes a Compose Text with a Kotlin string template.
The view takes no model objects, so only the kind string is a parameter.
An extra Modifier parameter with a default value was added, as is conventional for Compose composables.
The copy is kept inline rather than moved to strings.xml so the Swift and Kotlin sources stay readable side by side; it can be extracted later with stringResource.

SFSpeechRecognizer, SFSpeechAudioBufferRecognitionRequest, SFSpeechRecognitionTask and SFSpeechRecognizerDelegate come from the speech shim (platform/speech), so the class keeps the Swift shape and no Context.

On Android 13 and newer the audio appended with appendAudioSampleBuffer is converted to 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM and fed to the recognizer through RecognizerIntent.EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE, preferring the on-device recognizer; older versions let the recognizer use the microphone.
requestAuthorization reports authorized, denied without the microphone permission and restricted without a recognition service; the when over the closed enum drops Swift's @unknown default.
The result handler runs on the main thread like SFSpeechRecognizer's default queue; return inside it is return@recognitionTask.
ContinuousClock.Instant becomes Long nanoseconds from SystemClock.elapsedRealtimeNanos(), the clock Model passes to tick(now:).
String.suffix(150) becomes takeLast(150) on UTF-16 units, matching the offsets Subtitles uses.
delegate cannot be weak in Kotlin; Model drops the SpeechToText instance on stop.
The @Binding selectedRotation becomes a plain Double parameter plus an onSelectedRotationChange lambda, per the ui tier convention.
Picker is rendered as a Material 3 ExposedDropdownMenuBox with a read-only OutlinedTextField anchor.
The ForEach over the literal rotation list is a Kotlin loop over listOf(0.0, 90.0, 180.0, 270.0); the degree labels use Int conversion to match "\(Int(rotation))°".
No navigation callback is needed because the Swift view has no NavigationLink.
Top-level `graphicsEpsilon` and the lazily built `kernel` mirror Swift's file globals; the warp kernel is loaded from the app's default.metallib asset through the CIWarpKernel shim.

`Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:)` plus `Data(contentsOf:)` become `Bundle.url(...)` plus `File(url).readBytes()`, and both `try?` become `runCatching{}.getOrNull()`, so the kernel is null when the metallib is missing.

`outputImage` is an override computed property that returns null when `inputImage` or the kernel is missing, matching the Swift `guard`; the two guards are read into local vals so the mutable properties can be used.
`extension SIMD3<Float> { toCiVector() }` stays a top-level extension function on the SIMD3 shim in this package; `CIVector(values:count:)` takes a List<Double>.
`float3x3(rows:)` uses the platform simd typealias and `rotation[i]` selects column i, exactly as in Swift.

`cos`, `sin` and `tan` come from kotlin.math and stay Float, matching Darwin's Float overloads, and the integer literals in the matrix rows are written as `0f`/`1f` for Kotlin's Float parameter types.
CIContext is not stored: readback goes through CVPixelBuffer.toBitmap(), reached via the private createBitmap helper as the platform layer requires.
The constructor takes an android.content.Context, the shape the platform layer declares for VideoSnapshots; the Swift CIContext argument has no Kotlin counterpart.
UIImage and CIImage callbacks become Bitmap callbacks, so takeSnapshotComplete is (Bitmap, Bitmap, Bitmap) -> Unit and is invoked as onComplete(image, image, portraitImage).
Deque<CMSampleBuffer> becomes ArrayDeque<MediaSample>; last(where:) maps to lastOrNull { } and first to firstOrNull().
DispatchQueue.main.async and Task become CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main.immediate).launch and CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Default).launch; DispatchQueue.global().async uses Dispatchers.Default.
presentationTimeStamp stays in seconds, and sample times are read as MediaSample.presentationTimeUs / 1_000_000.0 (microseconds on MediaSample).
#available(iOS 18, *) is dropped and the aesthetics branch is always taken, so findBestSnapshotUsingAesthetics runs on every Android version.
orientedLeft rotates the Bitmap by -90 degrees with android.graphics.Matrix, standing in for CIImage.oriented(.left).
VideoToolbox has no Android counterpart, so the extension receiver is android.media.MediaCodec (per the media tier mapping); the Swift receiver name VTCompressionSession is therefore not preserved.
OSStatus -> Int, CMTime -> Long microseconds, CVPixelBuffer -> android.media.Image, CMSampleBuffer -> MediaSample (com.moblin.android.media).
VTCompressionOutputHandler -> (status: Int, flags: Int, sampleBuffer: MediaSample?) -> Unit.

All four bodies are TODO(): MediaCodec is configured/started/stopped/released rather than prepared/invalidated, the async output callback must be registered at configure time, and there is no VTSessionSetProperties equivalent.
setProperties keeps the pure dictionary-building logic unchanged; it assumes VTSessionPropertyKey.value is a String (port of CFString) so it can key a MutableMap<String, Any?>.
@inline(__always) has no Kotlin counterpart and was dropped.
The Swift `duration _: CMTime` parameter is kept as an unused `duration: Long` to match the signature; only `.invalid` was ever passed.
No top-level Kotlin type is declared in this file; only extension functions.
Swift struct -> Kotlin class: it has mutable stored bytes plus parsing constructors, so a data class is not applicable.
Kotlin has no failable initialiser, so init?(formatDescription:) became the companion factory fromFormatDescription(formatDescription:) returning null when no avcC is available.
getAvcC() depends on CMFormatDescription atoms, which have no Android counterpart, so its body is TODO(); fromFormatDescription() therefore throws until an Android avcC source is supplied.

makeFormatDescription() cannot take an out-pointer, it returns MediaFormat? and uses csd-0/csd-1 ByteBuffers (MediaCodec parameter-set representation), null replacing kCMFormatDescriptionBridgeError_InvalidParameter.
reserveNumOfSequenceParameterSets stays a UByte and the mask arithmetic is kept identical to Swift (UByte.inv() + and).
Parsing is wrapped in runCatching/onFailure instead of do/catch, logging via Log.i with the class name as tag, matching the Swift catch branch.
ByteReader is imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util and assumed to expose readBytes(count)/readUInt8()/readUInt16() that throw on underflow.
MediaFormat.MIMETYPE_VIDEO_AVC is set because CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateFromH264ParameterSets is H.264-specific and an Android MediaFormat needs a mime type.
stroke is implemented as a Modifier extension using drawWithContent to replicate SwiftUI's shadow-based stroke.
The four shadow layers are drawn with BlurMaskFilter and PorterDuffColorFilter, offset by the stroke width.
Values are scaled by density to convert dp to pixels, matching SwiftUI's point-based coordinates.
compositingGroup() is emulated by the saveLayer compositing in drawWithContent.
The @ViewBuilder conditional is translated to an if expression returning the original modifier when width <= 0.
ElementaryStreamType and ElementaryStreamDescriptiorTag became enum classes with a UByte rawValue plus a companion fromRawValue, mirroring the Swift raw-value initializer (nullable result).
ElementaryStreamDescriptiorRegistration is an object; the String.utf8Data extension has no Kotlin counterpart so opus uses "Opus".toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8).
ElementaryStreamSpecificData is a data class; Swift's init(reader:) became a secondary constructor because ByteReader parses the wire format synchronously.
esDescriptors stays a private property declared in the class body (not a constructor parameter), matching Swift's private stored property being excluded from the memberwise initializer.
Kotlin ByteArray has no append, so += (ByteArray.plus) is used; each appendDescriptor call allocates a new array, which matches Swift Data semantics but is O(n).

ByteReader/ByteWriter are assumed to expose readUInt8(): UByte, readUInt16(): UShort, readBytes(Int): ByteArray, skipBytes(Int), writeUInt8(UByte), writeUInt16(UShort), writeBytes(ByteArray) and a data: ByteArray property, per the wire-format unsigned convention.
getDescriptor's do { while true } catch {} was translated to try/catch(Exception) returning null, so any reader failure yields null exactly like the Swift version.
The Swift name typo 'Descriptior' is preserved so both codebases stay readable side by side.
KickWebView's nested Coordinator becomes a top-level class KickWebViewCoordinator because Kotlin cannot nest a class inside the KickWebView composable function.

WKWebView is translated to androidx AndroidView with android.webkit.WebView; the per-cookie httpCookieStore API has no Android equivalent, so periodicallyCheckForAccessTokenCookie polls CookieManager.getCookie(loginUrl) and parses the session_token pair.

WKWebViewConfiguration.websiteDataStore = .nonPersistent() is approximated with CookieManager.getInstance().removeAllCookies(null) when the WebView is created; Android has no per-WebView ephemeral store.
allowsInlineMediaPlayback has no WebSettings counterpart; only mediaPlaybackRequiresUserGesture (matching mediaTypesRequiringUserActionForPlayback = .all) is applied.

Keychain call sites keep the Swift member names (store(value = ...), load(), remove(), Keychain.loadStreamIds(server = ...)); adjust the parameter names if com.moblin.android.various.Keychain differs.
MainTimer was replaced by a coroutine loop with delay(1000) on Dispatchers.Main, per the periodic-timer mapping rule.
ignoresSafeArea(.keyboard) has no direct Compose counterpart and was dropped; use Modifier.imePadding()/WindowInsets if keyboard behaviour matters.
@Binding var presenting became a value parameter presenting plus an onPresentingChange lambda; the value itself is never read in the Swift body either.

AudioPlayer is translated against android.media.MediaPlayer as the platform shim prescribes: constructor(contentsOf: String) uses the asset path returned by Bundle.url, constructor(data: ByteArray) plays through a MediaDataSource kept in a field.
The MediaDataSource subclass overrides the abstract readAt(position, buffer, offset, size) (the newer read(long, byte[], int, int) delegates to it), so the file also works on API 26.

ContinuousClock.Instant becomes java.time.Instant and duration(to:) becomes Duration.between(latestPlayTime.value, now).seconds, keeping the guard that only plays after more than 5 * 60 seconds of silence.
latestPlayTime is Atomic<Instant> from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util and is updated with latestPlayTime.mutate { it.value = Instant.now() } as the shim states.
try? AudioPlayer(contentsOf: soundUrl) is runCatching { ... }.getOrNull(), and the previous player is simply replaced exactly like Swift's optional assignment.

setDelegate stores the delegate as Any and fires the ported audioPlayerDidFinishPlaying(successfully = true) from the MediaPlayer completion listener, per the speaker keep-alive shim; the delegate is the ChatTextToSpeech instance declared alongside this file's package.
KeepSpeakerAlivePlayer.shared is a companion object val, standing in for nonisolated(unsafe) static let shared.
SwiftUI struct StreamOverlayTextView becomes a single @Composable function taking text as a parameter.
.foregroundStyle(.white) maps to the Text color parameter with Color.White.
.padding(.horizontal, 2) becomes Modifier.padding(horizontal = 2.dp).
.cornerRadius(5) becomes Modifier.clip(RoundedCornerShape(5.dp)).
backgroundColor is imported from com.moblin.android.common.various and used unchanged as the Modifier.background color.
Swift struct MuteIntent becomes a Kotlin class implementing AppIntent, with the static constants moved into a companion object of the same names.
@MainActor func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult becomes override suspend fun perform(): IntentResult, returning IntentResult.result().
@Dependency private var model becomes private val model: Model by Dependency<Model>().
model.setQuickButton(type: .mute, isOn: true) maps the Swift enum case .mute to SettingsQuickButtonType.mute from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
LocalizedStringResource is the platform typealias for String, so title and description keep their Swift literals.
No Android-side permission or UI is needed: the intent runs when its launcher shortcut is used.

AVAudioPCMBuffer has no Android type; per the media mapping it becomes a ShortArray extension function, with sampleRate and channels passed as extra parameters because they were properties of the Swift buffer.

CMAudioSampleBufferCreateWithPacketDescriptions and CMSampleBufferSetDataBufferFromAudioBufferList are replaced by building a MediaSample directly (data + presentationTimeUs + MediaFormat), which is the Android-side equivalent of a non-data-ready audio sample buffer plus attached block buffer.
CMTime presentationTimeStamp becomes Long microseconds, matching MediaSample.presentationTimeUs.
frameLength is recomputed as size / channels to mirror AVAudioPCMBuffer.frameLength (sample frames, not samples).
PCM samples are written little-endian 16-bit into a ByteArray, which is the native PCM layout expected by Android audio codecs.
The format is audio/raw with KEY_PCM_ENCODING = ENCODING_PCM_16BIT (API 24+, fine for minSdk 26).
null is returned when the buffer is empty or channels <= 0, keeping the Swift guard-let behaviour.
MediaSample is constructed with named arguments data/presentationTimeUs/isKeyFrame/format as listed in the project mapping; isKeyFrame is always true because raw PCM has no key frames.
Swift struct UnmuteIntent becomes a Kotlin class implementing AppIntent; it stays constructed with no arguments, as MoblinShortcuts does.
The three Swift static lets move into the companion object; the AppIntent interface does not declare them, so they are plain vals without override.
@MainActor func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult becomes override suspend fun perform(): IntentResult and returns IntentResult.result().
@Dependency private var model: Model becomes a property delegated by Dependency<Model>(), resolved through AppDependencyManager.

model.setMuted(value = false) and model.setQuickButton(type = SettingsQuickButtonType.mute, isOn = false) are Model members, so no import is needed for them; SettingsQuickButtonType comes from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
The two LocalizedStringResource literals are wrapped in localized() from package com.moblin.android, as every localizable String literal in this port.
perform() runs when the Android launcher shortcut for this intent is used; the body is fully ported, no TODO().
AppIntent maps to the AppIntents shim: SnapshotIntent is a plain class implementing AppIntent, with title/description/openAppWhenRun in its companion object.
@Dependency private var model: Model becomes `private val model: Model by Dependency<Model>()`, which resolves the model that was registered with AppDependencyManager.

@MainActor func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult becomes `override suspend fun perform(): IntentResult`; the TODO-free body calls the Model extension takeSnapshot() and returns IntentResult.result().
takeSnapshot() is the Model extension imported from com.moblin.android.various.model, not a member declared here.
LocalizedStringResource is a typealias of String in the shim, so the title and description strings are stored unchanged.
The declaration order of the Swift file (title, description, openAppWhenRun, perform, model) is preserved.

CMVideoFormatDescription is a CoreMedia value type; on Android it maps to android.media.MediaFormat, so the Swift extension becomes a static-only object named CMVideoFormatDescription holding the factory.
The Swift static func create(imageBuffer:) becomes CMVideoFormatDescription.create(imageBuffer) taking an android.media.Image (the CVPixelBuffer counterpart), preserving the call site shape.

There is no Android API that derives a MediaFormat from an Image: MediaFormat instances come from MediaCodec (getOutputFormat) or MediaExtractor (getTrackFormat), so the creation call and its return value are TODO().
The noErr status check and its logger.info failure message are kept as a Log.i call with tag "CMVideoFormatDescription", as required by the Logger mapping.
CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateForImageBuffer is a CoreVideo/CoreMedia function with no counterpart; nothing here is pure logic, the entire body is hardware/vendor bound.
No other Moblin types from the glossary are referenced by this file, so no cross-package imports beyond the Android framework are needed.
The failable Swift init AdtsHeader(data:) becomes a companion operator invoke(data: ByteArray, offset: Int = 0); the Data slice advanced(by:) turns into an explicit offset into the ByteArray.
UInt8/UInt16 fields stay UByte/UShort because this is ADTS wire-format parsing; every byte read goes through .toInt() and 0xFF to reproduce Swift's unsigned shifts.
The statics size and sync live in AdtsHeader.Companion; the instance property sync defaults to AdtsHeader.sync.
CMFormatDescription is replaced by android.media.MediaFormat (MIMETYPE_AUDIO_AAC plus KEY_AAC_PROFILE); AudioStreamBasicDescription fields such as mFramesPerPacket have no MediaFormat equivalent.
AudioSpecificConfig enums are rebuilt with fromRawValue from the same package; frequency.sampleRate is assumed to be Double and every rawValue is assumed UByte.
ADTSReader.makeIterator() is translated as the Iterable.iterator() override required by Kotlin.
ADTSReaderIterator.next() returns non-null Int and throws NoSuchElementException when exhausted; hasNext() re-validates the header so a corrupt frame ends iteration, matching Swift's nil return.
Equatable on AdtsHeader is preserved through data class equality.

UInt8/UInt16 stay UByte/UShort because this file parses and serialises MPEG-TS wire bytes; the shared constants live in the companion object with their Swift names (size, fixedHeaderSize, syncByte, programAssociationTableId).
The Swift throwing initialiser init(reader:) becomes a secondary constructor delegating to the primary one; Kotlin has no checked exceptions, so the read calls are simply invoked.
Swift's `throw "Invalid sync byte"` (String as Error) is mapped to IllegalStateException("Invalid sync byte") because Kotlin has no String-Error conformance.
encodeFixedHeaderInto(pointer:) took an UnsafeMutableRawBufferPointer; it now writes into a ByteArray at an explicit offset (default 0), same byte layout.
Data is ByteArray; concatenation uses the explicit form `data = data + ...` so no plus/plusAssign ambiguity is involved.
TSTimestamp and TSProgramClockReference are caseless Swift enums used as namespaces, so they become Kotlin objects; resolution stays 90 kHz and the 33-bit PTS/DTS mask 0x1_FFFF_FFFF is preserved.
decode still masks each byte with 0xFF before widening, since Kotlin's Byte is signed and would otherwise sign-extend.
The zero check `if (length > 0u)` mirrors the Swift `length > 0`; MpegTsAdaptationField(reader, length) is assumed to be the ported initialiser of the sibling type.
CMSampleBuffer extension members become top-level functions and extension functions on MediaSample in com.moblin.android.common.various, keeping the Swift declaration order.
create() is a TODO because on Android a MediaSample only comes into existence from a MediaCodec output buffer; there is no API to build one from an android.media.Image plus timestamps.
MediaSample is built with named arguments (data, presentationTimeUs, isKeyFrame, format); if com.moblin.android.media.MediaSample is a data class, copy(...) is equivalent.
setIsSync now returns a new MediaSample because MediaSample is immutable, whereas the Swift version mutated the sample attachment in place.
foreachAudioSample maps the two unsafe-pointer callbacks to (FloatArray, Int) and (ShortArray, Int) lambdas; edits are written back into the ByteArray via a native-order ByteBuffer.
PCM layout is read from MediaFormat.KEY_PCM_ENCODING, defaulting to AudioFormat.ENCODING_PCM_16BIT when the key is missing (the analogue of the mFormatFlags/mBitsPerChannel check).
createSilent replaces AVAudioFormat with sampleRate/channels, emits zeroed 16-bit PCM (AVAudioPCMBuffer -> ByteArray) and attaches a raw PCM MediaFormat.
muted() and deepCopyAudioSampleBuffer() operate on the ByteArray directly: zeroing a fresh array and copying the bytes respectively, since CMBlockBuffer has no Android counterpart.
AVFoundation import had no used symbols and was dropped; no Kotlin import is required.
UInt32 maps to UInt and Data maps to ByteArray.
The two Swift initializers become Kotlin secondary constructors, both delegating to super with RtmpMessageType.audio.
Swift 'final class' maps to a plain Kotlin 'class' (final by default).
streamId, timestamp and encoded are assigned, so they are assumed to be mutable properties inherited from RtmpMessage in the same package.
No Android APIs are involved, so the bodies are translated in full without TODO().
RtmpMessage and RtmpMessageType are declared in the same package, so no import lines are needed.
Swift UInt32 fields stay as Kotlin UInt because this is RTMP wire-format code; RtmpMessage.streamId and RtmpMessage.timestamp must use UInt in the parent class for these assignments to compile.
payload: Data maps to encoded: ByteArray, matching the RtmpMessage property name used by the second initializer.
The two Swift designated initializers become two Kotlin secondary constructors delegating to the RtmpMessage(type) superclass constructor.
The AVFoundation import is unused in the Swift source and has no counterpart here.
CMTime is represented as Long microseconds; CMTime.invalid is mapped to the new constant OptionalHeader.invalidTimestamp (Long.MIN_VALUE).
The 90kHz TSTimestamp.resolution is used to convert between microseconds and PES timestamp ticks.
OptionalHeader is a plain class with a no-arg constructor and a ByteArray constructor; Swift's implicit struct memberwise init is not reproduced.
MpegTsPacket is a reference type (class) in Kotlin, so the Swift loop that reuses a single 'packet' var now instantiates a fresh MpegTsPacket per iteration to preserve struct value semantics.
The inout Int payloadOffset buffers of the private append* helpers are replaced by passing the offset in and returning the updated value.
Swift's 'throw "Bad PES start code"' (throwing a String) becomes IllegalStateException("Bad PES start code").
Bit operations on UByte values are done through Int masks/shifts since Kotlin's UByte has no bitwise operators.
MpegTsPacket.payload slices (Data subscripts) become ByteArray.copyOfRange.
CIContext has no Android counterpart, so the constructor parameter and the private context field are typed as Any; the Core Image work itself is inside the TODO.
CVImageBuffer maps to android.media.Image; the 400 px scale used image.height/image.width of that Image.
The serial DispatchQueue is replaced by a file-private CoroutineScope backed by a single-thread executor, so image creation stays sequential.
Swift's clamped(to:) becomes Double.coerceIn(0.2, 1.0); the Float division 1 / fps is kept as Float before conversion.
weak var processor has no Kotlin equivalent; the reference is a plain nullable var, which is safe because Processor owns this object.
UInt64 frameNumber is translated as Long (counter, not wire format); adjust if ProcessorDelegate declares ULong.
streamLowFpsImage is called with named arguments matching the Swift labels lowFpsImage and frameNumber.
CVImageBuffer.isPortrait() is not in the glossary, so that branch of the scale computation lives inside the TODO("OpenGL ES port") body.
Swift extension on Model becomes a top-level extension function fun Model.setupAppIntents() in the same package.
AppDependencyManager.shared.add(dependency: self) maps to the AppIntent shim call with the explicit parameter name dependency.
No new types are declared; the extension is an import-only helper so nothing else in the file needs translating.

UIView with an AVSampleBufferDisplayLayer is replaced by android.view.TextureView: its SurfaceTexture is the target a MediaCodec decoder renders into, and it is the only Android view exposing a real Matrix transform.
Both Swift initialisers collapse into one primary constructor (context + AttributeSet); the NSCoder initialiser is dropped because Android views are inflated by the framework.
The overridden layerClass/layer members have no Android counterpart, so PreviewView simply extends TextureView.
AVLayerVideoGravity becomes a VideoGravity enum with identical raw values; the property only stores the value because Android applies scaling in the renderer, not on the view.
render() and flushAndRemoveImage() are TODO("OpenGL ES port") because turning a MediaSample into a displayed frame needs MediaCodec plus an OpenGL ES/SurfaceTexture pipeline.
CGAffineTransformMakeScale(isMirrored ? -1 : 1, 1) is translated with android.graphics.Matrix#setScale about the view centre via TextureView.setTransform, matching the CALayer anchor-point behaviour.
DispatchQueue.main.async becomes CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main).launch.
enqueue takes MediaSample instead of CMSampleBuffer.
The generic SwiftUI view SwiftUI View with Content/Content2 builders becomes a single @Composable CacheAsyncImage taking two slot lambdas (content, placeholder).
URL maps to java.net.URI: it is both the cache key and the source for the OkHttp request.
SwiftUI's AsyncImage is not part of Compose, so loading is done with OkHttp + BitmapFactory on Dispatchers.IO; no third-party image library was assumed.
The @MainActor global cache becomes a file-private val with @Synchronized get/set, keeping the in-memory, process-lifetime semantics.
