The cache stores androidx.compose.ui.graphics.ImageBitmap instead of SwiftUI.Image; callers draw it with Image(bitmap = it).
The scale parameter is kept for signature parity but has no effect because content is a composable slot.
The placeholder slot is rendered while the download is in flight and when it fails, matching AsyncImage's placeholder behaviour.
The load runs in LaunchedEffect(url) so re-composition with the same URL does not refetch, and a successful load is stored into the shared cache.
NWWebSocket/WebSocketConnection are replaced by OkHttp WebSocket + WebSocketListener; every listener callback is marshalled onto Dispatchers.Main to reproduce Swift's @MainActor isolation.
The `delegate` property keeps Swift's `weak` semantics through a WeakReference-backed property that still exposes the original name and type.
The stored `URL` becomes a plain String because it is only handed to OkHttp.

Each connection attempt builds a fresh OkHttpClient with pingInterval(10, SECONDS) (the NWProtocolWebSocket.Options.autoReplyPing equivalent) and sends `protocols` through the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header, as OkHttp has no setSubprotocols call.

NetworkInterfaceTypeSelector is used only as an availability check: OkHttp cannot bind a socket to a chosen NWInterface.InterfaceType, so the loopback override is dropped (loopback hosts are reached through the URL). The constructor is called as NetworkInterfaceTypeSelector(Dispatchers.Main, cellular).
`webSocket` starts as null instead of an idle NWWebSocket instance, so send() before start() is a no-op instead of queueing onto an unconnected socket.
MainTimer from com.moblin.android.various is reused unchanged; this file assumes startSingleShot(timeout, function), startPeriodic(interval, initial, function) and stop().
webSocketDidReceivePong has no caller because OkHttp does not surface pong frames, and the manual ping path is marked TODO because OkHttp owns ping/pong via pingInterval.
URL.documentsDirectory.appending(component:) becomes a File under AppDelegate.context.filesDir, stored as a String path in the global faceBackgroundImagePath.
Model is an ObservableObject, so the @Published faceBackgroundImage is read and written as a MutableStateFlow: faceBackgroundImage.value = ...
try? Data(contentsOf:) and try? data.write(to:) become runCatching { File(...).readBytes() }.getOrNull() and runCatching { File(...).writeBytes(data) }.
UIImage(data:) is the platform shim from com.moblin.android.platform.uikit and returns a Bitmap?, whose .cgImage identity extension feeds CIImage(cgImage = ...).
The nonisolated keyword is dropped; Kotlin has no actor isolation.
The Swift extension on Model becomes top-level extension functions in the same package, so Model itself needs no import.
updateFaceFilterSettings() is expected to exist as a Model extension in another file of this package and is called unchanged.

`@MainActor` on the protocol and the class has no Kotlin equivalent; delegate callbacks are dispatched on a private `CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main)` so the main-thread isolation of the Swift code is preserved.

`CIImage(data:)` becomes `BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray`, and `FaxReceiverDelegate.faxReceiverPrint` now takes an `android.graphics.Bitmap`. Core Image is not involved here (no filtering or rendering), so no Metal/OpenGL ES TODO is needed.
`weak var delegate` becomes a plain nullable property; Kotlin needs `java.lang.ref.WeakReference` for weak semantics, which was left to the caller to avoid inventing behaviour.
`URL` is only used to build the request, so it is mapped to `String` per the type mapping table.

`httpRequest` is Moblin's helper from `com.moblin.android.various.network`; the completion is assumed to deliver `(ByteArray?, NetworkResponse?, Throwable?)` and the request is built with `okhttp3.Request`. Adjust the argument/parameter shape if the real signature differs.
`response?.http?.isSuccessful` is assumed to keep the same shape it had on the Swift `NetworkResponse`.
The `CoreImage` and `ImagePlayground` imports are dropped; neither is used by the translated logic.
The Swift extension on Model becomes top-level Kotlin extension functions on Model in the same package.
isKeyboardActive() is a plain predicate; the createStreamWizard sub-flags are read directly off the model.
DispatchQueue.main.async is replaced by a private file-scoped mainScope CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main).
handleKeyPressCharacters uses firstOrNull + early return instead of guard let.

SwiftUI's KeyPress / KeyPress.Result has no Android counterpart, so a minimal placeholder class KeyPress with a nested Result enum keeps the original signature; real key events must be bridged from Compose key events.
The @available(iOS 17.0, *) attribute is dropped; Kotlin has no visibility into OS version here.
No imports are needed for Model, ShowingPanel or the other peer types because they live in this same package.
handleControllerFunction is called with named arguments to mirror the Swift parameter labels.
Class name typo "RtmpAbortMessge" (missing 'a' in Message) is preserved verbatim from Swift.
`Data` maps to `ByteArray`; array equality uses `contentEquals` because ByteArray has no `==`.
`chunkStreamId` stays an unsigned `UInt` since it is a 32-bit wire-format field.
The Swift `UInt32.bigEndian.data` and `UInt32(data:)` extension helpers are not in the glossary, so they are inlined as explicit big-endian read/write of the first 4 bytes.
`override var encoded` reads and writes `super.encoded`, i.e. the base class accessors, avoiding recursion.
Swift `init()` calling `super.init(type: .abort)` becomes a secondary constructor `constructor() : super(RtmpMessageType.abort)`.
No apple-only APIs are used here, so nothing is replaced with TODO().
The Swift `extension Model` becomes top-level Kotlin extension functions on Model in the same package; no type is redeclared.

`URL.documentsDirectory.appending(component:)` has no context-free Android equivalent, so the top-level `stealthModeImagePath` getter is TODO() that resolves to File(context.filesDir, "stealthModeImage.img").
`Data` becomes ByteArray; `try? data.write(to:)` becomes runCatching { file.writeBytes(data) } so a failed write is silently ignored as in Swift.
`loadStealthModeImage` decodes the stored bytes with android.graphics.BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray and assigns null when the file is missing, matching the guard-let early return.
`UIImage` is mapped to android.graphics.Bitmap, which is the expected type of StealthMode.image in this port.
`FileManager.default.removeItem(at:)` becomes File.delete(), which also reports failure via its Boolean result instead of throwing.
RemoteControlState is not part of the provided glossary, so it is referenced by name from the same package as Model without being redeclared.
This file contains no SwiftUI views, so no @Composable functions are produced despite the ui tier.
Kotlin has no `super.property` access, so the overridden `encoded` uses a private `_encoded` backing field; the base class stores nothing else for this property, so it is equivalent.
`size` is kept as `UInt` because `UInt32` is wire-format data.
Added file-private helpers `uint32ToBigEndianBytes` and `readUInt32BigEndian` to replace the HaishinKit `UInt32.bigEndian.data` and `UInt32(data:)` conversions.
Assumes `RtmpMessage` exposes `open var encoded: ByteArray` and a constructor taking `RtmpMessageType`; the override follows Android's `: View { constructor() : super(...) }` delegation pattern.
The two Swift initializers become two secondary Kotlin constructors, since the base constructor requires an argument.
The `import AVFoundation` line is dropped: no AVFoundation API is actually used in this file.
Getter returns the existing bytes when non-empty, otherwise encodes `size`; setter early-returns on equal bytes and decodes `size` from the first four big-endian bytes.
CMFormatDescription maps to android.media.MediaFormat; the HEVC parameter sets are carried in the "csd-0" byte buffer as the ISO/IEC 14496-15 hvcC box.
getHvcC() reads csd-0 and strips the 8-byte hvcC box header (size + 'hvcC' type) when it is present, returning the raw configuration record the parser expects.
init?(formatDescription:) becomes the companion factory create(formatDescription:) because Kotlin has no failable constructors; callers must null-check the result.
The raw hvcC record is kept in an extra private property (hvcC) so makeFormatDescription() can rebuild the complete hvcC box for csd-0.
kCMFormatDescriptionBridgeError_InvalidParameter is kept as a private Int placeholder; on Android any non-zero return value means the format could not be created.
logger.info maps to android.util.Log.i with the class name as tag.
ByteReader is assumed to throw on truncated input, matching the Swift do/catch around the whole loop.
The exact csd-0 hvcC box layout should be verified against the target MediaCodec HEVC decoder during device integration.

AVPictureInPictureController, its ContentSource, AVPictureInPictureSampleBufferPlaybackDelegate and CMVideoDimensions come from the AVKit shim (platform/avkit), which shows the stream preview in an Activity picture-in-picture window: auto-enter on API 31+, enterPictureInPictureMode on user leave before.
setupPictureInPicture(), updatePictureInPicture() and pictureInPictureEnabled() are top-level extension functions on Model reading pipController, stream, isLive and isRecording like Swift.

Kotlin extensions cannot add interface conformance, so the delegate methods are Model extensions and the private ModelPictureInPicturePlaybackDelegate forwards to them; it is passed as playbackDelegate where Swift passes self.
CMTimeRange is the avfoundation shim's CMTimeRange with Long microseconds, Long.MIN_VALUE/Long.MAX_VALUE for negative/positive infinity; skipByInterval is Long microseconds.
The no-op delegate callbacks keep empty bodies and skipByInterval invokes the completion callback, preserving the Swift behaviour.
StoreKit has no Android counterpart; every function that touches StoreKit products or transactions got the body TODO("no Android counterpart for StoreKit").
struct Icon -> data class Icon(name, id, price) keeping both helper functions imageNoBackground() and image(); Swift's Identifiable has no Kotlin equivalent, equals/hashCode come from the data class.
The Model extension becomes top-level extension functions on Model in com.moblin.android.various.model, matching the original declaration order.
listenForAppStoreTransactions() returned Task<Void, any Error>; it now takes a CoroutineScope and returns the Job of the launched coroutine.
checkVerified(result:) used Swift's opaque VerificationResult<StoreKit.Transaction>; its parameter and return type are Any? because those StoreKit types do not exist in the port.
purchaseProduct(id:) and restorePurchases() were async throws; Kotlin has no checked exceptions, so they stay plain suspend functions (their bodies are TODO).
The global logger is replaced by a file-private Log tag constant named TAG with value "Model".
updateIcons(myProductIds:) keeps its full loop and store bookkeeping; only the Icon built from StoreKit product metadata (displayName/displayPrice/id) is a TODO.
needs_user: StoreKit: Product.products(for:), Transaction.updates, VerificationResult, AppStore.sync(), Product.purchase(), Transaction.currentEntitlements, Transaction.finish() (needs Google Play Billing and the icon products in the Play Console)

notes: WebBrowserState keeps its name; @Published isSmall becomes a MutableStateFlow exposed as StateFlow plus setIsSmall(value) for the views that toggle it.
The Model extension becomes top-level extension functions on Model in this package (loadWebBrowserUrl, loadWebBrowserHome, loadWebBrowserPage, getWebBrowser, setWebBrowserProxy).
WKWebView maps to android.webkit.WebView, so webBrowserUrl becomes a String and getWebBrowserUrl returns String? (WebView.loadUrl takes a String, not a URL object).
URL scheme detection uses java.net.URI with runCatching, matching Swift's URL(string:) leniency; the search fallback is built by string interpolation as in Swift.
The WKNavigationDelegate method becomes Model.webViewDidStartProvisionalNavigation and is wired in through a WebViewClient.onPageStarted override installed by getWebBrowser().
getWebBrowser() needs a Context to build android.webkit.WebView; Model does not expose one in this file, so the Context argument is a TODO that must be filled in.
mainScope is a file-private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) used for the DispatchQueue.main.async call.
WKWebViewConfiguration.setHttpProxy and WKUIDelegate have no Android counterpart and are TODO placeholders.
CrtEffect is final in Swift, so the Kotlin class is a plain class extending VideoEffect().
CrtBarrelDistortionFilter.outputImage is declared as Any?, so it is cast back with `as? CIImage` before the Swift `?? image` fallback.
CrtBarrelDistortionFilter.width is a Float while Swift's CGFloat becomes Double, so the width argument is converted with toFloat().
Swift CGFloat values (extent.width, cropRect.height) become Double throughout; Core Image filter scalar properties stay Float as declared by the shims.
CIColor literals are written with Double values (0.0, 0.25) because the shim has no Int constructor overload.
scanlineWidth keeps Swift's Float computation with maxOf(1.0f, ...).
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped.
stripes.center = .zero becomes CGPoint.zero and CGAffineTransform(rotationAngle: .pi / 2) becomes CGAffineTransform(rotationAngle = PI / 2).
Swift final class maps to a plain Kotlin class extending VideoEffect; the @unchecked Sendable conformance is dropped because Kotlin has no Sendable.
The Swift `.init(content:position:size:)` shorthand inside the layers array becomes an explicit MTILayer(...) with named arguments.
`.black` on MTIImage resolves to the MTIImage.black companion value; `CIImage.black` keeps its platform name.
CGRect is built with the (x, y, width, height) labelled constructor using Double values (0.0 instead of the Int literal 0 to avoid overload ambiguity).
`filter.outputImage ?? image` stays as `filter.outputImage ?: image`.
The unused VideoEffectInfo parameters are named `info` to satisfy the platform signature.
TripleEffect is a final Swift class, so it becomes a plain class extending VideoEffect() and keeps its two CIFilter instances as reusable properties.

The project's CIImage.translated(x:y:) helper is not part of the Core Image shim, so both calls are written as transformed(by: CGAffineTransform(translationX = x, y = 0.0)), the exact equivalent of that helper.
Swift's unused second parameter (_) becomes the named parameter info, matching VideoEffect's Kotlin signature.
The MetalPetal path builds filter.layers from a (0 until 3).map { } range, exactly as the Swift (0 ..< 3).map does.
@unchecked Sendable is dropped; Kotlin has no concurrency annotation counterpart here.
CGSize/CGRect/CGPoint are the platform CoreGraphics shims with Double fields, so width and height stay Double and index + 0.5 promotes to Double.
No TODO() is needed: every call used here exists in the Core Image and MetalPetal shims.

Swift `final class MovieEffect: VideoEffect` becomes a plain `class MovieEffect : VideoEffect()` with `override fun` members; the `@unchecked Sendable` conformance is dropped since Kotlin has no Sendable protocol.

The Swift `execute(_ image: CIImage, _: VideoEffectInfo)` shape is translated to the declared base signature `override fun execute(image: CIImage, info: VideoEffectInfo): CIImage`, keeping the same call sites.
Core Image chain stays as shim calls: `cropped(to:)`, `composited(over:)` and `CIImage.black` are unchanged apart from named arguments.

MTIImage array elements written as `.init(content:position:size:)` become explicit `MTILayer(content = …, position = …, size = …)` constructors, using MetalPetal's defaults for the remaining parameters.
`filter.layers` takes a `List<MTILayer>`, so the Swift array literal is a `listOf(...)`.
`filter.outputImage ?? image` keeps the MetalPetal fallback as the Kotlin elvis operator.
CGRect/CGSize/CGPoint come from com.moblin.android.platform.coregraphics and take Double fields, so the Swift CGFloat arithmetic is unchanged.
The Swift diff only adds the @Published property nativeLowLightBoost; only the 4 matching Kotlin spots were touched.
nativeLowLightBoost is @Published, so it became val nativeLowLightBoost = MutableStateFlow(false) placed right after allowVideoRangePixelFormat, matching the Swift member order.

The hand-written SettingsDebugSerializer was extended by appending the new element as index 33 (element, encode call, decode branch) instead of inserting it at position 11, so no existing index had to be renumbered and every untouched line stays byte-identical.

Because the serializer uses keyed (named) elements, the added field appearing last in the descriptor/JSON keeps the JSON key name nativeLowLightBoost; iOS-written JSON containing that key still decodes and JSON without it falls back to false, like the Swift container.decode(..., false) default.
SwiftUI Text with an empty string and a full-size frame becomes a Box with Modifier.fillMaxSize() wrapping an empty Text.
.background(.black.opacity(0.01)) maps to Modifier.background(Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.01f)).
.onTapGesture(count: 2) maps to Modifier.pointerInput(Unit) { detectTapGestures(onDoubleTap = { ... }) }.
model is passed in as a Compose parameter exactly like the SwiftUI View property; toggleLockScreen() is called directly on it.
No state or navigation is needed, so no remember or onNavigate parameter is introduced.
Snapshot's published properties are modelled as StateFlow and read with collectAsState().
The Swift `if let ... && countdown > 0` guard becomes an early return on the collected nullable job and a countdown check.
`.frame(maxWidth: 300)` maps to Modifier.widthIn(max = 300.dp); `.fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)` has no direct Compose equivalent and is covered by wrapping content sizing.
`.font(.title)` becomes MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge.
`.multilineTextAlignment(.center)` becomes textAlign = TextAlign.Center.
`.background(.black.opacity(0.75))` becomes Modifier.background(Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.75f)).
`.cornerRadius(10)` becomes Modifier.clip(RoundedCornerShape(10.dp)).
@MainActor on getOrientation/isPhone/isPad/getWindow/getRootViewController/screenScale is dropped; the Kotlin functions are plain and are called from the main thread.
getOrientation's body starts at the interface orientation, as specified: the port's platform hook prepends the com.moblin.android.platform.uikit.UIDevice.current.orientation check before it.
This file declares object UIDevice (vibration only), which shadows the UIKit UIDevice, so the UIKit one is referenced fully qualified as com.moblin.android.platform.uikit.UIDevice.

DeviceOrientation mirrors UIDeviceOrientation with UPPER_SNAKE entries; UIInterfaceOrientation.landscapeLeft maps to LANDSCAPE_RIGHT and landscapeRight to LANDSCAPE_LEFT, exactly as the Swift switch does.
interface Identifiable<ID> { val id: ID } is declared here because Kotlin has no standard-library equivalent, and makeOffsets is generic over it.
makeOffsets returns Int? (the index) instead of IndexSet?, matching the shape its callers use.
UIImage.resize(height:) becomes Bitmap.resize(height: Float) with Bitmap.createScaledBitmap at 1x instead of UIGraphicsImageRenderer, as the port specifies.
screenScale() returns Float and keeps the UIScreen.main.scale fallback; isMac() is always false and ProcessInfo is not instantiated.

Swift's CIImage `translated(x:y:)` and `scaled(x:y:)` helpers are not declared in the Kotlin platform layer, so both are written with the declared `transformed(by = CGAffineTransform(...))`, which produces the identical matrices.
`@unchecked Sendable` is dropped; the effect is executed on the pipeline thread only, as in Swift.
The private `CIFilter.sourceOverCompositing()` instance is reused across frames, exactly like the Swift stored `filter` property (it is only mutated on the pipeline thread).
`CGRect`, `CGSize` and `CGPoint` come from com.moblin.android.platform.coregraphics and hold Double values, so `width` and `height` are Double and feed `CGAffineTransform` directly.

MTILayers are built with the Kotlin constructor's named parameters `content`, `contentRegion`, `contentFlipOptions`, `position`, `size`, and `contentFlipOptions` uses `MTILayer.FlipOptions.flipHorizontally` instead of `.flipHorizontally`.
`filter.outputImage ?? image` becomes `filter.outputImage ?: image`, keeping the Core Image / MetalPetal fallback.
NavigationLink destinations become an onNavigate: (String) -> Unit callback using the destination view name as the route string.
.navigationTitle is rendered with a Scaffold plus a Material 3 TopAppBar (requires @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)).
Form and ScrollView both map to LazyColumn; ForEach maps to LazyListScope.items with the attribution name as key.
.font(.title2) maps to MaterialTheme.typography.headlineSmall.
Purely layout-driving Spacer() views from the SwiftUI HStack/LazyVStack were dropped since LazyColumn already fills the screen.
The Swift `private let` attribution tables are kept as private top-level vals so they stay file-scoped, matching the Swift visibility.
The Attribution struct has only stored properties and became a private data class.
The trailing space in "Credit Richie Velasquez " is preserved verbatim.
WatchDisplaySettingsView becomes a single @Composable function with the same name; the SwiftUI Form/Section is rendered as a LazyColumn inside a Scaffold.

The NavigationLink destination is expressed through the onNavigate callback with the destination name "WatchLocalOverlaysSettingsView"; no navigation-compose dependency is added here (the destination composable lives in com.moblin.android.view.settings.watch.display.localoverlays).
navigationTitle("Display") is mapped to a Material 3 TopAppBar title inside Scaffold.
The show: WatchSettingsShow parameter is kept so the call site signature matches, even though this screen no longer forwards it (the destination receives it from the nav graph).
WatchSettingsShow is not listed in the glossary; it is imported from com.moblin.android.model. Adjust that import if the model lives in a different Moblin package.
TopAppBar requires the ExperimentalMaterial3Api opt-in.
Material 3 ListItem replaces the plain Form row plus its chevron.
This file contains no SwiftUI Views (only an unused SwiftUI import), so no @Composable functions are generated even though the tier is 'ui'.
getReplaysDirectory() now returns java.io.File and assumes the shared helper is createAndGetDirectory(name: String).

ReplaysDatabase.replays is a read-only StateFlow backed by a private MutableStateFlow; because the Swift code mutated the @Published array directly, an added setReplays(...) is used for all mutations. Views should read it with collectAsState().

Hand-written Codable is replaced by kotlinx.serialization through a private ReplaysDatabaseDto that keeps the 'replays' coding key; Json is configured with ignoreUnknownKeys + encodeDefaults to match JSONDecoder/JSONEncoder behaviour.
java.util.UUID has no built-in kotlinx.serialization serializer, so a private UUIDSerializer (string based) is attached to ReplaySettings.id.
toString()/fromString(settings:) keep their Swift names; toString() overrides Any.toString and may throw SerializationException.
FileManager.enumerator is replaced by File.walkTopDown() and URL.resolvingSymlinksInPath() by File.canonicalFile.
Assumes the sibling SimpleStringStorage exposes get(): String and set(String).
AddButtonView is a stateless view, so it becomes a @Composable function taking the Swift closure as a Kotlin lambda.
TextButtonView comes from the same package com.moblin.android.view.utils and is called with (text, action); adjust the argument names if that helper's signature differs.
No state, no lifecycle effects and no navigation, so the body is a single call.
SwiftUI Canvas becomes Compose Canvas; the draw commands use DrawScope with Path.moveTo/lineTo and drawPath with Stroke.
cameraLevel.angle is a @Published Double? in the model, so it is read with collectAsState() and unwrapped via an early `return@Canvas` instead of `guard let`.
CGFloat sizes map to Float inside DrawScope, so cos/sin results are converted with toFloat().
Color.yellow/.white become Compose Color.Yellow/.White.
.allowsHitTesting(false) has no Compose equivalent and was dropped; a Canvas without pointerInput does not consume touches anyway.
The whole drawing body sits inside the Canvas lambda, one @Composable function per SwiftUI View with the same name.
Top-level Swift global colorMatrix becomes a file-private val of the same name holding an MTIColorMatrix built from four SIMD4 columns.
Swift 'final class SepiaEffect' maps to a plain Kotlin class extending VideoEffect(); the Swift 'override init()' becomes an init block that sets filterMetalPetal.colorMatrix.
CIFilter.sepiaTone() keeps its name and the CISepiaTone shim's inputImage/intensity members; intensity 0.9 is written as 0.9f.
execute and executeMetalPetal keep the ?? image fallbacks on outputImage.
MTIColorMatrixFilter is a MetalPetal shim class, so no MetalPetal context or TODO is needed.

The iOS 18 `moveSubranges`/`#available(iOS 18, *)` branch of `removeNalUnitStartCodes` is re-implemented with a source copy plus System.arraycopy into a new buffer of size dataLength *+ 3-byte start code count*, which is the AVCC to Annex-B length rewrite.
All byte comparisons mask with `and 0xFF` because Kotlin's Byte is signed, whereas Swift's Data subscript returns UInt8.
`nalUnitStartCode` is a top-level `val ByteArray` in this package, matching the Swift global.

ExternalButtonView and ExternalUrlButtonView take their Swift @ViewBuilder content as a @Composable () -> Unit parameter.
Section { } has no direct Compose container here, so the wrapped content is emitted as a Column.
Image(systemName: "arrow.turn.up.right") maps to Icon(Icons.Default.ArrowForward, contentDescription = null).
openUrl is imported from com.moblin.android.various.utils and called with the url argument.
Changed createEventSubSubscription to pass the full OperationResult through instead of collapsing it to Boolean.
Added sendShoutout posting to chat/shoutouts with from_broadcaster_id, to_broadcaster_id and moderator_id.
Everything else in the Kotlin file is unchanged, including the hand-written OkHttp, coroutine and json handling.
UIImage/CGContext/CALayer rendering is replaced by android.graphics.Bitmap + Canvas, and SDWebImage loading by OkHttp + BitmapFactory.
android.graphics.Movie exposes no per-frame timing, so animated emote frames are sampled at 15 fps across the clip's total duration (animatedFrameRate).
EmotesPlayer.shared is a companion getter that requires EmotesPlayer.initialize(context) before first use, so it can resolve bundled drawables.
CADisplayLink is replaced by a coroutine loop on Dispatchers.Main ticking every ~66 ms.
sizesVersion is exposed as a StateFlow of Int and incremented by the load callbacks.
EmoteUiView is a plain state-holder class; layoutSubviews became onSizeChanged, while the sibling @Composable EmoteUiView(...) draws the frame and drives register/unregister.
EmoteBorder and EmoteKey are internal instead of private because EmotesPlayer's internal members expose them in their signatures.
ChatImageSource.Symbol cannot resolve a dynamic icon name on Android, so its render branch is TODO().
HevcNalUnitType keeps its Swift raw values as UByte and gains a companion fromRawValue plus the static isPicture helper.
Swift's enum-with-associated-values HevcNalUnitPayload became a sealed class; vps/sps/pps/prefixSeiNut are nested classes holding their value in a `payload` property, unspec is an object.

The failable Swift init?(data:offset:) has no Kotlin constructor counterpart, so it is a companion operator fun invoke(data, offset): HevcNalUnit? which keeps the HevcNalUnit(data, offset) call shape.
HevcNalUnitHeader's throwing reader initialiser is a companion operator fun invoke(reader) so HevcNalUnitHeader(reader) keeps the same call shape.

NalUnitReader.readBits/skipBits and NalUnitWriter.writeBit/writeBits/bitOffset/data are assumed to come from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg with UByte bit values, mirroring the Swift UInt8 parameters.

The [HevcNalUnit] extension became a top-level extension on List<HevcNalUnit>; CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateFromHEVCParameterSets has no Android equivalent so the format description creation is TODO().
The file-global 'calendar' maps to a java.util.Calendar pinned to UTC (Swift Calendar(identifier: .iso8601) with UTC time zone).
writeRbspTrailingBits and writeMoreDataInPayload are unchanged top-level functions.
Only the new sortedBySearchPrefix helper was added after makeUniqueName, before createSpeechSynthesizer.
Everything else stays byte-identical to the current Kotlin file.
Swift hasPrefix/lowercased map to Kotlin startsWith/lowercase on the String name, matching the stable part of a search string.
The name closure keeps the same generic shape as the Swift trailing/parameter closure.
SwiftUI Form/Section with footer becomes a LazyColumn whose last item is the footer Text.
navigationTitle is rendered as a Material 3 TopAppBar inside a Scaffold.
The Swift trailing-closure argument of ExternalUrlButtonView is passed as the trailing @Composable content lambda.
The multi-line Swift string literal (joined with a backslash) is written as a single concatenated localised string.
@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class) is required for TopAppBar.
The view takes no parameters, matching the Swift struct's empty property list.
DispatchQueue is replaced by a single thread Executor dispatcher (srtClientQueue) plus a CoroutineScope (srtClientScope); every queue.async block becomes srtClientScope.launch { }.

libsrt C calls are declared as external functions on a new SrtNative object (SRT_INVALID_SOCK and SRT_ERROR are both -1); the native library still has to be loaded once elsewhere with System.loadLibrary.

sockaddrIn builds the 16 byte sockaddr_in layout (AF_INET, big endian port, 4 byte address resolved through InetAddress) and hands the ByteArray to SrtNative.srt_connect, which assumes the JNI layer accepts a byte array for the sockaddr pointer.

The Swift 'extension SrtClient: MpegTsReaderDelegate' is merged into the class body because Kotlin cannot satisfy interface members with extension functions; the reader delegate methods take MediaSample instead of CMSampleBuffer.
delegate is stored as a plain nullable field because Kotlin has no weak property; callers must clear it themselves if needed.
URL is parsed with java.net.URI (host and port); a port of -1 means the URL has no port, matching the failed guard-let path.

SimpleTimer.startSingleShot(timeout = ..., block), Atomic.mutate { }, BitrateStats.add(bytesTransferred = ...) and BitrateStats.update() signatures are taken from the shared Moblin files and assumed unchanged.
srtClientLatency stays a Double seconds constant and is passed to MpegTsReader(targetLatency = ...) exactly like the Swift code.
Swift `weak var server: RistServer?` becomes a plain nullable `var server` because Kotlin has no weak stored properties for arbitrary classes; callers must clear it themselves.
The `MpegTsReaderDelegate` conformance moves from a Swift extension to the class header; the two callback methods become `override fun`.
`CMSampleBuffer` becomes `MediaSample` from `com.moblin.android.media`; `Data` becomes `ByteArray`; `UUID` stays `java.util.UUID`.
`try reader.handlePacketFromClient(...)` is expressed with `runCatching { }` plus `onFailure`, matching `try`/`catch` without forcing a `@Throws` signature.
`logger.info` becomes `android.util.Log.i` with the class name as tag.
`MpegTsReader` and `ristServerQueue` are imported from `com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg` and the current package respectively; nothing is redeclared here.
The delegate forwarding uses safe calls so a detached server silently drops buffers, matching Swift optional chaining.
UInt16 ports and virtual destination ports become Int; they are keys, delegate parameters and log values rather than wire-format byte fields.
The failable Swift init? never returns nil, so it becomes a plain Kotlin constructor (callers can drop force unwraps).
ristServerQueue is a serial (single-thread) coroutine dispatcher so the ordering guarantees of the Swift serial DispatchQueue are preserved; start/stop/peer events run as coroutines on it.

RistReceiverContext and RistReceiverContextDelegate come from the iOS 'Rist' Swift package and have no glossary entry, so they are declared in this file with TODO() bodies for start()/stop(); the delegate callbacks must be driven by the native librist binding.

Atomic<BitrateStats>.mutate is assumed to return the lambda result (needed by updateStats) and Atomic.value is assumed settable (used by clientsChanged); adjust imports/usage if com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util.Atomic exposes a different surface.
CMSampleBuffer delegate parameters become MediaSample from com.moblin.android.media.
Logging uses android.util.Log with the tag "RistServer" (the class name).
stopInternal iterates over a snapshot of the client keys (keys.toList()), matching Swift's value-semantics Dictionary iteration while those keys are removed afterwards.
This file exists only for macCatalyst; Android has no status-item bridge, so the helper entry points keep their signatures with TODO() bodies.
The MoblinMac plugin types MacStatusItem and MacStatusItemDelegate have no counterpart and no glossary entry, so minimal Kotlin interfaces are declared in this file.
macStatusItem is a stored Model property in Swift (extensions cannot store properties); here it is a top-level extension property on Model backed by a WeakHashMap.
makeMacStatusItemStatusTitle() is translated in full because it only joins localized strings.
String(localized:) maps to localized() imported from com.moblin.android.
logger.info maps to Log.i with the tag "Model".
The Swift #else branch (empty stubs) is represented by the same three function names; their bodies are TODO because the macCatalyst plugin bundle cannot be loaded on Android.
apple_only: NSBundle.main.builtInPlugInsURL / Bundle(url:) / principalClass plugin bundle loading (MoblinMac.bundle)
macCatalyst NSStatusItem bridge (MacStatusItem helper object)
UIImage(named:)?.pngData() icon encoding
MacStatusItemDelegate conformance declared from an extension

notes: ThermalStateView is a SwiftUI struct: it becomes a @Composable function with the same name, an extra trailing Modifier parameter and thermalState kept first.
Image(systemName: "flame") with .font(.system(size: 11)) and .foregroundStyle(...) is the platform SystemImage composable with fontSize = 11.sp and tint = thermalState.color().
ProcessInfo.ThermalState comes from com.moblin.android.platform.core and keeps its Swift case names (nominal, fair, serious, critical).
thermalState.color() is the existing Kotlin extension fun ProcessInfo.ThermalState.color(): Color; it is imported from the same com.moblin.android.common.view package as this view.
compactAudioLevelColors returns Pair<Color, Color> because Kotlin has no tuples; callers use .first/.second (Swift callers destructure the tuple).
Image(systemName:) is resolved by the private helper compactAudioLevelIcon, mapping the SF Symbol speaker/mic names to Material Icons.Filled.VolumeUp/VolumeDown/VolumeOff/VolumeMute.
.foregroundStyle(foregroundColor) becomes the Icon tint parameter.
.font(smallFont) has no effect on a Material Icon, which is sized purely by Modifier.size(17.dp); it is therefore not applied.
.contentShape(Rectangle()) only widens the hit-test region and has no Compose counterpart; it is dropped (no gesture is attached in this file).
.padding(20) followed by .padding(-20) only expands the tap area in SwiftUI; Compose rejects negative padding, so both are dropped and the wrapped layout is unchanged.
clippingThresholdDb/redThresholdDb/yellowThresholdDb/zeroThresholdDb/defaultAudioLevel stay top-level Float vals in the same package so other files keep the same names.
The composable parameter backgroundColor intentionally shadows the package-level backgroundColor color, exactly as in the Swift struct.
Enum cases beforeIcon/afterIcon/hide became PascalCase entries BeforeIcon/AfterIcon/Hide; comparison kept identical.
The row is Compose Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(1.dp)) with vertical centering, matching HStack(spacing: 1).
Image(systemName: icon) uses a dynamic SF Symbol name, so there is no Material icon to substitute; the painter is TODO() and listed as unsupported.
.font(smallFont) applied to StreamOverlayTextView is passed as the child composable's style parameter; smallFont is imported from com.moblin.android.common.various.
color has default Color.White and iconBackgroundColor defaults to the imported top-level backgroundColor val from com.moblin.android.common.various.

Icon sizing chain maps to Modifier.size(17.dp, 17.dp).padding(horizontal = 2.dp).clip(RoundedCornerShape(5.dp)).background(iconBackgroundColor) so the background is clipped like Swift's .cornerRadius(5).
Swift's .contentShape(Rectangle()) plus .padding(-20) hit-area expansion has no Compose counterpart (negative padding is not supported); it is left as TODO().
enum case names differ in casing only, so the Swift and Kotlin sources can still be read side by side.

The four private enums with associated values (PublishMessage, SubscribeTopic, Message, MessageToMoblin, MessageToBrowser) became private sealed classes with hand-written JsonObject encode/decode that match Swift's synthesized Codable shape ({"caseName":{...}}, optional associated values omitted).
ChatPostSegment/ChatPostUrl are encoded by hand into id/text/url/bigGifUrl (url: {moving, still}) instead of relying on a serializer, because their Kotlin ports are not shown as @Serializable.
JSON is parsed and printed with codableJson; MessageToBrowser.toJson returns null when encoding fails, like Swift's try?.
moblinScript() calls loadStringResource("moblin", "js") from com.moblin.android.various.utils in place of Bundle.main url+Data.
NSObject, weak and @MainActor are dropped; the delegate is a plain nullable property.
DispatchQueue.main.async became CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main.immediate).launch.
logger.info/debug became Log.i/Log.d with the tag "BrowserEffectServer".
The class implements WKScriptMessageHandler in its header (the Swift extension) and is open with open members because the Swift class is not final.
ChatLineContent gains `var font: SettingsFont = SettingsFont()` at the same position as the Swift property.
New private makeBaseFont(content, bold) builds the Typeface from content.font.family / content.font.name(), falling back to the design family and weight.
makeFont now calls makeBaseFont, then adds ITALIC and (bold && family != nil || italic) BOLD via Typeface.create(base, style), mirroring the SymbolicTraits logic.
makeLayout now sets basePaint.typeface from makeBaseFont(content = content) instead of the hard-coded default Typeface.
Typeface carries no size on Android, so the font size stays on the paint (textSize = content.fontSize), as in the rest of this port.
UIFont(name:size:) returning nil has no direct equivalent; Typeface.create(name, style) falls back to the default typeface instead, so the two branches of makeBaseFont both produce a Typeface.
SettingsFont is imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings; `family` and `name()` keep their Swift names.
No Apple framework API is newly introduced by this change.
CMTime is ported to Long microseconds: `.invalid` becomes the sentinel Long.MIN_VALUE and `.zero` becomes 0L.

AVAudioPCMBuffer is replaced by the new PcmBuffer type (ByteArray + frameLength) because the original does raw memcpy of int16/int32/float32 samples, interleaved or planar; ShortArray alone could not express all three sample formats.
The AVAudioFormat stored in `format` is replaced by the new PcmAudioFormat type which carries sampleRate, channels, isInterleaved and commonFormat plus derived bytesPerSample/bytesPerFrame.
AudioStreamBasicDescription/`kAudioFormatLinearPCM` become android.media.MediaFormat with KEY_PCM_ENCODING; the guard still returns null for non 16-bit linear PCM.
AudioEncoder.makeAudioFormat is expected to exist in this package and to return PcmAudioFormat? for a MediaFormat argument.
Swift `init?` becomes a companion `operator fun invoke` returning AudioEncoderRingBuffer?, with the primary constructor kept private.
`defer` inside createOutputBuffer is translated by capturing the tuple first, then resetting latestPresentationTimeStamp/outputIndex before returning.
setWorkingSampleBuffer no longer wraps an AudioBufferList without copying; it wraps the supplied PCM bytes into a PcmBuffer view and derives frameLength from the byte size.
VideoToolbox configuration is kept as a list of VTSessionProperty entries; the consumer of these settings must map the keys onto MediaFormat/MediaCodec, nothing here touches MediaCodec directly.
Format.codecType returns the Android MIME type ("video/avc" / "video/hevc") instead of the Apple CMVideoCodecType FourCC constant.
CMVideoDimensions is replaced by android.util.Size (width 854, height 480 default); Size implements equals so shouldInvalidateSession still works.
createDataRateLimits returns List<Double> (bytes per second limit, seconds limit) instead of a CFArray of CFNumbers; Android MediaCodec has no data-rate-limits key.

The iOS #available gates became two top-level vals, videoEncoderAverageBitRateOnlySupported (false) and videoEncoderVariableBitRateSupported (true), which pick the same branches as the old iOS 26/27 checks.

VideoToolbox/CoreVideo string constants (kVTProfileLevel_H264_Baseline_3_1, kVTH264EntropyMode_CABAC, the ITU-R ones) are declared here as top-level const vals with their original CoreVideo string values, since Android has no such constants.
The struct became a mutable class; profileLevel's didSet observer became a custom setter that switches format between h264 and hevc.
UInt32 bitrate and adaptive-resolution thresholds became Int to match MediaFormat KEY_BITRATE; UInt32 maxKeyFrameIntervalDuration became Int.

The Swift file is wrapped in #if targetEnvironment(macCatalyst); the whole capture pipeline is Apple-only, so the three ScreenCaptureKit call sites are TODO() while the rest of the structure (delegate, latency constant, sample-buffer rewriting) is translated.
SCStream has no Kotlin type, so the private 'stream' property is kept as an Any? placeholder.
makeContentFilter returned (SCContentFilter, SCDisplay); those types do not exist here, so it returns Pair<Any, Any> with a TODO body.
CMSampleBuffer -> MediaSample; presentationTimeStamp (CMTime) -> presentationTimeUs (Long microseconds) and the 0.15 s latency becomes +150000 us.
sampleBuffer.imageBuffer != nil is mapped to MediaSample.data.isNotEmpty(), because MediaSample carries the pixels in data.
weak var delegate has no Kotlin equivalent; it is kept as a plain nullable reference (strong).
logger.info is translated to Log.i with tag "MacScreenCapture"; the start log cannot reproduce the SCStream width/height pixels, so it logs the filter/display/scale instead.
TODO() throws NotImplementedError (not an Exception), so startInternal/stopInternal short-circuit before the delegate callbacks run; the TS-adjustment callback logic is still fully translated.
apple_only: no Android counterpart for ScreenCaptureKit SCStream
no Android counterpart for ScreenCaptureKit SCStream.stopCapture
no Android counterpart for ScreenCaptureKit SCShareableContent

notes: CMSampleBuffer maps to MediaSample, so every presentationTimeStamp.seconds becomes presentationTimeUs / 1_000_000.0 and CMTime is kept as Long microseconds (deltaLimit arithmetic unchanged).

CMSampleBuffer.numSamples has no MediaSample counterpart, so frameLength is TODO(); startOutput, makePresentationTimeStamp and the whole periodic output path depend on it being supplied by the platform capture side.
formatDescription.audioStreamBasicDescription?.mSampleRate maps to MediaSample.format (android.media.MediaFormat) + KEY_SAMPLE_RATE; sampleRate is only touched when a format is present, as in Swift.

CMSampleBuffer.replacePresentationTimeStamp is emulated by building a new MediaSample with the same data/isKeyFrame/format and the corrected presentationTimeUs (MediaSample is assumed to have those constructor parameters).
CMBlockBuffer data pointer zeroing becomes latest.data.fill(0) because MediaSample.data is a mutable ByteArray.
consumeBuffer's inout Int parameter becomes a returned Int (Kotlin has no inout); the call sites assign the result.

Assumes the ported SimpleTimer takes the queue in its constructor and exposes startPeriodic(interval, initial) { } and stop(), that DriftTrackerMedia's entry is Audio and DriftTracker.update/addMedia keep the Swift parameter order, and that currentPresentationTimeStamp() returns microseconds.
logger.info/debug become android.util.Log with tag "BufferedAudio"; logger.debugEnabled becomes Log.isLoggable(tag, Log.DEBUG).
Deque<CMSampleBuffer> became kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque<MediaSample>; CMTime comparisons use presentationTimeUs and 'seconds' became presentationTimeSeconds (presentationTimeUs / 1e6).
The Swift 'weak let processor' is stored as a plain nullable reference because Kotlin has no weak stored properties; a WeakReference would have changed every call site.
deinit has no JVM counterpart, so it is exposed as close() and must be called by the owner when the BufferedVideo is discarded.
logger.debugEnabled maps to Log.isLoggable(TAG, Log.DEBUG) and the stats.getStats() call stays inside that guard so its short-circuit side effects match Swift exactly.
Assumes DriftTrackerMedia.Video and BufferedStats.getStats() returning Pair<Int, Int>? so the Swift tuple destructuring still compiles; adjust if the sibling Kotlin files name these differently.
replacePresentationTimeStamp is provided as a file-private MediaSample extension using copy(); if the sibling file declares the same helper, delete this one.
The inout 'numberOfBuffersConsumed' parameter of consumeBuffer became a returned Int because Kotlin has no inout.
processor.delegate is reached with safe calls (processor?.delegate?.streamVideoBufferedVideoReady/Removed) to avoid depending on its nullability.
WhipServerClient keeps the same members and order: streamId, ingestClient, answerCompletion, delegate, init, handleOffer, stop, then the WebrtcIngestClientDelegate callbacks.

The weak Swift delegate is a plain nullable Kotlin reference (val delegate: WhipServerClientDelegate?) because Kotlin has no weak let equivalent, which means the server must clear it by dropping the client.
CMSampleBuffer callback payloads became MediaSample from com.moblin.android.media, matching the media-tier mapping.
whipServerDispatchQueue is passed straight through to WebrtcIngestClient.dispatchQueue; it is assumed to be a CoroutineDispatcher declared in the sibling package-level file.
The throwing createPeerConnection/setRemoteDescription calls are wrapped in try/catch that calls completion(null) and stop(), exactly like the Swift do/catch.
The guard-let on ingestClient binds a local val so the coroutine-safe path never dereferences a field that stop() may null out.
WebrtcIngestClient creates the peer connection; no WebRTC API is touched directly in this file.
No iOS-only API is used here, so there are no TODO() markers.

catPrinterDispatchQueue is a single-thread Executors dispatcher; every `DispatchQueue.async { }` became `CoroutineScope(catPrinterDispatchQueue).launch { }` and the same dispatcher is passed to SimpleTimer and to CBCentralManager through a wrapping CoroutineScope.
The stored central manager uses `by CBCentralManager.holder()`, so assigning null in reset() releases the manager and stops scanning like ARC on iOS.

CatPrinter.getState() is annotated @JvmName("currentState") because the private `state` property's generated getter would otherwise clash with it; CurrentJob.setState keeps @JvmName("updateState") as the existing port does.
Swift `throw "text"` became `throw CatPrinterError(message)`, a private exception whose toString() is the message, so the logged text matches the iOS log.

CFDataGetLength/CFDataGetBytePtr are gone: CGDataProvider.data already returns the ByteArray, so only the "Failed to get length" guard was dropped; bitsPerComponent/bitsPerPixel/dataProvider come from the CoreGraphics shims and the UInt8 comparisons use `and 0xFF`.
Deque<PrintJob> became MutableList with removeFirstOrNull(), and Data slices use copyOfRange(offset, min(offset + mtu, size)).
AtkinsonDithering takes MutableList<UByteArray> while FloydSteinbergDithering takes List<List<UByte>>, so pixels are converted with toList()/toUByteArray() when the floydSteinberg algorithm is used.
catPrinterEncodeImageRow takes a UByteArray row, matching the row type of catPrinterPackPrintImageCommands(image: List<UByteArray>).
Only the makeSession signature and the two call sites changed: videoSize is now a non-nullable Size parameter with no default.
The second makeSession call in encodeImageBuffer now passes oldBitrateVideoSize, matching the new Swift behaviour.
The session creation width/height now read the passed videoSize directly; the pixel buffer attributes still use settings.videoSize as on iOS.
All other lines, including imports, lockQueue usage, logging and platform calls, are unchanged.
No SwiftUI views are declared here; the file only provides data models and a formatter, so no @Composable functions were added.
Swift UInt64 usage/percentage values are mapped to Long, matching the Android side which does not use unsigned types for these counters.
The Swift tuple return of format(_:) becomes Triple<String, String, List<BondingPercentage>>; callers read .first/.second/.third.
Identifiable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped; BondingPercentage keeps its id property for LazyColumn keys.
RgbColor(red:green:blue:).color() is assumed to exist as a member call on RgbColor from com.moblin.android.common.various with Int red/green/blue arguments.
The file-private top-level `colors` array keeps its name and file-privacy; nothing outside this file can see it.
getNameColor uses indexOfFirst (-1 when absent) instead of Optional firstIndex, preserving the same colour selection order (Cellular, WiFi, then interface names offset by 2).
percentages is a MutableList so the last entry's usage can be normalised to 100 minus the sum of the earlier entries, exactly as in Swift.

NWListener is replaced with java.net.ServerSocket and NWConnection with java.net.Socket; neither has a state-update or new-connection handler, so the accept loop is started directly inside setupListener.
handleListenerStateChange no longer takes an NWListener.State and is invoked manually right after the socket is bound.
rtmpServerDispatchQueue becomes a Dispatchers.IO CoroutineDispatcher, so Swift's serial-queue execution ordering is not preserved.
Atomic<T> is accessed through its mutable value property; the Swift mutate(_:) API is not assumed to exist.
settings.port is assumed to be an Int property on SettingsRtmpServer, with DefaultTcpPorts.rtmpServer as fallback.
RtmpServerClient.latestReceiveTime is assumed to be a java.time.Instant and the 10 second receive timeout is computed with Duration.between.
SimpleTimer is assumed to accept the CoroutineDispatcher passed into its constructor.
RtmpServerClient is constructed positionally as (server, socket, softwareDecoding); the 'connection' parameter of handleNewListenerConnection keeps the Swift name.
Only the scopes list changed: 'moderator:manage:shoutouts' added after 'moderator:manage:announcements'.
All other declarations remain byte-identical to the previous Kotlin translation, including the hand-written WebView and Keychain platform code.
The Swift extension on Model becomes top-level Kotlin extension functions on Model in the same package, so the two files can be read side by side.
`database.appMode == .chatPhone` assumes the port keeps an enum `AppMode` in this package with a `chatPhone` entry; `AppMode` is not declared here and must already exist.
AVAudioPlayer is replaced with android.media.MediaPlayer: numberOfLoops = -1 becomes isLooping = true and play() becomes start().
The member `chatPhoneBackgroundAudioPlayer` is assumed to be declared in the Model file as `var chatPhoneBackgroundAudioPlayer: MediaPlayer? = null`.
Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:) for the Alerts.bundle subdirectory has no direct Android equivalent, so only the asset resolution plus MediaPlayer construction is deferred with TODO().
`resetSelectedScene(changeScene: false)` is called with a Kotlin named argument; the parameter name must be `changeScene` in the Model file.
The long Swift switch lists every SettingsQuickButtonType case explicitly, all returning false, with `default` returning true; the Kotlin `when` mirrors this with `else -> true`.
No new types are declared by this file; it only adds extension functions to Model.
Only the `#if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst)` branch is translated; the empty `#else` extension is dropped and no other Android API replaces it.
Swift's nested `LiveActivityAttributes.ContentState` stays nested in Kotlin.

`Activity<LiveActivityAttributes>.activities` becomes `Activity.activities<LiveActivityAttributes>()`; the stored `liveActivity` property keeps its `Activity<LiveActivityAttributes>?` type and is assumed declared on Model.
`logger.info` becomes `android.util.Log.i` with the class name "Model" as tag.
`String(localized:)` becomes the top-level `localized()` from com.moblin.android.
`stopLiveActivity` replaces the dispatch semaphore over a global queue with `runBlocking { }` around `end`, as the shim prescribes.
`updateLiveActivity`'s `Task { await ... }` body is run with `runBlocking`; the shim's `update` never suspends and needs no main thread.
`functions.prefix(2)` becomes `functions.take(2)` and the state carries a `List<LiveActionFunction>` instead of a Swift Array.
Despite the ui tier, this file declares no SwiftUI views; it is a Model extension with control bar background image helpers, so no @Composable functions are produced.
UIImage is mapped to android.graphics.Bitmap and UIGraphicsImageRenderer drawing is replaced with android.graphics.Canvas plus android.graphics.Matrix.

URL.documentsDirectory has no equivalent without a Context: a top-level lateinit appContext must be assigned the application context at app startup, and controlBarBackgroundImagePath is derived from appContext.filesDir.
FileManager.removeItem is File.delete and Swift's try? becomes runCatching, matching the silent failure behaviour.
The crop factors (backgroundImageCropX/Y/Width/Height) and backgroundImageOpacity are treated as Float, since CGFloat maps to Float.
image.jpegData(compressionQuality: 0.9) becomes Bitmap.compress(Bitmap.CompressFormat.JPEG, 90, ...).
BitmapFactory returns null on undecodable data, mirroring the optional returned by UIImage(data:).
Crop + scale rendering keeps the same order as Swift: scale by min(1, 1024 / max(width, height)) and translate by -x*scale, -y*scale.

Kotlin cannot add a protocol conformance to an existing class, so the `extension Model: RistServerDelegate` became a small adapter class `ModelRistServerDelegate(model)` plus identically named `Model` extension functions for the four callbacks and the two private internals.
The adapter is kept alive in a file-private `ristServerDelegate` var and passed to `RistServer(...)` in place of Swift's `delegate: self`.
Ports are `UShort` (Swift `UInt16`, RIST virtual destination port is a wire-format field); this must match the `RistServerDelegate` declaration in com.moblin.android.media.ristserver.

Callbacks arriving on ristServerQueue hop to `Dispatchers.Main` with `mainScope.launch`, matching `DispatchQueue.main.async`; the audio/video buffer callbacks stay on the calling thread exactly as the Swift nonisolated ones do.
`String(localized: "\(camera) connected")` became `localized("$camera connected")` from package com.moblin.android.
CMSampleBuffer parameters became MediaSample from com.moblin.android.media.
Assumes Model exposes database, ingests, media and makeToast(title:) as package-visible members, and that Ingests has a mutable `rist: RistServer?` field.
The three `getRistStream` overloads keep the Swift argument labels as parameter names; the disconnected `reason` parameter is unused, as in Swift.
This file is a networking layer despite being flagged ui tier, so there are no Compose views; the translation is a plain Kotlin/Swift-parallel API client.
UIImage is mapped to android.graphics.Bitmap via BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray; fetchKickProfilePicture therefore returns Bitmap?.

Helper signatures are taken as: httpRequest(Request, (ByteArray?, okhttp3.Response?, Throwable?) -> Unit), suspend httpGet(url: String): Pair<ByteArray, okhttp3.Response>, makeUrl(path: String, parameters: List<Pair<String, String>>), all from com.moblin.android.various.network.
OperationResult and NetworkResponse are used as sealed classes with Success(data)/Success(value), AuthError and Error members, as declared in com.moblin.android.various.network.

ChatterRole enum entries and the ChatterInfo constructor parameter names are assumed to be ChatterRole.Owner/Staff/Moderator/Viewer and profilePicture/bio/accountCreated/role/followingSince/subscribedMonths/giftedSubs/followers.

Swift property names are kept byte-identical (snake_case coding keys included) so kotlinx.serialization uses them as JSON keys; Json is configured with ignoreUnknownKeys to match JSONDecoder behaviour.
weak var delegate has no Kotlin equivalent, so it is a plain nullable reference; callers must avoid leaking KickApi instances.
KickApi was @MainActor in Swift: all completion handlers here are invoked on the OkHttp callback thread, so UI code must switch to Dispatchers.Main itself.
The two Swift extensions on Model become top-level extension functions on Model in package com.moblin.android.various.model, in the same order as the Swift file.

Swift's `extension Model: RtspClientDelegate` cannot be expressed in Kotlin (extensions cannot add interface conformance), so the four nonisolated callbacks live in a new ModelRtspClientDelegate class that forwards to its Model instance and implements com.moblin.android.media.rtspclient.RtspClientDelegate.

reloadRtspClient constructs one ModelRtspClientDelegate(this) before the loop and passes it in place of Swift's `delegate: self`; the delegate owns a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) used to replace DispatchQueue.main.async.
URL(string:) becomes java.net.URI built inside runCatching(...).getOrNull(), so an unparsable URL skips the stream exactly like the Swift `guard let ... else { continue }`.
CMSampleBuffer maps to MediaSample from com.moblin.android.media, so rtspClientOnVideoBuffer receives a MediaSample.
String(localized: "...") becomes localized("...") imported from com.moblin.android.

Assumes Model already exposes database, ingests, media, makeToast(title:), makeErrorToastMain(title:), database.ingestsSoftwareVideoDecoding, and that SettingsRtspClientStream has camera(), latencySeconds(), transport, enabled and url (settings package).
`ingests.rtsp = []` becomes `ingests.rtsp = mutableListOf()`, assuming Ingests.rtsp is a `var MutableList<RtspClient>`; the append call becomes add.

libsrt calls stay on the SrtNative binding object (SrtNative.srt_*), imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.srt together with SRT_INVALID_SOCK, SRT_ERROR and SRTO_STREAMID; if the binding exposes those constants at package level, import them instead.
Swift `throw "message"` becomes IllegalStateException and the `throws` clauses disappear (Kotlin exceptions are unchecked).
`@unchecked Sendable` is dropped and `weak var srtlaServer` becomes a plain nullable property, so the reference is strong.
port is Int here (Swift UInt16) and listenerSocket/clientSocket are Int (SRTSOCKET).
startBlockingThread keeps its blocking thread model: thread name plus a trailing lambda; it is called with a named argument.

bind() writes the 16 byte Linux sockaddr_in by hand (family 2, big-endian port, 0.0.0.0, no sin_len as on Darwin); the JNI marshalling signature of srt_bind/srt_accept/srt_getsockflag should be checked against the binding.
getStreamId truncates the 513 byte buffer at the first NUL byte and decodes UTF-8, and srt_getlasterror_str is assumed to return a String already.
logger.info maps to android.util.Log.i with tag SrtServer.

libdatachannel's C API is bound as external funs on a new internal RtcNative object; the NDK/JNI layer and the constant values (RTC_DIRECTION_RECVONLY = 2, RTC_NAL_SEPARATOR_LONG_START_SEQUENCE = 1, rtcState/rtcGatheringState values) must be verified against the shipped native library.

Unmanaged.passRetained/toOpaque is replaced by an IngestClientHandles registry that maps a client to a stable Long handle; the handle is released again in stopInternal so a stopped client receives no further native callbacks.

DispatchQueue -> CoroutineDispatcher, dispatchQueue.async -> scope.launch on a private CoroutineScope created from that dispatcher; the delegate is held strongly because Kotlin has no weak references.

CMTime -> Long microseconds: WrappingTimestamp.update(timestampUs) is expected to return microseconds and currentPresentationTimeStamp() is expected to return microseconds, hence the explicit / 1_000_000.0 conversions.
MediaFormat has no structural equality, so a format change is detected by comparing the string representations of the old and new format descriptions.

isKeyFrame for MediaSample is derived from the frame bytes by scanning NAL start codes (H264 type 5, H265 16..21); the mpeg readers are still used for the format description and their filter is assumed to be a List<NalUnitType> with SPS/PPS/VPS/IDR entries.
DataChannelConnectionState and DataChannelGatheringState came from the Swift DataChannel package and are declared here as private enums with fromValue(rawValue).
Opus audio decoding has no drop-in Android equivalent in this file, so setupOpusDecoder and decodeOpusPacket are TODO(); the PCM16 helper pcm16ToBytes is pure logic and fully translated.
The Swift diff only adds a lutUpdated() call to importSucceeded(); the Kotlin file gets the same call between reloadStream() and chatBotCustomCommandsTextChanged().
Everything else in the Kotlin file, including the Android-specific clipboard handling and settingsImportScope, is unchanged.
Model extension in a separate Swift file became top-level Kotlin extension functions on Model in the same package; public ones are public, private ones are file-private.
DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter was mapped to a file-private `mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main)` plus delay() launches; the nested asyncAfter(10s) becomes a nested launch.

UIImage and CIImage have no Android equivalent, so they are typed as android.graphics.Bitmap; jpegData(compressionQuality: 0.9) becomes Bitmap.compress(Bitmap.CompressFormat.JPEG, 90, ...) into a ByteArrayOutputStream.
getDiscordWebhookUrl returns String? instead of URL?, using takeIf { it.isNotBlank() } because URL(string:) returns nil for invalid urls and the url is only forwarded to the upload helper.
snapshotJobs must be a MutableList/ArrayDeque<SnapshotJob>: popFirst() -> removeFirstOrNull() and append(_:) -> add(_); snapshot.currentJob is nullable and is reset with null.

media.takeSnapshot(age:completion:) and media.takeVideoSourceSnapshot(videoSourceId:onComplete:) are assumed to be callback APIs of the media layer, with the completion parameters typed Bitmap / Bitmap?.
String(localized: "...\(x)...") kept its interpolation inside localized(...), matching the rest of the port.
takeVideoSourcePreviewImage collapses the two-part guard into a single if that calls onComplete(null) before returning.
Swift `extension Model` members become top-level extension functions on Model in package com.moblin.android.various.model, keeping identical names and order.

Kotlin cannot add an interface to a class declared in another file: Model must declare `: SrtClientDelegate` itself for the four delegate callbacks to be wired up; here they are translated as extension functions with the same names and signatures.
DispatchQueue.main.async is replaced by a file-private `mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main)` plus `launch { }`.
`URL(string:)` is validated with `runCatching { URI(stream.url) }.getOrNull() ?: continue` and the resulting java.net.URI is handed to SrtClient; adjust if the Kotlin SrtClient takes a String.
CMSampleBuffer parameters become MediaSample (com.moblin.android.media).
`camera()` on SettingsSrtClientStream is imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings as a top-level extension; String(localized:) becomes localized().
`ingests.srt = []` is expressed as `ingests.srt.clear()` so it works whether the property is var or val.
`isSrtClientStreamConnected` keeps its (unused) id parameter exactly as in Swift.
The private serial DispatchQueue is a top-level private CoroutineDispatcher from a single-thread executor; every `lockQueue.async` becomes `CoroutineScope(lockQueue).launch`.
`images: Deque<VideoImage>` (swift-collections) maps to `ArrayDeque<VideoImage>`; `images += newImages` becomes `images.addAll(newImages)` and `images.count` becomes `images.size`.
`AVAssetReaderTrackOutput.copyNextSampleBuffer()` blocks and stays on the reader's own (lock) queue, never on processorPipelineQueue.
Sample offsets use `sampleBuffer.presentationTimeUs / 1_000_000.0` (CMTime -> Long microseconds).
`CIImage(cvImageBuffer:)` becomes `CIImage(cvPixelBuffer = imageBuffer)` and `.toEffectImage(isOpaque: true)` comes from com.moblin.android.videoeffects.
`try? AVAssetReader(asset:)` becomes `runCatching { ... }.getOrNull()`; the `guard let trackOutput` after construction is kept as a local nullable read.
The `[weak self]` in the loadTracks completion is dropped; the coroutine launched on lockQueue references the reader directly, as the completion ends with the load.
Pixel buffer output settings use the Map<String, Any> form with the kCVPixelBuffer* keys from com.moblin.android.platform.video.
BeautyEffect is a final Swift class, so it becomes a plain Kotlin class; @unchecked Sendable is dropped.
framesPerFade keeps the Swift declaration order: the stored default 30f plus an init block that assigns 15f * (fps / 30f).
setSmoothnessSettings/setShapeSettings keep the processorPipelineQueue hop, written as processorPipelineQueue.launch { } since the scope is already a CoroutineScope.
VideoEffectDetectionsMode cases are referenced as the nested members VideoEffectDetectionsMode.Now(null) and VideoEffectDetectionsMode.Off, matching the sealed class declared in VideoEffect.kt.
In executeMetalPetal the Swift local `var image` shadows the parameter; Kotlin forbids that, so the running value is named `result` and the parameter keeps its name.
`var detections` in addBeautyShapeMetalPetal shadows the parameter, so the mutated copy is named faceDetections.
guard let image, var detections -> an early return of the nullable image plus a smart cast; points.first/last become firstOrNull/lastOrNull with a continue.
The third parameter of addBeautyShapeMetalPetal is unnamed in Swift and named info in Kotlin; it is unused.
CMTime is translated to Long microseconds; kCMTimeInvalid uses the sentinel `invalidPresentationTimeUs` (Long.MIN_VALUE).
AVAudioPCMBuffer is represented by a ShortArray (`pcmAudioBuffer`) and AVAudioFormat by android.media.AudioFormat (PCM 16 bit, sample rate + channel mask).
MediaSample has no timing-duration field, so CMSampleTimingInfo.duration is computed but not carried to the delegate (only presentation/decode timestamps survive).

android.media.MediaFormat has no value equality, so the Swift `formatDescriptions[id] != newFormat` checks are done with toString() comparison; the same trick is used for the Opus/AAC/video format-description dictionaries.

Audio decoding (AVAudioConverter + AVAudioCompressedBuffer) is mapped onto MediaCodec (audio/mp4a-latm); the codec creation and the decode call are TODO() because the MediaCodec async plumbing cannot be inferred safely here.

Assumptions about neighbouring mpeg types: `NalUnitType` is a top-level enum in this package keeping the Swift case names (idr/sps/pps/vps/prefixSeiNut), `ADTSReader` implements Iterable<Int>, `removeNalUnitStartCodes`/`getNalUnits`/`readH264NalUnits`/`readH265NalUnits` take and return ByteArray/List.

`data.getDescriptor(ElementaryStreamDescriptiorTag.registration)` is kept exactly as in the Swift source (returning the registration enum) while `…Tag.extension` is read as descriptor bytes; adjust if the Kotlin ElementaryStreamSpecificData exposes a single byte-array accessor.
The delegate is a strong reference (Kotlin has no weak references) and the decoder queue is a kotlinx.coroutines CoroutineDispatcher instead of DispatchQueue.
DispatchQueue is replaced by the single threaded CoroutineDispatcher rtspClientQueue plus a file private rtspClientScope; DispatchQueue.sync in updateStats becomes runBlocking(rtspClientQueue).

URL maps to java.net.URI: removeCredentialsAndPort uses the 7 argument URI constructor, and user/password/port are parsed from URI.userInfo/URI.port in an init block because the URL must be rewritten after the credentials are read.
The two Swift partition overloads are renamed partition(text, separator) and partitionOptional(text, optionalSeparator); Kotlin cannot overload on argument label only.

CMSampleBuffer/CMSampleTimingInfo creation is replaced by a MediaSample built from the reassembled NAL units; presentationTimeUs is the rebased timestamp in microseconds and the sample size is still written big endian into the first four bytes.
MediaSample.isKeyFrame is set to false because the Swift code never determines the frame type; add IDR/IRAP detection if the decoder needs it.
The weak client reference of RtpVideoProcessor is a plain reference (JVM GC collects cycles) and fileprivate latency/softwareDecoding become internal so the RTP processors can read them.
RTP sequence numbers use Int masked to 16 bits instead of UShort so the wrapping arithmetic (&- and &+) stays explicit.
String(utf8) splitting uses filter { it.isNotEmpty() } to reproduce Swift's omittingEmptySubsequences behaviour.
The Swift enum with associated values is declared here as a sealed class Dewarp360EffectSettings with nested data classes Direct and Animate, keeping Swift's default values.
setSettings posts through processorPipelineQueue.launch, matching the original processorPipelineQueue.async.
info.videoUnit.canvasSize is an android.util.Size, so it is converted with toCGSize() before being stored in Dewarp360Filter.outputSize (a CGSize).
The Swift comment about a physics model in updateParameters is dropped because Kotlin output has no comments.
Smart casts cannot be applied to a mutable property, so updateParameters/applySettings bind the settings value to a local val inside when.
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped; the class stays a plain final class.
Dewarp360Filter and graphicsEpsilon are in the same package and need no import.
The Animate branch of updateParameters keeps the Swift placeholders: currentPan/Tilt/FieldOfView are assigned from the case payload as before.
final class CameraManEffect : VideoEffect gets a primary constructor; moveVertically, speed and alwaysMove are private var constructor properties.
highQualityDownsampling is referenced from the ported VideoEffect base class exactly as in Swift; it is not part of the declaration excerpt given in the request.
setSettings uses processorPipelineQueue.launch to stand in for DispatchQueue.async on the serial pipeline queue.
VideoEffectInfo.presentationTimeStamp is Long microseconds, so Swift's .seconds is divided by 1_000_000.0 at both call sites.
calcCropRegion keeps the stateful isStill / previousScale / previousIsRising logic; isStill.toggle() becomes isStill = !isStill.
All geometry stays in CoreGraphics types (CGRect, CGSize, CGPoint, CGAffineTransform) because the effect boundary is CIImage / MTIImage.
executeMetalPetal builds one MTILayer with the crop as contentRegion and yields filter.outputImage ?: image.
@unchecked Sendable is dropped; the class has no Kotlin counterpart.
OpacityEffect keeps its Swift shape: a final class becomes a plain class deriving from VideoEffect, and @unchecked Sendable is dropped.

processorPipelineQueue is a CoroutineScope in Kotlin, so the Swift processorPipelineQueue.async { } becomes processorPipelineQueue.launch { }; this@OpacityEffect.opacity is used because launch's lambda receiver is the CoroutineScope.
CIFilter.colorMatrix() returns the CIColorMatrix shim, whose aVector is a CIVector and inputImage a CIImage?.
The MetalPetal path uses MTIOpacityFilter directly, with opacity as Float and outputImage a nullable MTIImage.
The opacity field has no synchronisation primitive in Swift either, so it stays a plain private var read on the pipeline thread.
Unused parameter info in both overrides is kept so the signatures match VideoEffect.
The Swift private top-level helper makeGrayScaleColorMatrix stays a file-private top-level Kotlin function with the same name and return type.
SIMD4<Float>(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722, 0) * 0.75 becomes SIMD4(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722, 0) * 0.75f using the platform.simd SIMD4 Number constructor and Float times operator.
simd_float4x4(columns: (...)) becomes simd_float4x4(columns = listOf(...)) with the four SIMD4 columns in Swift order.
SWIFT final class GrayScaleEffect: VideoEffect becomes a plain Kotlin class extending the open VideoEffect, since a final Swift class has no open members.
The Swift override init() body is written as a Kotlin init block; property initialisers (CIFilter.colorMonochrome(), MTIColorMatrixFilter()) stay property declarations.
filter.intensity = 1.0 assigns a Float on the Kotlin CIColorMonochrome shim, so it is written 1.0f.
CIColor(red:green:blue:) drops to the positional CIColor(0.75, 0.75, 0.75) call because the shim's alpha parameter defaults to 1.0.
Both execute and executeMetalPetal keep the ?? image fallback as ?: image, since outputImage is nullable on the CIFilter and MTIFilter shims.
PinchEffect is a final Swift class extending VideoEffect, so it becomes a plain Kotlin class extending the open class VideoEffect.
setSettings uses processorPipelineQueue.async; translated to processorPipelineQueue.launch from kotlinx.coroutines.
The MetalPetal filter is created once as a stored property and reused, exactly as in Swift; its center is a SIMD2 so the Swift .init(Float, Float) becomes SIMD2(...).
The Core Image path builds a fresh CIPinchDistortion filter per frame and keeps the ?? image fallback via the elvis operator.
Float(min(w, h) / 2) is preserved by dividing the Double values first and converting to Float afterwards.
CIImage.extent and MTIImage.extent are both CGRect from platform.coregraphics, so min/width/height are Double.
pixellateCalcScale keeps Swift's Float arithmetic; 20/1920/5/1 literals become 20f/1920f/5f/1f and size.maximum() is a CGSize member returning Double, narrowed with toFloat().
final class PixellateEffect: VideoEffect -> plain class with an override of the open VideoEffect members. The private stored strength becomes the primary-constructor property.
The CIFilter.pixellate() companion factory returns the CIPixellate shim, so filter.center takes CGPoint.zero and filter.scale a Float.
execute/executeMetalPetal take the base-class parameter names (image, info); the Swift unnamed second parameter is not reproduced.
filterMetalPetal.scale is the SIMD2 member of MTIPixellateFilter, so .init(scale, scale) becomes SIMD2(scale, scale).
setSettings dispatches onto processorPipelineQueue (a CoroutineScope) with launch and qualifies the property as this@PixellateEffect.strength to avoid shadowing.
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped.

ControlBar is an ObservableObject in Swift, so here it is a parameter whose StateFlow properties are read with collectAsState(); backgroundImage is expected to be a StateFlow<android.graphics.Bitmap?> and backgroundImageOpacity a StateFlow<Float>.
Color.black becomes Modifier.background(Color.Black) on a Box that fills the available space with Modifier.fillMaxSize().
Image(uiImage:) becomes Compose Image(bitmap = bitmap.asImageBitmap()) with ContentScale.Crop for .resizable().scaledToFill().
.opacity is applied with Modifier.alpha and .clipped() with Modifier.clipToBounds().
.allowsHitTesting(false) has no direct Compose counterpart and is dropped: the overlay contains no clickable or scrollable content, so it never steals pointer events.
.ignoresSafeArea() is a SwiftUI-only concept; the Box fills its parent's constraints, so the caller decides whether to extend behind the system bars.
No modifier parameter is added so the composable signature stays identical to the Swift view's stored properties.

final class WhirlpoolEffect: VideoEffect becomes `class WhirlpoolEffect(angle: Float) : VideoEffect()`, with the Swift `self.angle = angle` init body expressed as a body property initialised from the constructor parameter (same name).
`private let filterMetalPetal = MTITwirlDistortionFilter()` stays a private val of the MetalPetal shim; the Swift calls (`inputImage`, `angle`, `radius`, `center`, `outputImage`) are kept verbatim.

`processorPipelineQueue.async { ... }` becomes `processorPipelineQueue.launch { ... }` (processorPipelineQueue is a CoroutineScope); the mutation targets `this@WhirlpoolEffect.angle` so the lambda captures the effect, not the shadowed parameter.

CITwirlDistortion values are CGFloat in Swift, i.e. Double in the CoreGraphics shim, so `image.extent.width/height` stay Double and only the `radius` assigned to the filter's Float property is converted with `.toFloat()`.
`.init(Float(x), Float(y))` for the MetalPetal filter's SIMD2 center becomes `SIMD2(x, y)` with both components converted to Float.
`filter.outputImage?.cropped(to: image.extent) ?? image` keeps the `?:` fallback to the input image, as does `filterMetalPetal.outputImage ?? image`.
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped; the class is not marked open because Swift declares it final.
A SwiftUI ViewModifier cannot be a Compose Modifier here because it emits a dialog, so QuickButtonChatLinkConfirmationModifier is a @Composable function instead.
@Binding var url: URL? becomes a value parameter url: String? plus an onUrlChange: (String?) -> Unit callback; setting null dismisses the dialog.
confirmationDialog maps to Material 3 AlertDialog with the URL as its title; titleVisibility is always visible in Material 3.
UIApplication.shared.open(url) maps to Context.startActivity(Intent(ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse(url))) using LocalContext.current.
URL is only displayed and handed to the system browser, so it is translated as String rather than java.net.URI.
The View extension quickButtonChatLinkConfirmation is kept as a top-level @Composable that delegates to the modifier composable, preserving the call-site name.
The implicit SwiftUI Cancel button is provided by AlertDialog's onDismissRequest, which clears the URL.
Callers should place quickButtonChatLinkConfirmation(url, onUrlChange) alongside the chat content it used to modify.
BatteryView became a @Composable function; Battery and Model are passed in as parameters and are imported from com.moblin.android.various.model.
