The rtmps branch passes TlsOptions(); the port's TLS options type name must be confirmed against RtmpSocket.connect.
SimpleTimer is created with the CoroutineDispatcher and queue.async became scope.launch on a CoroutineScope(queue) property.
RtmpChunk.ChunkStreamId.control.rawValue, RtmpChunkType.zero, RtmpUserControlMessage.Event.ping/pong and RtmpMessageType.amf0Command are kept exactly as in the Swift source.
The weak stream reference is a plain nullable var in Kotlin, and bitrateStats.mutate { } plus info.onAck/onWritten/onTimeout are assumed to exist on RtmpStreamInfo as in Swift.
AVAudioEngine plus AVAudioPlayerNode collapse into a single android.media.AudioTrack inside TalkbackPlayer; start/stop/appendSampleBuffer keep their names.
AVAudioFormat maps to android.media.AudioFormat built from MediaFormat KEY_SAMPLE_RATE/KEY_CHANNEL_COUNT; AVAudioPCMBuffer maps to ShortArray of 16-bit PCM.
DispatchQueue.async on processorPipelineQueue becomes CoroutineScope.launch; processorPipelineQueue is assumed to expose CoroutineScope.

MediaSample helpers used here (muted, withGain, deepCopyAudioSampleBuffer, replacePresentationTimeStamp, numberOfAudioChannels, sampleRate) are not in the glossary, so they are implemented in this file as private 16-bit PCM extensions.
AVCaptureSession/AVCaptureDeviceInput/AVCaptureAudioDataOutput have no audio counterpart: session stays a nullable AudioRecord and attachDevice is TODO.
sampleBuffer.foreachAudioSample(float32:int16:) is replaced by direct little-endian PCM16 parsing; the float32 branch is unreachable on Android.
CMSampleBuffer -> MediaSample and CMTime -> Long microseconds; NSNumber channel maps become List<Int>.
captureOutput keeps its AVCaptureAudioDataOutputSampleBufferDelegate signature but is not wired to any capture loop in this port.
Swift `extension Model` becomes top-level extension functions on Model in the same package com.moblin.android.various.model.

Kotlin cannot add interface conformance through an extension, so the `extension Model: WhepClientDelegate` block is realised by a small adapter class `ModelWhepClientDelegate` whose four overrides delegate to identically named Model extension functions.
DispatchQueue.main.async maps to a private top-level main-scope coroutine (`whepMainScope`) declared in this file because the project-wide main scope is not part of the glossary.
`ingests.whep = []` is translated as `ingests.whep.clear()` so the translation does not require the property to be a `var`.
`URL(string:)` becomes `runCatching { URI(stream.url) }.getOrNull()` and WhepClient is assumed to take a java.net.URI.
`stream.camera()` and `stream.latencySeconds()` are assumed to be top-level extension functions in com.moblin.android.various.settings and are imported as such.
`String(localized:)` becomes the top-level `localized()` from package com.moblin.android.
Camera constructor is called as Camera(id = <uuidString>, name = <camera>) and buffered-media calls pass the stream UUID as cameraId.
generic (a settings class) is read directly like every Moblin settings object; its Published properties need no collectAsState.
VStack/HStack become Column/Row and the SwiftUI inside-out modifier order is reversed: the row's .padding then .background becomes .background(...).padding(...).
.foregroundStyle(textColor) is applied with CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentColor provides textColor) around the whole Column, so every child Text takes that colour.

.font(.system(size:)) on the two rows is provided through CompositionLocalProvider(LocalTextStyle provides SwiftUIFonts.system(...)), the SwiftUI behaviour where a parent font reaches the child Texts; the clock Text overrides it with .monospacedDigit().
Spacer(minLength: 0) inside the team-name columns and Spacer() beside them become Modifier.weight(1f) spacers.
scale is applied to lengths as Dp ((...*scale).dp) and to fonts as a Double handed to SwiftUIFonts.system.
.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 5 * scale)) is the outer Modifier.clip(RoundedCornerShape(...)) on the Column, clip ordered before background as Compose draws outside-in.
generic.clock.format() resolves to the Duration.format() extension in com.moblin.android.common.various, and TeamScoreView/PoweredByMoblinView are the ones already declared in this package.

Tesla's @Published properties become MutableStateFlow (vehicleState, vehicleVehicleSecurityConnected, vehicleInfotainmentConnected); views read them with collectAsState, and every assignment here writes .value.

Model's conformance to TeslaVehicleDelegate becomes three Model extension functions plus a private ModelTeslaVehicleDelegate forwarding class, which reloadTeslaVehicle assigns to tesla.vehicle?.delegate.

Tesla protobuf oneof reads use casts: optionalSpeed/optionalPower as CarServer_DriveState.OneOf_* classes, and optionalNowPlayingArtist/optionalNowPlayingTitle as CarServer_MediaState.OneOf_* classes, taking .value.
optionalBatteryLevel and optionalMinutesToChargeLimit are presence checks, so they are translated as '!= null'.

Miles per hour to meters per second is a Measurement(value = speed.toDouble(), unit = UnitSpeed.milesPerHour).converted(to = UnitSpeed.metersPerSecond) from com.moblin.android.common.various, then formatSpeed(speed = ...).
String(localized:) is localized(...) and makeToast(title = ...) stays the existing Model extension.
The switch over TeslaVehicleState uses the Kotlin enum entries idle, connecting and connected.
The switch over the shift oneof uses is-branches on CarServer_ShiftState.OneOf_Type inside a null check.
The three private Swift View structs become private @Composable functions with the same names and parameter lists.
`.foregroundStyle(textColor)` on the root container is translated as CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentColor provides textColor) so the player-name Text inherits it.
`.bold()` on the header HStack is folded into each Text's TextStyle weight instead of a parent text-style override.
`.minimumScaleFactor(0.5)` is implemented by the private GolfShrinkText composable, which lowers the font size while TextLayoutResult.hasVisualOverflow, down to half size.
ForEach over golf.players has no edit actions, so it stays players.forEach { key(it.id) { ... } }.
Under par uses iOS green 0xFF34C759 and over par iOS red 0xFFFF3B30, not Material colours.

ThruView's private func format() became a private top-level function taking the player and hole count, and keeps the Swift labels of holesPlayed(numHoles:) and totalRelativeToPar(pars:numberOfHoles:).
Modifier lists are reversed: padding(.leading) after frame(height:) becomes padding then height, while padding before frame(width:height:) becomes width/height then padding.

NWConnection becomes a java.net.Socket that is handed in already connected, so start() only resets the RTMP state machine; handleStateUpdate stays an empty no-op since java.net.Socket has no state callbacks.
rtmpServerDispatchQueue is used as a CoroutineDispatcher for a per-client CoroutineScope that runs the blocking socket read loop and the writes.
The Swift Data extensions used by this file (getUInt32Be, getThreeBytesBe, getFourBytesLe, Data.random) are provided as file-private ByteArray helpers appended at the bottom of this file.
Assumes RtmpServerChunkStream.messageTimestamp/messageStreamId are UInt, messageTypeId is Byte, and RtmpAcknowledgementMessage.sequence is UInt; adjust if the haishinkit port used other types.
server is a plain nullable property instead of a weak reference; Kotlin GC collects the RtmpServer <-> RtmpServerClient cycle.
Socket writes are serialised with a lock because NWConnection.send serialised concurrent sends; IO failures report through stopInternal instead of the ignored completion handler.
latestReceiveTime uses System.nanoTime() instead of ContinuousClock.now; currentPresentationTimeStamp() is treated as Long microseconds.
connectionState uses a custom setter so the log fires on real transitions only, never during construction (matching Swift didSet semantics).
Added hasHlg() right after hasAppleLog(), matching the Swift diff position.
AVCaptureColorSpace.HLG_BT2020 already exists in the avfoundation shim and is imported, so no new import is needed.

ScoreboardEffectPadelView is a @Composable function; the private Swift helper structs stay private Kotlin data classes and the private helper functions stay private top-level functions with the same names.
Each Swift `let id: UUID = .init()` becomes a data class property defaulted to UUID.randomUUID(), so the call sites keep using only the named home/away or name arguments.
`.foregroundStyle(textColor)` is written as CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentColor provides textColor), which the ported Text reads as its default colour.
`.font(.system(size: x))` applied to a container becomes CompositionLocalProvider(LocalTextStyle provides SwiftUIFonts.system(x)); the Row's font sizes stay Double * Double.

`.bold(score.isHomeWin())` is not a parameter of the ported TeamScoreView, so boldness is applied by wrapping each call in CompositionLocalProvider(LocalTextStyle provides SwiftUIFonts.system(size, weight = FontWeight.Bold)) — the same size with the bold weight.

SwiftUI's implicit 8 point VStack/HStack spacing is written as Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp) on every Column and Row that has no explicit spacing argument; the outer `spacing: 0` Column gets no arrangement.
Spacer(minLength: 0) becomes Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f)); modifier order is reversed (background before padding, clip on the outer Column).
ForEach over the Identifiable players and scores becomes items.forEach { key(it.id) { ... } }.
NavigationLink has no direct Compose counterpart here: the row body is rendered as a clickable Row and a local `editing` state reveals TextEditView in place of the pushed destination.
`preset.bitrate` is assigned directly, assuming SettingsBitratePreset exposes a settable `bitrate` var (MutableStateFlow-backed) as in the rest of the port.
TextEditView is called with title, value, keyboardType and a trailing submit lambda in the same order as the Swift call; confirm the ported parameter names in com.moblin.android.view.utils.
Swift `Float(bitrate)` with optional binding becomes `bitrate.toFloatOrNull()` with an early return.
`value.clamped(to: 0.05 ... 50)` becomes `coerceIn(0.05f, 50f)` on the Float value.
KeyboardType `.numbersAndPunctuation` maps to Compose KeyboardType.Decimal so fractional Mbps values can be typed.
`String(bitrateToMbps(...))` becomes `.toString()`; `Int64(preset.bitrate)` becomes `.toLong()` for formatBytesPerSecond.
The struct View is emitted as a data class holding the preset, with `body` translated to a @Composable `Body()` function.
SwiftUI struct View with no local state is kept as a plain Kotlin class holding model/preset/minX/maxX plus a @Composable body(), so submitX and formatX keep their names and stay callable members.
model is declared as a constructor parameter (the Swift @EnvironmentObject) since the Kotlin Model instance must be provided by the caller.
NavigationLink push is emulated with androidx.compose.ui.window.Dialog driven by a remember { mutableStateOf(false) } flag; the row is made clickable instead of a navigation label.
String(localized:) became localized(...) from com.moblin.android; the interpolated Float values print the same as Swift's String interpolation.
Swift .numbersAndPunctuation keyboard has no exact Android equivalent and was mapped to androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType.Text.
String(preset.x) became preset.x.toString(), which produces the same decimal representation as Swift Float interpolation.
"...".replace(".0", "") maps to Kotlin String.replace which also replaces every occurrence.
TextEditView is called with title/value/footers/keyboardType/onSubmit matching the Swift call site; adjust if the Kotlin signature differs.
QuickButtonObs @Published properties become MutableStateFlow fields keeping the Swift names; Compose callers read them with collectAsState().
@MainActor has no Kotlin counterpart, so it is dropped; callers are expected to run on the main dispatcher.
CGImage/UIImage is replaced by android.graphics.Bitmap produced with BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray from the OBS screenshot bytes.
ContinuousClock.Instant maps to java.time.Instant and duration(to:) maps to java.time.Duration.between(...), compared against Duration.ofSeconds(...).

The 'extension Model: ObsWebsocketDelegate' conformance cannot be expressed with extension functions, so those functions are emitted as top level extensions on Model and must be declared as overrides in Model.kt (or Model must delegate to them).
private func members of the Swift extension become file-private top-level extension functions on Model, matching Swift file-private scope.
Identifiable has no counterpart; ObsSceneInput/ObsSceneMediaSource expose a plain UUID id used as a Compose key.
CameraPosition and StreamState are referenced unqualified assuming they live in com.moblin.android.various.model; imports must be added if they live elsewhere.
Added the Native low light boost toggle with its own state and onChange-equivalent LaunchedEffect, inserted right after the Allow video range pixel format toggle to match the Swift diff.
New state reads debug.nativeLowLightBoost as a StateFlow, so SettingsDebug must expose it.
The onChange handler translates to LaunchedEffect(nativeLowLightBoost) calling model.setNativeLowLightBoost(), mirroring the existing setAllowVideoRangePixelFormat pattern.
Everything else in the file is unchanged, including the hand-written Unit() placeholders in onPixelFormatChange.
SwiftUI View struct became a @Composable function; @EnvironmentObject model and @ObservedObject defaultZoom are plain function parameters.

AVCaptureDevice.Position has no Android equivalent and is kept as an Int here; callers pass CameraSelector.LENS_FACING_BACK or LENS_FACING_FRONT from androidx.camera.core, and Model.getMinMaxZoomX(position: Int) is expected to take it.
The NavigationLink destination is rendered when the local 'editing' state is true; tapping the row opens TextEditView.
Keyboard type .numbersAndPunctuation maps to androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType.Number.
String(localized:) maps to the top-level localized() function in package com.moblin.android, which is imported explicitly.
SettingsZoomSwitchTo.x and .enabled are read/written as plain mutable properties; if that class exposes StateFlow instead, read them with collectAsState() and write through its setter.
Helpers x() and formatX(x:) that used self in Swift are private top-level functions here; x() now takes defaultZoom as a parameter.

TextEditView and TextItemLocalizedView come from com.moblin.android.view.utils; their exact Kotlin parameters are not in the glossary, so named parameters title/value/keyboardType/onChange plus an assumed onDone to leave the editor are used.
Added `font: SettingsFont` published property to SettingsChat, encoded as the separate `fontFamily`/`fontStyle` keys as in Swift.
Added `textToSpeechBluetoothSpeakerOnly` published property with its encode and decode entries in the same positions as the Swift source.
SettingsFont is mutable, so `chat.font.family = ...` / `chat.font.style = ...` are assigned in place after `fontSize`, matching the Swift decode order.
fontFamily is decoded as a nullable String with null default, matching the existing `textToSpeechDefaultLanguage` handling in this file.
No new imports were needed: SettingsFont lives in the same package.
@EnvironmentObject model has no environment in Compose, so both composables take model as an explicit parameter.
The five submit* methods become private top-level functions taking model/stream, because composables cannot own methods; names and order are kept.
Form/Section become a LazyColumn whose single item is the inner Column, with section headers rendered as header Text items; .navigationTitle becomes a Material 3 TopAppBar title.
Toggles (including the two computed Bindings) become Row { Text(...) ; Switch(checked, onCheckedChange) }, with .disabled mapped to Switch enabled.
model.database.showAllSettings is read with collectAsState() since it is a StateFlow-backed published property.
TextEditNavigationView is called positionally by name (title, value, onChange, onSubmit, footers, sensitive, capitalize) assuming the Kotlin port of that helper keeps the SwiftUI parameter names.
Strings wrapped in String(localized:) use localized(); literal Swift Text("...") headers/footers are kept unlocalized exactly as in the Swift source.
No iOS-only framework is used in this file, so no TODO() placeholders were needed.

StreamingHistoryDatabase is assumed to expose MutableStateFlow properties (totalStreams, totalTime, totalBytes, streams); the observed values are read with collectAsState() and the stream list is replaced with a filtered copy on delete, mirroring the @Published var + store() flow.

List.onDelete and .contextMenuDeleteButton have no direct Compose equivalent: each row now has a trailing delete IconButton that calls the same deleteStream/2 logic, so the makeOffsets() helper is not needed because LazyColumn supplies the row index.

NavigationLink is replaced by an onNavigate: (String) -> Unit parameter; the destination name carries the stream id ("StreamingHistoryStreamSettingsView/<id>") so the parent graph can rebuild StreamingHistoryStreamSettingsView(stream = ...).
Typography mapping: .title2 -> MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge, .subheadline -> bodyMedium, .footnote -> bodySmall (Material 3 has no footnote/subheadline styles).
Form/Section/List/ForEach collapse into a single LazyColumn with itemsIndexed; the Section header was omitted because the Swift section had no header text.
formatStreamTitle() stays a file-private top-level function (a @Composable function cannot own member helpers, so deleteStream() also takes the database/model it needs as parameters).
format() and formatDate() are used as extension functions (Double.format(), Instant.formatDate()); they are imported from com.moblin.android.common.various.
formatBytes() is not present in the provided glossary but is used by the Swift source, so it is imported from com.moblin.android.common.various alongside the other formatting helpers.
Form/Section becomes a scrollable Column whose first item is the section header Text ("General").
The Slider's onEditingChanged(false) is mapped to onValueChangeFinished, which calls model.sendSettingsToWatch().
The Swift .onChange handlers on the toggles and the picker are folded into the change callbacks: they write the new value into the chat model and immediately call model.sendSettingsToWatch().
Picker is rendered as an ExposedDropdownMenuBox; on Material 3 1.3+ this needs MenuAnchorType.PrimaryNotEditable, hence @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class).

WatchSettingsChat is not in the request glossary, so it is declared here in com.moblin.android.view.settings.watch.chat with public MutableStateFlow properties so that the two-way bindings ($chat.fontSize etc.) keep working.
onDisappear becomes DisposableEffect(Unit) { onDispose { ... } } and navigationTitle("Chat") becomes the Scaffold TopAppBar title.
User facing literals go through localized() from package com.moblin.android.
View body translated to a single @Composable function keeping the name StreamSrtAdaptiveBitrateSettingsView.
SwiftUI Form -> LazyColumn and each Section -> a header Text item followed by the section's content and footer items.
Picker bound to $adaptiveBitrate.algorithm -> ExposedDropdownMenuBox with DropdownMenuItem entries; the .onChange handler is folded into the item onClick.
SliderView is reused from com.moblin.android.view.utils with the same value/minimum/maximum/step/onSubmit/width/format arguments.
@ObservedObject srt and adaptiveBitrate are taken as plain constructor parameters since their StateFlow shape is defined elsewhere.
powf(_, 0.2) and powf(_, 5) map to kotlin.math.pow on Float.
The private helper methods became local functions inside the composable so they can capture model/stream/srt/adaptiveBitrate.
.navigationTitle("Adaptive bitrate") is not rendered here; the surrounding screen's TopAppBar must supply that title.
SettingsStream's published properties are assumed to be MutableStateFlow: read with collectAsState() and written through .value.
SwiftUI Section has no Compose counterpart, so it is rendered as a header Text, the content, then the footer as a Column.
Form is a LazyColumn; .navigationTitle becomes a Scaffold with a Material 3 TopAppBar on the destination screens.
NavigationLink becomes an onNavigate("GoLiveNotificationDiscordSettingsView") callback; no navigation-compose is pulled in here.
@FocusState plus .focused($editingText) becomes remember { mutableStateOf(false) } driven by Modifier.onFocusChanged.
.keyboardType/.textInputAutocapitalization/.disableAutocorrection become a KeyboardOptions argument passed to MultiLineTextFieldView.
The Markdown link in the Toggle label is rendered as plain literal text because Compose Text does not interpret Markdown.
GoLiveNotificationDiscordSettingsView stays private as in the Swift source, and the emoji-hint string keeps its exact backslash escaping.
Added the new `font` field to ChatLineStyle and forwarded it to ChatLineContent, matching the Swift diff.
SettingsFont is imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings; it is a non-serialized settings class so it stays a plain constructor property without a delegate.
Everything else in the file, including the hand-written messageItem URL translation and the content() call shape, is unchanged.
@EnvironmentObject model is received as a Model parameter; it is only used to call bttvEmotesEnabledUpdated/ffzEmotesEnabledUpdated/seventvEmotesEnabledUpdated.
The Swift Binding get/set toggles map directly onto Switch(checked, onCheckedChange), mutating stream.chat flags and notifying model when stream.enabled.
Form/Section have no header text, so they become a LazyColumn with the three rows rendered inline.
.navigationTitle("Emotes") becomes the TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold.
Toggles are laid out as Row(Text + Spacer(weight(1f)) + Switch).
Each toggle mutation also triggers the same model callback as the Swift setter when stream.enabled is true.
FilesLocationView receives 'text: Text' in Swift; it is translated as a String parameter rendered with Text(localized(text)), so call sites pass the raw literal.
FilesLocationView's 'path: URL' becomes 'path: java.net.URI' and path.path() becomes the URI's path property, matching the hand-written platform note for this screen.
The struct's private methods makeSharedUrl/openInFilesApp/openInFinder/copyPathToClipboard became private top-level functions; model is threaded through the ones that need it.
UIPasteboard.general.string is translated to ClipboardManager.setPrimaryClip with AppDelegate.context, and UIApplication.shared.open uses the java.net.URI overload with its success completion.
RecordingsSettingsView collects model.stream with collectAsState before reading stream.recording.recordingPath, since model.stream is a StateFlow.
The Swift .sheet modifier on TextButtonView is translated to Sheet placed inside the same Section, next to TextButtonView, so it can animate in and out.
The multi-line ffmpeg string literals and the long Help paragraphs were joined into single-line Kotlin strings with escaped quotes.
Text is androidx.compose.material3.Text so it picks up the app's LocalTextStyle (17.sp body by default).

The SwiftUI struct became one @Composable fun StreamOpenStreamingPlatformSettingsView(model, stream) with the same name; the model and stream are plain parameters instead of @EnvironmentObject and a stored property.
The Swift methods submitUrl and submitRoom cannot be members of a composable, so they are top-level functions with explicit model and stream parameters and identical names.
Form/Section became a LazyColumn with one item per TextEditNavigationView row; .navigationTitle became the title of a Material 3 TopAppBar inside a Scaffold.
String(localized:) calls use the shared localized(...) helper from package com.moblin.android.
guard isValidWebSocketUrl(url: value) == nil else { return } became an early return when isValidWebSocketUrl(value) is non-nil.
onChange: isValidWebSocketUrl is passed as a lambda { value -> isValidWebSocketUrl(value) } because the Kotlin TextEditNavigationView takes a function-typed onChange parameter.
TextEditNavigationView is imported from com.moblin.android.view.utils with the same title/value/onChange/onSubmit/placeholder argument names as in the Swift call site.
No declared Kotlin types: the file only declares the composable and two top-level helper functions.
Swift @State var bitrate is filled by the SwiftUI memberwise initializer, so the Composable takes it as an initialBitrate parameter and mirrors it with remember { mutableStateOf() }.
model.isRecording is a StateFlow on Model and is read with collectAsState().
Slider step 32 over 0...320 becomes steps = 9 (Compose counts the values between the endpoints); onEditingChanged's end-of-drag branch becomes onValueChangeFinished.
.disabled(stream.enabled && model.isRecording) is applied to the whole HStack in Swift; in Compose only the Slider supports an enabled flag, so the Text keeps its normal colour.
The empty Text("") spacer line in the footer is rendered as Spacer(Modifier.height(16.dp)) to reproduce the line break.
.navigationTitle("Audio") is rendered by a Scaffold TopAppBar inside the same composable.
calcBitrate keeps its name as a private top-level function and returns Int (the Swift UInt32 maps to Int outside wire-format code).
Form/Section are translated to a LazyColumn with a header Text item, the bitrate row item and a footer item.
@Published/ObservableObject settings objects became plain @Serializable classes with var properties; StateFlow is not used because these models are persisted with kotlinx.serialization.
Swift's defensive container.decode(key, Type, default) fallbacks are expressed as Kotlin property/constructor defaults, and enums keep the persisted Swift string via @SerialName.
Post-decode work (Srt/Stream migrations, keychain token moves, layout string updates) lives in init blocks, so it also runs when a fresh object is constructed.

Keychain side effects Swift performs inside encode(to:) cannot be hooked by kotlinx.serialization; encodeYouTubeAuthState() is kept but not called by the generated serializer, so callers must persist it.
youTubeAuthState is the AppAuth shim's OIDAuthState? (hooks HOID.1-6): isYouTubeAuthorized() reads isAuthorized and the auth state is archived to and unarchived from the keychain as JSON.
CMVideoDimensions became android.util.Size; the static '>' operator is companion fun greaterThan because Kotlin enum comparison is final.
UInt32/Int32 fields (bitrate, maxKeyFrameInterval, latency, packetsInFlight) are Int, and the iOS 26 availability gates around VBR rate control were dropped.
Date -> java.time.Instant and Data -> ByteArray; their JSON representation differs from the Swift encoders, and clone() shares nested class instances where Swift copied structs.
Form is rendered as a LazyColumn inside a Scaffold whose TopAppBar title is the Swift navigationTitle "Audio".
The Picker becomes an ExposedDropdownMenuBox; SettingsStreamAudioCodec.allCases maps to the Kotlin enum .entries and $0.toString() maps to .toString().
@State bitrate becomes remember { mutableStateOf(...) } seeded from stream.audioBitrate (converted from bps to Mbps).
Slider onEditingChanged(begin) is mapped to onValueChangeFinished so the new bitrate is only committed when the drag ends.
onChange(of: stream.audioCodec) becomes LaunchedEffect(audioCodec).
.disabled(stream.enabled && model.isLive) becomes enabled = !locked on the codec field and slider.
@ObservedObject/@EnvironmentObject properties are assumed to be MutableStateFlow and are read with collectAsState(); writes go through .value.
calcBitrate is translated as a private top-level function using kotlin.math.ceil to match rounded(.up).
Diff only adds the new ChatLineStyle constructor argument `font: chat.font` in makeChatLineStyle.
Kept the existing Android style of hoisting SettingsChat reads into locals, so `val font = chat.font` is passed as `font = font`.
No imports were added; type inference covers the new argument as in the rest of the file.
Everything else in the file is unchanged, byte-identical to the current Kotlin version.
The SwiftUI views became @Composable functions with identical names; @EnvironmentObject/SettingsStream model objects are now explicit parameters.
Model.objectWillChange.send() calls were dropped: Compose recomposes from the model's StateFlow updates, so no manual invalidation is needed.
Form/Section/footer became a Column with verticalScroll; section headers are plain Texts and blank separator lines are 8.dp Spacers.
ForEach + .onDelete + .contextMenuDeleteButton became one per-row delete IconButton that uses makeOffsets(...) and the private deletePriority helper.
Slider's onEditingChanged(begin) maps to onValueChangeFinished, which commits the clamped priority and calls model.updateSrtlaPriorities().
.navigationTitle became a Scaffold with a Material 3 TopAppBar (hence @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)).
Verify the Kotlin enum constant used in the when-branch: SettingsStreamDetailedProtocol.SRTLA (Swift case .srtla).
deletePriority expects a List<Int>, so makeOffsets(...)'s result is converted with toList(); adapt if it already returns List<Int>.
final class AnamorphicLensEffect -> plain class AnamorphicLensEffect, since VideoEffect is an open class and this is the leaf.
The Swift init(settings:) becomes the primary constructor with a private var property; the base VideoEffect takes no constructor arguments so it is called as VideoEffect().
setSettings hops to processorPipelineQueue with launch, matching Swift's processorPipelineQueue.async; this@AnamorphicLensEffect disambiguates the property from the parameter.
executeEarly keeps the Swift two-parameter shape (image, info) so it overrides VideoEffect.executeEarly.
The stretch crop filter is the CIFilter.stretchCrop() shim (CIStretchCrop) with inputImage, centerStretchAmount as Float and size as CGPoint.
filter.outputImage ?? image keeps the Apple fallback through the Kotlin elvis operator.
settings.scale is read inside the pipeline hop, so the latest settings value applies as on iOS.
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped.
Swift `deinit { stop() }` has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped; stop() must be called by the caller (VideoEffect.removed() is the natural hook).
The device-motion handler drops `[weak self]` and uses a WeakReference so the CMMotionManager does not keep the effect alive.
`minimalBoundingRectWithAspect` stays a file-private top-level function, with CGFloat mapped to Double throughout.
execute/executeMetalPetal override VideoEffect with the base parameter names; Swift's unnamed second argument becomes `info`.
CMMotionManager, OperationQueue and CMDeviceMotion come from com.moblin.android.platform.coremotion; operationQueue.underlyingQueue is assigned the processorPipelineQueue scope in the init block.
MTILayer is constructed with named arguments (content, position, size, rotation) matching Swift's .init(content:position:size:rotation:), and filter.outputImage keeps the `?: image` fallback.
The CIImage chain keeps Swift's translated/transformed/scaled/cropped calls from the Core Image shim.
`operationQueue` is declared after the other properties so its initializer runs before the init block, as the Swift `override init()` did.
HandleSettingsUrls is an extension of Model, so every method becomes a file-private or public top-level `fun Model.` extension in com.moblin.android.various.model.

handleSettingsUrls takes Set<android.net.Uri> instead of Set<UIOpenURLContext>; the file extension test uses `(url.path ?: "").substringAfterLast('.', "")` compared case-insensitively with equals(ignoreCase = true).

Flow-backed settings used here (isLive, isRecording, presentingStreamImportCollisionConfirmation, quickButtonsGeneral.twoColumns/showName/enableScroll and each quick button's enabled/page) are read and written through `.value`; pendingStreamImportCollisionTitle/Action, createStreamWizard.presenting and presentingSetup stay plain vars.
MoblinSettingsUrlStream.video.bitrate stays UInt? and is range-checked as UInt (50000u..50000_000u) then stored with toInt(); assistant.port is UShort and is stored with toInt().
streamImportCollisionTitle replaces %@ with java.util.Formatter's %s, as java.util.Formatter throws on %@.
startAccessingSecurityScopedResource/stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource are dropped: a .moblinSettings file always arrives as a readable file URI, so importSettingsFromFile is called with url.path.
try/catch around MoblinSettingsUrl.fromString is kept as a Kotlin try expression returning error.localizedMessage from the catch block.
nativeLowLightBoost is declared as a top-level var exactly like the Swift file; nothing on Android binds it yet, it is only read by the setLowLightBoost TODO in setDeviceFormat.

DeviceOutputHandler replaces the removed AVCaptureVideoDataOutputSampleBufferDelegate extension: it already knows device and cameraId, so the old AVCaptureConnection.inputPorts lookup (and its TODO) is gone.
DeviceOutputHandler.delegate is a plain reference; Kotlin has no weak property, use java.lang.ref.WeakReference if a retain cycle shows up.
makeCaptureSession stays an opaque Any stub: neither AVCaptureMultiCamSession nor automaticallyConfiguresCaptureDeviceForWideColor exist on Android.
The isVideoOrientationSupported guard was dropped because CaptureSessionDevice.connection is typed Any; the hand-written setOrientation in the platform layer performs the support check.

configure() was inlined into attach() by the Swift change, so the Kotlin attach() now calls removeDevices/attachDevice/updateCameraControls/attachCameraPreviewLayers directly and no longer calls updateDevicesFormat().
removeDevices now removes photoConnection and photoOutput before the video connection/input/output, matching the new Swift order; Swift's devices.removeAll() becomes devices.clear().
AVCaptureConnection mirroring/stabilization and setSampleBufferDelegate remain a TODO inside the device loop of attach().
URL values are stored as String everywhere; java.net.URI is used only inside lowResolutionGiphyUrl.
Swift's inout Int id is threaded through createTwitchSegments as an IntArray of size 1; Emotes.createSegments must use the same convention.
TwitchApi calls keep the completion-handler style of the Swift source instead of suspend functions.
@MainActor class isolation has no Kotlin equivalent; MainTimer keeps the 30 second retry loop for badges and cheermotes.
The weak delegate becomes a nullable constructor property.
ChatMessageEmote ranges map to IntRange and text offsets use Unicode code points, mirroring Swift's unicodeScalars.
TwitchChatMessage parses the raw IRC line inside its init block and throws MessageError for missing or unknown commands.
logger.debug maps to Log.d with the tag TwitchChat.
@main MoblinApp becomes object MoblinApp (holding globalModel) plus a top-level @Composable MoblinApp() that creates the Model once with remember and stores it in globalModel.
Android has no App/Scene entry point, so MainActivity is added at the end to host MoblinApp(); it and AppDelegate must be registered in AndroidManifest.xml.

AppDelegate maps to android.app.Application, using Application.registerActivityLifecycleCallbacks to track the current activity so orientationLock can call Activity.requestedOrientation like the Swift didSet did.
Sub-views (StreamView, CameraPreviewView, StreamPreviewView) are passed to MainView as @Composable lambdas, which is the Compose equivalent of the SwiftUI view parameters.
Model @Published state (show, toast, orientation, database) is read with collectAsState(); controllers (webBrowserController, createStreamWizard) stay plain properties.

SceneDelegate is not used on Android: settings URLs come through platform/AndroidHost, and the external display scene is platform/uikit/ExternalDisplay (DisplayManager presentation displays shown with android.app.Presentation), installed from MainActivity by a hook.
.background(.black) becomes a Box with Modifier.background(Color.Black); .ignoresSafeArea() is a no-op because nothing applies window insets here.
targetEnvironment(macCatalyst) branches (storeSettings, replaysStorage.store, exit(EXIT_SUCCESS)) are not part of the Android build and were dropped.
BingoView stays a private @Composable function; since it is no longer a type, its private squareSize helper becomes a private top-level function and the local val keeps Swift's name.
BingoCardEffect's constructor takes a Compose Size (E6 convention, ModelScene passes one) and converts it once with toCGSize().
ImageRenderer<BingoView> becomes the non-generic ImageRenderer; the Swift arguments are copied into settings0/sceneWidget0/canvasSize0 locals before the content lambda captures them, never this.
@MainActor on setSettings and setup is dropped: both are called on the main thread as on iOS.
The sink's [weak self] is a java.lang.ref.WeakReference to the effect, so the renderer never keeps the effect alive.
minimumScaleFactor(0.4) plus lineLimit(3) is a Text whose onTextLayout lowers the font size while hasVisualOverflow, down to 0.4 times the requested size.
SettingsWidgetBingoCard and SettingsSceneWidget are settings classes, so their properties are read directly (no collectAsState) and the renderer's objectWillChange drives re-rendering.
.foregroundStyle on the ZStack is applied by passing foregroundColorColor explicitly to each Text; the cell and grid outlines use Modifier.background plus Modifier.border.
Data is mapped to ByteArray; the file-private helpers getFourBytesBe() and hexString() replace the Swift Data extensions used by this file.
RTMP wire fields use UByte/UInt (messageTypeId, messageTimestamp, messageStreamId) and every Flv/Rtmp enum lookup goes through fromRawValue().
CMSampleBuffer becomes MediaSample with a microsecond presentationTimeUs; MediaSample has no duration/decode-timestamp field, so the CMSampleTimingInfo duration and DTS are computed but not carried.
AAC decoding is TODO: AVAudioFormat/AVAudioConverter/AVAudioCompressedBuffer/AVAudioPCMBuffer have to become a MediaCodec audio/mp4a-latm decoder that yields 16 bit PCM.
The Swift weak client reference is a plain nullable reference; stop() still clears it.
URL(string:) is replaced by java.net.URI built with runCatching, and URL.path() by URI.path.
Video still runs through VideoDecoder (MediaCodec based) from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.codec.video and frames are handed to RtmpServerClient.handleFrame as MediaSample.

stopInternal/sendMessage/handleClientConnected/handleAudioBuffer/handleFrame are called positionally, and RtmpChunk/RtmpCommandMessage use named type/chunkStreamId/message/streamId/transactionId arguments; verify those names against the other rtmpserver files.
Added the Platform.youTube branch to banUser and timeoutUser, calling banYouTubeUser with channelId = userId.
Kotlin keeps userId as a String (non-null after the early return), same as the other branches.
duration stays nullable: null for ban, the caller's Int for timeout.
No other line of the file changed.
Swift `final class` becomes a plain Kotlin `class`; the `@unchecked Sendable` conformance has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped.

`DispatchQueue.global().async` becomes `CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO).launch`; `processorPipelineQueue.async` becomes `processorPipelineQueue.launch` since processorPipelineQueue is already a CoroutineScope.
The Swift `init(imageStorage:widgetId:)` becomes the Kotlin primary constructor; `super.init()` is implicit through `VideoEffect()` in the class header and the body work moved into an `init` block.
`private let filter` keeps the inferred `CICompositeOperation` type returned by `CIFilter.sourceOverCompositing()`; writes go through its `inputImage`/`backgroundImage` members.
`guard let originalImage, let sceneWidget` is translated as two early-return `?: return image` bindings of the nullable properties.
CIImage is built with `CIImage(data = data, options = mapOf(CIImageOption.applyOrientationProperty to true))` and is nullable, so the read path uses a `?: return@launch`.
`self.originalImage` / `self.sceneWidget` inside coroutine lambdas are qualified as `this@ImageEffect` because the lambda receiver is the CoroutineScope.

The overrides keep the base-class parameter names `image`/`info` and call `applyEffectsResizeMirrorMove` / `applyEffectsResizeMirrorMoveMetalPetal` with named arguments; `widgetShape` uses its default.
@MainActor dropped: MutableStateFlow assignments are thread safe and the effect methods are called from the same places as on iOS.
EmoteComboState's @Published properties become MutableStateFlow and are read with collectAsState (the emote URL is kept as a java.net.URI because CacheAsyncImage takes one).
ImageRenderer<EmoteComboView> becomes the non-generic ImageRenderer, and its content lambda captures local copies (state0, sceneWidget0, canvasSize0) instead of `this`.
The objectWillChange sink uses a java.lang.ref.WeakReference for self, as required; the sink fires only when comboCount > 0, exactly like the Swift closure.
SwiftUI's .stroke(color:width:) on Text has no Compose counterpart: it is drawn as an outline-only Text (TextStyle drawStyle = Stroke, black) layered under the white filled Text in a Box.
CacheAsyncImage has no modifier parameter, so the Swift .frame(width:height:) is applied by wrapping it in a Box(Modifier.size(size.dp)).
.resizable().scaledToFit() is Image(bitmap = image, contentScale = ContentScale.Fit, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize()).
post.segments.firstOrNull()?.url?.url(animated = false) yields a String in Kotlin, parsed once with URI inside runCatching before the combo counter is updated.
deinit is dropped: the WebKit shim removes script message handlers itself, per the shim rules.

String.data(using: .utf8) cannot fail in Kotlin, so createStyleSheetSource has no failure branch; the logger.info call in that unreachable branch is omitted and the base64 uses java.util.Base64 (standard alphabet, padded like Swift).
@Published private(set) var layout is ported to `val layout = MutableStateFlow<SettingsWidgetLayout?>(null)` and every `layout = x` writes `layout.value`.

Per the BrowserEffect port note, `proxyServer` and `setProxyServer(endpoint:)` take java.net.InetSocketAddress? and are converted to NWEndpoint with NWEndpoint.hostPort(NWEndpoint.Host(a.hostString), NWEndpoint.Port(a.port)) before configuration.setHttpProxy.
MetalPetalWidgetShape is imported from com.moblin.android.videoeffects (declared next to the MTIImage compositing helpers); adjust the import if it lives in media.haishinkit.media.video.
@MainActor is dropped: timers run through MainTimer and pipeline work through processorPipelineQueue.launch, matching the Swift queues.

WidgetCrop is a data class and SettingsWidgetCrop keeps Int x/y/width/height, so the crop rect maths stays integer exactly like the Swift `Int(snapshot.extent.height) - crop.crop.y - crop.crop.height`.
`url.host()` becomes java.net.URI.host (nullable), falling back to "?" as in Swift.
DispatchQueue.main.async became CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main.immediate).launch { }, the main-thread form of the platform shims; the async block therefore returns with return@launch.
SwiftUI Canvas/Path/ImageRenderer are translated against the Compose-backed shims: the Canvas closures become Compose Canvas DrawScope lambdas and Path is androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Path.
In the Kotlin port DrawOnStreamLine.points are Compose Offsets, so each point is converted with toCGPoint() before being passed to transformPoint.
uiImage.cgImage is a non-null identity extension in the port, so Swift's optional chaining uiImage.cgImage?.toEffectImage() is written without the safe call.
SwiftUI .background(.clear).frame(w,h:) became Compose Modifier.size(w,h).background(Color.Transparent) so the modifier order matches SwiftUI's inside-out order.
path.addEllipse(in: CGRect(x:y:width:1,height:1)) is written as path.addOval(Rect(left, top, right, bottom)).
The class is a plain Kotlin class instead of Swift's final class, and @unchecked Sendable is dropped because Kotlin has no equivalent.
filter is left with an inferred CICompositeOperation type from CIFilter.sourceOverCompositing(), keeping the Swift property name.
makeFaceMask stays a file-private top-level function; FaceIconPlacement is a private data class replacing the Swift tuple return of calcIconPlacement.
FaceEffectPrivacyMode is a sealed class with nested Blur/Pixellate/BackgroundImage/Icon exactly as the platform layer expects (BackgroundImage holds CIImage?, Icon holds android.graphics.Bitmap?).

The detections-mode cases are referenced as the top-level Off and Now declarations in com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.media.video, and sceneDetections() is imported as a VideoEffectInfo extension from that package.
setSettings uses processorPipelineQueue.launch and assigns through this@FaceEffect so the captured locals do not shadow the properties.
faceMasks keeps Swift's [Float: MTIMask?] cache semantics: presence is tested with containsKey so a cached nil mask is not recomputed.
UIImage(named: "AppIconNoBackground") becomes Bundle.image("AppIconNoBackground") and the cgImage identity property is kept.
rotation in the icon placement is Double because detection helpers keep Double math; it is converted with toFloat() only for MTILayer.rotation and negated for the counter-rotation.
FaceEffectSettings is a plain data class (not a settings-file class), so it has val fields and is replaced wholesale by setSettings.
The Swift diff only adds `font: settings.font` to makeChatLineStyle; the Kotlin ChatLineStyle call gains `font = settings.font` after `displayStyle`.
Everything else in ChatEffect.kt stays byte-identical, including the Android-only hooks (PipelineStats.increment, Dispatchers.Main.immediate, WeakReference, toBitmap/cgImage usage).
The settings.objectWillChange subscription of the Swift renderer stays dropped, as in the current Kotlin file: setSettings calls renderer.scheduleRender() instead.
`settings.font` is a settings value object passed straight through; no extra import is required because its type is inferred from ChatLineStyle's `font` parameter.
QrCodeEffect is a final Swift class, so the Kotlin class is not open; only execute/executeMetalPetal keep override.
The Swift init(widget:) becomes the primary constructor parameter private val widget.
CGRect and CGSize are identity-compared classes in the platform layer, so the guard's extent/size inequality is written as explicit width/height comparisons.
The two execute methods use the local `val newSceneWidget = newSceneWidget ?: return image` to reproduce `guard let newSceneWidget` shorthand over the property.
processorPipelineQueue is already a CoroutineScope in Kotlin, so `async` becomes `.launch { }` staying on the pipeline thread.
String.data(using: .utf8) cannot fail in Kotlin, so `toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8)` is used without the failure branch.
image.scaled(x:y:) and toEffectImage(isOpaque:) resolve to the extensions in this same package (EffectUtils.kt).
filter.outputImage is the CIQRCodeGenerator shim; message and correctionLevel keep Apple's names.
Swift Deque<CIImage> maps to kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque with popFirst() -> removeFirstOrNull().

processorPipelineQueue.async becomes processorPipelineQueue.launch, and property writes inside the lambda are qualified with this@SnapshotEffect to avoid shadowing by the constructor/setter parameters.

VideoEffectInfo.presentationTimeStamp is Long microseconds, so CMTime.seconds becomes / 1_000_000.0; the kCMTimeInvalidUs sentinel is turned into Double.NaN to preserve Swift's CMTime.invalid comparison semantics.
SnapshotEffect is a final class, so the Kotlin class is not open and its overrides still use override.
toEffectImage(isOpaque = true) is the existing extension from EffectUtils.kt in the same package, so no import is needed.
applyEffectsResizeMirrorMoveMetalPetal is called without widgetShape, using its declared default null.
showtime is the Swift stored property initialised in init(showtime: Int); it is a constructor parameter plus a body property in Kotlin.
PollState keeps its Swift shape: a private class whose @Published text is a MutableStateFlow, read in PollView with collectAsState like @ObservedObject.
PollView becomes a private @Composable function; scaledFontSize is a private top-level helper returning Float (CGFloat -> Float) computed from CGSize.maximum().

The Swift modifier chain is reversed: clip(RoundedCornerShape(10.dp)) then background(Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.75f)) then padding(end = 7.dp); the font goes through CompositionLocalProvider(LocalTextStyle provides ...) so it reaches both children.
ImageRenderer<PollView> becomes the non-generic ImageRenderer built from a lambda that captures only the local state copy; the objectWillChange.sink body uses a WeakReference in place of [weak self].
init(canvasSize: Size) takes the Compose Size ModelScene passes, converts it once with toCGSize(), and defers setup() onto the main thread as DispatchQueue.main.async did.
setOverlay hops onto processorPipelineQueue to publish the rendered bitmap, matching the Swift async block.
execute and executeMetalPetal keep the Swift logic: sourceOverCompositing filter with the overlay moved to the top-right, and positionComposited for the MetalPetal path.
@State presentingVersionHistory becomes remember { mutableStateOf(false) }.
SwiftUI Form/List is rendered as a LazyColumn inside a Scaffold so .navigationTitle 'About' maps to the TopAppBar title.

NavigationLink to AboutAttributionsSettingsView has no navigation-compose dependency here; it is exposed through the new onNavigate: (String) -> Unit parameter using the destination type name as the route.
.sheet(isPresented:) becomes a conditional ModalBottomSheet with onDismissRequest clearing the flag.
The ZStack containing AboutVersionHistorySettingsView and CloseButtonTopRightView maps to a Box with the close-button overlay emitted after the content.

Helper composables TextItemLocalizedView, TextButtonView, ExternalUrlButtonView and CloseButtonTopRightView are imported from their packages and called with named parameters (name/value, text/onClick, url/content, onClick).
Plain Swift Text literals are kept as plain strings; nothing in this file used String(localized:), so localized() is not called here.
No iOS-only framework APIs are used, so no TODO markers are required.
processorPipelineQueue.async becomes processorPipelineQueue.launch; property writes inside the lambda are qualified with this@VTuberEffect because launch's block has the CoroutineScope as receiver.
info.presentationTimeStamp is Long microseconds in the port, so Swift's .seconds becomes / 1_000_000.0.
VTuberFace is a data class with var fields; the value handed to the open updateModel is passed through structCopy to preserve Swift's value-type copy on hand-off.

Vision detection helpers calcFaceAngle/calcFaceAngleSide/isMouthOpen/isLeftEyeOpen/isRightEyeOpen are extension functions imported from com.moblin.android.platform.vision, and VideoEffectInfo.faceDetections is imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.media.video.
.init(contentRegion:) becomes MetalPetalWidgetShape(contentRegion = renderedImage.extent), imported from com.moblin.android.videoeffects alongside resizeMirror/move/resizeMirrorMoveComposited.
VideoEffectDetectionsMode.Interval is a top-level class in com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.media.video, so the returned mode is Interval(videoSourceId, 0.1).
The class is open because Swift's VTuberEffect is not final; @unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped.
Unused Swift parameters (_ cameraFieldOfView, etc.) keep their names in the Kotlin signatures so call sites and overrides stay identical.
MaskEffect becomes a class extending VideoEffect(); the Swift @unchecked Sendable conformance has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped.
The CIImage shim has no translated(x:y:), so makeMaskImage uses transformed(by = CGAffineTransform(translationX = extent.minX, y = extent.minY)).
The shim CGRect has identity equality, so the Swift cachedExtent comparisons use the file-private isSameRectAs helper to keep the same cache hits as Swift.
MaskEffectPoint and MaskEffectSettings are settings value types: data classes with val fields and structural equality, matching the Equatable structs.
setSettings runs its body with processorPipelineQueue.launch, the stand-in for DispatchQueue.async; it resets exactly the caches Swift resets.
SettingsMaskBackgroundType entries transparent/solid/checkerboard are referenced directly, never through rawValue.
makeCheckerboardImage allocates a device-RGB CGContext and makeMaskCgImage a device-gray one; both return Bitmap? where Swift returned CGImage?.
The model file is decoded by hand with codableJson: the top-level JSON object maps numeric string keys to layers and is sorted by that numeric key, matching Swift's sorted(by: Int($0.key) ?? 0).
PngCoordinate parses the "Vector2(x, y)" string with a Kotlin Regex, standing in for Swift's firstMatch(of: /Vector2\(([-\d]+), ([-\d]+)\)/).
BlinkTalkState keeps its Int raw values and gets a companion fromRawValue, standing in for Swift's failable BlinkTalkState(rawValue:).
Base64 image data is decoded with java.util.Base64 inside runCatching (Swift's failable Data(base64Encoded:)) and turned into an EffectImageCgImage through the Bitmap.toEffectImage() extension.
DispatchQueue-style async calls become processorPipelineQueue.launch; the captured self is this@PngTuberEffect, exactly like Swift's strong self capture.
Face pose helpers (calcFaceAngle, isMouthOpen, isLeftEyeOpen) and VideoEffectInfo.faceDetections(videoSourceId) are called on the hand-written Vision and video shims.
MTILayer keeps MetalPetal's contentFlipOptions (donotFlip / flipHorizontally) and the default contentRegion; flipHorizontally replaces [.flipHorizontally].
The private Swift helper classes are plain Kotlin classes, and VideoEffect stays the open base class the effect overrides.
interpolate3d now takes a (Int, Int, Int) -> SIMD3 lookup lambda instead of a flat List<SIMD3>; all call sites pass a Kotlin lambda.
convertLutTo64 was replaced by makeLutCube(dimension, lut), which clamps the dimension to 64 and interpolates only when the source dimension differs.
lutEffectConvertCube now returns Pair<Float, ByteArray> (the Swift tuple (Float, Data)) instead of an SC3DLut; makeCubeData and convertLutTo64 were removed.
Data stays ByteArray, and both lutEffectConvertLut and lutEffectConvertCube return Pair<Float, ByteArray>.

makeLutCgImage's Accelerate vImage_Buffer/vImageConvert_PlanarFtoPlanar8 float-to-byte pass has no Android counterpart; the existing hand-written per-component rounding loop (floor(v * 255 + 0.5) clamped to 0..255) produces the same bytes and was kept.
The SIMD4 cube array is serialized little-endian with the existing lutFloatsToData helper (ByteBuffer LITTLE_ENDIAN), matching Swift's Data(bytes: cube, count: cube.count * 16).
The 16 bit LUT path reads two bytes per component little-endian instead of the removed loadUnaligned; the bitsPerComponent and length guards now match the Swift order.
LutEffect.loadCube is a new private function that installs the filter and MetalPetal lookup table on processorPipelineQueue; loadDiskCubeLut and loadImageLut now just delegate to it.
newLocations starts empty and nextNewLocation now returns Location?, so it uses firstOrNull() instead of first()
isSnapshotInProgress guards update() and is cleared on processorPipelineQueue in both the failure and success paths of the snapshotter completion
mapSnapshotter.start uses the non-optional local instead of the optional property, matching the Swift change
MusicKit has no Android counterpart: the subscription offer, MusicSubscription updates and the Apple Music player/queue state are stubbed with TODO() so the rest of the screen is fully translated.

musicPlayer.state / musicPlayer.queue are not in the Android glossary, so they are read through private TODO-backed @Composable helpers rememberMusicPlayerState()/rememberMusicPlayerQueue() that must be wired to a real Android music backend.
Form -> LazyColumn, each Section -> its own item (and items() for the playlist rows); the 'Playlist' Section header becomes a header Text.
Private placeholder data classes (MusicPlayerState, MusicPlayerQueue, MusicQueueEntry, MusicSubscriptionState) stand in for the MusicKit types until an Android music backend exists.
.font(.title) -> MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge sizing on the icons; the current playlist row uses FontWeight.Bold.
Icons.FastRewind/FastForward/Pause/MusicNote come from androidx.compose.material:material-icons-extended (only PlayArrow is in the core icon set).
.onSubmit -> KeyboardOptions(imeAction = ImeAction.Done) with KeyboardActions(onDone = ...).
.navigationTitle("Apple Music") is rendered by the Scaffold TopAppBar title.
apple_only: MusicKit MusicSubscription.subscriptionUpdates
MusicKit MusicSubscriptionOffer (musicSubscriptionOffer modifier)
MusicKit ApplicationMusicPlayer state and queue (musicPlayer)

notes: VideoSourceEffectSettings is a plain data class with var fields; PositionInterpolator stays a non-final class so current, target and update are open (current keeps Swift's private(set) via a private Kotlin setter).
DispatchQueue.async on processorPipelineQueue becomes processorPipelineQueue.launch { } with this@VideoSourceEffect for the captured self.
stableBoundingBox(imageSize:) is the VNFaceObservation extension of the hand-written Vision shim in com.moblin.android.platform.vision and is called unchanged.

Swift's CIImage helper translated(x:y:) has no counterpart in the declared Core Image shim, so it is written as transformed(by = CGAffineTransform(translationX = -cropRegion.minX, y = -cropY)), which is what the helper does.
VideoEffectInfo.presentationTimeStamp is microseconds, so every .seconds usage becomes presentationTimeStamp / 1_000_000.0.
guard let becomes ?: return / ?: continue, and .rounded(.down) becomes kotlin.math.floor.
The rotation switch stays a when over 90.0 / 180.0 / 270.0 using CIImage.oriented(CGImagePropertyOrientation...).
@unchecked Sendable is dropped; Kotlin has no sendability annotation.
Form/Section became a Scaffold + LazyColumn; .navigationTitle is rendered as the TopAppBar title.
.deleteDisabled plus .onDelete are implemented as a Material3 SwipeToDismissBox that is disabled while only one preset remains.
contextMenuDeleteButton has no Compose counterpart and is left as a TODO marker.
onMove (List drag-to-reorder) has no Compose counterpart and is left as a TODO marker.
database.bitratePresets is read with collectAsState() and updated by assigning a new list to the MutableStateFlow value.
The created preset uses SettingsBitratePreset(id = UUID.randomUUID(), bitrate = 1_000_000) matching the Swift initializer.
String(localized: "a preset") maps to localized("a preset") from package com.moblin.android.
The Section footer is the last LazyColumn item: SwipeLeftToDeleteHelpView(kind = localized("a preset")).

NavigationLink + Form + navigationTitle are collapsed into a Scaffold with a TopAppBar titled "Layout"; the link's label Text("Layout") is merged into that title, and no navigation-compose is pulled in.
SettingsChat writes assume the port exposes mutable state (chat.height.value = ..., etc.); if the port exposes read-only StateFlow, route these through setter functions instead.
Slider 'onEditingChanged' (reload only when editing ends) maps to Slider.onValueChangeFinished -> model.reloadChatMessages().
database.appMode and database.showAllSettings are read with collectAsState(); the enum case .chatPhone is assumed to be SettingsAppMode.chatPhone.
Slider step counts computed from Swift step: 0.01 over 0.2..1.0 -> 79 steps; 5 over 0.0..200.0 -> 39 steps.
top-level 'let sliderValuePercentageWidth = 60.0' kept as a top-level Double val and applied as sliderValuePercentageWidth.dp.
Text values use Kotlin string templates instead of Swift string interpolation.
NavigationStack and Form become a Scaffold with a LazyColumn; no onNavigate parameter is emitted because this screen pushes no destinations.
@Binding properties become a value parameter plus an onChange lambda: log -> onLogChange, presentingLog -> onPresentingLogChange.
SettingsDebug.logFilter is read with collectAsState() and written through .value, assuming the port exposes it as a MutableStateFlow<String>.
model.formatLog(...) is expected to return the share URL/path as a String, matching ShareItem.url.
.sheet(item:) becomes a ModalBottomSheet shown while ShareItem is non-null; presentationDetents and presentationCompactAdaptation have no Compose counterpart and were dropped.
Toolbar bar-trailing buttons become TopAppBar actions; CloseToolbar is placed in navigationIcon because in Swift it wraps its own ToolbarItem.
SF Symbols mapped: square.and.arrow.up -> Icons.Default.Share, trash -> Icons.Default.Delete, arrow.clockwise -> Icons.Default.Refresh.
isMessageVisible is a private top-level function that takes the current filter alongside the message.

@State properties became local remember { mutableStateOf(...) } state seeded from new @Composable parameters that keep the Swift property names (fontSize, fontDesign, fontWeight, textColor, accentColor).
@EnvironmentObject model and @ObservedObject alert became plain parameters; their StateFlow properties are read directly (no collectAsState needed in this file).
onChange(of:) was mapped to LaunchedEffect(key) as required by the port rules; note that unlike Swift's onChange it also fires on first composition, so alert/model are re-synced once on entry.
Picker -> ExposedDropdownMenuBox with an OutlinedTextField anchor; Modifier.menuAnchor(MenuAnchorType.PrimaryNotEditable) requires Material3 1.3.0 or newer.
Section headers are emitted as MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium Text placed before the section items.
Slider step: 5 over 10...80 maps to valueRange = 10f..80f with steps = 13 (intermediate points).
SettingsFontDesign.allCases / SettingsFontWeight.allCases map to the Kotlin enum 'entries' list and are rendered with the enum's toString(), matching the Swift .toString() call.

RgbColorPickerView is invoked as RgbColorPickerView(title, color, onChange) with the color passed by value and written back through a callback (Swift's Binding<Color>); verify against the real signature in com.moblin.android.view.utils.
First section is renamed to "Font" and keeps the size row; FontSettingsView plus the two bold toggles moved into it under database.showAllSettings.
The Big GIF scale row moved out of the size section into a new second Section titled "General", which is now wrapped in `if (database.showAllSettings)`.
The Display style picker and the Timestamp/Badges/Animated emotes/Shared chat icons/Compact events toggles moved with it, and the bold toggles were removed from that section.

FontSettingsView from com.moblin.android.view.utils is imported and called with the same shape used for RgbColorPickerView here: value property plus an ignored change callback and a trailing onChange lambda.
Colors section is untouched.
Size row keeps FormRow because it shares a row with the slider and the value text.
@EnvironmentObject model and the stream become plain parameters of the composable; no StateFlow is collected here because the view only calls model methods.
Section with only a footer becomes a Column of footer Texts placed after the two TextEditNavigationView rows.
TextEditNavigationView is imported from com.moblin.android.view.utils and called with the same argument labels (title, value, onSubmit, capitalize).
.navigationTitle("SOOP") is rendered as the TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold.
submitChannelName and submitStreamId are kept as top-level functions taking model and stream since they were instance methods on the View.
The Form is replaced by a scrollable Column, which is the direct equivalent for this small settings form.
localized() comes from package com.moblin.android.
No iOS-only API in this file required a TODO().
The Form becomes a LazyColumn inside a Scaffold; .navigationTitle("Snapshot") becomes the TopAppBar title.
SettingsStream / SettingsStreamRecording published properties are treated as MutableStateFlow, read with collectAsState() and written through .value.
The Swift onChange(of:) call to model.setCleanSnapshots() is reproduced with LaunchedEffect plus an initialized flag so it does not fire on first composition.
Section header/footer views become plain leading/trailing Text and Row elements inside the LazyColumn items.
Toggle + isOn binding becomes a Row with a Text label and a Material 3 Switch.
TextEditNavigationView and DiscordLogoAndNameView are reused from com.moblin.android.view.utils and com.moblin.android.view.settings.streams.stream.
String(localized:) maps to the top-level localized() from com.moblin.android.
No top-level Kotlin type is declared; the view is a top-level @Composable function, so declared_types is empty.
Each SwiftUI View becomes a @Composable function with the same name; @EnvironmentObject model is a parameter defaulted from LocalModel.current, as in the rest of the port.
store.iconsInStore, store.myIcons and store.iconImage are StateFlows, collected at the top of each view with collectAsState() so the view recomposes.
The ForEach rows have no onDelete/onMove/swipeActions, so they stay items.forEach { key(it.id) { ... } } and the surrounding List is dropped.
The .tag(icon.image()) modifiers are Picker-only and have no Compose counterpart outside Picker, which takes its options list instead.
Icon assets use AssetImage from com.moblin.android.platform.swiftui; .interpolation(.high) has no equivalent and is dropped.
ProgressView() is CircularProgressIndicator(Modifier.size(20.dp), formPalette().secondaryLabel, 2.dp) and Text is androidx.compose.material3.Text.
The opacity-0 button during a purchase keeps its layout with Modifier.alpha and enabled = !disabled, matching the SwiftUI disabled+opacity pair.
The Restore alert stays inside the Section content where the Swift .alert modifier is attached.
NavigationLink destinations (PasswordView, RelayStreamerUrlView) are reached through the onNavigate(route) callback; the destination wiring and arguments live in a NavHost outside this file.
Settings classes (SettingsMoblink, SettingsMoblinkRelay, SettingsMoblinkStreamer) are assumed to expose their mutable properties as MutableStateFlow: reads use collectAsState(), writes use .value =.
View-local @State variables became remember { mutableStateOf(...) }; the initial value passed by the parent is kept in an initial* parameter.
@Environment(\.dismiss) became an onDismiss: () -> Unit parameter on RelayStreamerUrlView.
.onChange(of:) became LaunchedEffect(value), which also runs on first composition, unlike SwiftUI's onChange.
.navigationTitle became a Scaffold + TopAppBar on the three screens that declared one.

.foregroundStyle(.red) -> color = Color.Red and .bold() -> fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold; .textInputAutocapitalization(.never)/.disableAutocorrection(true) -> KeyboardOptions(capitalization = None, autoCorrectEnabled = false).
Text minimumScaleFactor(0.5) has no Compose counterpart and was replaced by maxLines = 1.
NavigationLink destinations are split into separate Destination composables (NicknameViewDestination, ChatNicknamesSettingsViewDestination); the rows themselves only call onNavigate(name).
SettingsChatNicknames.nicknames is assumed to be a MutableStateFlow<List<SettingsChatNickname>>: reads use collectAsState(), writes assign a new list.
Form/Section/List are collapsed into a LazyColumn; the section footer (SwipeLeftToDeleteHelpView) becomes a plain item.
contextMenuDeleteButton becomes a long press on the row (Modifier.combinedClickable) calling deleteNickname via makeOffsets.
List.onDelete becomes a Material 3 SwipeToDismissBox (end-to-start swipe) that removes the item from the list.
List.onMove drag-to-reorder has no Compose counterpart; the handler is a TODO lambda.
TextButtonView is called with an enabled argument derived from .disabled(nickname.nickname.isEmpty); verify against the util signature.
IndexSet parameters are modelled as List<Int> and makeOffsets is assumed to return List<Int>?.
The SwiftUI Form becomes a LazyColumn; each Section becomes one item with a Column, its header stays a Text and its footer becomes a bodySmall Text.

StreamSrtSettingsView is a @Composable taking model, stream, srt and onNavigate: (String) -> Unit; the two NavigationLink destinations are dispatched as onNavigate("StreamSrtAdaptiveBitrateSettingsView") and onNavigate("StreamSrtConnectionPriorityView").

Published properties are read with collectAsState(); writes call setters assumed on the ported settings classes (srt.setLatency, setOverheadBandwidth, setAdaptiveBitrateEnabled, setMaximumBandwidthFollowInput, setBigPackets, setDnsLookupStrategy, setImplementation).

TextEditNavigationView is called with title/value/onChange/onSubmit/valueFormat plus an enabled flag that carries the Swift .disabled modifier; keyboardType .numbersAndPunctuation is not passed because the ported composable owns its own keyboard options.
StreamSrtAdaptiveBitrateSettingsView and StreamSrtConnectionPriorityView are not called directly so navigation-compose stays out of this file.
navigationTitle "SRT(LA)" becomes the TopAppBar title, which requires @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class) together with the ExposedDropdownMenuBox pickers.
Both Pickers use ExposedDropdownMenuBox; CaseIterable allCases maps to Kotlin enum entries and the cases keep the Swift names official/moblin.
Case values are compared as SettingsStreamSrtImplementation.moblin/official and the low latency warning is shown when implementation == moblin && latency < 1000.
SwiftUI Form/Section becomes a LazyColumn; the Section footer VStack becomes a Column of Texts placed right after the Picker item.

@ObservedObject whip is read with whip.headers.collectAsState()/whip.httpTransport.collectAsState(), so SettingsStreamWhip is assumed to expose MutableStateFlow properties (settings edit and reload need writable state).
Picker is rendered as an ExposedDropdownMenuBox; the .onChange(of:) reload is performed in the DropdownMenuItem onClick since Compose has no implicit binding change callback.
.navigationTitle("WHIP") is rendered as a Scaffold TopAppBar title.
getBearerToken/setBearerToken became top-level private functions taking model/stream/whip because Kotlin has no implicit self; getBearerToken takes the collected headers list so the field recomposes.
setBearerToken mutates whip.headers.value in place (or appends) and assumes SettingsHttpHeader.value is a mutable property.
.disabled(...) is mapped to the enabled parameter of TextEditNavigationView and OutlinedTextField.
Swift's /Bearer (.*)/ prefix match is translated to Regex("^Bearer (.*)$").

SwiftUI Views became @Composable functions: AuthenticationView, KickCategoryPickerView, KickStreamLiveSettingsView, KickAlertsSettingsView, StreamKickSettingsView; Form/Section became scrollable Columns with header Texts.

NavigationLink destinations were replaced by an onNavigate: (String) -> Unit callback; the destination names used here are "KickStreamTitle", "KickStreamCategory", "KickAlertsSettingsViewChat" and "KickAlertsSettingsViewToasts".
@Binding title/category are kept as a value parameter plus an onChange lambda (onTitleChange/onCategoryChange/onPresentingChange); the parent screen still owns that state.
@Environment(\.dismiss) became an onDismiss: () -> Unit parameter on KickCategoryPickerView, and .navigationTitle became the TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold.
.onAppear plus .onChange(of: searchText) were merged into a single LaunchedEffect(searchText) which also performs the initial default-category fetch when the query is empty.
loadKickStreamInfo is a suspend function; DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 1) became delay(1000) and it is invoked from a rememberCoroutineScope() coroutine.

Assumes the ported settings models (SettingsStream, SettingsKickAlerts) expose Compose-state-backed mutable properties (stream.kickChannelName = ..., alerts.subscriptions = ...) and that Model keeps the Swift completion-handler APIs (kickLogin, fetchKickCategories, createKickApi(...).getUser, getKickStreamInfo returning kotlin.Result).
AsyncImage comes from Coil and KickLoginView's presenting/onPresentingChange parameter names are assumed; verify both against the imported packages.

NavigationLink rows become Modifier.clickable calls that invoke onNavigate(name); each destination screen is also kept as a private composable (ChatFilterFormView, ChatFiltersFormView, ChatFilterUsernameEditView, ChatFilterMessageStartEditView) so the Form / TextEditView content is translated in full.
SettingsChatFilter and SettingsChat are treated as ObservableObject models whose @Published properties are MutableStateFlow: values are read with collectAsState() and written through .value.
Section -> a header Text plus its items plus a footer Text; Form/List -> Column + LazyColumn; Toggle -> a Row of Text + Switch.
String(localized:) -> localized() imported from com.moblin.android.
.navigationTitle("Filter" / "Filters") has no in-file equivalent and is left to the host TopAppBar.
The multiline footer string of ChatFilterFilterSettingsView is collapsed into one localized() string; the empty Text("") spacer line is kept as Text(text = "").

Sub-views from com.moblin.android.view.utils (TextItemLocalizedView, DraggableItemPrefixView, SwipeLeftToRemoveHelpView, TextEditView, AddButtonView) and GrayTextView from the streams package are reused as-is.
contextMenuDeleteButton and List.onMove have no Compose counterpart and are left as TODO markers.

WiFiAware and DeviceDiscoveryUI are Apple-only; the WiFiAware types are kept as minimal Kotlin stubs (WAPublishableService, WASubscribableService, WAFeature, WACapabilities, WAPairingInfo, WAPairedDevice) so every Swift signature survives, and their bodies are TODO().

AdvertiseView and SearchView consist entirely of DevicePairingView / DevicePicker, which have no Compose counterpart, so their bodies are TODO(); the picker labels and the SearchView logger.info callback are part of those pickers and are dropped.
SettingsWiFiAware is read via collectAsState() and written with `wiFiAware.enabled.value = ...` / `wiFiAware.role.value = ...`, assuming MutableStateFlow-backed settings properties.

WiFiAwareSettingsView uses a LazyColumn for the Form; PairedDevicesView renders its List with a Column plus forEach instead of a nested LazyColumn, which would be measured with unbounded height inside a LazyColumn item.

The Swift .onChange(of: wiFiAware.enabled) side effect is folded into the Switch onCheckedChange so model.wiFiAwareUpdated() is not fired on first composition (LaunchedEffect(value) always fires once).
The #if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst) guard and all @available(iOS 26, *) annotations are dropped; the file is compiled unconditionally for the Android target.
The role Picker becomes an ExposedDropdownMenuBox with MenuAnchorType.PrimaryNotEditable; .disabled(wiFiAware.enabled) maps to enabled = !enabled on both the anchored field and the expansion handler.
The private serviceName constant is retained for parity although it is only mentioned inside the TODO() reasons.
apple_only: WiFiAware (WAPublishableService.allServices, WASubscribableService.allServices, WAPairedDevice.allDevices, WACapabilities.supportedFeatures, WAFeature.wifiAware)
DeviceDiscoveryUI.DevicePairingView
DeviceDiscoveryUI.DevicePicker

notes: CurrentWiFiNetwork is a file-private class whose @Published properties become private MutableStateFlow fields exposed as read-only StateFlow, read in Compose with collectAsState().

CLLocationManager, CLLocationManagerDelegate and CLAuthorizationStatus come from the CoreLocation shim (platform/corelocation/CLLocationManager.kt): setting the delegate in init gives the first authorization callback, requestWhenInUseAuthorization asks for the location permission, and a denial shows the location warning.
The Form/Section structure becomes a LazyColumn: each Section header and footer becomes its own Text item, matching the Swift header/footer slots.
.navigationTitle("SSID") is rendered as the title of a Scaffold TopAppBar (requires ExperimentalMaterial3Api).
value is @State in Swift but is initialised by the parent, so this composable takes value plus an onValueChange callback and writes updates back through it.

.onChange(of: value) is handled by setting changed = true inside the OutlinedTextField onValueChange callback, which avoids the false positive a LaunchedEffect(value) would produce on first composition.
.onSubmit plus .submitLabel(.done) map to KeyboardOptions(imeAction = ImeAction.Done) with KeyboardActions(onDone = ...).
.onDisappear maps to DisposableEffect(Unit) { onDispose { ... } }; value and the callbacks are read through rememberUpdatedState so the disposal lambda does not capture stale values.
Compose state: published properties of Model, SettingsStream and SettingsTwitchAlerts are treated as MutableStateFlow, so they are read with collectAsState() or .value and written with .value.
NavigationLink destinations are delegated to an onNavigate(destination) callback; navigation-compose is not pulled into this file.
.navigationTitle is rendered as a Scaffold plus TopAppBar, which needs @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class) on those composables.
loadTwitchStreamInfo is a suspend function: the asyncAfter(1s) became kotlinx delay(1000), and callers run it inside rememberCoroutineScope().launch { }.
Inside StreamTwitchSettingsView the private helpers loadStreamInfo and loadTokenExpiresIn are declared before onLoggedIn because Kotlin resolves local functions in declaration order.
The onAppear effect and the searchText effect both run on first composition, so the default Twitch categories are fetched twice at start.
Text edit / button views are called as TextEditNavigationView(title, value, onSubmit, capitalize) and TextButtonView(text) { }, matching the Swift call sites.
CacheAsyncImage is called with url, contentDescription and a sized/clipped Modifier; the Swift placeholder and resizable/scaledToFit content closure are dropped.

NavigationLink is replaced by an onNavigate(title) callback on UrlsView; the Form destination of the link is emitted by an added composable UrlsViewDestination(status, formatUrl, title, showIPv6) that the navigation host should register under that route name.
The iOS fullScreenCover is rendered as Dialog(properties = DialogProperties(usePlatformDefaultWidth = false)) with a white Box that dismisses on tap.

Image(uiImage:) has no Compose counterpart: generateQrCode(url) is expected to return android.graphics.Bitmap? and is drawn with Bitmap.asImageBitmap(); .interpolation(.none) becomes filterQuality = FilterQuality.None.

urlImage(interfaceType:) returns an SF Symbol name as a String, so the file maps those names to Material icons in the private helper urlIconImageVector; the mapping is approximate and requires the androidx.compose.material:material-icons-extended dependency (Wifi, WifiTethering, QrCode, Link, SignalCellularAlt).

status.ipStatuses is read with collectAsState(), so StatusOther must expose that collection as a StateFlow; the IpType of each entry is compared through rawValue ("ipv4"/"ipv6") because that enum lives in another file.
