SwiftUI Section is translated as a Column with a MaterialTheme-styled header Text followed by its rows, so UrlsIpv4View/UrlsIpv6View can be placed inside a single LazyColumn item without nesting lazy lists.

CopyToClipboardButtonView, HCenter and the icons are composed exactly where the Swift code used them; CopyToClipboardButtonView and HCenter come from com.moblin.android.view.utils (same package, no import).
A Button with .buttonStyle(.borderless) holding the qrcode image becomes an IconButton with a 20.dp icon, matching the .font(.system(size: 20)).
DrawOnStreamLine becomes a data class; the Swift `let id = UUID()` maps to a constructor default so Identifiable identity is preserved.
`@MainActor private var drawing` becomes a private top-level `var drawing` in this file, since it must survive recomposition like the SwiftUI global did.

DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) maps to Modifier.pointerInput + detectDragGestures; Compose applies touch slop so a zero-length tap may not start a new line (drawing the single-point dot) as it does in SwiftUI.

GeometryReader is replaced by BoxWithConstraints; model.streamViewLayout(...) is called with maxWidth/maxHeight Dp values instead of a GeometryProxy, and the returned layout is expected to expose Dp size/offset - adjust if the model signature differs.
model.drawOnStreamSize is assigned inside the Canvas draw scope exactly like the Swift drawing closure; move it to Modifier.onSizeChanged if that write triggers a recomposition loop.
ColorPicker has no Compose counterpart, so it is a TODO and appears in unsupported.
SF Symbols map as: trash.fill -> Icons.Default.Delete, arrow.uturn.backward -> Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.Undo (requires material-icons-extended).
.font(.title) on the icons becomes Modifier.size(28.dp) and .accentColor becomes SliderDefaults.colors(thumbColor/activeTrackColor) on the Slider.
EffectSlider's Swift @Binding value became a value parameter plus an onValueChange lambda; Slider 'step: 0.01' is expressed as a derived 'steps' count.
SettingsFace is read via collectAsState(); the port's StateFlow properties expose no setter, so every @Binding write is a TODO listed in unsupported.
Picker -> ExposedDropdownMenuBox (with ExposedDropdownMenu) and .tint(.white) applied as white text color.
The PhotosPicker branch is one TODO; model.saveFaceBackgroundImage and model.loadFaceBackgroundImage are only reachable once an Android picker is wired in.
@State selectedImageItem (PhotosPickerItem?) is kept as a remembered ByteArray? placeholder feeding the unsupported photo picker.
title: LocalizedStringKey -> String rendered through localized().
onChange(of:) -> LaunchedEffect(value); note it also fires on first composition, unlike SwiftUI.
SettingsFacePrivacyMode case names are assumed to keep the Swift spellings (blur, pixellate, backgroundImage, icon) and are iterated with .entries.
SlideshowEffectSlide is a plain struct with only stored properties, so it becomes a data class with val fields; widgetId stays a java.util.UUID.
SWIFT `let (effect, prepareEffect) = getEffects(...)` uses `info.presentationTimeStamp.seconds`; in Kotlin presentationTimeStamp is Long microseconds, so it is converted with `/ 1_000_000.0`.
SWIFT `if let currentSlideEndTime` shadows the property with a local; translated as a local val read from `this.currentSlideEndTime`, keeping the same branching and the writes back to the property.
`slides.count` becomes `slides.size`.
logger.info(...) -> android.util.Log.i with the class name "SlideshowEffect" as tag.
setSceneWidget is not declared on the Kotlin VideoEffect base class, so it is a plain (non-override) function here, as in Swift.
The `@unchecked Sendable` conformance has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped.
execute/executeMetalPetal stay overrides and use the optional-call `?: image` fallback and `prepareEffect?.prepare(...)` exactly like Swift.
PomodoroTimerView becomes a private @Composable function with the same name and the same SwiftUI hierarchy (Column/Row/Box instead of VStack/HStack/ZStack).
The SwiftUI modifier chain .padding(.top).padding([.horizontal,.bottom]).frame(width:).background().clipShape() is reversed to clip/background/width/padding so the background covers the padding.
The effect's init parameter is androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Size and is converted once to CGSize (canvasSize.toCGSize()); the private view keeps Swift's CGSize maths and receives the CGSize property.
Point sizes derived from canvasSize are converted to dp/sp when applied, so the widget scales with the stream like on iOS.
phaseColor/phaseIcon/phaseName computed properties become local vals from an exhaustive when over PomodoroPhase (focus, shortBreak).
setup() keeps the single ImageRenderer plus one objectWillChange subscription stored in AnyCancellable?, and the renderer's arguments are copied into locals before the content lambda.
setTimerImage assigns timerImage on processorPipelineQueue with launch (Swift processorPipelineQueue.async).
Swift's @MainActor on setSettings/setup is not carried over; the identity guard, settings assignment and setup() stay synchronous as in the Swift source.

The SwiftUI View struct became the @Composable function ScoreboardEffectModularView; its private @ViewBuilder helpers became private @Composable functions whose names are the Swift method names with an uppercase first letter (StackedHistory, StackedHistoryTeam, Stacked, StackedTeam, SideBySide, SideBySideTeam, Stat, PrimaryScore, TeamName, Possession, MoreStats, InfoBox, Title).
Swift point values (fontSize() * scale, modular.width * scale, modular.rowHeight * scale) are emitted as .dp, since scale already folds the design scale in.
Modifiers are reversed to Compose order: .frame(height:).background(c) became Modifier.background(c).height(...), .padding().frame(maxWidth:.infinity) became Modifier.weight(1f).padding(...).
StackedHistoryTeam takes an extra config parameter because the Swift method read config.global.period implicitly from self.

minimumScaleFactor is implemented by the private MinimumScaleText helper: it lowers the font size in onTextLayout while hasVisualOverflow, down to the factor passed in (0.1 for names/info box, 0.3 for the more-stats cells).
Color.black.opacity(0.25) and .background(.black)/.foregroundStyle(.white) are drawn with background layers and CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentColor provides ...), never with Material defaults.
Stat uses Modifier.fillMaxHeight() so its grey box spans the whole row, as the flexible Color inside the SwiftUI ZStack does under the row's .frame(height:).

Calls kept assuming the existing Kotlin declarations: config.periodFull(), config.infoBoxStats(showClock = modular.showClock), modular.fontSize(), modular.width/rowHeight/home/away/layout/isBold/showTitle/showClock/showMoreStats/showGlobalStatsBlock.
SwiftUI Angle has no shim: WheelOfLuckEffectOption.textAngle is a Double of degrees and is applied with Modifier.rotate(degrees = ...).
WheelView and ArrowView become private @Composable functions; ZStack maps to Box with contentAlignment = Alignment.Center.
optionColors uses Compose colors; SwiftUI .pink maps to the iOS systemPink value #FF2D55.
DispatchQueue.main.async becomes CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main.immediate).launch; processorPipelineQueue is a CoroutineScope, so DispatchQueue.async becomes launch.
The '#available(iOS 17, *)' guard around ImageRenderer is dropped because the ImageRenderer shim always exists.
SwiftUI point sizes are written as dp and the system font size as sp; .minimumScaleFactor(0.1) shrinks the font inside onTextLayout while the layout still has visual overflow.
SettingsSceneWidget(widgetId: .init()) is built as SettingsSceneWidget(widgetId = UUID.randomUUID()).
CIImage helpers scaled(x:y:)/translated(x:y:) are written with the shim's transformed(by: CGAffineTransform(scaleX:y:)/translationX:y:) so only declared platform APIs are used.
formatDescription.extensions() is replaced by CMFormatDescriptionGetExtensions(formatDescription) (Map<String, Any>?), and poolFormatDescriptionExtension is typed Map<String, Any>?.
The pool attributes use the top-level pixelFormatType from VideoUnit.kt in the same package; width/height are passed as Int pixels and the IOSurface value as an empty map, MetalCompatibility as true.
pendingAfterAttachEffects stores a copy (toMutableList()) of the effect list so the Swift array value semantics are kept when VideoSourceEffects are unregistered afterwards.

sampleBuffer.duration/presentationTimeStamp/decodeTimeStamp become durationUs/presentationTimeUs/decodeTimeStampUs, and CMSampleBuffer.create(...) is the existing create(...) helper from com.moblin.android.common.various.
ContinuousClock.Instant differences are kotlin.time.Duration and the Swift .seconds are offset.toDouble(DurationUnit.SECONDS).
MetalPetalWidgetShape is mutated in place (its fields are var), and MTIImage/CIImage identity checks use === as required.
#available(iOS 17.2, *) around the Apple Log color space branch is dropped; the branch itself is translated.
ReplayImage becomes a data class; the Swift Deque maps to ArrayDeque (addLast/addAll, firstOrNull/removeFirst).
DispatchQueue.main.async -> mainScope.launch (com.moblin.android) and replayEffectQueue.async -> replayEffectQueue.launch (the queue already is a CoroutineScope).
Swift's global pixelFormatType is replaced with kCVPixelFormatType_32BGRA: every CVPixelBuffer in this port is RGBA8 whatever the tag.

CMVideoDimensions is android.util.Size; its isPortrait() has no Kotlin declaration and is inlined as width < height, and the stored CGSize keeps the Swift name size, so the overlay dimension is re-derived with this.size.toSize().
The guard around the freshly built AVAssetReaderTrackOutput is dropped because the Kotlin shim constructor never returns null; only the missing-track branch still calls markCompleted().
[weak self] captures and the nonisolated(unsafe) attribute are dropped; the @MainActor createOverlay runs inside mainScope.launch.

createOverlay renders the REPLAY badge with Compose Row/Box/Text/SystemImage inside the ImageRenderer shim; .bold() and .fontDesign(.monospaced) become FontWeight.Bold and FontDesign.Monospaced through SwiftUIFonts.system.
AVAsset(url = video.url) takes a String because ReplayBufferFile.url is a String path, not a URL.
StatusTopRight.catPrinterState is observed as a StateFlow with collectAsState; its collected value feeds the private formatCatPrinterState helper.

SettingsCatPrinter's enabled, printChat, printSnapshots, faxMeowSound, bluetoothPeripheralId and bluetoothPeripheralName are MutableStateFlows: read with collectAsState, written with .value; name stays a Published property read directly.

The Model helpers (isCatPrinterEnabled, enableCatPrinter, disableCatPrinter, catPrinterSetFaxMeowSound, catPrinterPrintTestImage, setCurrentCatPrinter) are imported from com.moblin.android.various.model and called with the Swift argument labels.

NavigationLink uses the real destination composables (CatPrinterScannerSettingsView, TwitchAlertsSettingsView, KickAlertsSettingsView) rather than string routes; the nested alerts Form is the destination itself.

The StateFlow values the inner destinations need (device.printTwitch, device.printKick) are collected inside the destination lambda, as the enclosing view leaves composition while a destination is shown.
.onAppear became DisposableEffect(Unit) calling setCurrentCatPrinter on first composition.
UUID(uuidString:) has no failable initializer in Kotlin, so the id is parsed with runCatching { UUID.fromString(value) }.getOrNull() and the guard becomes an early return.
scanner is only used inside the onChange callback, so it keeps discoveredPeripherals.value instead of a collected State.

QuickButtonMicMicView gained deleteEnabled/onDelete parameters because a Compose row owns its own gestures; the Swift deleteDisabled/contextMenuDeleteButton modifiers cannot be chained onto a composable.
contextMenuDeleteButton is marked TODO (no Compose context-menu counterpart); the same removal is still reachable through the swipe-to-delete box, which replaces SwiftUI List .onDelete.
.onMove (drag reordering inside a List) has no stable Compose/LazyColumn counterpart and is marked TODO.
Assumes the ported SettingsMics exposes `mics` and `autoSwitch` as MutableStateFlow and Mic exposes `current` as a StateFlow, all read with collectAsState(); writes use .value.
.navigationTitle("Mic") becomes a Material3 TopAppBar above the list inside a Column (no Scaffold/NavHost is pulled in).
Image(systemName: "cable.connector"/"cable.connector.slash") map to Icons.Filled.Cable / Icons.Filled.LinkOff, which require the material-icons-extended artifact.
.bold() on the checkmark Image has no Icon equivalent and was dropped; only the blue/clear tint is kept.
The `if false` block around the Auto switch Toggle is preserved verbatim (kept as an if (false) branch).

Two SwiftUI Views map to two @Composable functions: the private DeepLinkCreatorQuickButtonSettingsView item row first, then the DeepLinkCreatorQuickButtonsSettingsView screen, matching the Swift declaration order.
@EnvironmentObject model becomes an explicit Model parameter on the private item composable, and is therefore also added as a parameter on the parent composable that hosts it.

@ObservedObject objects are read and mutated directly (button.enabled, button.page, quickButtons.enableScroll, quickButtons.buttons) because DeepLinkCreatorQuickButton/DeepLinkCreatorQuickButtons are plain mutable settings holders in this port; assign the setter side of any binding-style parameter to this pattern if the model uses StateFlow instead.

Form/Section/List become a Column with verticalScroll, a header Text followed by its rows, and a plain Kotlin loop for the buttons list; a LazyColumn cannot be nested inside a vertically scrolling Column.

SwiftUI Picker + fixedSize becomes ExposedDropdownMenuBox with a readOnly OutlinedTextField anchored via Modifier.menuAnchor(MenuAnchorType.PrimaryNotEditable) and a fixed width of 120.dp; this needs @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class) on both composables.
The iOS 17 availability check around the Picker disappears; the page selector is always rendered on Android.
.navigationTitle becomes a Scaffold/TopAppBar title ("Quick buttons"); if the hosting screen already renders a top bar, drop this Scaffold and let the parent supply the title.
List.onMove has no Compose counterpart: the reorder logic is preserved as the private moveButtons(buttons, froms, toOffset) helper but no drag gesture is wired to it.
Image(imageName) for asset catalog images becomes AssetImage(name = imageName, ...) from com.moblin.android.platform.swiftui.
Modifier order is reversed: the Swift .background(.white).frame(height:) becomes Modifier.height(h).background(Color.White).
Section { List { ForEach ... } } drops the List; the ForEach keeps its onDelete and stays before CreateButtonView.
ForEach onDelete removes through the MutableStateFlow: catPrinters.devices.value = catPrinters.devices.value.removing(atOffsets = offsets).
.contextMenuDeleteButton becomes ContextMenuDeleteButton(action = { ... }) from com.moblin.android.view.utils; removeAll { $0.id == device.id } becomes filterNot { it.id == device.id }.
device.name from SettingsCatPrinter is read directly in the NavigationLink label, never through collectAsState.
The last Section uses footerContent because its footer is the SwipeLeftToDeleteHelpView composable, not a String.
Form(title = "Cat printers") replaces Form + .navigationTitle and provides the NavigationStack.

MediaPlayerFileSettingsView becomes a @Composable taking model, player, file and onNavigate; the inline SwiftUI NavigationLink destination (Form + TextEditNavigationView) is not rendered here and must live in the screen registered for the "File" route.
Model and file are passed as parameters; Swift's @EnvironmentObject/@ObservedObject have no state wrapper here because only file.name is read and written.
@State image: UIImage? becomes a remembered Bitmap? state, filled from createThumbnail inside LaunchedEffect(Unit), mirroring .onAppear.
createThumbnail is called with the same trailing-closure shape as the Swift completion handler; if the Kotlin helper is suspend or returns a value, adapt that call.
submitName is kept as a private top-level function (Swift member function) so the file stays complete, even though the pushed form that uses it is built in another file.

Image(uiImage:).resizable().scaledToFit().frame(width: 90) maps to androidx.compose.foundation.Image(bitmap, contentScale = ContentScale.Fit, Modifier.width(90.dp)); the foundation Image is fully qualified to avoid clashing with the imported material icon property.
Image(systemName: "photo") maps to Icon(Icons.Default.Image, contentDescription = null), which requires the androidx.compose.material:material-icons-extended artifact.
The navigationTitle "File" is reused as the route name passed to onNavigate.
@ObservedObject var dewarp360 becomes a parameter of type SettingsVideoEffectDewarp360 whose StateFlow properties are read with collectAsState().
Swift's .onChange(of:) on each slider becomes a LaunchedEffect keyed on the collected value; it also runs once on first composition.
Slider step: 1 over each range is translated into the Material 3 discrete steps count (359, 179 and 139).
Section with a header becomes a Column with a Text header followed by the three Rows.
Slider writes back to the MutableStateFlow (dewarp360.pan.value = ...) because Compose Slider needs a value change handler instead of a two-way Binding.
Image(systemName:) icons map to Icons.Default.ArrowBack/ArrowForward/ArrowDownward/ArrowUpward/ZoomOut/ZoomIn.
updateWidget() keeps the direct Model calls model.getWidgetDewarp360Effect(widget, effect)?.setSettings(dewarp360.toSettings()) as in the Swift source.

NavigationLink is translated to a clickable row calling onNavigate; the inline destination Form is translated in full into the extra composable RtmpServerStreamSettingsForm declared in this same file.
The three private Swift methods became private top-level functions with model/stream as first parameter (changeStreamKey, submitStreamKey, submitLatency).
@ObservedObject settings objects are assumed to expose their @Published data as StateFlows in the port; reads use collectAsState() and writes assign to .value.
Image(systemName: "cable.connector"/"cable.connector.slash") mapped to Icons.Default.Check / Icons.Default.Close because material-icons-core has no cable icon.
.disabled(...) is passed as the enabled parameter of NameEditView and TextEditNavigationView.
.numbersAndPunctuation is passed as Compose KeyboardType.Number to TextEditNavigationView.
.navigationTitle("Stream") becomes the TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold wrapping the destination LazyColumn.
Form Sections are flattened into LazyColumn items: a header Text, the fields, then the footer Text; the multi-line footer string is concatenated.
DeepLinkCreator's @Published properties are assumed to be exposed as MutableStateFlow so Compose can read them with collectAsState() and write them through .value from the Switch callbacks.

The private Swift methods stay private top-level Kotlin functions; updateDeepLink() now returns the new deep link string instead of mutating @State, so the composable owns the remember { mutableStateOf } value.
settings.toString() is translated to kotlinx.serialization Json.encodeToString(settings).

addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters: .urlQueryAllowed) is mapped to android.net.Uri.encode, which percent-encodes a slightly larger character set than urlQueryAllowed; the {}/[]/" un-escaping hack is kept verbatim.
GeometryReader has no Compose equivalent here, so qrCodeHeight() is called without arguments; adjust if the ported helper in com.moblin.android.view.settings.gopro expects screen dimensions.
The resolution comparison assumes the port nests the enum as MoblinSettingsUrlStreamVideo.Resolution.r1920x1080.
UIPasteboard.general.string becomes ClipboardManager obtained through LocalContext, setting a ClipData.
NavigationLink destinations are expressed as onNavigate("<TargetViewName>") callbacks, one per section.
TextViewState now holds one SettingsFont instead of fontFamily/fontStyle; Kotlin keeps it as MutableStateFlow<SettingsFont>.
The private font(...) helper takes font: SettingsFont and uses font.name() like Swift's if let name = state.font.name().
The collected value is named settingsFont locally so it does not shadow the top-level font(...) helper function.
The monospaced-digit check uses settingsFont.family == null, matching state.font.family == nil.
setFontFamily and setFontStyle are replaced by a single setFont(font: SettingsFont) member.
TextEffect's constructor now takes font: SettingsFont in place of fontFamily and fontStyle; callers must be updated.
SettingsFont comes from com.moblin.android.various.settings and is used through its name() function and family property as in Swift; no declarations were supplied for it.

EffectSlider is declared in this same package (com.moblin.android.view.stream.overlay.right), so it is called without an import; its Kotlin signature is assumed to be (title, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>, value: Double, onChange: (Double) -> Unit) mirroring the Swift (title:range:value:) initialiser with a Binding.
The Swift @ObservedObject database becomes a plain Database parameter; its @Published pinchScale is read with collectAsState().
The Swift onChange(of:) side effect is folded into the slider's onChange callback because Compose sliders report the new value directly, so no LaunchedEffect re-trigger is needed.
The $database.pinchScale binding becomes the current value plus an onChange lambda that both updates the model and would update the database StateFlow.
model.setPinchScale is called as a plain (non-suspend) function, matching the direct call in the Swift body.
range: 0.5 ... 1.0 maps to the Kotlin ClosedFloatingPointRange 0.5..1.0.
No NavigationStack, sheets, toolbars or platform-only pickers appear in this file, so nothing was dropped.
The view emits no declared Kotlin types of its own; it only contributes the composable function.
Database is an @ObservedObject, so torchLevel is treated as a MutableStateFlow<Float> read with collectAsState().
EffectSlider is imported from the same package and called with title/range/value/onValueChange; its body lives in EffectSlider.kt.
The Swift .onChange semantics are folded into EffectSlider's onValueChange callback so setTorchLevel is called exactly once per user edit instead of also on first composition.
The Swift ClosedRange 0.01 ... 1 becomes the Float range 0.01f..1f.
model.setTorchLevel keeps its Swift parameter label as a named Kotlin argument.
Kept the @Composable name StreamOverlayRightPixellateView, taking model and database as parameters.
database.pixellateStrength is read with collectAsState() and written back by the slider, so it is treated as a MutableStateFlow in the Database port.
The Swift onChange(of: database.pixellateStrength) became LaunchedEffect(pixellateStrength), which also fires once on first composition as the SwiftUI onChange does not.

EffectSlider lives in this same package (com.moblin.android.view.stream.overlay.right), so it is called without an import and its expected signature is (title: String, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>, value: Float, onChange: (Float) -> Unit).
The Swift 0 ... 1 Double range became 0f..1f because Compose Slider works with Float.
The $database.pixellateStrength binding is replaced by the value plus onChange parameter pair.

ObservableObject models (SettingsWidgetBingoCard) are taken as plain parameters and their properties are read/written directly; if the port exposes them as StateFlow, wrap the reads in collectAsState().

Signatures of the re-used Moblin views were inferred from the Swift call sites: MultiLineTextFieldView(value, onValueChange, placeholder, onFocusChanged), MultiLineTextFieldDoneButtonView(editingText, onEditingTextChange), TextButtonView(text, onClick) and RgbColorPickerView(title, color, onColorChange, opacity).
The SwiftUI @FocusState editingText is a local remember { mutableStateOf(false) } that is reported back through onFocusChanged.

backgroundColorColor / foregroundColorColor are assumed to be androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color and the picker callback to deliver the storable RgbColor value, matching the SwiftUI Binding<Color> plus (RgbColor) -> Void closure.

Icons.Filled.CheckBox and Icons.Filled.CheckBoxOutlineBlank replace the SF Symbols square.split.diagonal.2x2 / square and require the material-icons-extended artifact; .font(.title) became Modifier.size(28.dp).
Section headers and the Squares footer are emitted as plain Text / trailing composables, so this file must be placed inside a scrolling Column or LazyColumn by its caller.
LaunchedEffect(bingoCard.squaresText) also runs on first composition, unlike SwiftUI's onChange which skips the initial value; guard with a remembered previous value if that matters.
The private updateEffect() method became a local lambda of the same name so it can be passed to the child composables.

AudioBarView/ChannelsView/SampleRateView become private @Composable functions; their private Swift methods clippingBar/redBar/yellowBar/greenBar become private top-level functions taking the current level value and the bar scale.
audio.muted, audio.numberOfChannels, audio.sampleRate and level.level are StateFlow properties read with collectAsState(); the parent passes model.audio and model.audio.level as parameters.
The Swift modifier chain .background(x).cornerRadius(5) is emitted as .clip(RoundedCornerShape(5.dp)).background(x) because in Compose a clip placed after a background would not round it.
bgHeight is a Dp, so rectangle sizes are Modifier.width(w.dp).height(barHeight * scale) with Dp * Float arithmetic.
Image(systemName: "waveform") maps to Icons.Default.GraphicEq, which lives in the material-icons-extended artifact.
smallFont is applied to the Text children (SwiftUI inherited it from the container's .font modifier); the icon's .font is dropped since Icon sizes come from Modifier.size.
compactAudioLevelColors returns a Kotlin Pair that is destructured into foregroundColor/backgroundColor, shadowing the imported backgroundColor for that branch.
Empty HStack spacing 0 and HStack spacing 1 map to Arrangement.spacedBy(0.dp) / Arrangement.spacedBy(1.dp).

EffectSlider is assumed to expose (title: String, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>, value: Float, onChange: (Float) -> Unit) since the SwiftUI version used a Binding; adjust if the shared composable differs.

Database.whirlpoolAngle is read as a StateFlow (collectAsState) because StateFlow-backed published properties cannot be written in place, so a local remembered angle drives the slider and is synced from the flow via LaunchedEffect.
model.setWhirlpoolAngle(angle) is invoked from the slider callback, matching the Swift onChange(of: database.whirlpoolAngle) side effect.
The Swift range .pi / 2 ... .pi * 2 uses Double math; converted to Float with (PI / 2).toFloat() and (PI * 2).toFloat().
EffectSlider lives in the same package (com.moblin.android.view.stream.overlay.right), so no import is emitted for it.
The composable takes model and database as parameters, replacing @ObservedObject with a parameter whose StateFlow is collected.
@State/@Binding become remember/mutableStateOf plus onChange lambdas; the @State 'value' prop is kept as parameter 'value' and its mutable copy is named valueState to avoid a clash.

NavigationLink is translated to onNavigate(name) callbacks: the outer 'Stream' link and the inner 'URL' link. The inline Form that was the 'Stream' destination is preserved as RtspClientStreamSettingsViewDestination, and UrlSettingsView itself is exported for the 'URL' route.

onChange(of:) is applied directly inside the mutation callbacks instead of LaunchedEffect(value), because the watched settings properties are plain mutable vars and would not re-trigger a keyed effect.
.navigationTitle -> TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold (ExperimentalMaterial3Api opt-in).
.sheet -> ModalBottomSheet, still a Material 3 experimental API.

MultiLineTextFieldView is called with value/onChange/placeholder/enabled only: .onSubmit, .textInputAutocapitalization and .disableAutocorrection have no matching parameter on the ported component and are dropped.
Settings model objects (SettingsRtspClient, SettingsRtspClientStream) are treated as holders with mutable properties (name, url, transport, latency, enabled, streams).
onDisappear -> DisposableEffect(Unit) { onDispose { ... } } keeps the auto-submit-on-leave behaviour.
The SwiftUI View becomes a @Composable function with the same name; model and mediaPlayer are parameters instead of @EnvironmentObject/@ObservedObject.
Properties of Model and MediaPlayerPlayer are read from their StateFlow fields with collectAsState().
SF Symbols map to Material icons (Pause, PlayArrow, SkipPrevious, SkipNext) which come from the material-icons-extended artifact.
The `if false` slider block is preserved as-is under `if (false)`; SwiftUI's onEditingChanged maps to Slider onValueChange / onValueChangeFinished and onChange(of:) maps to LaunchedEffect(value).
playPauseImage() is kept as a private top-level helper returning the SF Symbol name string used to select the icon.
.accentColor(.white) becomes SliderDefaults.colors(thumbColor = Color.White).
.font(.title) on the images has no direct Compose equivalent and is approximated with Modifier.width(30.dp).
The dead slider branch reads model.mediaPlayerPlayer.position.value, assuming Model exposes a MediaPlayerPlayer whose properties are StateFlows.
SettingsBeauty @Published properties are read with collectAsState(); writes assume the shared class exposes a public MutableStateFlow backing property, so they use `.value = ...`.

EffectSlider(...) is called with an assumed signature (title: String, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>, value: Double, onValueChange: (Double) -> Unit) to match the Double-valued settings; adjust if the shared composable takes Float.
The private helper `setSettings()` is kept as a local function inside each @Composable so both copies can keep the Swift name without clashing.

Toggle -> Row with a Switch plus the picker; the Picker becomes an ExposedDropdownMenuBox with a read-only OutlinedTextField using Modifier.menuAnchor(MenuAnchorType.PrimaryNotEditable), which needs Material 3 1.3+.
onChange(of:) -> LaunchedEffect(value); unlike SwiftUI it also runs once on first composition, so the beauty settings/state are applied on entry as well.
`.fixedSize()` has no Compose counterpart and is omitted; Compose sizes to content by default.
SettingsBeautySettings.allCases -> SettingsBeautySettings.entries, with the lowercase entry names smoothness/shape from the shared enum in com.moblin.android.various.settings.

segmentHeight is used as a Dp and pickerBackgroundColor / pickerBorderColor as androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color top-level values declared in this same package; the Swift .overlay(RoundedRectangle.stroke) becomes Modifier.border.
Only makeChatLineStyle changed: the ChatLineStyle construction now passes font = chat.font after displayStyle, matching the new Swift argument.
Every other declaration, import and line is byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file.
ChatLineStyle.font is a SettingsFont field that already exists in com.moblin.android.view.utils.ChatLineStyle, so no new import is needed.

ActionButtonView takes an androidx.compose.ui.graphics.vector.ImageVector instead of an SF Symbol name and gains an `enabled` parameter (Swift's .disabled modifier); the icons Block/Timer/ContentCopy/PersonAdd come from material-icons-extended.

@Binding properties (selectedPost, linkUrl) became plain value parameters plus onChange lambdas (onSelectedPostChange, onLinkUrlChange); @State properties became remember { mutableStateOf() } holders in ChatActionButtonsView.

confirmationDialog and alert became Material3 AlertDialog: destructive entries use MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error instead of role: .destructive, and the timeout dialog renders its three choices in a Column inside confirmButton.

ChatLineView and QuickButtonChatChatterInfoView are called from com.moblin.android.view.utils / com.moblin.android.view.controlbar.quickbutton.chat with their callback passed as a trailing lambda, because the exact Kotlin callback parameter names are not known from this file.

The private view-builder methods (banButton, timeoutButton, deleteButton, copyButton, nicknameButton, infoButton, lineView, saveNickname) are top-level private declarations here; dialog state and the dismiss() helper are passed in as parameters/callbacks.
ChatPost.platform is compared against ChatPlatform.kick, assuming the platform enum lives in com.moblin.android.various, which was not listed in the glossary.
Timeout durations are passed as Int seconds (5 * 60, 3600, 24 * 3600) to model.timeoutUser(post, duration).
swiftui contentShape(Rectangle()) on the dismiss Spacer was replaced with Modifier.clickable; the toast/toast-free layout otherwise matches the Swift body.
SwiftUI Sections become a header Text followed by the section content in a Column; the parent settings screen must supply the scrolling container.
UIImage preview images are translated to android.graphics.Bitmap and drawn with Image(bitmap = ....asImageBitmap()).

SettingsVideoEffectMask properties (points, tension, inverted, backgroundType, backgroundColor, backgroundColorColor, backgroundColorColor2) are assumed to be StateFlow and are read with collectAsState()/.value, written with .value = ...
makeCatmullRomPath is called with (List<Offset>, Float tension) and assumed to return androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Path - verify the signature in com.moblin.android.videoeffects.
The fallback photo asset 'GamlaLinkoping' must be added as R.drawable.gamla_linkoping in com.moblin.android.R.
SF Symbols square.resize.down/square.resize.up/minus.circle/plus.circle/arrow.clockwise map to Icons.Default.Remove/Add/Refresh (material-icons-extended may be required).
The Type picker uses ExposedDropdownMenuBox with Modifier.menuAnchor(MenuAnchorType.PrimaryNotEditable), which needs Material3 1.3 or newer.
model.stream.portrait is read directly; if Model exposes stream as a StateFlow it must be wrapped in collectAsState().
The @available(iOS 26, *) gates on the upstream structs have no Android counterpart branch, so every view is always rendered (glassEffect is a platform shim).

GeometryProxy becomes a CGSize taken from BoxWithConstraints maxWidth/maxHeight (dp values used as points); shouldStackVertically, mapSide and offset take the collected isSmall value instead of reading navigation.isSmall.

Navigation and SettingsNavigation StateFlows are collected with collectAsState in each composable and passed to the local helpers; writes to followUser/followHeading go through a cast to MutableStateFlow.
`.onChange(of: navigation.destination)` is folded into Map's onSelectionChange, which calls navigation.updateDirections() right after assigning destination.
The two `.onChange` on navigationSettings.followUser/followHeading become one LaunchedEffect(followUser, followHeading).
`.onChange(of: navigation.searchText)` side effect moved into BasicTextField's onValueChange (clears searchResults when the text becomes empty).

ControlSearchView emits two siblings (field + picker); the `.padding(.trailing, 10)` of the stacked branch is applied by wrapping the call in an inner Row, since Compose cannot pad a group of siblings.
.onAppear is LaunchedEffect(Unit) with statement bodies and an explicit null check instead of `?.let`; MapView helper serLongPressLocation takes a CoroutineScope from rememberCoroutineScope.

AVSpeechSynthesisVoice and AVSpeechSynthesizer are mapped to android.speech.tts.Voice and android.speech.tts.TextToSpeech; getVoice() compares Voice.locale.language and Voice.name (the Swift identifier).

createSpeechSynthesizer() is assumed to return android.speech.tts.TextToSpeech and textToSpeechLanguages(appleVoices) to take List<Voice> and return items exposing name/code; both come from other Moblin files.
SettingsVoiceType entries are assumed to be SettingsVoiceType.APPLE and SettingsVoiceType.TTS_MONSTER, and SettingsVoice is a mutable class exposing apple.voice and ttsMonster.name/voiceId.
Image("TtsMonster") becomes painterResource(id = R.drawable.ttsmonster); verify the drawable name in the Android resources.
There is no Material apple.logo icon, Icons.Default.Phone is used as the closest core icon for Apple voices.
@Binding rate and volume are only read in these views, so they are plain Float parameters instead of value/onChange pairs.
The parent-provided @State selectedVoice becomes an initialSelectedVoice parameter plus remember { mutableStateOf(...) } inside LanguageView; selection writes go through onVoiceChange as before.
NavigationLink becomes an onNavigate: (String) -> Unit callback carrying language.code, and TextButtonView is called with a positional title plus a trailing onClick lambda.

The SwiftUI NavigationLink's label (IngestStreamItemView + model.isRistStreamConnected) is not rendered here: this composable is the pushed destination, so the parent list screen renders that row and calls onNavigate.
The navigationTitle("Stream") becomes the TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold wrapping the LazyColumn.
Form Sections become LazyColumn items: a header Text, the content, and the footer Text rendered with MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall.
@ObservedObject/@EnvironmentObject state is read with collectAsState() and written through the flow's .value (settings properties are treated as MutableStateFlow fields).
NameEditView's @Binding name: $stream.name becomes name = <value> plus an onChange lambda.
.disabled(x) is inverted into enabled = !x on NameEditView and TextEditNavigationView.
String(localized: "...") -> localized("..."); the multi-line Swift string literal is collapsed into one sentence.
keyboardType .numbersAndPunctuation maps to KeyboardType.Number and the latency valueFormat closure is passed as a lambda producing "<value> ms".
Swift enum without raw values becomes a plain Kotlin enum class with the same case names (working, ok, failed).
Collections.Deque<ReplayImage> becomes ArrayDeque; images.first -> firstOrNull(), images.removeFirst() stays, images += newImages -> images.addAll(newImages).
replayEffectQueue.async and processorPipelineQueue.async become CoroutineScope.launch, because both queues are already CoroutineScopes in Kotlin.
private(set) var duration and setupState become open var with a private setter; they are only written inside the class.
CMVideoDimensions is android.util.Size on Android, so the stored field is converted once with android.util.Size.toCGSize() to feed the CIImage/ImageRenderer helpers.
sampleBuffer.presentationTimeStamp.seconds becomes presentationTimeUs / 1_000_000.0 and sampleBuffer.imageBuffer stays nullable, so the guard-let becomes a combined null check.
nonisolated(unsafe), @unchecked Sendable and the [weak self] captures are dropped; the coroutine lambdas capture the receiver directly.
scaledTo(size:), centered(size:) and toEffectImage(isOpaque:) are resolved through wildcard imports of com.moblin.android.platform.coreimage and com.moblin.android.videoeffects.
WKWebView/UIViewRepresentable becomes AndroidView wrapping model.getWebBrowser(); updateUIView has no counterpart and AndroidView's update callback is left out.

Model, Database, Orientation and WebBrowserState published properties are read with collectAsState() and written through the MutableStateFlow .value, matching the @Published -> MutableStateFlow convention of this port.
@Binding parameters became a value parameter plus an on...Change lambda: onShowingBookmarksChange, onIsSmallChange, onPresentingBookmarksChange.
The .sheet becomes ModalBottomSheet and the NavigationStack title/toolbar of BookmarksView becomes a TopAppBar with CloseToolbar as navigation icon.
SwiftUI list editing (.contextMenuDeleteButton, .onDelete, .onMove) has no Compose counterpart: the context menu is TODO() and the delete/reorder mutations are kept as local onDelete/onMove lambdas.
The iOS 26 .glassEffect() branch of the small browser button is dropped; the button uses plain padding and the pre-iOS-26 rendering.
Icons.Default.OpenInFull and Icons.Default.CloseFullscreen come from material-icons-extended, which must be on the classpath.
GeometryReader metrics are replaced by BoxWithConstraints maxWidth/maxHeight; smallBrowserSide is 250.dp and mapSide/offset keep their original names.
LinearProgressIndicator is used with the lambda progress form (Material 3 1.3+) and the Swift scaleEffect(x:1,y:4) is expressed as an explicit height on the bar.

ObservedObject models are read with collectAsState(); writes to @Published properties (raid.message/state, banners.minimized) use `property.value = ...`, assuming the ported models expose MutableStateFlow-backed published properties.
Swift private helper members (percentage(), fraction(votes:), fraction(channelPoints:), color(outcome:), icons(), close()) became local functions inside their composables so the names stay identical.
Image(systemName:) is resolved through the new top-level private helper bannerIcon(name), which maps the SF Symbol names used here to the closest Material icons.
The iOS 18 symbolEffect(.wiggle) animation on the hype train icons has no Compose counterpart and is simply rendered statically.
Link(destination:) became a clickable, underlined Text that calls LocalUriHandler.current.openUri(url).
GeometryReader -> BoxWithConstraints, onGeometryChange -> Modifier.onSizeChanged; the measured content height is kept in pixels and converted to Dp with LocalDensity for the scroll area height.

BannerView's @ViewBuilder content is a trailing @Composable lambda; Swift's two trailing closures map to onClose (unlabelled) and content (labelled). .buttonStyle(.bordered) -> TextButton and .font(.footnote) -> MaterialTheme.typography.labelSmall.

NavigationLink is split into the row composable RtmpServerSettingsView (calls onNavigate("RtmpServerSettings")) and the destination composable RtmpServerSettingsForm which holds the Form content plus the TopAppBar title.

rtmpServer.enabled and model.statusOther are read with collectAsState(); the Toggle writes through rtmpServer.enabled.value, assuming those published properties are MutableStateFlow/StateFlow in the ported model.
The Swift sections become a single LazyColumn: description, toggle, optional InfoBannerView, port editor, footer text, "Streams" header, stream items, CreateButtonView and the streams footer.
SettingsRtmpServerStream.baseName, model.rtmpServerEnabled() and model.getRtmpStream(streamKey) are reused as-is from the ported model/settings types.
.contextMenuDeleteButton has no Compose equivalent, so deletion is wired to a long press with Modifier.combinedClickable (disabled while the server is enabled) instead of a context menu.
TextEditNavigationView is called with enabled and keyboardType arguments (KeyboardType.Number for .numbersAndPunctuation); adjust to its real signature in com.moblin.android.view.utils.
CreateButtonView receives enabled = !model.rtmpServerEnabled() to mirror the .disabled modifier.
Port is stored as Int (UInt16 is used only for settings, not wire format) and UInt16(value) parsing is emulated with toIntOrNull plus a 0..65535 range check.

NavigationLink destinations cannot be pushed from inside a single Compose screen, so the pushed Form is declared here as SrtClientStreamSettingsForm and reached through onNavigate("srtClientStreamSettings"); the hosting NavHost must register it.
The nested URL NavigationLink navigates to the route "url"; SrtClientStreamUrlSettingsView wraps UrlSettingsView and must be registered for that route.

@ObservedObject/@Binding writes (stream.name, stream.enabled, stream.url) become value parameters plus onNameChange/onEnabledChange/onUrlChange callbacks, since StateFlow properties are read with collectAsState().
onChange(of: stream.enabled) maps to LaunchedEffect(enabled) guarded by a remembered previous value so reloadSrtClient() only runs on a real toggle change, not on first composition.
onSubmitted: model.reloadSrtClient becomes onSubmitted = { model.reloadSrtClient() }; Model.reloadSrtClient() is assumed to exist in com.moblin.android.various.model.

NameEditView, TextItemLocalizedView and UrlSettingsView are imported from their packages and called with the Swift argument labels kept as named parameters, including an extra onNameChange/onUrlChange callback replacing each Swift binding.
The Swift tuple array of URL examples becomes List<Pair<String, String>> built with 'to'.
navigationTitle "Stream" is not rendered here; the hosting screen must show it in its TopAppBar.
The NavigationLink label becomes the composable body: IngestStreamItemView wrapped in a clickable Box that calls onNavigate("Stream").
The inline Form destination of the NavigationLink is translated into the companion composable SrtlaServerStreamSettingsDetailView in the same file, since navigation-compose is not pulled in here.

Parameter names of the util components (NameEditView, TextEditNavigationView, UrlsView, IngestStreamItemView) are inferred from the Swift argument labels; adjust if the Kotlin signatures differ. NamesEditView receives the name value plus an onChange lambda, replacing the Swift @Binding.
SwiftUI Text with a string literal is localized by SwiftUI, so those literals are wrapped in localized(...); string literals that were not localized in Swift stay raw.
wholeMatch(of: /[a-zA-Z0-9]*/) becomes Regex("[a-zA-Z0-9]*").matches(...) because Kotlin's Regex.matches requires a full-string match.
The UInt16 port argument is translated as Int, since this is not wire-format/byte-parsing code.
The three private helper methods became private top-level functions with the same names, taking model and stream explicitly.

Form sections are rendered as LazyColumn items: the section header/footer texts become separate Text items, and .disabled(srtlaServer.enabled) cannot be forwarded to the util components and is therefore not applied.

NavigationLink became an onNavigate callback: WhipServerStreamSettingsView keeps its name and renders the tappable IngestStreamItemView row, while the pushed Form content lives in the added WhipServerStreamSettingsDetail composable.
SwiftUI Form/Sections were mapped to a LazyColumn whose items are the section fields, with section headers and footers as plain Text items styled with MaterialTheme.typography.
Toggle 'Sync timestamps' became a Row with a label, Spacer(weight) and a Material 3 Switch bound directly to stream.syncTimestamps.
.navigationTitle("Stream") became a Scaffold + TopAppBar title in the detail composable (requires ExperimentalMaterial3Api opt-in).

TextEditNavigationView, NameEditView and UrlsView are called from com.moblin.android.view.utils with the Swift argument labels converted to camelCase parameters (title/value/onChange/onSubmit/footers/keyboardType/valueFormat/enabled).
keyboardType: .numbersAndPunctuation was translated to androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType.Number.

isValidIngestLatency is used as the latency onChange validator; changeStreamKey/submitStreamKey/submitLatency stay private top-level functions taking model/stream because the Swift private methods referenced them.
Int32 latency was mapped to Int and valueFormat uses "$it ms" to mirror the Swift interpolation.

The outer NavigationLink is translated into an onNavigate("whepClientStream") callback on the row composable; the destination Form is rendered by WhepClientStreamSettingsViewInner in this same file and the NavHost must wire that route to it.

The inner NavigationLink to UrlSettingsView becomes onNavigate("whepClientUrl"); the URL screen is built by the navigation host, so its inline arguments (placeholder, allowedSchemes, onSubmitted) are not passed from here.

@EnvironmentObject/@ObservedObject become plain parameters; stream and whepClient are mutated directly because their fields are StateFlow backed, and the Swift onChange handlers are folded into the Switch onCheckedChange lambdas that call model.reloadWhepClient().
Form/List are translated to a LazyColumn of items with HorizontalDivider between sections; the Section footer became a small Text below the latency row.
.navigationTitle("Stream") became the TopAppBar title inside the Scaffold of WhepClientStreamSettingsViewInner (needs ExperimentalMaterial3Api opt-in).
keyboardType .numbersAndPunctuation has no Compose counterpart, KeyboardType.Number is used for the latency field.

Parameter names for NameEditView (onNameChange, enabled), TextEditNavigationView (keyboardType, valueFormat, enabled) and TextItemLocalizedView (sensitive) are assumed from the com.moblin.android.view.utils signatures.
Text literals inside Text/Toggle were treated as localized keys (SwiftUI LocalizedStringKey behaviour) and go through localized().

NavigationLink is split into a clickable row composable (RtspClientSettingsView) that calls onNavigate("rtspClientSettings") and a destination composable (RtspClientSettingsViewDestination) holding the Form/Section content, both in this file.
The Form + Section + List become a LazyColumn with a header Text("Streams"), the footer SwipeLeftToDeleteHelpView, and the navigationTitle becomes the TopAppBar title.
numberOfEnabledStreams is no longer @State refreshed in onAppear: it is derived from the streams StateFlow with collectAsState() so it stays in sync.

SettingsRtspClient.streams is assumed to be a MutableStateFlow<List<SettingsRtspClientStream>>: reads go through collectAsState(), writes assign .value. If the port exposes a read-only StateFlow, route these mutations through the model's mutator methods instead.
contextMenuDeleteButton has no Compose counterpart, so each stream row gets an overflow IconButton with a Material 3 DropdownMenu whose Delete item runs the translated deleteStream().
status() and deleteStream(at:) are kept as private top-level functions; since a @Composable has no self, they take the count, model and rtspClient they need as explicit parameters.
makeOffsets() is called with (streams, stream.id) and assumed to return the deletion index set as Set<Int>?.
String(localized: "a stream") becomes localized("a stream") from package com.moblin.android.
NavigationLink became an onNavigate callback (destination name "urlSettings"); UrlSettingsView itself is composed by the caller because it needs the url value plus onUrlChange.
Form/Section were rendered as a verticalScroll Column with the explanation text as the first item; navigationTitle "Preview stream" must be set by the hosting screen's TopAppBar.
.navigationTitle("Preview stream") is exposed through the host scaffold, no title composable is declared here.
resolutions() and videoBitrates() are private top-level functions, videoBitrates() is List<Int> since the values are bitrates in bits per second.
Preview stream fields are read with collectAsState(); writes (resolution/bitrate selection) use .value, assuming SettingsStreamPreviewStream exposes MutableStateFlow properties.
Both Pickers use ExposedDropdownMenuBox, which requires @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class).
whipExamples is not needed in this file anymore because the UrlSettingsView construction moved to the navigation destination.
formatBytesPerSecond(speed = ...) is called with a Long, matching the Swift Int64 argument.
Swift file-private @MainActor globals become private top-level vals in the Kotlin file; whipExamples stays public since other files use it.
LocalizedStringKey example tuples become List<Pair<String, String>> with the keys as plain strings (no localized() wrapper, because Swift only localizes String(localized:)).
@EnvironmentObject/@ObservedObject become plain composable parameters; their published Boolean/String state is read with collectAsState().
Writes to stream.url / destination.url use MutableStateFlow.value on the public property of the ported model classes.
The Swift @Binding $stream.url is expressed as a url value plus an onUrlChange lambda on the ported UrlSettingsView.
UrlSettingsView is imported from com.moblin.android.view.settings.ingests.rtspclient and called with disabled/url/onUrlChange/value/placeholder/allowedSchemes/examples/onSubmitted.
allowedSchemes nil maps to Kotlin null; the multi-streaming case maps to listOf("rtmp", "rtmps").
@MainActor is dropped: Compose composables already run on the main thread.

NavigationLink is expressed as onNavigate("SrtClientSettingsDestination") on the label row; the link's Form destination is kept in an extra SrtClientSettingsDestination composable that a NavHost should register.
Form/Section/List collapsed into a single LazyColumn: header item "Streams", one item per stream, CreateButtonView item, then the swipe-help footer item.
srtClient.streams is assumed to be a MutableStateFlow<List<SettingsSrtClientStream>>: read with collectAsState() and mutated through .value.
Swift IndexSet is mapped to Set<Int> and makeOffsets is assumed to return Set<Int>?; deleteStream(model, srtClient, indexes: Set<Int>) removes those indices and calls model.reloadSrtClient().
contextMenuDeleteButton became a long-press (combinedClickable) DropdownMenu with a Delete entry per stream row.
.onDelete(perform:) became a Material 3 SwipeToDismissBox (end-to-start only) wrapping each stream row.
.navigationTitle("SRT client") became the Scaffold TopAppBar title inside the destination composable.
SettingsSrtClientStream() must have a no-arg constructor with a mutable name, and Model.reloadSrtClient() is called synchronously (non-suspend).

NavigationLink became a clickable row calling onNavigate("whepClient"); the inline destination Form is exposed as a second composable WhepClientSettingsDestinationView so no navigation-compose dependency is needed in this file.

@EnvironmentObject model and @ObservedObject whepClient are plain parameters; whepClient.streams is read with collectAsState() and SettingsWhepClientStream.baseName/name are accessed as class/companion members.
@State numberOfEnabledStreams stays a remember { mutableStateOf(0) } filled from LaunchedEffect(Unit), mirroring onAppear, and status() takes it as a parameter instead of reading view state.

deleteStream takes an explicit List<Int> of indexes (IndexSet counterpart) and assumes whepClient.streams is a MutableStateFlow-backed list so a filtered copy can be assigned back; adjust if the port exposes it as a read-only StateFlow with mutation helpers.

The .contextMenuDeleteButton and .onDelete affordances have no Compose counterpart and became a trailing delete IconButton per stream that calls the same deleteStream path (context-menu previews are not reproduced).
Form Sections became LazyColumn item blocks: the description Text, a "Streams" header Text, one row per stream, the CreateButtonView, and the SwipeLeftToDeleteHelpView footer.
WhepClientStreamSettingsView is called as (whepClient, stream, onNavigate), following the same navigation-callback convention as the row.
model.reloadWhepClient() is invoked synchronously after each deletion; if the port makes it suspending, wrap the call in a coroutine scope.

The SwiftUI body is a NavigationLink, so it is split in two: RistServerSettingsView renders the tappable list row (label + status) and calls onNavigate("RIST server"), while RistServerSettingsDetailView holds the Form content the caller shows for that destination (the two functions replace the one Swift View).
The private Swift members became top-level private functions taking model/ristServer: submitPort(), status() and deleteStream().
IndexSet is modelled as Set<Int>, both for deleteStream() and for the assumed Set<Int>? return of makeOffsets().

SettingsRistServer properties are read and written directly (assumed Compose-observable vars, needed because the Swift code assigns enabled and port); model.statusOther is read with collectAsState() per the @EnvironmentObject rule.
.disabled(...) on TextEditNavigationView and CreateButtonView is approximated by wrapping them in a Box with Modifier.alpha, because those utility composables' signatures are unknown here.

contextMenuDeleteButton and List.onDelete have no Compose counterpart, so both are expressed as a combinedClickable long press on each stream row that calls deleteStream() (only while the server is disabled, matching the Swift guard).
onChange(of: ristServer.enabled) is mapped to LaunchedEffect(enabled), which additionally fires once on first composition unlike the Swift original.
String(localized:) became localized(); keyboardType .numbersAndPunctuation became KeyboardType.Number.
Form is rendered as a LazyColumn; each Section becomes a header/rows block following the LazyColumn content lambda.

The Swift `if #available(iOS 26, *), false` guard on the WiFi Aware row is dead code in the original; it is kept as a constant `showWiFiAware = false` flag so the row still navigates through onNavigate when enabled.
database.ingestsSoftwareVideoDecoding is read with collectAsState() and written through MutableStateFlow.value; if Database exposes a read-only StateFlow, add an explicit setter there.

onChange(of: database.ingestsSoftwareVideoDecoding) becomes LaunchedEffect(softwareVideoDecoding), so model.reloadIngests() also runs once on first composition, matching the SwiftUI change observation closely enough for settings reloads.
.navigationTitle("Ingests") becomes the TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold; remove the Scaffold if the hosting navigation already provides an app bar.
Section footer is a Column of Text composables placed after the toggle row.
The embedded RtmpServer/SrtlaServer/SrtClient/RistServer/RtspClient/WhipServer/WhepClient settings views are called as composables from their own packages with only the data objects they need.
ReplayProvider's @Published properties become MutableStateFlow, matching the other Model providers (DebugOverlayProvider, StreamUptimeProvider).
The Model extensions become top-level extension functions in com.moblin.android.various.model.

Kotlin cannot add an interface conformance (extension Model: ReplayDelegate / ReplayEffectDelegate) from another file, so replayOutputFrame/replayEffectStatus/replayEffectCompleted/replayEffectError are emitted as top-level extension functions named exactly as in Swift; Model must declare the conformance in Model.kt.
The Swift parameter `delay` shadows kotlinx.coroutines.delay, so the coroutine delay is called fully qualified as kotlinx.coroutines.delay.
DispatchQueue.main.async / asyncAfter -> mainScope.launch with kotlinx.coroutines.delay (mainScope is assumed available in this package).
FileManager.default.copyItem is File(...).copyTo(...) inside runCatching, matching try?.
ReplayBufferFile takes a String path, so ReplayBufferFile(url: video.url()) becomes ReplayBufferFile(url = video.url().path, ...).
The transitionType switch uses SettingsStreamReplay.TransitionType entries inside an explicit when.

NavigationLink(destination:label:) is rendered as a clickable label Row that calls onNavigate("WhipServerSettingsView") followed by the destination form, since navigation-compose must not be pulled in here.
SettingsWhipServer state (enabled, port, streams) is read with collectAsState() and written through .value, assuming the settings object exposes its state flows as mutable (MutableStateFlow).
onChange(of: whipServer.enabled) becomes LaunchedEffect(enabled) calling model.reloadWhipServer().
remove(atOffsets:) is translated to filterIndexed on a Set<Int> of indexes applied to the streams flow value.
contextMenuDeleteButton is implemented with combinedClickable + DropdownMenu; onDelete is implemented with Material 3 SwipeToDismissBox (EndToStart).
UInt16(value) port parsing becomes value.toIntOrNull() plus a 0..65535 range check.
keyboardType .numbersAndPunctuation maps to KeyboardType.Number.
.disabled(...) is passed as enabled = !enabled into TextEditNavigationView and CreateButtonView; if those helpers lack that parameter they must be extended.

State objects (SettingsWidgetWheelOfLuck, SettingsWidgetWheelOfLuckOption) are observed with collectAsState() and mutated through their public MutableStateFlow .value, following the port's ObservableObject convention.
NavigationLink becomes the onNavigate callback: OptionView calls onNavigate("Option") and additionally shows the inline destination form in a ModalBottomSheet so the editor stays reachable.
The weight Picker becomes a Row with an ExposedDropdownMenuBox writing options.weight and calling updateTotalWeight()/updateEffect().
.contextMenuDeleteButton(disabled:) becomes a trailing delete IconButton with enabled = !deleteDisabled; .onDelete/.deleteDisabled are folded into that button.
onMove reordering has no Compose counterpart, so the logic is kept as the local helper moveOptions() (not attached to a drag gesture).
@FocusState editingText is kept as remember state but the .focused() modifier is dropped; MultiLineTextFieldView is expected to own its focus.
Section is rendered as a header Text followed by its items inside a Column, since a Form/LazyColumn is owned by the parent screen.
widget.wheelOfLuck is treated as a plain (non-Flow) property of SettingsWidget; user-visible literals use localized().

The Swift NavigationLink embeds its destination, so this file declares two composables: SrtlaServerSettingsView (the tappable 'SRT(LA) server' row, which calls onNavigate) and SrtlaServerSettingsForm (the destination Form). The navigation host should route the key "SrtlaServerSettingsForm" to SrtlaServerSettingsForm.

SettingsSrtlaServer and SettingsSrtlaServerStream are treated as plain mutable objects (direct property reads/writes such as srtlaServer.enabled = ..., srtlaServer.srtPort = port), not as MutableStateFlow-backed observable objects.
Ports are Int: Swift UInt16(value) becomes value.toIntOrNull() plus a 0..65535 range check, and String(srtlaServer.srtPort) becomes srtlaServer.srtPort.toString().
IndexSet has no Android counterpart; makeOffsets(...) is assumed to return List<Int>? and deleteStream removes the offsets in descending order via removeAt.
TextEditNavigationView is called with keyboardType = KeyboardType.Number and enabled = !srtlaServer.enabled; these must match the already-ported signature in com.moblin.android.view.utils.
CreateButtonView is called as CreateButtonView(enabled = ...) { ... } with a trailing action lambda.

List's .onDelete(perform:) has no LazyColumn counterpart, so it is rendered as a trailing delete IconButton that is only shown while the SRT(LA) server is disabled; the swipe gesture itself is not reproduced.
.navigationTitle("SRT(LA) server") becomes the Scaffold TopAppBar title of the destination form, and Section header/footer texts are emitted as plain Text items inside the LazyColumn.

Swift's three enums with associated values (ReplayEffectTransitionMode, ReplayEffectOutput, StingersState) become a sealed class, a private sealed class and a private enum class with the same case names.
`private weak let delegate` is kept weak with java.lang.ref.WeakReference<ReplayEffectDelegate>, so every call site reads delegate.get()?.replayEffectStatus(...).
The two Swift `extension ReplayEffect` blocks are translated as private member functions so they can still reach the class's private state.
`processorPipelineQueue.async { ... }` becomes `processorPipelineQueue.launch { ... }` with an explicit this@ReplayEffect for the self-assignments in setLayout/cancel.
`Int((duration / speed - offset).rounded(.up))` becomes ceil(...).toInt(); Kotlin saturates on overflow where Swift traps.

MetalPetalWidgetShape is taken from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.media.video, the package that declares VideoEffect's MetalPetal API (applyEffectsResizeMirrorMoveMetalPetal / modifyMetalPetalWidgetShape).
ReplayEffect is declared `internal constructor` because it takes a ReplayBufferFile, like ReplayEffectReplayReader.
replayEffectQueue is a single-thread CoroutineScope over a named serial executor, replacing the Swift serial DispatchQueue.
WatchConnectivity has no Android counterpart, so every function keeps its Swift signature with a TODO("no Android counterpart for WatchConnectivity") body.
sendMessageToWatch's type parameter (WatchMessageToWatch) is mapped to Any because the watch message enums are watch-only.
sendScenesToWatch takes List<Any> since WatchProtocolScene has no Android equivalent.
UIImage in makePng maps to Any; no direct Android UIImage type is introduced.
ProcessInfo.ThermalState maps to ThermalState from com.moblin.android.various.storages.
All members are top-level extension functions on Model; the file declares no Kotlin type.
This file declares no SwiftUI View, so no @Composable functions are generated despite the ui tier.
Data maps to ByteArray and UUID to java.util.UUID in the retained signatures.
apple_only: WatchConnectivity (WCSession, WCSessionDelegate, WCSessionActivationState)
WatchMessageToWatch and WatchMessageFromWatch
WatchProtocol* payload types (WatchProtocolScene, WatchProtocolChatMessage, WatchProtocolPadelScoreboard, ...)
UIImage (UIKit)

notes: ReplayProvider / Orientation / ReplaysDatabase published properties are treated as MutableStateFlow fields: read with collectAsState(), written with `.value = ...`.
The Swift @EnvironmentObject `model` has no Compose equivalent and is passed as an explicit `model: Model` parameter to every composable that used it.
SwiftUI @State/optional image state becomes `remember { mutableStateOf<Bitmap?>(null) }`; UIImage maps to android.graphics.Bitmap rendered with asImageBitmap().
Binding + onChange pairs (Slider startFromEnd, SpeedPicker speed) are folded into one onValueChange/onSelectedItemChange callback that writes the flow and calls the Model method.
glassEffect() (iOS 26) has no Compose counterpart, so the iOS <26 trash-button layout (icon inside a stroked circle) is used for all API levels.
Icons.Default.Stop, Save and PhotoCamera are not in material-icons-core and require the material-icons-extended artifact.
SegmentedHPicker is invoked as (items, selectedItem, onSelectedItemChange, modifier, trailing content lambda) - adjust to its real signature.
SettingsReplay.stop is assumed to be a Float; the Slider step count is derived as ((stop - 0f) / 0.1f).toInt() - 1.

RecordingProvider keeps the published `length` as a var backed by a private MutableStateFlow (_length) so Model code can assign it exactly like @Published; expose the flow publicly if Compose needs to observe it.
The Model extension members become top-level extension functions on Model in this package, in the same order as the Swift file.
URL.fileSize is replaced with java.io.File(path).length() and an assumed Long.formatBytes() helper from com.moblin.android.common.various.

Swift enum cases .startRecording/.stopRecording become SettingsMacrosEvent.START_RECORDING/.STOP_RECORDING and .record becomes QuickButtonType.RECORD (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE conversion, enum types themselves are declared in other files).
String(localized:) becomes localized(...) imported from com.moblin.android.

makeErrorToast/makeToast, media.*, stream.*, recordingsStorage.*, currentRecording, isRecording, isRecorderRecording, isChatPhone, isWatchLocal and macrosEventOccurred are Model members declared in other files and are only called here.
WatchConnectivity calls (sendRecordingLengthToWatch, sendIsRecordingToWatch), ActivityKit/PiP/mac status updates and remote control state are kept as plain calls; their bodies live in other files.
Optional default arguments of stopRecording and stopRecorderIfNeeded are preserved as Kotlin default parameters.

Only the three setter call sites changed: video.torch = value became video.setTorch(value), video.torchLevel = value became video.setTorchLevel(value) and video.videoOrientation = value became video.setVideoOrientation(value).

The VideoUnit properties torch, torchLevel and videoOrientation are replaced by the matching method calls on VideoUnit as in the Swift source; every other line of the file is byte-identical to the previous translation.
processorControlQueue and processorPipelineQueue stay as CoroutineScope wrappers over single-thread executors, since DispatchQueue.main.async is already mapped to mainScope.launch.
setVideoEncoderSettings remains a deliberate no-op from the earlier translation because VideoEncoderSettings is exposed through the encoder's own settings holder in Kotlin.
takeSnapshot and takeVideoSourceSnapshot keep the Android Bitmap signatures declared by VideoUnit instead of UIImage/CIImage.
startRecording and setUrl keep URI? parameters and pass url?.toString() into Recorder, which takes a String url as declared in Recorder.kt.
Log.i("Processor", ...) is used for the two logger.info calls with the class name as the tag.
Everything else, including delegate fan-out for audio and video encoders and the recorder delegate methods, is unchanged.
Single-line change: kickPusherStreamHost now reports the .kickRaid macro event instead of .kickHost.
Kotlin already used the SCREAMING_SNAKE macro-event entries, so this becomes SettingsMacrosEvent.KICK_RAID in the existing macrosEventOccurred call.
The #if targetEnvironment(macCatalyst) branch is dropped: Android has no Mac screen capture, so sceneNeedsMacScreenCapture always returns false.
nonisolated has no Kotlin equivalent; the delegate callbacks are plain top-level extension functions on Model.
DispatchQueue.main.async becomes mainScope.launch with a private file-level CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main).

Kotlin cannot add interface conformance from another file, so SampleBufferReceiverDelegate is declared here; Model must implement it in its own declaration (drop this copy if the media layer already declares it).
ReplayKit's RPSampleBufferType is replaced by the local enum SampleBufferType; Android screen capture (MediaProjection) only yields video frames.
CMSampleBuffer maps to MediaSample from com.moblin.android.media.
Swift UUID.uuidString is uppercase while java.util.UUID.toString() is lowercase, every CameraId producer must agree on one form.
screenRecordingLatency is used as written and must exist as a Model property or a media-layer global.
Zoom's @Published properties become public MutableStateFlow fields (same names), so the Model extensions can write them with .value; Compose reads them with collectAsState().

AVCaptureDevice.Position is mapped to an assumed CameraPosition enum in com.moblin.android.media with BACK, FRONT and the iOS low-energy variants; if the port uses CameraSelector.LENS_FACING_* ints instead, replace those constants.
getMinMaxZoomX assumes preferredCamera(position) returns androidx.camera.core.Camera? and reads camera.cameraInfo.zoomState.value.minZoomRatio/maxZoomRatio.

Model members used here (cameraPosition, cameraDevice, database, media, zoom, getSelectedScene, remoteControlStateChanged, isWatchLocal, sendZoomToWatch, sendZoomPresetsToWatch, attachBack*LowEnergyCamera, cameraZoomLevelToXScale, cameraZoomXMinimum/Maximum, isChatPhone) live in other Model+*.kt files in this package.
media.setCameraZoomLevel / media.stopCameraZoomLevel are the Media-layer counterparts of the AVCaptureDevice zoom calls and are called with positional arguments.
String(format:) is replaced by String.format(Locale.US, ...); UUID by java.util.UUID; noBackZoomPresetId/noFrontZoomPresetId stay file-private top-level vals.
The low-energy camera branches only re-attach iOS low-energy camera configurations; the calls are kept unchanged for the media layer to implement on Android.
Watch helpers are kept as calls although WatchConnectivity itself has no Android counterpart in this port.
ScoreboardEffect's constructor takes an androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Size (ModelScene passes a Compose Size) and converts it once with toCGSize(); all internal maths stays in CGSize as in Swift.
The four update* helpers build a one-shot ImageRenderer per update; their content lambdas capture local copies of the arguments instead of reading this.
scoreboard.sport is mapped with an explicit when over SettingsWidgetScoreboardSport; the Swift default branch becomes Kotlin else (modular).
setSceneWidget and setScoreboardImage make their pipeline-thread assignment with processorPipelineQueue.launch, since processorPipelineQueue is a CoroutineScope.
execute/executeMetalPetal chain the CIImage.move/cropped/composited and MTIImage.moveComposited extensions from com.moblin.android.videoeffects with a null fallback to the incoming image.
TeamScoreView and PoweredByMoblinView are @Composable functions; the VStack/HStack Spacers become Modifier.weight(1f).
PoweredByMoblinView reverses Swift's padding/background order so the background covers the padding, and merges the horizontal and vertical padding into one call.
formatScore and the two font-size globals stay top-level in this package because other scoreboard files use them.
The diff only adds two calls at the top of handleAudioRouteChange and the new public func updateIsBluetoothAudioOutput.

isBluetoothAudioOutput is a Model state property declared in the hand-written Model.kt; it is written directly (plain var), matching the other Model booleans used in this file (isAppActive, defaultMic, initialVolume).
stopTextToSpeechIfOutputNotAllowed() lives in the Model text-to-speech file of the same package and is only called here, never re-declared.
Swift's collection.contains { predicate } becomes Kotlin's any { predicate } on the outputs list.
The port-type list uses the AVAudioSession.Port string constants (bluetoothA2DP, bluetoothHFP, bluetoothLE) that the platform shim declares, so portType compares as a String equality test.
Everything else in the file is byte-identical to the previous Kotlin port.
SwiftUI Form/NavigationStack child becomes a Scaffold with a TopAppBar titled 'Auto scene switcher' and a LazyColumn body.
Section is rendered as a plain Column inside a single LazyColumn item; no Section wrapper exists in Compose.

AutoSwitchersSelectView and AutoSwitchersSettingsView are imported from com.moblin.android.view.settings.scenes.autoswitchers and ShortcutSectionView from com.moblin.android.view.utils; they are assumed to already be @Composable and to accept a trailing content lambda where used.
The @ObservedObject models are only forwarded to child composables, so no collectAsState() call is needed in this file.
AutoSceneSwitcherProvider comes from com.moblin.android.various.model and SettingsAutoSceneSwitchers from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
.pickerStyle(.inline) and .labelsHidden() have no Compose equivalent; the selector style must be handled inside AutoSwitchersSelectView.
The string literal used by Text is localized through the top-level localized() helper from com.moblin.android.
Scaffold usage requires the ExperimentalMaterial3Api opt-in on Android with the current Material 3 release.
Only the Kick channel search sorting changed: the inline sorted(by:) closure is replaced by the shared helper sortedBySearchPrefix(results, searchText = newValue) { it.username }.
Added the import com.moblin.android.various.utils.sortedBySearchPrefix, placed between the various.network and view.controlbar imports to keep the import block ordered.
The local val text = newValue.lowercase() was removed because the helper lowercases the prefix itself.
Everything else in the file is unchanged, including the Android-only IosTextField helper and the onPlatformChange / LaunchedEffect hook.
BitratePresetView and QuickButtonBitrateView are composable functions; the Swift private struct keeps its private visibility on the Kotlin function.

SwiftUI Picker(.inline) + .tag() + .labelsHidden() become an ExposedDropdownMenuBox whose DropdownMenuItem onClick writes the selected preset bitrate; the .tag value is dropped because Compose carries it in the click handler.
Picker selection write `$stream.bitrate` is translated as `stream.bitrate.value = ...`, assuming SettingsStream exposes its published property as a MutableStateFlow.
database.bitratePresets is treated as a StateFlow and read with collectAsState().
onChange(of: stream.bitrate) -> LaunchedEffect(bitrate); note that LaunchedEffect also runs on first composition, so setBitrate is called once at start-up.
NavigationLink is replaced by the onNavigate: (String) -> Unit callback with the destination name "BitratePresetsSettingsView"; navigation-compose is not used.
.navigationTitle("Bitrate") becomes the TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold.
Icons.Default.SettingsInputAntenna is the closest match for SF Symbol dot.radiowaves.left.and.right and requires the material-icons-extended artifact.
@Binding presenting became a value parameter plus onPresentingChange: (Boolean) -> Unit; the caller keeps the sheet/panel state.
onAppear became LaunchedEffect(Unit) calling a local suspend fetchInfo(); Model.getKickChatterInfo is assumed to be a suspend function in the port (Swift used a completion handler).
The Kick branch matches post.platform?.name lowercased against "kick" because Platform is not in the glossary; adjust if Platform is modelled differently in the port.
CacheAsyncImage is called with url plus a content lambda whose parameter is an ImageBitmap, since Compose has no AsyncImagePhase.
The platform icon name from imageName() is resolved with Resources.getIdentifier(name, "drawable", packageName), so those drawables must exist in the app.
View member helpers profileHeader/infoRows became private top-level composables; setErrorMessage/fetchInfo became local functions inside the composable.
.foregroundStyle(.white) and .background(.black) became CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentColor provides Color.White) over Modifier.background(Color.Black).
formatDate(...) is expected to take the raw ISO string and return a nullable formatted String; ChatterInfo keeps every Swift property including the required role and subscribedMonths.
AlertsEffectAlert (sealed class with the same case names, keeping the 'TwitchSubscrptionGift' typo) and AlertsEffectDelegate (interface) are declared in this file.
Swift's 'private weak let delegate' becomes a plain strong property: Kotlin has no weak properties; switch to java.lang.ref.WeakReference if a Model->effect->Model cycle shows up.
The private Pipeline struct becomes a private class so the pipeline thread (getImage) and the main thread (play) mutate one shared instance, exactly as Swift's struct property does.
Swift's labelled tuple return of calcFacePlacement becomes the private data class FacePlacement(center, height, rotation).

createSpeechSynthesizer() is translated as AVSpeechSynthesizer().also { it.usesApplicationAudioSession = false }; the Kotlin helper of that name returns TextToSpeech and is only for chat text-to-speech.

settings.fontWeight.toFontWeight() and settings.fontDesign.toFontDesign() are assumed names for the settings -> Compose FontWeight/FontDesign conversions (like RgbColor.color()); verify against the settings port.
AudioPlayer(contentsOf = soundUrl) mirrors Swift's failable AudioPlayer(contentsOf:); verify the constructor signature of the Kotlin AudioPlayer.
settings.textToSpeechLanguageVoices[language]?.apple?.voice is assumed for the language voice table; verify the Kotlin settings type.
Toggle with a title becomes a Row holding a Text label and a Material 3 Switch, matching the other settings rows.
.onChange(of:) is translated to LaunchedEffect(cameraControlsEnabled), which, unlike SwiftUI's onChange on older iOS, also fires on first composition.
