Nothing else in the file was touched: all other declarations, imports and the hand-written Android helpers remain byte-identical.
sendTwitchShoutout is added between startRaidTwitchChannel and cancelRaidTwitchChannel, calling TwitchApi.sendShoutout with the same broadcasterId/toBroadcasterId/onComplete shape as startRaid.
The failure log in the no-callback overload used NetworkResponse.Success instead of isSuccessful() so no new network extension import is needed.

MacroEvent calls now pass variables; keys are built with MacroVariable.fromRawValue("...") using the Swift case names, matching the SettingsMacrosEvent.fromRawValue convention already used in this file.
MacroVariable is imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings and the map is passed as a plain mapOf, which matches a MacroVariables typealias over Map<MacroVariable, String>.
twitchEventSubChannelShoutoutCreate is added right after twitchEventSubChannelModerate, matching the Swift declaration order.
Because TwitchEventSubDelegate is implemented as an explicit anonymous object here, an override for twitchEventSubChannelShoutoutCreate was added there too so reloadTwitchEventSub keeps compiling.
Swift .orange is translated as Color(0xFFFF9500), the orange value already used elsewhere in this file.
Pre-existing TODO()s for Alert playback, EventCat printers and ChatHighlightKind cases were kept unchanged.
SettingsBlackSharkCoolerDevices.devices is a read-only List here, so append/removeAll/remove(atOffsets:) all assign a new list back onto the property.
The Swift List wrapper around the ForEach is dropped: the ForEach is the Section content, keeping CreateButtonView after it.
The ForEach keeps onDelete and reads device.id for its key; contextMenuDeleteButton becomes ContextMenuDeleteButton around the row.
@EnvironmentObject model becomes a parameter defaulting to LocalModel.current, @ObservedObject becomes a plain parameter.
navigationTitle is folded into Form(title = "Black Shark coolers").
Section's trailing footer closure becomes footerContent, since it contains the SwipeLeftToDeleteHelpView composable.
String(localized: "a cooler") becomes localized("a cooler").
Only change: model.reattachCamera() becomes model.attachCamera() in the LaunchedEffect that persists the mode.
All hand-written Android code (modeState/applied state, ExposedDropdownMenuBox, onModeChange callback, LocalModel default) kept byte-identical.
SwiftUI Form/Section are rendered as a LazyColumn with section header Text items, matching the original order (Buttons then Thumb sticks).

.navigationTitle("Controller") became the TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold, which needs the ExperimentalMaterial3Api opt-in.
Section titles use MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium; no explicit colors or fonts were present in the Swift source.

GameControllersControllerButtonSettingsView and GameControllersControllerThumbStickSettingsView are not imported because they live in the same package com.moblin.android.view.settings.gamecontrollers.

SwiftUI Form/Section are replaced by scrollable Columns; .navigationTitle(...) is mapped to a Material 3 TopAppBar (requires @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)).
NavigationLink destinations (OBS settings, media source settings) are shown in a androidx.compose.ui.window.Dialog because this file has no NavHost / NavController.

Cross-file composables are called with assumed signatures: TextButtonView(text, action), HCenter(content), ShortcutSectionView(content), TextEditNavigationView(title, value, onSubmit, placeholder), ValueEditView(title, number, value, minimum, maximum, onSubmit, increment, unit).

NavigationLink becomes an onNavigate(route) callback; the wrapper uses the route string "DjiDeviceSettingsView" and the destination is built by the navigation host, so the wrapper keeps model/djiDevices parameters purely for signature parity.

djiDevices.devices.append(device) becomes a copy-and-reassign on the backing MutableStateFlow, since Kotlin lists are immutable.
String(localized: "a device") maps to the top-level localized() helper from package com.moblin.android.
`.navigationTitle("DJI devices")` is rendered as the Material 3 TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold.
The private Swift struct becomes a private @Composable function of the same name so the two files read side by side.

status' @Published values are collected with collectAsState at the top of the composable; blackSharkCoolerDevices and device are settings objects and are read/written directly.
scanner.discoveredPeripherals is read as .value inside the onDeviceChange callback, since only the callback reads it.
Toggle's .onChange becomes the onChange lambda that assigns the plain var first and then calls the model action, matching SwiftUI's order.
The RGB brightness Slider became FormSlider over 0f..100f inside a FormRow, and the ColorPicker uses onSelectionChange with an early return instead of guard let.
formatBlackSharkCoolerDeviceState keeps the Swift if/else chain and the else branch, even though the Kotlin enum has no other entries.
logger.info became Log.i with the view name as the tag.
model.blackSharkCoolerDevices is looked up by UUID (entries.firstOrNull { it.key == ... }?.value) because it is a plain MutableMap without .value.
Added the new makeRaidSuggestions(channels, streams) overload just before RaidChannelSearchView, as in the diff, and kept the two existing overloads untouched.

RaidChannelSearchView's second Section now renders RaidSuggestionsView(model, suggestions) instead of a ForEach over TwitchApiChannel.
Everything else in the file, including the platform hooks, Form layout and the PickerRow/IosTextField helpers, is byte-identical.

SettingsKeyboardKey properties (key, function, functionData) are treated as MutableStateFlow fields: read with collectAsState() and written through .value; the setter names must match the model from the settings package.

SwiftUI NavigationLink destinations are inline in this file, so two extra destination composables are declared: KeyboardKeySettingsForm (reached with onNavigate("keyboardKey")) and KeyboardKeyPickerView (reached with onNavigate("key")).
The Swift private helper functions() became a file-private top-level function returning SettingsControllerFunction.entries without .zoomIn/.zoomOut.
ControllerButtonView is called with the project binding convention: function/functionData values plus onFunctionChange/onFunctionDataChange lambdas.

model.getSceneName/getWidgetName receive UUID.randomUUID() where Swift used the default UUID initializer for missing ids.

Everything else in the Kotlin file, including hand-written Android helpers (MinimumScaleText, ConfirmationDialog, SystemImage, AssetImage) and imports, is kept byte-identical.
The existing TODO("walking") for the walking workout type is preserved since it is unrelated to this diff.

Everything else in the file is byte-identical to the previous translation.
Form/Section are rendered as a LazyColumn; section headers become plain Text items with MaterialTheme.typography.titleSmall.
@ObservedObject SettingsDebug properties are read with collectAsState() and written through assumed setters named set<Property>(value); check those names against SettingsDebug.kt.
The navigationTitle is rendered as a Material3 TopAppBar inside a Scaffold (requires the ExperimentalMaterial3Api opt-in).

fullScreenCover is rendered as a conditional composable inside a Box overlay, and its .task/.onAppear becomes LaunchedEffect(Unit) { reloadLog() }.

The Swift context-menu delete closure is preserved as the local val onContextMenuDelete; it must be wired to a trigger (for example a long press) manually.
makeOffsets is assumed to return List<Int>? (IndexSet in Swift); deletion removes indices in descending order.

logger.info calls become android.util.Log.i with the tag "MediaPlayerSettingsView".
List.onMove and List.onDelete have no LazyColumn equivalent and are marked TODO; deletePlaylistFile is kept because it is the target of onDelete.
LocationSettingsView takes model, database, location, locationManager, stream and onNavigate as parameters; @EnvironmentObject, @ObservedObject and @Binding become plain parameters.

name.capitalized is replaceFirstChar { it.titlecase() } and removeAllWhitespaces() is inlined as filterNot { it.isWhitespace() } after lowercase().
navigationTitle is rendered as a Material 3 Scaffold with a TopAppBar title.
String(localized:) uses localized() from com.moblin.android; Form/List became LazyColumn and the Section became plain items plus header/footer texts.

@Published properties are modelled as MutableStateFlow: they are read with collectAsState() and written with `.value = ...`.

contextMenuDeleteButton, onMove and onDelete have no Compose counterpart and are TODO(); the delete/reorder bodies they contained are kept in local lambdas so no behaviour is lost.
The inline NavigationLink destination Form of AutoSwitcherSceneSettingsView has no sibling Swift view, so it is translated into the extra composable AutoSwitcherSceneSettingsDestinationView.

Image(systemName: "flame") becomes Icon(Icons.Filled.LocalFireDepartment, ...), which requires the material-icons-extended artifact.

.foregroundStyle(...) on the image maps to the Icon tint parameter and .overlay(RoundedRectangle.stroke(.secondary)) maps to Modifier.border(1.dp, MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outline, shape) after clip+background(Color.Black).
stream.startTime.formatted() is translated with java.time DateTimeFormatter.ofLocalizedDateTime(FormatStyle.MEDIUM).withZone(ZoneId.systemDefault()).
stream.highestThermalState! is translated to the Kotlin !! forced unwrap, matching the Swift force unwrap inside the device-health row.

toProcessInfo().color() is kept unchanged and is expected to be an extension on ThermalState in com.moblin.android.various.storages; likewise duration().formatWithSeconds(), totalBytes.formatBytes() and the *String() members are assumed to exist on the ported StreamingHistoryStream / Settings types.
Nothing in this file is iOS-only, so no TODO() placeholders were introduced.
WorkoutDevicesSettingsView is a composable function; @EnvironmentObject model and @ObservedObject workoutDevices become parameters, model defaulting to LocalModel.current.
SettingsWorkoutDevices.devices is a PublishedList mutated in place, so it is read directly (no collectAsState) and ForEach receives the live list.
The Swift Form + .navigationTitle becomes Form(title = "Workout devices"), which supplies the NavigationStack.
ForEach with .onDelete and .contextMenuDeleteButton maps to the swiftui ForEach with onDelete plus ContextMenuDeleteButton around each row.
remove(atOffsets:) uses the MutableList extension from com.moblin.android.platform.swiftui; removeAll { } is the Kotlin MutableList.removeAll predicate form.
String(localized: "a device") becomes localized("a device") and is passed to SwipeLeftToDeleteHelpView.
VStack default spacing is 8.dp, so it is a Column with Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp) and CenterHorizontally.
model.statusTopRight is passed through to WorkoutDeviceSettingsView as the StatusTopRight parameter.
formatTeslaVehicleState stays a private top-level function; TeslaVehicleState? null and .idle both map to the Disconnected string.
TextButtonView has no enabled state on Android, so every .disabled(...) row became FormButton(title = ..., centered = true, enabled = ...); the enabled rows stay TextButtonView.
The configuration view's enabled condition reads the collected vehicleState first, so the plain database checks cannot short-circuit the state read and leave the row stale.
tesla.vehicleState, tesla.vehicleInfotainmentConnected and tesla.vehicleVehicleSecurityConnected are StateFlows collected with collectAsState() at the top of each composable that uses them.
UUID(uuidString:) is translated to runCatching { UUID.fromString(value) }.getOrNull(), so an invalid string returns early as the Swift guard did.
ObservedObject parameters tesla and settings are plain required parameters; model keeps the LocalModel.current default of @EnvironmentObject.
NavigationLink destinations keep their real composables (TeslaVehicleScannerSettingsView, TeslaSettingsConfigurationView) instead of a string route.
String(localized:) is localized(...); Image("Tesla") is AssetImage with ContentScale.Fit.
status.workoutDeviceState is a MutableStateFlow on the Kotlin model, so it is collected with collectAsState() and the file-private state() helper reads the collected value to keep recomposition.

The Model helpers enableWorkoutDevice, disableWorkoutDevice, isWorkoutDeviceEnabled, setCurrentWorkoutDevice and setWorkoutDeviceWheelCircumference are extension functions, imported one by one from com.moblin.android.various.model.
The Form destination's .onAppear becomes DisposableEffect(Unit) as the first child of the Form, so it runs when the destination appears.
scanner.discoveredPeripherals is a MutableStateFlow in the BluetoothScanner shim, so the search uses .value.firstOrNull { it.identifier == deviceId }.
UUID(uuidString:) has no throwing Kotlin equivalent, so it becomes runCatching { UUID.fromString(value) }.getOrNull() with an early return.
Int(value) keeps its ASCII digits-only 64-bit semantics with toLongOrNull(); the parsed Long is narrowed with toInt() when stored in the settings property.
A Compose Toggle does not observe a binding, so the enable/disable model call that Swift ran in .onChange is executed inside the toggle's onChange after assigning device.enabled.
Section footers and headers use the String parameters of the swiftui Section component and are passed through localized(), like Text literals.

@Published properties of SettingsWidgetPomodoroTimer are read with collectAsState() and written through setter methods (setFocusDuration, setSecondsRemaining, ...); the exact setter names and the *Color* property types are inferred from the port's settings model.
The RgbColorPickerView and TextEditNavigationView calls keep the Swift argument labels (title/value/opacity/onSubmit); their Kotlin signatures (color: Color, onChange: (Color) -> Unit) were assumed.
NavigationLink became an onNavigate callback with the destination names "pomodoroSoundSelectorFocusToBreak" and "pomodoroSoundSelectorBreakToFocus".
The sound preview uses android.media.MediaPlayer instead of AVAudioPlayer and is released in a DisposableEffect, mirroring onDisappear.
The static SF Symbols map to Material icons; SkipNext and Stop come from material-icons-extended, so that artifact must be on the dependency list.
ExposedDropdownMenuBox and Modifier.menuAnchor() require @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class), which is applied on the two views using them.
PomodoroPhase entries are assumed to be Focus and ShortBreak, and PomodoroFocusIcon/PomodoroBreakIcon are used through the Kotlin enum 'entries'.
PomodoroSoundSelectorView is not file-private so the screen that renders navigation destinations can instantiate it.
The private enum ScheduleStreamState with an associated value became a sealed class with data objects Idle/InProgress/Succeeded and a Failed(message) data class.
SwiftUI @Binding parameters became a plain value plus an onChange lambda where the child really writes back; read-only bindings (StreamsView streams/loadError) are passed as plain values only.
CacheAsyncImage is called with url/modifier/placeholder; its content slot is omitted and the AppIconNoBackground asset is referenced as R.drawable.app_icon_no_background.
NetworkResponse is assumed to be Success(value)/AuthError/Error and OperationResult is assumed to expose Success; adjust the when branches if the real port differs.
@Published model/stream properties are read with collectAsState() inside composables and with .value inside plain callbacks; direct assignment is used for writes.

TextButtonView, TextEditNavigationView, CloseToolbar and HCenter are invoked with assumed parameter names (text/enabled/onClick, title/value/onSubmit/placeholder, presenting/onPresentingChange, modifier/content).
ISO8601DateFormatter, Date.formatted and Date.distance were replaced with java.time OffsetDateTime/Instant and a localized DateTimeFormatter.
The destroy SF Symbol names map to Icons.Default.Close for "stop" and Icons.Default.Delete for "trash".
SwiftUI Form/Section has no direct Compose counterpart: a private SettingsSection helper renders a header Text, the items and a footer Text above a HorizontalDivider.
Picker is implemented once in a private generic SettingsPicker composable using ExposedDropdownMenuBox plus DropdownMenuItem; enablement from .disabled is passed through the enabled parameter.

NavigationLink becomes onNavigate(name) callbacks (destination names: 'Bitrate presets', 'Key frame interval', 'Adaptive resolution', 'Timecodes'); the nested TextEditView/Form destinations are separate screens, so only the navigation call is kept here.
Toggle is implemented once in a private SettingsToggle composable: a Row with a label and a Material 3 Switch; .onChange(of:) is folded into onCheckedChange.

Model/Database published flags (isLive, isRecording, showAllSettings) are assumed to be StateFlow and are read with collectAsState(); SettingsStream properties are treated as plain mutable vars so the settings can be written directly.
The 'Low light boost (LLB)' section loses its `if #available(iOS 18, *)` gate because Android has no comparable OS-version restriction.
Slider's onEditingChanged(begin=false) maps to onValueChangeFinished, and step 0.1 over 1...3 maps to valueRange 1f..3f with steps = 19; the Double property is converted to/from Float for the Slider.
All user facing literals are wrapped in localized(); Image(systemName: "speedometer") maps to Icons.Default.Speed which requires material-icons-extended on the classpath.
Model.isLive and Model.isRecording are StateFlows read with collectAsState(); SettingsStream and SettingsStreamMultiStreamingDestination keep plain mutable properties so Switch/Toggle can write them.
NavigationLink is replaced by an onNavigate route-name callback; the routes used here are "Destination", "StreamMultiStreamingUrl" and "Multi streaming".

The two NavigationLink destination bodies are exposed as extra top-level composables DestinationSettingsView and MultiStreamingSettingsView so no Form content from this file is lost; the navigation host renders them for those route names.
StreamMultiStreamingSettingsView only renders the row ("Multi streaming" plus the enabled-destination count), so it takes the objects it needs: multiStreaming and onNavigate.
onChange(of: destination.enabled) is folded into Switch.onCheckedChange and the reload runs in a remembered coroutine scope so a suspend reloadStreamIfEnabled also compiles.
contextMenuDeleteButton becomes a long-press DropdownMenu with a Delete item; SwiftUI's .onDelete swipe gesture has no Compose equivalent here, deletion stays available through that menu.
navigationTitle -> TopAppBar inside Scaffold, and .disabled(x) -> enabled = !x on the row / Switch.
String(localized:) -> localized(); numberOfEnabledDestinations is a private top-level function taking the multiStreaming settings.

SegmentedHPicker/SegmentedVPicker live in this same package in another file; their Kotlin signature was assumed to be (items, selectedItem, onSelectedItemChange, selectedColor, onLongPress, content) because the Swift code passes a Binding plus trailing ViewBuilder closure.
SceneSelector.sceneIndex is assumed to be a MutableStateFlow<Int>: read with collectAsState() and written via .value because the Swift code assigns to it directly.
Model.enabledScenes is assumed to be a StateFlow<List<SettingsScene>> read with collectAsState().
SwiftUI .foregroundStyle(.white) is mapped to CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentColor provides Color.White) so it propagates to the picker's Text children.
.minimumScaleFactor has no Compose counterpart and was dropped rather than faked.
ZStack -> Box; the quickSwitchGroup badge uses Row/Column with weight(1f) spacers to reproduce the bottom-trailing alignment.
.cornerRadius(7) plus .overlay(RoundedRectangle().stroke(...)) become Modifier.clip(RoundedCornerShape(7.dp)) and Modifier.border(1.dp, pickerBorderColor, RoundedCornerShape(7.dp)).
The segment dimension globals (segmentHeight, sceneSegmentWidth, ...) are treated as Float and converted with .dp at call sites.
UIDocumentPickerViewController / UIViewControllerRepresentable has no Compose counterpart: PickerView is a TODO() and the folder picker is shown in a ModalBottomSheet.

The inline NavigationLink destinations are replaced by onNavigate(route) rows, and their content is kept in destination composables declared in this file (RecordingPathFormView, StreamRecordingVideoBitrateView, StreamRecordingKeyFrameIntervalView, StreamRecordingAudioBitrateView) so no SwiftUI content is lost. Route strings are "recordingPath", "videoBitrate", "keyFrameInterval", "audioBitrate".
SettingsStreamRecording, SettingsStream and Model @Published properties are treated as StateFlows: read with collectAsState(), written with .value.
onChange(of:) becomes LaunchedEffect(value), so it also runs on first composition; guard with a previous-value remember if the reload must not happen on entry.

recording.recordingPath is treated as ByteArray? (Swift Data bookmark) and model.onDocumentPickerUrl as ((String) -> Unit)? - adjust both to the Model/SettingsStreamRecording declarations from their own files.
makeRecordingPath(recordingPath).path replaces FileManager bookmark resolution; URL.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource/bookmarkData have no Android counterpart (see unsupported).
.navigationTitle("Recording") / "Recording path" are not rendered here; the hosting Scaffold/TopAppBar owns the titles.

truncationMode(.head) and .tint(.red) have no direct Compose equivalent; Text uses maxLines/TextOverflow.Ellipsis and TextButtonView keeps its default colors (and its signature may need text/onClick parameter renaming).

@Published properties became private MutableStateFlow fields with public StateFlow getters plus setX(...) setters (setFunction, setFunctionData, setButtons, setLeftThumbStickFunction, setRightThumbStickFunction).

The hand-written Codable implementations became custom KSerializer objects (SettingsGameControllerButtonSerializer, SettingsGameControllerSerializer) backed by surrogate @Serializable data classes so the flattened JSON shape of SettingsGameControllerButton (functionData fields on the top level) is preserved.
UUID is persisted as a String; java.util.UUID.toString() is lowercase while Swift's UUID string is uppercase, so an iOS-written payload would need case-insensitive parsing.

SettingsGimbalMotion has no raw values in Swift, so its rawValue is the lowercased-case-name (kapow/yes/no/wakeup) which matches the coding keys Swift synthesises for that enum; the value is stored as a plain string rather than Swift's {"kapow":{}} object.

SettingsControllerThumbStickFunction.color() and SettingsControllerFunction.color() are @Composable member functions because they read MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary; Color.gray maps to Color.Gray.
toString() overrides Any.toString(); the two-argument overload toString(sceneName, widgetName) is kept as a normal overload and falls back to toString() for all other cases.
SettingsControllerFunctionData stays a plain data class (it is not Codable in Swift; it is encoded inline into the button document).
No iOS-only frameworks are used in this file, so nothing had to be replaced by TODO().

SwiftUI @EnvironmentObject / @ObservedObject models (Model, CameraState, Database, CameraShow) become plain @Composable parameters; their @Published properties are read with collectAsState() and written through the public MutableStateFlow's .value.
LocalizedStringKey parameters are kept as String and passed through the top-level localized() helper when rendered.
@Binding parameters are translated to a value parameter plus an onChange lambda (onValueChange for the slider).
Slider step (0.01 / 0.1) is converted to the Material3 steps count (number of intervals minus one).
Slider onEditingChanged(true/false) is approximated with onValueChange (editing started) and onValueChangeFinished (editing finished).
Each SwiftUI View whose body is a multi-child ViewBuilder emits its children as sibling composables into the enclosing layout, so the parent Column keeps the same 1dp-spaced stack.
CameraShowType enum entries are assumed to be SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE Kotlin enum constants (BIAS, WHITE_BALANCE, ISO, EXPOSURE, FOCUS) from com.moblin.android.various.model.
Icons.Default.LockOpen lives in material-icons-extended; add that dependency if only the core icon set is present.
SwiftUI views became @Composable functions; PickerItemView, ZoomPresetView and ZoomPresetVView stay private composables with the same names and order.

@EnvironmentObject/@ObservedObject published state is read with collectAsState() on StateFlow properties (model.cameraPosition, database.bigButtons, zoom.front/backZoomPresets, zoom.front/backPresetId, preset.name).
CGFloat dimensions map to Float and are converted to Dp with .dp; segmentWidth()/height() are kept as local helper functions inside each composable.
The @Binding presets and selectedPresetId are never mutated in this file, so they map to a plain List<SettingsZoomPreset> parameter and a plain UUID parameter (no onChange lambda added).
minimumScaleFactor(pickerLabelMinimumScaleFactor) has no Compose equivalent and is replaced by maxLines = 1 with TextOverflow.Ellipsis.
The RoundedRectangle stroke overlay maps to Modifier.border, .cornerRadius(7) to Modifier.clip(RoundedCornerShape(7.dp)) and .foregroundStyle(.white) to the Text color inside PickerItemView.
SegmentedHPicker/SegmentedVPicker are invoked with items, selectedItem, onSelectedItemChange, selectedColor, modifier and a content slot; verify against the port's actual signature.
model.cameraPosition is compared against CameraPosition.front (CameraPosition is not in the glossary, so the enum name and package may need checking).
Form/Section become a LazyColumn with primary-colored section header Texts; the two footer Texts are plain items at the end.
Each SwiftUI `Label { Toggle } icon: { Image }` becomes the private helper composable LocalOverlayToggle (Icon + label Text + Material 3 Switch in a clickable Row).

@ObservedObject SettingsShow is read with collectAsState(); the write path assigns to MutableStateFlow.value, so SettingsShow is assumed to expose each toggle as a MutableStateFlow<Boolean> - adjust the write path if the model exposes plain vars.

SF Symbols are mapped to the closest Material icons (some come from material-icons-extended: CameraAlt, Mic, Chat, Visibility, GraphicEq, Memory, Storage, Link, SettingsRemote, VideogameAsset, Speed, AccessTime, Public, Pets, DirectionsWalk).
.navigationTitle("Local overlays") becomes a Scaffold TopAppBar, which needs the ExperimentalMaterial3Api opt-in.

Toggle order, titles and model property names match the Swift source one-for-one (stream, cameras, microphone, zoom, obsStatus, events, chat, viewers, audioLevel, systemMonitor, location, ingests, moblink, remoteControl, djiDevices, gameController, speed, uptime, browserWidgets, bonding, bondingRtts, catPrinter, workoutDevice, zoomPresets).
No navigation destinations exist in this screen, so no onNavigate callback was added.
Added `font: chat.font` to the ChatLineStyle construction in makeChatLineStyle.
Everything else is unchanged from the previous Kotlin file.
SwiftUI struct -> top-level @Composable fun; the private helper gameControllerIndex stays a file-private top-level function that now takes the Database as its first parameter.

NavigationLink -> onNavigate callback; because the callback only carries a String, the destination view plus the tapped controller id are encoded into the route string "GameControllersControllerSettingsView/<id>" and the caller must decode it.
model is kept as a parameter for signature parity but is unused here, since the destination view is no longer constructed in this file.

database.gameControllers is treated as a MutableStateFlow<List<SettingsGameController>>: it is read with collectAsState() and mutated by assigning .value (filterNot for delete, plus for append). If the port exposes a read-only StateFlow plus mutator methods on Database, replace those three assignments.
contextMenuDeleteButton (long press) and List.onDelete (swipe) both collapse onto Modifier.combinedClickable(onLongClick = ...); the SwipeLeftToDeleteHelpView footer is preserved unchanged.
Form -> LazyColumn, Section -> header text separated by HorizontalDivider, .navigationTitle -> TopAppBar inside a Scaffold (that is why ExperimentalMaterial3Api is opted in).
String(localized: "a controller") -> localized("a controller") from package com.moblin.android.
GameControllersControllerSettingsView lives in this same package, so it needs no import; only the route string references it.
Swift @Published properties are modelled as public MutableStateFlow fields (a MutableStateFlow is-a StateFlow) so both reading via collectAsState() and writing work.

The hand-written Codable encode/init(from:) are translated with private @Serializable surrogate classes so the Swift coding keys are preserved exactly (systemImageNameOn/Off, blackScreenShowChat/Status, backgroundImage*).
SettingsQuickButtonType keeps its raw strings byte-identical through SettingsQuickButtonTypeSerializer; the 'Pause chat' alias is mapped to chat in fromRawValue as the Swift decoder did.
Missing JSON keys fall back to the same defaults Swift supplied (Swift decode(_:default:) equivalent: surrogate defaults).
id stays a java.util.UUID and is persisted as a string inside the surrogate.
color remains an androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color StateFlow; backgroundColor remains an RgbColor.
The enum's Swift toString() becomes an override of Any.toString() returning localized text (live -> "Stream", stream -> "Switch stream").
RgbColor.color() is assumed to be a member provided by com.moblin.android.common.various; no extra import was added.

ZoomSettingsView became a @Composable function; Form/Section are a LazyColumn whose sections are a header Text, the items and a footer Text, and .navigationTitle("Zoom") is rendered with Scaffold + TopAppBar.

SwiftUI List onDelete / contextMenuDeleteButton / deleteDisabled are implemented with Material 3 SwipeToDismissBox (swipe left), which matches the "Swipe left to delete" footer text; the minimum of one preset is enforced in confirmValueChange.
onMove drag reordering has no Compose counterpart and the move helpers keep TODO() bodies, so they are not wired to any gesture.
model.zoom.objectWillChange.send() has no counterpart; state changes are expected to propagate through the StateFlow-backed settings object, so only a TODO() marker is kept.
Assumed SettingsZoom.speed is a Double (Slider uses toFloat()/toDouble() conversions) and SettingsZoomPreset.x is a Float, matching minZoomX and getMinMaxZoomX.
CameraPosition is not in the glossary; imported from com.moblin.android.various.model with BACK/FRONT constants, and getMinMaxZoomX is assumed to return a Pair (uses .second).
makeOffsets is assumed to return List<Int>?; the delete helpers remove the offsets in descending order and then notify the model.
oldZoomPresetSettingsUpdated naming is kept exactly as in Swift, including the front variant frontZoomPresetSettingUpdated (no 's').
@ObservedObject/@EnvironmentObject models are passed in as parameters and their published properties are read with collectAsState().
Enum entries keep the Swift names (StreamOverlayIconAndTextPlacement.afterIcon/.hide) and are referenced as constants of the ported enum class.

The Swift `.padding(20).contentShape(Rectangle()).padding(-20)` tap-area trick has no Compose equivalent (negative padding is invalid), so that padding pair is dropped; the enclosing LeftOverlayView keeps the tap gesture.
Platform logos use Image(platform.imageName()); the drawable is resolved with Resources.getIdentifier and nothing is drawn when the drawable is missing.

model.isShowingStatus*()/is*Configured()/is*Connected() style calls are made directly; if the Model port exposes them as StateFlow-backed state, hoist those reads into collectAsState() so recomposition still works.
Inline SF Symbols are mapped to material-icons-extended: eye -> Visibility, message -> Chat; other symbols stay as strings because StreamOverlayIconAndTextView takes the symbol name.
countFormatter.format(viewerCount) keeps the shared formatter from com.moblin.android.common.various.
StreamingPlatformStatus status is handled as a sealed hierarchy StreamingPlatformStatus.Status with Live(viewerCount)/Unknown/Offline.
Executor.state is a StateFlow collected with collectAsState(); the 3 second reset uses a coroutine on Dispatchers.Main with delay(3000).
ExecutorState and ModActionType keep the Swift lowercase case names as Kotlin enum constants so both codebases read identically.

ExecutorView takes model as an explicit parameter instead of @EnvironmentObject, so ToggleActionView, DurationActionView, ActionRowView, RaidChannelView, SlowModeView, FollowersOnlyView, SubscribersOnlyView and EmotesOnlyView each gained a leading model parameter to forward it.
@Binding parameters became a value plus an onChange callback: presentingModeration/onPresentingModerationChange, options/onOptionsChange, platform/onPlatformChange.
Picker is rendered with ExposedDropdownMenuBox and Modifier.menuAnchor(), which needs @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class).
NavigationLinkView cannot push a screen without navigation-compose, so it renders a clickable row that reveals its content inline when tapped.
contextMenuDeleteButton, deleteDisabled and onDelete on poll options were replaced by an explicit delete IconButton shown when more than two options exist.
CacheAsyncImage(url, modifier) and R.drawable.app_icon_no_background are assumed shapes for com.moblin.android.various and the app resources; verify them against those files.
DispatchQueue maps to kotlinx.coroutines CoroutineDispatcher (parameter names `queue` kept), and DispatchQueue.main.async becomes mainScope.launch on CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main).
URLRequest/URLResponse become okhttp3.Request/okhttp3.Response, Data becomes ByteArray, UUID becomes java.util.UUID and @MainActor is dropped (plain functions).
CGSize/CMVideoDimensions are mapped to android.util.Size; the snapshot callbacks (UIImage/CIImage) are mapped to android.graphics.Bitmap.
AVCaptureColorSpace -> android.graphics.ColorSpace (API 26) and AVCaptureVideoOrientation -> android.view.Surface rotation constants (portrait -> ROTATION_90, landscapeRight -> ROTATION_0).
AVCaptureDevice and AVCaptureVideoStabilizationMode are replaced by CaptureDevice and SettingsVideoStabilizationMode; AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer by PreviewView.
The Recorder settings dictionaries use android.media.MediaFormat keys/constants instead of AVVideoCodecKey, AVFormatIDKey, kAudioFormatMPEG4AAC etc.
`any AudioEncoderDelegate & VideoEncoderDelegate` has no Kotlin intersection type and is expressed as a generic `<T> where T : AudioEncoderDelegate, T : VideoEncoderDelegate`.
URLQueryItem/URLComponents are replaced by android.net.Uri + Uri.Builder; `numberOfFailedEncodings` is referenced but declared in another Media file of this package.
Swift's macro.variables is translated as the MacroVariables type from com.moblin.android.various.settings, called with removeAll(), set(...), get(...) and substitute(...) as in the Swift source.
The new sendTwitchShoutout action is dispatched through SettingsMacrosActionFunction.SEND_TWITCH_SHOUTOUT (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE to match the other cases already used in this file).
MacroVariable.TWITCH_RAID_CHANNEL_ID is the translation of the Swift case .twitchRaidChannelId; it is now imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
MacroEvent is assumed to expose the variables that the queued event carries, matching the new Swift event.variables usage.
executeSendChatMessage and executeIfCondition now take the macro variables and substitute them before formatting the text, exactly as in the new Swift code.
Everything outside the Swift diff, including the deliberate absence of the #available(iOS 17) guard in executeReaction, is unchanged.
MediaPlayerPlayer's @Published properties became MutableStateFlow: read `.value` outside Compose, `collectAsState()` in views.
Model's MediaPlayerDelegate conformance is emitted as Model extension functions; Model.kt must list MediaPlayerDelegate in its class header so `mediaPlayer.delegate = this` compiles.
`guard scene.videoSource.cameraPosition == .mediaPlayer` became a `!is SettingsCameraId.MediaPlayer` check, because SettingsCameraId is a sealed class whose MediaPlayer case carries an id.
Swift's uppercase UUID.uuidString is `id.toString().uppercase()` in playerCameras() and in getMediaPlayer(idString:).
DispatchQueue.main.async in mediaPlayerStateUpdate became mainScope.launch (mainScope from com.moblin.android).
The local `name` in mediaPlayerFileLoaded was renamed to bufferedName, because Kotlin forbids shadowing the parameter.
The playerId parameter of mediaPlayerStateUpdate is unused but kept to match MediaPlayerDelegate.
Calls media.addBufferedVideo/addBufferedAudio/removeBufferedVideo/removeBufferedAudio/appendBufferedVideoSampleBuffer/appendBufferedAudioSampleBuffer exactly as declared in Media.kt.
Settings models are assumed to expose MutableStateFlow properties: they are read with collectAsState() and written with .value, matching the mapping used elsewhere in the port.
key.colorColor maps to androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color and key.color to an Int RGB value; the Swift toRgb()/RGB black fallback becomes toArgb() and 0x00FFFFFF.
ColorPicker has no Compose counterpart and is left as TODO().

The NavigationLink in StreamDeckLayoutSettingsView is split into the row composable StreamDeckLayoutSettingsView (label + onNavigate) and the destination composable StreamDeckLayoutSettingsDetailView (the Form, kept public so a navigation graph in another file can host it).

The three Swift member helpers key(index:) became a single file-private composable streamDeckKeyView, and the static let size constants became file-private consts streamDeckMiniViewSize / streamDeckClassicViewSize / streamDeckXlViewSize.
List onMove/onDelete are not available in LazyColumn; each layout row gets arrow up/down and delete IconButtons that rewrite streamDecks.layouts.
Picker plus its onChange became an ExposedDropdownMenuBox whose item click sets the selection and calls model.setSelectedStreamDeck() directly.
minimumScaleFactor(0.5) on the key caption has no Compose equivalent; the Text is limited to maxLines = 2.
apple_only: ColorPicker -> TODO("ColorPicker has no Compose counterpart")

notes: Only the RemoteControlRemoteSceneSettingsWidgetTypeText mapping changed: the Swift font family/style pair is now stored as a whole SettingsFont value.
Constructor now reads text.font.family and text.font.style instead of the former text.fontFamily / text.fontStyle properties.
toSettings() now assigns text.font = SettingsFont(family = fontFamily, style = fontStyle ?: "") in one statement, mirroring the Swift single assignment.
Added the import com.moblin.android.various.settings.SettingsFont; nothing else in the file was touched.
The RemoteControlRemoteSceneSettingsWidgetTypeText wire fields fontFamily/fontStyle stay unchanged, so the JSON contract with remote clients is untouched.
Every other Kotlin line is byte-identical to the current file, including the hand-written Android hooks and the remoteControlJson setup.

MediaPlayersSettingsView takes model and mediaPlayers as parameters instead of @EnvironmentObject/@ObservedObject; the caller must supply them and read any StateFlow with collectAsState() so rows recompose.
Form/List/Section became one LazyColumn: the two explanatory Sections are header Text items, the player list is itemsIndexed, and the create button is a trailing item.
deletePlayer is a private top-level function receiving model and mediaPlayers, because a Kotlin top-level function has no access to the view's stored objects.
The Kotlin port of makeOffsets is assumed to return a nullable Int collection, and SettingsMediaPlayers.players is assumed to be a MutableList (add/removeAt are used).
onDelete(perform:) has no Compose equivalent; each row gets a trailing delete IconButton that runs the same deletePlayer path.
contextMenuDeleteButton is replaced by that delete IconButton; no Compose context-menu preview is used.
.navigationTitle("Media players") is expected to be rendered by the hosting screen's TopAppBar, which is not built in this file.
String(localized:) maps to the top-level localized() helper from package com.moblin.android.
Observed-model state is read with collectAsState(); writes assume the exposed StateFlow is backed by a MutableStateFlow (quickButtons.page.value = page).

ControlBarPageScrollTargetBehavior has no Compose counterpart: the iOS 17 page-scrolling branch becomes a HorizontalPager, which snaps pages natively; the class is kept as a thin wrapper over controlBarScrollTargetBehavior.
Only the iOS 17 branch of PagesView is translated; the legacy horizontal ScrollView fallback is dropped.
Size constants (controlBarWidthDefault, controlBarButtonSize, controlBarQuickButton*) are Double and converted to Dp with .dp; PageIndicatorView's size was CGFloat and becomes Float.
Image("\(store.iconImage)NoBackground") is resolved at runtime with Resources.getIdentifier and drawn with painterResource.
Small font is passed as the Text style parameter (smallFont is treated as a TextStyle).
The thermal state .sheet becomes a ModalBottomSheet driven by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }.
Modifiers with no Compose equivalent were dropped: .interpolation(.high) and .ignoresSafeArea(.all, edges:); edgesToIgnore() is kept but unused.
Renamed the Kick host event to Kick raid: KICK_HOST -> KICK_RAID with rawValue "Kick raid", updated toString() and the TWITCH_RAID/KICK_RAID branch of minimumAmountTitle().
Removed SettingsMacrosEvent.variablesToString() exactly as the Swift diff removes it.
Added MacroVariable.description() with the nine localized strings from Swift, placed after toString() as in the source.
Enum names in Kotlin keep UPPER_SNAKE entries; raw values stay byte-identical because they are persisted.
MacroVariable.description() is exhaustive over all entries, so no else branch is needed.
No other members of the file were touched; formatting, imports and declaration order are unchanged.
Callers outside this file that used SettingsMacrosEvent.KICK_HOST must be renamed to KICK_RAID separately.

RemoteControl's @Published properties become `_name` MutableStateFlow backings (declared `internal` so the Model extension functions in this same file can write them) plus public `name: StateFlow`, so assignments read `remoteControl._scene.value = ...`.

The three `extension Model: ...Delegate` blocks are emitted as top-level extension functions; Kotlin cannot add interface conformance from another file, so `Model` itself must declare `RemoteControlStreamerDelegate`, `RemoteControlAssistantDelegate` and `RemoteControlWebDelegate` (imports of those interfaces are left to Model.kt).

UIKit/Foundation types mapped: UIImage -> android.graphics.Bitmap, Data -> ByteArray, Date -> java.time.Instant, UUID -> java.util.UUID, CLLocation -> android.location.Location, `URL(string:)` -> java.net.URI built in runCatching, file URLs -> java.io.File.
WeatherKit `.converted(to: .celsius)` / `.converted(to: .metersPerSecond)` are dropped: the Kotlin weather model is assumed to already expose temperature in Celsius and wind speed/gust in m/s.
`statusOther.thermalState` is assumed to be an Int matching android.os.PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS_* constants (NONE/LIGHT -> white, MODERATE -> yellow, rest -> red).
AVFoundation AVURLAsset/AVAssetImageGenerator for recording thumbnails is replaced with android.media.MediaMetadataRetriever + Bitmap JPEG compression (quality 90, max 480x480).

Enum entries keep the Swift spelling in lowerCamelCase (RemoteControlAssistantPreviewUser.panel/.watch, RemoteControlFilter.movie, RemoteControlStatusGeneralFlame.white, ...) to stay readable next to the Swift source.

`SettingsQuickButtonType`, `SettingsWidgetType.scene` and `CameraPosition` are assumed to live in this same package (com.moblin.android.various.model) as in the Swift layout; `formatBytes` is assumed to be a numeric extension in com.moblin.android.common.various.

CreateStreamWizard keeps Swift property names and order; each @Published property is backed by a private MutableStateFlow exposed as a read/write property so the wizard form can still be mutated from UI code.
ContinuousClock.Instant has no direct Android type here, so it is modelled as Long milliseconds via SystemClock.elapsedRealtime(); updateStreamUptime/updateSpeed/checkLowBitrate take that Long.

MediaDelegate conformance cannot be added to Model from an extension in Kotlin, so the delegate callbacks are emitted as ordinary top-level Model extension functions and Model must be wired to MediaDelegate (or the calls dispatched) elsewhere.
VideoToolbox profile constants are mapped to android.media.MediaCodecInfo.CodecProfileLevel values (AVC/HEVC baseline/main/high/main10) passed to media.setVideoProfile.
Formatters from com.moblin.android.common.various (uptimeFormatter, sizeFormatter, formatBytesPerSecond) are assumed to expose a format(...) entry point, mirroring the Swift formatter call sites.
The UIKit snapshot (UIImage.jpegData) is converted with android.graphics.Bitmap.compress to a JPEG ByteArray before upload.
URLRequest/URLResponse/Data in mediaOnWhipPerform map to OkHttp Request/Response/ByteArray; the OkHttp body is materialised through an okio Buffer before forwarding to the remote-control assistant.
UIDevice.current.name becomes Build.MODEL, CGSize becomes android.util.Size, and the SwiftUI toast font (.system(size: 64).bold()) becomes FontWeight.Bold.

Everything else in the file is unchanged and kept byte-identical.

Each SwiftUI private struct becomes a private @Composable function with the same name; StreamButton stays public.

The shared generic RemoteControlPicker helper wraps ExposedDropdownMenuBox for every SwiftUI Picker (scene, auto scene switcher, mic, bitrate, zoom preset).

Calls into other Moblin files (NameEditView, TextItemLocalizedView, IconAndTextSettingView, StreamMultiStreamingSettingsView) assume parameter names matching their Swift counterparts.

onTapGesture(count: 1) becomes Modifier.clickable with indication = null and a MutableInteractionSource; Rectangle().foregroundStyle(.clear) becomes a Spacer with a fixed width.
RightOverlayTopView is wrapped in a Box carrying the padding so the translation does not have to assume a modifier parameter on that composable.
Added SettingsFont as an immutable data class (settings value) with name(), familyString() and styleString().

Private SwiftUI views became private @Composable functions with identical names (TwitchView, KickView, YouTubeView, SoopView, GoLiveNotificationView, ShortcutView).

.contextMenuDeleteButton has no Compose counterpart and was replaced by TODO().
.onMove reordering of database.scoreboardPlayers has no LazyColumn counterpart and was replaced by TODO(); the IndexSet based deletePlayer now takes a List<Int> of indices.

The padel scoreboard action struct passed to handleUpdatePadelScoreboard is not in the port glossary, so the argument is TODO().
The .font(.title) on the quick button container is dropped; the referenced button views carry their own typography.

NavigationLinks that carry a closure (GoProDeviceScannerSettingsView and WiFiSsidEditView) are rendered inline behind a remember state so their selection/save logic is preserved; the plain device row uses onNavigate("GoProBleDeviceSettingsView").

GoProBleDeviceSettingsView is public so the navigation host can reach it; the other helper views stay private as in the Swift source, and GoProDeviceSelectionSection gained a model parameter because it composes the scanner inline.

Section headers/footers become plain Text rows; .disabled on TextEditNavigationView rows cannot be expressed on a composable call and was dropped (the flag is passed through as-is where a component accepts it).
contextMenuDeleteButton + onDelete are translated to Modifier.combinedClickable(onLongClick = ...) calling model.removeGoProDevices(offsets).
Label(systemImage:) icons are mapped to Icons.Default.Info because the Swift symbol names have no guaranteed material-icons-core equivalent.
onChange(of: device.serverRtmpStreamId) is folded into the stream DropdownMenuItem click, which clears device.serverRtmpUrl like the Swift onChange did.
Form becomes a LazyColumn; every Section becomes a header Text followed by its rows, and the empty Text("") separators are kept verbatim.
onAppear becomes LaunchedEffect(Unit) at the top of the composable.
createStreamWizard.platform = .mobcam has no known counterpart enum member in this port, so it stays a TODO(); since TODO throws, the following name assignment only runs once that line is filled in.
navigationTitle plus toolbar become a Scaffold with a TopAppBar titled "Mobcam" whose actions host CreateStreamWizardToolbar.

The NavigationLink to StreamWizardGeneralSettingsView becomes onNavigate("StreamWizardGeneralSettingsView") on a clickable wrapper around WizardNextButtonView(), which is called with no arguments exactly as in Swift.
The OBS step text keeps its Markdown link inside a plain Text, so Compose renders the Markdown literally; real link handling needs AnnotatedString/LinkAnnotation.
makeUniqueName is called positionally as makeUniqueName(localized("Custom Mobcam"), model.database.streams).
model and createStreamWizard are plain parameters; no StateFlow collection is needed because this view only writes to createStreamWizard.
LutView stays a private top-level @Composable with the same parameter names (model, lut) as the Swift struct.
Swift Toggle(lut.name, isOn: $lut.enabled) becomes a Row holding a label Text with Modifier.weight(1f) and a Material 3 Switch.
SettingsColorLut.enabled is read with collectAsState(); the port is assumed to expose setEnabled(Boolean) for writing because the published StateFlow is read-only.
onChange(of: lut.enabled) is translated as LaunchedEffect(enabled) guarded by the previously seen value so sceneUpdated is not fired when the row first composes.
Form with a Section becomes a LazyColumn, and ForEach(color.allLuts()) becomes the items() extension over that list.
.navigationTitle("LUTs") becomes a Scaffold with a Material 3 TopAppBar title.
NavigationLink to CameraSettingsLutsView becomes onNavigate("CameraSettingsLutsView"); the color argument cannot be carried by the string destination, so the caller must resolve it.
Icons.Default.PhotoCamera stands in for systemImage "camera" and requires the material-icons-extended artifact.
SwiftUI Section + inline Picker becomes a Column with a header Text and an ExposedDropdownMenuBox picker, since Compose has no inline picker.

The `$lut.lut` binding is modelled as local remember state initialised from `lut.lut` and written back to `lut.lut` on selection; if SettingsVideoEffectLut exposes its published value as a StateFlow, replace these reads/writes with collectAsState().
LaunchedEffect(selectedLutId) also runs on first composition, so an `initialized` guard keeps it equivalent to SwiftUI's onChange(of:).
NavigationLink to CameraSettingsLutsView becomes an onNavigate callback parameter; the host screen must route the "CameraSettingsLutsView" destination.
ShortcutSectionView is called with a trailing content lambda; if its Kotlin signature differs, adjust the call site.
Icons.Default.PhotoCamera is the closest Material icon to the SF Symbol "camera".
Modifier.menuAnchor() is the classic Material 3 anchor; newer Material 3 versions prefer menuAnchor(MenuAnchorType.PrimaryNotEditable).
.pickerStyle(.inline) and .labelsHidden() have no Compose equivalent and are dropped.
CreateStreamWizard is assumed to expose its wizard fields as MutableStateFlow, so the screen reads them with collectAsState() and writes them with .value = it.
The Form is a LazyColumn; every Section became a Material 3 header Text followed by its items, and each footer a Column item.
.navigationTitle and .toolbar map to the Scaffold TopAppBar title and actions (CreateStreamWizardToolbar).

NavigationLink to StreamWizardGeneralSettingsView became onNavigate("StreamWizardGeneralSettingsView") on a clickable Box around WizardNextButtonView; nextDisabled() is used as Modifier.clickable(enabled = ...).
Image("ObsRemoteControl") is resolved as R.drawable.obs_remote_control with ContentScale.Fit and Modifier.fillMaxWidth() for resizable().scaledToFit().
.onAppear and .onChange(of: obsRemoteControlUrl) are LaunchedEffect(Unit) and LaunchedEffect(obsRemoteControlUrl), both calling the local updateUrlError lambda.
nextDisabled() stayed a private member-style helper, moved to a top-level private function taking createStreamWizard and urlError because it must not read Compose state.
model is kept only for signature parity; it is referenced by the navigation destination that is now a route name.
SwiftUI Form/Section becomes a LazyColumn where each section header Text is emitted before its fields.

CreateStreamWizard published properties (directIngest, directStreamKey, platform, twitchChannelName, networkSetup) are assumed to be MutableStateFlow in the port: reads use collectAsState(), writes use .value.
StreamingPlatformStatus cases are assumed to be Twitch, Kick, YouTube, Soop, Custom, Obs and Mobcam.
The networkSetup assignment uses CreateStreamWizard.NetworkSetup.Direct; adjust if NetworkSetup is a top-level enum in com.moblin.android.various.model.
Link(...) is rendered as a clickable Text that opens the URL through LocalUriHandler.

NavigationLink is replaced by an added onNavigate: (String) -> Unit parameter carrying the destination name "StreamWizardGeneralSettingsView"; model is kept for signature parity and is only needed by that destination.
String(localized:) literals become localized(...) and the toolbar composable is emitted in the TopAppBar actions slot while .navigationTitle becomes the TopAppBar title.
KeyboardOptions.autoCorrect is deprecated in recent Compose; use autoCorrectEnabled if the project builds against Compose UI 1.7 or newer.

The SwiftUI NavigationLink destination is extracted into a separate GimbalPresetDetailView composable; GimbalPresetView now only renders the clickable name row and reports navigation through an onNavigate(name) callback (no navigation-compose pulled in).

SettingsGimbal and SettingsGimbalPreset are assumed to expose MutableStateFlow properties: values are read with collectAsState() and written with .value. Bindings ($preset.name, $gimbal.zoomSpeed, ...) become a value plus an onChange lambda.
contextMenuDeleteButton has no Compose counterpart and is kept as a TODO() marker; the actual row deletion (Swift onDelete/remove(atOffsets:)) is implemented with a Material 3 SwipeToDismissBox.
Float.toRadians() is not part of the glossary, so the degree->radian conversion is inlined as value * PI / 180.
Slider step 1 over the closed range 10...100 becomes valueRange = 10f..100f with steps = 89, and the slider takes Modifier.weight(1f) so it fills the remaining row space like in SwiftUI.
The #available(iOS 18, *) availability check is dropped since the Android port targets API 26+; its content (Save current position) is always shown.
.navigationTitle is rendered with a Scaffold + TopAppBar ('Gimbal' and 'Preset').
The @ViewBuilder position() helper is inlined, and onAppear's LaunchedEffect(Unit) is declared before the state-change effects so it initialises the local x/y/zoomX before the onChange handlers run.
The SwiftUI Form is rendered as a LazyColumn inside a Scaffold whose TopAppBar title is "Custom" and whose actions slot hosts CreateStreamWizardToolbar, matching the .navigationTitle + .toolbar pair.
The four NavigationLink rows plus the WizardSkipButtonView row become clickable Rows that call onNavigate with the destination view name (no navigation-compose in this file).
.onAppear becomes LaunchedEffect(Unit) and runs the same wizard reset plus makeUniqueName(...) call; localized("Custom") comes from com.moblin.android.

CreateStreamWizard.platform and .customProtocol are set to Swift enum cases .custom and .none; the Kotlin enum type names were not part of the glossary, so those two assignments are TODO() and must be filled in with the real enum cases.
CreateStreamWizardToolbar is invoked with the createStreamWizard parameter exactly as in Swift and is placed in the TopAppBar actions slot.
The Section header "Protocol" is emitted as a plain header Text above the items, per the section mapping rule.
The destination views are not referenced directly because navigation is delegated to onNavigate; they live in the same package as this file.
@ObservedObject createStreamWizard becomes a parameter; its StateFlow properties are read with collectAsState() inside nextDisabled.
@State urlError becomes remember { mutableStateOf("") } and is forwarded to StreamWizardSrtUrlSettingsView as value plus an onUrlErrorChange lambda (SwiftUI Binding).

NavigationLink is replaced by the onNavigate: (String) -> Unit callback with destination name "StreamWizardObsRemoteControlSettingsView"; model is unused in this file but kept for signature parity with the Swift view.
Form/Section become LazyColumn items, .navigationTitle becomes the TopAppBar title ("SRT(LA)") and .toolbar places CreateStreamWizardToolbar in the TopAppBar actions.
.onAppear becomes LaunchedEffect(Unit).
WizardNextButtonView is called with named parameters enabled and onClick, matching the .disabled modifier on the NavigationLink.
Only composable functions are declared here, no top-level types.

@ObservedObject createStreamWizard is consumed as MutableStateFlow fields: belaboxUrl is read with collectAsState() and written via createStreamWizard.belaboxUrl.value = it; networkSetup is written the same way.
The Swift nested enum is assumed to stay nested, so the Kotlin reference is CreateStreamWizard.NetworkSetup.belaboxCloudObs.

NavigationLink to StreamWizardObsRemoteControlSettingsView becomes the onNavigate callback with route name "StreamWizardObsRemoteControlSettingsView"; model is kept for signature parity but is otherwise unused.
onChange(of: belaboxUrl) -> LaunchedEffect(belaboxUrl), onAppear -> LaunchedEffect(Unit) which also assigns networkSetup.
Form is a LazyColumn; the Section header "Ingest URL" is its own item and the footer VStack sits in a following item.
.navigationTitle becomes the TopAppBar title and .toolbar renders CreateStreamWizardToolbar in the TopAppBar actions slot.
Image asset "BelaboxCloudIngest" is mapped to R.drawable.belabox_cloud_ingest, which must exist in the Android resources.
nextDisabled() and updateUrlError() are kept as local functions inside the composable; urlError is a remember { mutableStateOf("") }.

NavigationLink became an onNavigate("Button") callback on GameControllersControllerButtonSettingsView; the destination Form (with ControllerButtonView) is kept as the extra composable GameControllersControllerButtonSettingsViewDestination, which the nav host must register, and the 'Button' navigationTitle is expected to be rendered by that host's TopAppBar.

@ObservedObject button is read via button.function.collectAsState() / button.functionData.collectAsState(); writes assume those published properties are exposed as MutableStateFlow (button.function.value = ...).
@Binding function/functionData became value parameters plus onFunctionChange/onFunctionDataChange lambdas; updates build a new SettingsControllerFunctionData via copy(...).
Picker -> ExposedDropdownMenuBox with ExposedDropdownMenu; the 'General'/'Filters' Sections are rendered as non-clickable label rows inside the menu.

Scene and widget dropdown entries re-look-up the model object by id so SceneNameView/WidgetNameView can render the item, and the collapsed field text uses model.getSceneName/getWidgetName plus the palette of listed names.

SettingsControllerFunction.toString(), SettingsControllerFunction.toString(sceneName:widgetName:) and SettingsControllerFunction.color() are expected as members/extensions in com.moblin.android.various.settings; SettingsControllerFunctionSection.general/.filters and SettingsGimbalMotion.entries are used for the sections and motions.
The Swift switch on function is translated as a Kotlin when with the same cases plus else -> Unit for the default EmptyView() branch.

CreateStreamWizard's published fields customRtmpUrl/customRtmpStreamKey/customProtocol are treated as MutableStateFlow: read with collectAsState() inside the composable and mutated with .value in callbacks and helpers.

model is not consumed here; the caller builds StreamWizardObsRemoteControlSettingsView when onNavigate("StreamWizardObsRemoteControlSettingsView") is invoked (NavigationLink became the onNavigate callback).
.disabled(nextDisabled()) became WizardNextButtonView(enabled = ...) on the next button.
navigationTitle("RTMP(S)") has no counterpart in this file: CreateStreamWizardToolbar is used as the Scaffold topBar and is expected to render the app bar title.
updateUrlError() returns the new error string instead of writing @State, because the state lives in the composable (urlError = remember { mutableStateOf("") }).
textInputAutocapitalization(.never) plus disableAutocorrection(true) map to KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.None, autoCorrectEnabled = false).
The .rtmp case assigned in onAppear is written as SettingsStreamProtocol.rtmp; adjust the enum name/entry to match the model package.
Form/Section/TextField placeholders map to LazyColumn with a header Text per section and OutlinedTextField placeholder texts.
Form is rendered as a LazyColumn; each SwiftUI Section becomes a header Text followed by its fields.
The navigation title "OBS" and CreateStreamWizardToolbar are rendered inside a Scaffold TopAppBar (actions slot).
createStreamWizard.obsAddress / obsPort are read with collectAsState() and written through their .value, so they are assumed to be MutableStateFlow in the ported CreateStreamWizard.
createStreamWizard.networkSetup = CreateStreamWizard.NetworkSetup.obs assumes the enum is nested in CreateStreamWizard and keeps the Swift case name 'obs'.
WizardNextButtonView is invoked with onClick/enabled; if the ported view is only a label, wrap it in a Modifier.clickable Box instead.
Image("ObsMediaSourceSrt") becomes painterResource(com.moblin.android.R.drawable.obs_media_source_srt).
Port validation uses toUShortOrNull() to mirror Swift's UInt16(port) initializer and its 1...65535 range check.
model is kept in the signature for parity but is unused here because the destination screen is reached through onNavigate.

Each SwiftUI View struct became a @Composable function with the identical name; because navigation-compose must not be pulled into this file, NavigationLink destinations are exposed through an onNavigate route callback.
Route strings follow the destination view names used in the Swift source: WidgetSettings, ScenesSettings, StreamPlatformsSettings, RemoteControlSettingsWeb, RemoteControlStreamers, IngestsSettings.
ShortcutSectionView's generic @ViewBuilder Content became a @Composable () -> Unit parameter; the SwiftUI Section header is a MaterialTheme.typography.titleSmall Text followed by the content.

The pushed destination views (WidgetSettingsView, ScenesSettingsView, StreamPlatformsSettingsView, RemoteControlSettingsWebView, RemoteControlStreamersView, IngestsSettingsView) are imported by the caller's navigation graph, so the model/database/widget/stream parameters are kept here for signature parity but are not consumed in the bodies.
The Form and navigationTitle of the pushed screens belong to the destination composables and are therefore not emitted here.

SF Symbols were mapped to the closest Material core icons: photo.on.rectangle -> Icons.Default.List, dot.radiowaves.left.and.right -> Icons.Default.Share, appletvremote.gen1 -> Icons.Default.PlayArrow, server.rack -> Icons.Default.Build; only core material-icons (no extended set) were used.
WidgetShortcutView keeps a plain Text label, matching the Swift source which has no systemImage.
settingsHalfWidth is kept as a top-level Double val (it is not referenced by this file).
AppModeView stays a private @Composable in the same file; @EnvironmentObject/@ObservedObject become explicit Model and Database parameters.
Form -> LazyColumn and each Form Section becomes a consecutive run of items (the Swift sections in this file have no headers); .navigationTitle("Settings") -> TopAppBar inside a Scaffold.
NavigationLink destinations are replaced by onNavigate("<DestinationViewName>") route strings per the navigation rule; the destination composables live in their own files.
database.appMode / database.showAllSettings are read with collectAsState() and written through the MutableStateFlow backing property (database.appMode.value = ...).
.onChange(of: database.appMode) -> LaunchedEffect(appMode) { model.appModeChanged() }; the Picker is disabled while live or recording.
The iOS 17 availability check for the Keyboard row is dropped (API 26+ target); the macCatalyst #if and isPad()/isPhone()/isMac() runtime checks are kept via the various.utils helpers.
SF Symbols are mapped to the closest Material icons with contentDescription = null; several of them live in material-icons-extended.
Form/Section layout becomes plain Columns with Text headers so these composables can be embedded by a caller's LazyColumn; no LazyColumn is created inside.
The Sport Picker is translated to a Row with an ExposedDropdownMenuBox, which requires @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class) and Modifier.menuAnchor().

ScoreboardColorsView was a NavigationLink, so it now renders only the 'Colors' label row and calls onNavigate("Colors"); its destination form lives in the new ScoreboardColorsFormView composable in this same file.
onChange(of: scoreboard.sport) maps to LaunchedEffect(sport), which also fires once on the first composition (SwiftUI's onChange does not).
Model objects are assumed to expose their @Published properties as MutableStateFlow: reads use collectAsState() (mostly with 'by') and writes use '.value ='.
Nested settings containers (modular/generic/padel/golf) are collected as whole objects; their own published fields such as config and clock are touched through '.value'.
All user visible strings are routed through localized(...) from package com.moblin.android, including the emoji warning text.
RgbColorPickerView and TextButtonView are invoked with a trailing lambda so the ported callback parameter name does not matter.
Form is translated to a LazyColumn; .navigationTitle becomes the title of a Material 3 TopAppBar inside a Scaffold (requires ExperimentalMaterial3Api opt-in).

The Swift @Binding arguments (sceneWidget.layout and database.sceneNumericInput) become a value parameter plus an onChange lambda; rename the lambda parameters if WidgetLayoutView's Kotlin signature differs.
database.sceneNumericInput is read with collectAsState() and written via MutableStateFlow.value.
widget.type == .scene becomes SettingsWidgetType.scene; keep the Kotlin enum constant naming used in com.moblin.android.various.settings.
model.database.scenes.first(where:) becomes firstOrNull { } inside the same if block, mirroring Swift's combined if/let.
SceneShortcutView is declared in this same package, so it is called without an import.
SceneWidgetSettingsView is emitted as a top-level @Composable function, not a type; the only declared top-level symbol is that function.
ShortcutSectionView's Swift ViewBuilder closure becomes a trailing @Composable lambda.
SwiftUI Form/Section becomes a LazyColumn with a header Text item followed by the two protocol rows.
NavigationLink destinations are replaced by an onNavigate: (String) -> Unit callback carrying the destination name; navigation-compose is not pulled in here.
navigationTitle and .toolbar become a Scaffold TopAppBar whose title is "My server(s)" and whose actions host CreateStreamWizardToolbar.
.onAppear becomes LaunchedEffect(Unit).
Background execution of the wizard-setup assignment is not needed; the assignment happens once when the composable enters composition.
The CreateStreamWizard network-setup enum case has no known Kotlin counterpart, so the assignment body is TODO().
GeometryReader/GeometryProxy became BoxWithConstraints; qrCodeHeight now takes a Dp width and returns Dp (Swift returned Double from a GeometryProxy).
Form/List/ForEach became Columns with Kotlin loops so the section composables can emit several children; only the outermost container scrolls to avoid nested verticalScroll crashes.
contextMenuDeleteButton became a long-press Modifier.pointerInput; SwiftUI .onMove drag reordering has no Compose counterpart and is not emitted.

NavigationLink destinations are surfaced as onNavigate route strings; the WiFiSsidEditView / TextEditView / TextEditNavigationView destination screens and their submit callbacks are wired by the caller.
navigationTitle has no Scaffold/TopAppBar in this file, so titles are left to the caller.
@ObservedObject/@EnvironmentObject settings and model types are treated as plain observable classes with mutable properties (read and written directly).

Assumed cross-file call shapes: NameEditView(name, existingNames, onChange), makeOffsets(list, id): List<Int>?, QrCodeImageView(image: Bitmap, height: Dp), rtmpServerStreamUrl(address, port, streamKey), IpType.ipv4/ipv6 from com.moblin.android.various.model.
UIImage became android.graphics.Bitmap and IndexSet became List<Int> (deleted in descending order).
SwiftUI views become @Composable functions with the same names; @EnvironmentObject/@ObservedObject properties become composable parameters, so no class is declared in this file.

Form/Section/List collapse into a single Column; the list of scene widgets is rendered with forEach over model.widgetsInCurrentScene(onlyEnabled = false), whose element type exposes widget and sceneWidget.
NavigationLink is replaced by Modifier.clickable on the row with TODO('NavigationLink to SceneWidgetSettingsView') because this port has no navigation graph type in the glossary.
Toggle(isOn:) + onChange is a Material 3 Switch whose onCheckedChange performs the same side effects (enabled write, reloadSpeechToText, sceneUpdated).
The switch over widget.type maps to a Kotlin when on SettingsWidgetType with else -> {} standing in for SwiftUI's default: EmptyView().
The trailing closure of WidgetBingoCardQuickButtonControlsView is kept as a trailing lambda and calls model.getBingoCardEffect(id = widget.id)?.setSettings(settings = widget.bingoCard).
navigationTitle("Scene widgets") has no equivalent in a plain composable and must be applied by the hosting screen; sceneSelector is kept as a parameter even though the body does not read it.

Property access (widget.image(), widget.name, widget.text, widget.bingoCard, widget.scoreboard, widget.pomodoroTimer, model.database) relies on the settings/model types from com.moblin.android.various.settings and com.moblin.android.various.model.
SwiftUI Form/Section becomes a LazyColumn with one item per navigation row plus its footer text.
NavigationLink closures become onNavigate(destinationName) calls; destination names are the Swift destination view type names.
navigationTitle goes to the TopAppBar title and the toolbar content becomes the TopAppBar actions with CreateStreamWizardToolbar.
Section footers are rendered as Text with MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall in onSurfaceVariant below each row.
The trailing SwiftUI Spacer() is implicit: the LazyColumn fills the remaining height via Modifier.weight(1f).
Icons.Default.ArrowForward stands for Image(systemName: "arrow.right"); icons are decorative so contentDescription is null.
model, createStreamWizard and platform are kept as parameters even though model is only forwarded to the destinations.
The multi-line footer string is collapsed into a single line, preserving the exact wording.

UIImage is replaced by androidx.compose.ui.graphics.ImageBitmap: GoPro.generateLaunchLiveStreamQrCode-style helpers, GoPro.generateWifiCredentialsQrCode, GoPro.generateRtmpUrlQrCode and QrCodeImageView are all assumed to use ImageBitmap in this port.
GeometryReader is replaced by BoxWithConstraints; qrCodeHeight is assumed to take the container height in dp as a Double and return the QR code height in dp.

The iOS 17 paging ScrollView (scrollPosition / scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)) becomes HorizontalPager; it is given a bounded height of qrCodeHeight + 90dp because pager children inside a LazyColumn need a bounded height.
SF Symbols 'circle'/'circle.fill' are not in material-icons-core, so the page dots are Boxes clipped to CircleShape with a theme colour; 'appletvremote.gen1' uses Icons.Default.Settings.
GoProRtmpUrlType is assumed to be the Kotlin enum for Swift's GoProRtmpUrl.type with the entries SERVER and CUSTOM.
@ObservedObject mutations are moved into callbacks (selection and selected* values) because the Kotlin models expose read-only StateFlows; the sub-views only read state in collectAsState().
onChange(of:) is a LaunchedEffect keyed on the watched value with a first-run guard so it does not fire on the first composition, matching SwiftUI.

NavigationLink to GoProSettingsView is reported through onNavigate("GoProSettingsView"), ShortcutSectionView is assumed to take a trailing composable content lambda, and .navigationTitle("GoPro") is left to the hosting screen's TopAppBar.

NavigationLink destinations are not rendered in this file: the pushed slide settings screen (WidgetSlideshowSlidePickerView + SwitcherTimePickerView + CloseToolbar) must be registered on the navigation host under the route name "widgetWizardSlideshowSlideSettings", which SlideView passes to onNavigate.
Swift's file-private SlideView and SlidesView are kept private here and shadow the same-named composables in com.moblin.android.view.settings.scenes.widgets.widget.slideshow.
contextMenuDeleteButton (SwiftUI long-press context menu) is implemented with pointerInput + DropdownMenu, since Compose has no context-menu modifier.
SwiftUI's onMove drag-to-reorder has no Compose counterpart, so it is exposed as Move Up / Move Down entries in the same long-press menu, backed by the private moveElement helper.
onDelete is handled by the menu's Delete entry calling slideshow.slides.removeAll { it.id == slide.id }.
@Binding presentingCreateWizard becomes a Boolean value parameter plus an onChangePresentingCreateWizard lambda.
.disabled(slideshow.slides.isEmpty) becomes enabled = slideshow.slides.isNotEmpty() on WidgetWizardSelectScenesNavigationView.
SlidesView keeps the mutable-list API (add/removeAll), so SettingsWidgetSlideshow.slides must be a MutableList; SlideView keeps its unused database/presenting parameters for signature parity.
Form/Section is rendered as a vertically scrolling Column with header and footer Text elements instead of SwiftUI sections.
CreateStreamWizard (and its nested kickStream) are treated as exposing MutableStateFlow properties: values are read with collectAsState() and written with .value = .
createStreamWizard.kickStream is treated as a plain object whose members are MutableStateFlow, matching the direct nested access of the Swift code.
.sheet(isPresented:) becomes a ModalBottomSheet shown while showKickAuth is true; dismissal writes false back to the flow.
NavigationLink is replaced by an onNavigate callback emitting "StreamWizardNetworkSetupSettingsView"; the platform argument ("Kick") is supplied by the caller that owns the navigation graph.
KickLoginView is invoked with only its completion lambda because its Kotlin parameter list is not known here; the presenting state is handled by the surrounding ModalBottomSheet.
TextButtonView is called with text/action parameters mirroring the Swift initializer labels.
.navigationTitle("Kick") and .toolbar are mapped to Scaffold + TopAppBar with CreateStreamWizardToolbar in the actions slot.

NavigationLink destinations are not inlined: SlideView renders a clickable summary row and calls onNavigate("slideSettings"); WidgetSlideshowSlidePickerView stays public so the destination screen can reuse it.
Settings holders (Database, SettingsWidgetSlideshow, SettingsWidgetSlideshowSlide) are treated as @Serializable settings classes with plain properties, so no collectAsState is used.
ForEach.contextMenuDeleteButton becomes a long-press (Modifier.combinedClickable) that calls deleteSlide, mirroring the single-delete context menu.
ForEach.onMove (drag to reorder) has no Compose counterpart and is left to the host list; the reorder logic is not wired here.
Section becomes a header Text, its items, and a footer Text/SwipeLeftToDeleteHelpView inside a Column.
Form becomes a Column; String(localized: "a slide") becomes localized("a slide").
SlideView still takes database (and model) because the slide detail screen needs them.
IndexSet becomes List<Int> from makeOffsets; deleteSlide removes indices in descending order.
SwiftUI Section became a Column with a header Text; this composable is not itself scrollable, it must be hosted inside the parent settings Column/LazyColumn.
NavigationLink became an onNavigate callback with the destination name "WidgetSettingsView"; the host navigation graph must resolve that destination and pass the widget (e.g. by widget id).

Toggle(isOn: $widget.enabled) became a Material 3 Switch reading and writing widget.enabled directly; if the Kotlin SettingsWidget exposes enabled as a StateFlow, read it with collectAsState() instead.
onChange(of: widget.enabled) became LaunchedEffect(widget.enabled), which also fires once on first composition, unlike Swift's onChange.
.swipeActions(edge: .trailing, allowsFullSwipe: false) became SwipeToDismissBox with enableDismissFromStartToEnd = false.
.contextMenuDeleteButton has no Material 3 counterpart, so the long press is a TODO(); deletion itself still works through the swipe action.
ForEach.onMove drag reordering has no Material 3 counterpart: the reorder logic is kept in the (currently unwired) onMove lambda and must be attached to a drag gesture by hand.

.sheet became ModalBottomSheet around WidgetWizardSettingsView; the @Binding became value plus onPresentingCreateWizardChange, .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline) has no equivalent, and if the Kotlin WidgetWizardSettingsView also declares onNavigate it must be threaded from here.

StreamWizardSoopSettingsView becomes a top-level @Composable with the same name taking model, createStreamWizard and an onNavigate callback; the Swift NavigationLink to StreamWizardNetworkSetupSettingsView is expressed as onNavigate("StreamWizardNetworkSetupSettingsView").

createStreamWizard.soopChannelName / soopStreamId are read with collectAsState() and written back through the MutableStateFlow .value setter, since SwiftUI's $createStreamWizard binding has no direct Compose equivalent.
The Swift .onAppear block runs in a LaunchedEffect(Unit) and assigns platform, name and directIngest on the shared CreateStreamWizard instance.
createStreamWizard.platform = .soop is translated as CreateStreamWizard.Platform.soop; adjust the enum name/case if CreateStreamWizard declares it differently.
