WizardNextButtonView is assumed to expose an onClick lambda, which is triggered by the navigation callback.

Form/Section become a LazyColumn of items, each with a plain section header Text, and .navigationTitle/.toolbar become a Scaffold TopAppBar with title "SOOP" and the CreateStreamWizardToolbar in its actions.
disableAutocorrection/ textInputAutocapitalization map to KeyboardOptions(autoCorrectEnabled = false, capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.None).
SwiftUI ToolbarContent became a @Composable CreateStreamWizardToolbar placed in the TopAppBar actions slot, with the xmark Image(systemName:) mapped to Icon(Icons.Default.Close).

NavigationLink destinations became onNavigate("<DestinationTypeName>") callbacks; the caller is responsible for routing to StreamWizardTwitchSettingsView, StreamWizardKickSettingsView, StreamWizardYouTubeSettingsView, StreamWizardSoopSettingsView, StreamWizardObsSettingsView, StreamWizardMobcamSettingsView and StreamWizardCustomSettingsView.
The Swift YouTube link forwards createStreamWizard.youTubeStream explicitly; in Kotlin the destination view receives the same CreateStreamWizard instance so it can read youTubeStream itself.
Form + Section became a LazyColumn with a titleSmall header Text and a footer Text, matching the Swift header/footer placement.
Color.accentColor on the Next/Skip labels became MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary via the Text color parameter.
The Mobcam row stays behind the same if (!isMac()) guard imported from com.moblin.android.various.utils.
StreamWizardSettingsView takes model and createStreamWizard as parameters as in Swift; model is not read directly in this file.
TopAppBar is used with @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class).

SwiftUI View structs become top-level @Composable functions; @Binding is modelled as MutableState and nested property bindings (layout.x, widget.name, database.sceneNumericInput) are passed as value + on*Change lambdas so the external edit views can write back.
@EnvironmentObject / @ObservedObject become plain constructor parameters (Model, Database, SettingsWidget) since Compose has no environment object concept here.
Form/Section/Toggle become Column + Text header + Row/Switch; the .navigationTitle modifier has no in-composable equivalent and must be supplied by the navigation host (see unsupported list).
.onChange(of: layout.alignment) becomes LaunchedEffect(layout.value.alignment), which also fires on first composition rather than only on change.
SF Symbols are mapped to Material icons (square/lock/lock.open/arrow.*.circle); this requires the material-icons-extended artifact.
CMVideoDimensions is mapped to android.util.Size and read through its width/height properties.

Enum entries of SettingsAlignment/SettingsWidgetType are kept in the original Swift camelCase spelling (topLeft, qrCode, vTuber, pomodoroTimer, ...) to preserve naming fidelity with the shared settings module.
widget.image() is assumed to return an androidx.compose.ui.graphics.vector.ImageVector consumed by Icon.

@Published properties of CreateStreamWizard are read with collectAsState() and written through `.value`, so CreateStreamWizard must expose MutableStateFlow-backed properties (twitchChannelName, twitchChannelId, twitchAccessToken, twitchLoggedIn, directStreamKey, showTwitchAuth, name, directIngest).

onLoginComplete() wraps the TwitchApi.getStreamKey completion handler in a coroutine launched from rememberCoroutineScope(); getStreamKey is assumed to be a suspend function returning the nullable stream key.
model.twitchLogin is called positionally because the Swift third (unlabeled trailing closure) parameter has no name we can mirror.
The `.sheet(isPresented:)` binding becomes a value parameter plus an onPresentingChange lambda on TwitchLoginView.
The NavigationLink becomes WizardNextButtonView(enabled = ..., onClick = ...) calling onNavigate("StreamWizardNetworkSetupSettingsView"); the host must map that route.
Swift's `.twitch` enum case is emitted as CreateStreamWizard.Platform.Twitch.
.navigationTitle / .toolbar map to a Scaffold with a Material3 TopAppBar whose actions are CreateStreamWizardToolbar.
.disableAutocorrection(true) and .textInputAutocapitalization(.never) map to KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.None).
Every SwiftUI View became one @Composable function with the same name; @Binding became a value parameter plus an onChange lambda.
NavigationLink destinations are reported through an added onNavigate: (String) -> Unit parameter that carries the destination view name as route.
SceneToAddWidgetTo keeps its @Published enabled as a private MutableStateFlow exposed as StateFlow; the view mutates it through the added toggleEnabled() function.

Assumes model objects (CreateWidgetWizard, Database) expose their published state as public MutableStateFlow: reads use collectAsState(), writes use .value; Database collections are StateFlow<List<...>> that are replaced on write.
WizardNextButtonView is called with an assumed enabled parameter, CloseToolbar with assumed presenting/onPresentingChange parameters; TextButtonView uses a trailing onClick lambda.
Picker became an ExposedDropdownMenuBox in a Row, Form/Section became a LazyColumn with header Texts, toolbar became the CloseToolbar composable.
Enum members and SettingsWidgetType case names are assumed to match the Swift spellings (text, browser, videoSource, image, slideshow, vTuber, pngTuber, wheelOfLuck, bingoCard, scoreboard).
The two user-facing strings go through localized() from com.moblin.android, keeping Swift string interpolation.
Form/Section is translated to a vertically scrolling Column with header and footer Text composables in place of Section header/footer.
.navigationTitle and .toolbar become a Scaffold TopAppBar whose title is "YouTube" and whose actions slot hosts CreateStreamWizardToolbar.
NavigationLink is replaced by the onNavigate: (String) -> Unit callback, invoked by WizardNextButtonView with the destination name "StreamWizardNetworkSetupSettingsView".
WizardNextButtonView, CreateStreamWizardToolbar and TextButtonView are called with their ported Compose signatures; the action/click handler is passed as a trailing lambda.
createStreamWizard and youTubeStream published properties are read with collectAsState() and written through .value on the backing MutableStateFlow.
.onAppear becomes LaunchedEffect(Unit) and .onChange(of: youTubeStream.youTubeAuthState) becomes LaunchedEffect(youTubeAuthState).
.textInputAutocapitalization(.never) and .disableAutocorrection(true) become KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.None, autoCorrectEnabled = false).
The YouTube API result switch inside fetchLiveStreams/fetchChannelHandle is left as TODO because the YouTube API port type is not part of the glossary.

The diff adds `.id(button.id)` to QuickButtonsButtonSettingsView; in Kotlin this is modelled with `key(button.id) { ... }`, matching the existing `key(sceneSettingsPanelSceneId)` pattern for sceneSettings.
Only the ShowingPanel.quickButtonSettings branch of MenuView changed; every other line is byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file.
`key` is already imported from androidx.compose.runtime, so no import changes were needed.
The added `key(...)` wraps only the QuickButtonsButtonSettingsView call so the composable is recreated when the edited quick button changes.
WatchProtocolWorkoutStats.update(statistics:) relied on HealthKit; its body is TODO and the parameter is typed Any because HKStatistics has no Android counterpart in the glossary.
Codable structs became @Serializable data classes; Swift optionals (which decode as missing-key -> nil) keep = null defaults so kotlinx.serialization accepts absent keys.
Raw-value enums keep their Swift case names as entries plus a rawValue property and a companion fromRawValue, so packed strings stay byte-identical.
pack/unpack are companion functions returning Map<String, Any> and Pair<WatchMessageToWatch, Any>? instead of [String: Any] and a Swift tuple.
The two enums with associated values (padel and generic scoreboard actions) became @Serializable sealed classes with nested object/data class cases and @SerialName matching the Swift case names.
URL properties are stored as String, as this file never parses them.
The SwiftUI extension on WatchProtocolColor is now a file-private colorScale extension followed by a Compose Color extension; colors are converted to Float channels.
WatchProtocolChatHighlightKind and WatchProtocolWorkoutType have no raw values, so they are plain @Serializable enum classes whose entry names match the Swift case names.
apple_only: HealthKit (HKStatistics, HKUnit, heart rate / energy / distance / step / power / cadence quantity types)

notes: @Published properties map to a private MutableStateFlow backing field plus a public read-only StateFlow, so the Compose/Wear UI can collect them.
StateFlow is not serializable, so each class is annotated @Serializable(with = ...) and carries a nested Serializer object with a private Snapshot data class that reproduces the Swift CodingKeys.
JSON keys and the missing-key fallbacks (17.0, true, false, 30, ...) are byte-identical to the Swift encode(to:)/init(from:) helpers.
The nested CodingKeys enums are kept from Swift for side-by-side reading; the actual element names are set with @SerialName.
chat and show stay plain mutable properties, matching Swift's non-@Published vars; the outer class encodes them through the nested serializers.
The app must serialize with Json { encodeDefaults = true } to match Swift, which always writes every key.
The types stay reference types (plain classes), so equality is identity based, exactly like the Swift classes.
Serializer and Snapshot are Kotlin-only additions required by kotlinx.serialization; no other API was invented.

FontFamilyPickerView and FontStylePickerView are private SwiftUI structs and become private @Composable functions; FontSettingsView stays public and emits its two NavigationLinks as siblings, exactly like the SwiftUI TupleView body.

@Binding var font: SettingsFont becomes font: MutableState<SettingsFont>; SettingsFont is an immutable data class, so font.style = s is font.value = font.value.copy(style = s) and FontSettingsView passes the same state down to both pickers.

The Swift List inside the Form Section is dropped: its rows are rows of the Section, and each row HStack becomes FormRow(onClick = ...) so the whole row is the button, with the checkmark drawn by SystemImage.
Form + navigationTitle is Form(title = "Family") / Form(title = "Style"); the FontStylePickerView List is wrapped in a Section so its rows keep iOS insets and separators.
.onAppear is DisposableEffect(Unit) with an empty onDispose, and it only loads the families when the remembered list is empty.
loadFontFamilies() (a static method of the struct) and fontStyles() (a private method of the second struct) exist as file-private top-level functions with the same names.

fontStyleName keeps Swift's grapheme-cluster semantics: hasPrefix/count/dropFirst are done with java.text.BreakIterator character instances instead of UTF-16 units, since the truncated suffix is displayed.

CoreText and UIFont come from the hand-written shims (CTFontCollectionCreateFromAvailableFonts/CreateMatchingFontDescriptors/CopyAttribute, UIFont.familyNames, UIFont.fontNames), and GrayTextView is imported from com.moblin.android.view.settings.streams.stream.
The Swift #if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst) block is dropped: the whole file applies to Android, so both types are declared unconditionally.
LiveActionFunction is a Codable, Hashable struct, so it becomes @Serializable data class with the same property order (image, text).
LiveActivityAttributes conforms to ActivityAttributes, which is an Android interface without members, so the class header keeps the conformance and the nested ContentState stays nested.
ContentState is Codable, Hashable, so it is an @Serializable data class inside LiveActivityAttributes; 'functions' maps the Swift array to List<LiveActionFunction> and 'showEllipsis' to Boolean.
Section headers come from com.moblin.android.platform.activitykit, the shim that renders the Live Activity as Moblin's ongoing notification; never use NotificationManager for it.
The Swift property names become the JSON keys, so the activity content stays wire-compatible between the two apps.
The Swift labelled tuple (toLinear:toHlg:) becomes the file-private HlgKernels data class so the field labels survive side-by-side reading.
hlgKernels stays a file-private val evaluated with lazy, matching the one-shot Swift initializer.
Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:) plus Data(contentsOf:) collapse into Bundle.readBytes("default", "metallib").
try? CIColorKernel(functionName:fromMetalLibraryData:) becomes runCatching { ... }.getOrNull(), so a failing kernel leaves hlgKernels null as on iOS.
hlgToLinear() and linearToHlg() return the receiver when the kernels are unavailable, exactly like Swift's ?? self.
CIColorKernel.apply is called with named extent/arguments so it resolves to the shim member instead of Kotlin's stdlib apply.
The hlgToLinear and linearToHlg kernels must be registered in CIKernelLibrary (the GLSL port of default.metallib); otherwise the shim constructor throws and both functions pass the image through.
